每天早上醒来，我面对的都是这样的场景。早在运营“黑灯工厂”时，我就不断碰到各种限制：令牌被限流、内存或算力耗尽，或者 CI 持续集成出现瓶颈。问题从来不是我能让智能体跑多快。我起初并行运行 10 到 15 个智能体，后来增加到 60 个。昨天我看了一眼，自己的“工厂”里已经有 300 多个智能体在并行工作。我昨天大概提交了 1000 到 1500 个 PR，前一天接近 2000 个。顺便说一句，当时我人在中国，只是在酒店房间里用笔记本电脑工作，其中一半操作还是通过手机上的 Telegram 完成的。这仍然是在用框架构建框架。

但无论我们跑得多快，总会遇到某个瓶颈。在我这里，瓶颈已经不是能否自动合并 PR、能否让框架包办所有工作，而是**如何证明成果有效**：我们怎么知道它真的能运行、真的达到了预期？当然，我们可以写单元测试，有些情况也能由人来验证，但人工验证的吞吐量很低。我们的发布流程已经高度自动化，AI 就像一座工厂，但瓶颈始终存在。有时瓶颈甚至不在测试本身，而在测试容量：我的机器能同时验证多少个 PR，并将它们合入代码库？这里存在理论上的上限。Open Claw 是 GitHub 上迭代最快的开源代码库之一，我们很快就发现了这一点——能想到的各家公司、各家服务商的限流，我们几乎都碰过。

于是，我想合并一个 PR，智能体也已经完成了工作，但我们都在等验证结果。它们可能在写测试，也可能把功能放进 Telegram 或虚拟环境里，实际操作并确认它能运行。等待的时候，我会再启动一个智能体，但这有代价。我希望尽快合入改动，因为改动合入得越快，其他智能体就越早能用上它。我们是在用 Open Claw 构建 Open Claw，等于一边飞一边造飞机。飞机升级得越快，大家受益就越快；但这个过程会产生滚雪球效应，也会遇到瓶颈。

举个例子，Peter 大概在九月发过一条推文，展示了我们称为 Open Claw 2 的新版本。它是一个多人协作环境，具备完全开源的电脑操作能力、虚拟化等很多功能。我们想改进电脑操作功能，于是把《毁灭战士》放了进去，让智能体玩游戏，再让它反复优化自己的速度：每发现一个拖慢自己的环节，就设法加速。游戏运行和智能体操作得越快，它完成游戏的表现就越好。智能体已经了解这个游戏；如果它能获胜，又能进一步加速，延迟就会下降，能力也会提升。而这种延迟优化最终会改善产品，让 Open Claw 成为更快的框架，也让我们这些使用 Open Claw 构建 Open Claw 的工程师受益。

这里有两类工作。一类是**后台工作**：目标明确，我们检查结果、做出改进，再不断重复。这就是我们熟悉的传统循环式工程。另一类是**前台工作**：比如需要大量人工关注的功能开发。即使在这些工作中，我现在也越来越倾向于先问：能否在动手之前，就定义好什么算有效、期望的结果是什么？我的前台工程工作正朝这个方向转移，而后台工作则持续自动进行。如果你现在去看 Open Claw 仓库的 Git 提交记录，很可能此刻就有代码正在提交。我这里有笔记本，手机也带在身上；那些能够自动验证的具体修复和问题，后台流程会自行测试、验证并合并。

变化在于：过去我们做的是“循环式工程”。后来我开始谈“意图工程”——循环虽然有效，但产出不一定符合我的意图。于是问题变成：如何把我的意图、行为方式、理解和目标，注入框架或模型？比如我们有一个叫 Claw Sweeper 的系统，其中的审查智能体会检查每一个 PR 和议题，它也是开源的。顺便说一句，我们的整个基础设施都是开源的。意图工程会尝试主动检查、验证，并做合理性判断，但即便如此，功能发布后仍可能退化、出错。

所以我现在认为，我们正在从“意图工程”走向**“验证工程”**：能否把验证条件写成代码？能否告诉机器什么是理想结果，以及如何核实？我发现自己越来越多地在做这件事：教会机器判断自己的工作是否有效。一旦能够证明有效，我们就能更好地围绕这个结果持续迭代。换句话说，我从“工厂经理”变成了我所说的“验证工程师”，或者通俗点说，成了一个凭直觉设计评测的人。验证工程很大一部分就是评测，稍后我会展开讲。

我们的目标是先选定一座要攀登的山，再让登山的成本降下来。一旦我们能清楚地定义验证标准、奖励机制或任务目标，让智能体理解什么是成功，接下来的问题就是：怎样让它以最快、最低的成本达到目标。今天很多人都在讨论框架工程，也能看到大量相关实践。但我不想只停留在某个编程基准测试的分数上，而是想弄清它在实际工作中意味着什么。

拿《毁灭战士》的例子来说，真正要问的是：智能体能不能玩这个游戏？能不能越玩越快？再比如稍后我要讲的 CI/CD：为了让持续集成更便宜、更快，我们会关闭某些测试，采取一些更智能的做法。但代价是跳过了部分检查，只能希望不会引入回归。因此关键问题是：我们有没有抓住那些回归问题？我们是在运用常识判断，觉得自己知道会发生什么……

zh: 如果工厂运转慢下来，它就无法自行修复。
en: If the factory slows down, the factory can't fix itself.

source_text: So there is this point where it becomes unusable.
zh: 所以慢到一定程度，这套系统就没法用了。
en: So there is this point where it becomes unusable.

source_text: So bringing the CI cost down was one component, but we also had to bring the speed up. And usually those two things don't go hand in hand.
zh: 所以，降低 CI 成本只是其中一方面，我们还得提升速度。而这两件事通常很难兼顾。
en: So bringing the CI cost down was one component, but we also had to bring the speed up. And usually those two things don't go hand in hand.

source_text: So on the left we have the number of jobs of CIs.
zh: 左边展示的是 CI 作业的数量。
en: So on the left we have the number of jobs of CIs.

source_text: And we see that, yes, we're now running less jobs because of all the changes we've done, but also at the same time the price of the jobs do go up at the same time,
zh: 可以看到，经过这一系列调整，现在运行的 CI 作业确实少了，但单个作业的成本也在上升。
en: And we see that, yes, we're now running less jobs because of all the changes we've done, but also at the same time the price of the jobs do go up at the same time,

source_text: because we're adding more complexity, or we're doing things like spending more compute to make things faster. So those two things are like asymmetrical, and they don't tend to go well together.
zh: 因为我们增加了系统复杂度，或者投入更多算力来提升速度。所以，降低成本和提升速度这两个目标并不对等，通常很难兼顾。
en: because we're adding more complexity, or we're doing things like spending more compute to make things faster. So those two things are like asymmetrical, and they don't tend to go well together.

source_text: We also have this problem where if we create more work for ourselves, it doesn't equal more proof.
zh: 我们还面临一个问题：给自己增加更多工作，并不等于能得到更多验证。
en: We also have this problem where if we create more work for ourselves, it doesn't equal more proof.

source_text: It actually becomes more worse.
zh: 情况实际上会变得更糟。
en: It actually becomes more worse.

source_text: And what we've noticed is that the more and more and more and more code we were shipping,
zh: 我们发现，随着我们发布的代码越来越多，
en: And what we've noticed is that the more and more and more and more code we were shipping,

source_text: it actually reached a point, I believe, about a month or so ago, where the volume of commits actually eclipsed and started to become a real bottleneck for us.
zh: 大约一个月前，提交量已经增长到超过 CI 的处理能力，开始成为我们真正的瓶颈。
en: it actually reached a point, I believe, about a month or so ago, where the volume of commits actually eclipsed and started to become a real bottleneck for us.

source_text: And when we look at that, we started seeing that things started to kind of slow down a little bit.
zh: 回头看这些数据，我们发现整个流程开始有点放慢了。
en: And when we look at that, we started seeing that things started to kind of slow down a little bit.

source_text: So one of the main factors of slowing—fixing this—was actually we turned off CI checks on main entirely.
zh: 所以，为了解决这个速度变慢的问题，我们采取的一项主要措施，就是彻底关闭了主分支上的 CI 检查。
en: So one of the main factors of slowing—fixing this—was actually we turned off CI checks on main entirely.

source_text: So what happens now is you have, like, a limited check that happens on a PR, the agent will go through the review process,
zh: 现在的流程是：PR 上只会运行有限的检查，然后由智能体完成代码审查。
en: So what happens now is you have, like, a limited check that happens on a PR, the agent will go through the review process,

source_text: there's some smart smarts in there about how often it reviews and when it doesn't.
zh: 它还有一套智能机制，会判断多久审查一次，以及什么时候不需要审查。
en: there's some smart smarts in there about how often it reviews and when it doesn't.

source_text: And then once that PR is merged, the main doesn't do a CI check.
zh: 然后，PR 一旦合并，主分支就不会再运行 CI 检查。
en: And then once that PR is merged, the main doesn't do a CI check.

source_text: That happens every, say, 30 minutes to an hour, and we have some more extensive testing that happens as part of our release process.
zh: 这类检查大约每 30 分钟到一小时运行一次；发布流程中还会进行更全面的测试。
en: That happens every, say, 30 minutes to an hour, and we have some more extensive testing that happens as part of our release process.

source_text: Now, the more interesting thing that I'm going to get to is a little bit later.
zh: 不过，更有意思的部分我稍后再讲。
en: Now, the more interesting thing that I'm going to get to is a little bit later.

source_text: You see on the left-hand side, the total cost of the runs has started to go down.
zh: 大家可以看到，左侧显示的运行总成本已经开始下降。
en: You see on the left-hand side, the total cost of the runs has started to go down.

source_text: So 100 CI runs was costing us about 1,000-something US dollars, and we've been able to get that down to 200-something dollars which is good.
zh: 也就是说，原来跑 100 次 CI 要花一千多美元，现在我们已经把成本降到了两百多美元，效果不错。
en: So 100 CI runs was costing us about 1,000-something US dollars, and we've been able to get that down to 200-something dollars which is good.

source_text: And on the right-hand side you'll see—actually I'm going to keep going—
zh: 再看右边，你会发现——算了，我还是接着往下讲。
en: And on the right-hand side you'll see—actually I'm going to keep going—

source_text: You can see the time taken for CI.
zh: 可以看到 CI 运行所花的时间。
en: You can see the time taken for CI.

source_text: So yes, we've made the optimizations, it does the big spikes that we're seeing, like where it was taking 20 to 30 minutes to run a PR through CI checks, no longer takes that long.
zh: 对，我们做了优化。图中那些耗时高峰，比如以前一个 PR 跑完 CI 检查要 20 到 30 分钟，现在已经不需要那么久了。
en: So yes, we've made the optimizations, it does the big spikes that we're seeing, like where it was taking 20 to 30 minutes to run a PR through CI checks, no longer takes that long.

source_text: The actual total time for a PR to get merged was something like an hour or two hours in the peak of it, because we've run other agents doing other security checks and things like that. So bringing the time down was, like, critical for us.
zh: 在最慢的时候，一个 PR 从提交到合并总共要一两个小时，因为我们还会运行其他代理，做安全检查之类的工作。所以，缩短这个时间对我们至关重要。
en: The actual total time for a PR to get merged was something like an hour or two hours in the peak of it, because we've run other agents doing other security checks and things like that. So bringing the time down was, like, critical for us.

source_text: But also keeping it cheap was critical.
zh: 但同时，控制成本也至关重要。
en: But also keeping it cheap was critical.

source_text: Now,
zh: 那么，
en: Now,

source_text: the real question actually became proof, because if we knew there was a more systematic way for us to understand the proof,
zh: 真正的问题其实变成了如何验证：如果我们能用更系统的方法来理解这些验证依据，
en: the real question actually became proof, because if we knew there was a more systematic way for us to understand the proof,

source_text: we wouldn't have to test everything in theory, right?
zh: 理论上，我们就不用测试所有东西了，对吧？
en: we wouldn't have to test everything in theory, right?

source_text: We wouldn't have to test entire everything every single time.
zh: 我们就不必每次都把所有东西从头到尾测试一遍。
en: We wouldn't have to test entire everything every single time.

source_text: We can be a little bit smarter and actually understand what was affected and only test that part.
zh: 我们可以更有针对性地判断哪些部分受到了影响，只测试这些部分。
en: We can be a little bit smarter and actually understand what was affected and only test that part.

source_text: This concept is known as adaptive testing, where your tests are adapting to the environment that it's testing.
zh: 这个概念叫作自适应测试，也就是让测试根据被测环境的变化进行调整。
en: This concept is known as adaptive testing, where your tests are adapting to the environment that it's testing.

source_text: It's a little bit more different than just,
zh: 这跟单纯地……还是有些不同。
en: It's a little bit more different than just,

source_text: like, hey, see what code changed and let's just test that.
zh: 比如说，“看看改了哪些代码，只测试那些代码就行了。”
en: like, hey, see what code changed and let's just test that.

source_text: This was merged into our main codebase as of, like, the last few days, and hasn't been fully activated yet.
zh: 这项功能前几天才合并到我们的主代码库，还没有完全启用。
en: This was merged into our main codebase as of, like, the last few days, and hasn't been fully activated yet.

source_text: Because my compute bill is about to arrive next week.
zh: 因为我的算力账单下周就要到了。
en: Because my compute bill is about to arrive next week.

source_text: So I've got a few more days to solve this problem before the compute becomes a problem.
zh: 所以我还有几天时间解决这个问题，不然算力开销就要成问题了。
en: So I've got a few more days to solve this problem before the compute becomes a problem.

source_text: But essentially what we're doing here is building a model of proof using classifiers and tree-based classifiers to essentially see based on the code that was changed and what was executed,
zh: 但本质上，我们是在利用分类器和基于树的分类器构建一个验证模型，根据改动了哪些代码、执行了哪些代码来判断……
en: But essentially what we're doing here is building a model of proof using classifiers and tree-based classifiers to essentially see based on the code that was changed and what was executed,

source_text: can we kind of have a good understanding of what's going to have a likelihood of regression,
zh: 我们能否比较准确地判断哪些部分有较高的回归风险，
en: can we kind of have a good understanding of what's going to have a likelihood of regression,

source_text: and then just test that component?
zh: 然后只测试那部分组件？
en: and then just test that component?

source_text: And then by doing that, we're able to actually get the same hit rate of finding failures with just a very, very limited subset.
zh: 这样一来，我们只需运行极少一部分测试，就能达到同样的故障检出率。
en: And then by doing that, we're able to actually get the same hit rate of finding failures with just a very, very limited subset.

source_text: So this was before even this huge check changed and happened.
zh: 所以，这还是在那次大规模检查变更发生之前。
en: So this was before even this huge check changed and happened.

source_text: So my understanding, I'm hoping for, is something close to a 90.5 to 98 percent reduction in our total CI cost.
zh: 所以按我的理解，我希望能把我们的 CI 总成本降低约 90.5% 到 98%。
en: So my understanding, I'm hoping for, is something close to a 90.5 to 98 percent reduction in our total CI cost.

source_text: And that's going to enable us to continue to hill climb across a number of other factors as well.
zh: 这样一来，我们也能在其他多个方面持续迭代优化。
en: And that's going to enable us to continue to hill climb across a number of other factors as well.

source_text: So the other component to this as well is, like I mentioned, is, like, understanding what was changed and getting a little bit more smarter around this as well.
zh: 另外，正如我刚才提到的，我们还需要弄清楚具体改动了什么，并在此基础上更智能地判断该测哪些部分。
en: So the other component to this as well is, like I mentioned, is, like, understanding what was changed and getting a little bit more smarter around this as well.

source_text: So that's going to drastically speed up what's going to happen.
zh: 这样就能大幅加快整个流程。
en: So that's going to drastically speed up what's going to happen.

source_text: But also the order in which we put the tests as well.
zh: 还有测试的执行顺序。
en: But also the order in which we put the tests as well.

source_text: So going beyond this, I talked about hill climbing.
zh: 接下来，我想进一步谈谈刚才提到的持续迭代优化。
en: So going beyond this, I talked about hill climbing.

source_text: CI was one example.
zh: CI 就是其中一个例子。
en: CI was one example.

source_text: But actually what we've been doing in the background and working on for the last two or three months with a number of partners is we've been building our own benchmark for personal AI agents.
zh: 但实际上，过去两三个月里，我们一直在与多家合作伙伴一起，默默构建一套自己的个人 AI 智能体评测基准。
en: But actually what we've been doing in the background and working on for the last two or three months with a number of partners is we've been building our own benchmark for personal AI agents.

source_text: And this is called Shellbench, and it's going to be released hopefully in the next few days.
zh: 这套基准叫 Shellbench，希望能在未来几天发布。
en: And this is called Shellbench, and it's going to be released hopefully in the next few days.

source_text: I keep putting my words on that.
zh: 这话我一直都挂在嘴边。
en: I keep putting my words on that.

source_text: And it's 135 tasks and a small subset will be public.
zh: 它包含 135 项任务，其中一小部分会公开。
en: And it's 135 tasks and a small subset will be public.

source_text: And this was our way of ensuring that we had a way of measuring the proof.
zh: 这样一来，我们就有办法衡量实际成效。
en: And this was our way of ensuring that we had a way of measuring the proof.

source_text: And this was designed by humans and carried out a number of tasks, like tax returns or, like, what happens when two different people disagree on an outcome.
zh: 这些任务由人设计，涵盖报税，以及两个人对某个结果意见不一致时该如何处理等情境。
en: And this was designed by humans and carried out a number of tasks, like tax returns or, like, what happens when two different people disagree on an outcome.

source_text: And these were a little bit more ambiguous and that level of ambiguity enabled us to test things like the harness, the memory, the messaging,
zh: 这些任务的要求没那么明确，而这种模糊性让我们能够测试智能体的运行框架、记忆和消息处理等能力。
en: And these were a little bit more ambiguous and that level of ambiguity enabled us to test things like the harness, the memory, the messaging,

source_text: and then by doing so we could see at a grander scale were we getting worse or better as a product,
zh: 这样一来，我们就能从整体上判断，产品究竟是在进步还是退步。
en: and then by doing so we could see at a grander scale were we getting worse or better as a product,

source_text: and we could run these tests maybe in a more shorter space of time rather than every day or every hour, you know, doing crappy unit tests that don't add any value.
zh: 而且，我们可以在更短的时间内跑完这些测试，不用每天甚至每小时都做那些没什么价值的单元测试。
en: and we could run these tests maybe in a more shorter space of time rather than every day or every hour, you know, doing crappy unit tests that don't add any value.

source_text: Can we run like real benchmarks?
zh: 我们能不能跑一些真正有代表性的基准测试？
en: Can we run like real benchmarks?

source_text: So one thing that we're seeing a lot of companies now doing is developing their own internal benchmarks.
zh: 所以，我们看到现在很多公司都在开发自己的内部基准测试。
en: So one thing that we're seeing a lot of companies now doing is developing their own internal benchmarks.

source_text: Try to stay away from synthetics and try to spend time to build real datasets if you can,
zh: 尽量少用合成数据；如果条件允许，多花些时间构建真实数据集。
en: Try to stay away from synthetics and try to spend time to build real datasets if you can,

source_text: but as a team we're going to continue to develop this.
zh: 但作为一个团队，我们会继续完善这套基准测试。
en: but as a team we're going to continue to develop this.

source_text: And this benchmark will be made public and cover a range of harness and model combinations when it comes to coding agents and non-coding agents for, like, personal use.
zh: 我们也会公开这套基准测试，涵盖编程智能体和个人用途的非编程智能体所采用的多种运行框架与模型组合。
en: And this benchmark will be made public and cover a range of harness and model combinations when it comes to coding agents and non-coding agents for, like, personal use.

source_text: So we talked about, like, computer use, we talked about CI, we talked about UX changes.
zh: 我们聊了计算机操作，也聊了持续集成（CI）和用户体验（UX）方面的改进。
en: So we talked about, like, computer use, we talked about CI, we talked about UX changes.

source_text: So these are some of the ways that we can take an existing loop and provide much better feedback and in which by doing so start to engineer the proof into the system.
zh: 所以，我们可以通过这些方式改进现有的工作循环，提供更有效的反馈，并逐步把验证机制融入系统。
en: So these are some of the ways that we can take an existing loop and provide much better feedback and in which by doing so start to engineer the proof into the system.

source_text: An example of, like, what's to come, and these are some of my experiments that are working on, this is a screenshot from, like, two or three days ago,
zh: 举个例子，看看接下来可能会有什么进展。这是我正在做的一些实验，截图是两三天前截的。
en: An example of, like, what's to come, and these are some of my experiments that are working on, this is a screenshot from, like, two or three days ago,

source_text: where we take a traditional index of a codebase.
zh: 我们先用传统方式为代码库建立索引。
en: where we take a traditional index of a codebase.

source_text: This is the Open Claw codebase.
zh: 这是 OpenClaw 的代码库。
en: This is the Open Claw codebase.

source_text: But what we've done is essentially started to map out the proof components or the areas of slop of high regression around some of the stuff that we're using for our CI engine.
zh: 但我们实际上已经开始梳理验证环节，并找出持续集成（CI）引擎所用的一些组件中，哪些地方质量不稳定、容易出现回归问题。
en: But what we've done is essentially started to map out the proof components or the areas of slop of high regression around some of the stuff that we're using for our CI engine.

source_text: So the little models that are, like,
zh: 所以，那些小模型，比如……
en: So the little models that are, like,

source_text: helping us create better tests and improve which tests run and don't run, we can actually learn from that over a simulation going back, say, the last two or three months.
zh: 这些小模型能帮我们编写更好的测试，并优化哪些测试该运行、哪些不用运行。我们还可以回溯过去两三个月进行模拟，从中不断改进。
en: helping us create better tests and improve which tests run and don't run, we can actually learn from that over a simulation going back, say, the last two or three months.

source_text: And we can map this out into our codebase.
zh: 我们还可以把这些分析结果映射到代码库中。
en: And we can map this out into our codebase.

source_text: So one of the experiments I'm now running is, like, can this data be used to then drive agents to go back and essentially de-slop the codebase.
zh: 所以，我现在正在做的一个实验是：能不能利用这些数据，让智能体回过头来清理代码库中那些粗糙、低质量的代码。
en: So one of the experiments I'm now running is, like, can this data be used to then drive agents to go back and essentially de-slop the codebase.

source_text: And change parts of it.
zh: 并修改其中的部分代码。
en: And change parts of it.

source_text: So again, once this is stable, and has been verified, we'll also become an open source contribution to the community as well.
zh: 所以，等这套方案稳定下来并经过验证后，我们也会将其开源，回馈社区。
en: So again, once this is stable, and has been verified, we'll also become an open source contribution to the community as well.

source_text: So lastly, just to kind of iterate to people,
zh: 最后，我想再跟大家强调一下，
en: So lastly, just to kind of iterate to people,

source_text: you want to turn recurring pain, not just a single pain that you have.
zh: 你要解决的是反复出现的痛点，而不只是某一次遇到的问题。
en: you want to turn recurring pain, not just a single pain that you have.

source_text: In our case, the factory that we'd built was working really well, but eventually that factory slowed down.
zh: 就我们而言，之前搭建的那套流程一开始运转得很好，但最终还是慢了下来。
en: In our case, the factory that we'd built was working really well, but eventually that factory slowed down.

source_text: And the factory was no longer working to my expectations.
zh: 那套流程也不再能达到我的预期。
en: And the factory was no longer working to my expectations.

source_text: The factory couldn't build other factories, which was our biggest pain.
zh: 那套流程无法复制出更多同样的流程，而这正是我们最大的痛点。
en: The factory couldn't build other factories, which was our biggest pain.

source_text: So you want to create that into a better machine.
zh: 所以，你要把它改造成一套更高效的体系。
en: So you want to create that into a better machine.

source_text: So for us, going from the factory to Lobsterville was essentially kind of creating these, like, deeper levels of agentic engineering.
zh: 所以对我们来说，从“工厂”走向“Lobsterville”，本质上就是构建更深层次的智能体工程体系。
en: So for us, going from the factory to Lobsterville was essentially kind of creating these, like, deeper levels of agentic engineering.

source_text: That we're now sort of going into sort of the space of proof engineering.
zh: 我们现在正逐步进入“证明工程”这一领域。
en: That we're now sort of going into sort of the space of proof engineering.

source_text: How do we get models and harnesses to better understand what they're doing is having a real-world impact. And is verifiable to some extent. Thank you.
zh: 我们怎样才能让模型和智能体运行框架更清楚地认识到，它们的行为会对现实世界产生影响，而且这种影响在一定程度上是可以验证的？谢谢。
en: How do we get models and harnesses to better understand what they're doing is having a real-world impact. And is verifiable to some extent. Thank you.

source_text: All right.
zh: 好的。
en: All right.

source_text: Thank you all for the great sharing.
zh: 感谢各位的精彩分享。
en: Thank you all for the great sharing.

zh: 接下来我们稍作休息。
en: So we're going to take a short break.

zh: 我们会短暂的休息一下，然后大概
en: We’ll take a short break, and then, in about...

zh: 两点半这个样子回来。
en: We’ll be back around 2:30.

source_text: We're going to be back on to 2:30.
zh: 我们会在两点半继续。
en: We're going to be back on to 2:30.

source_text: 我们短暂休息一下。多谢。
zh: 我们短暂休息一下。多谢。
en: We’ll take a short break. Thank you.

en: Yes.

source_text: 好了，我们现在开始，然后呃，还有还在找座位的各位尽快就坐。
zh: 好了，我们现在开始，然后呃，还有还在找座位的各位尽快就坐。
en: All right, we’re starting now. If you’re still looking for a seat, please find one as soon as you can.

source_text: Please take a seat.
zh: 请就座。
en: Please take a seat.

source_text: 嗯， so next speaker is Alex, um, from the Auto Arc.
zh: 嗯，下一位演讲嘉宾是来自 Auto Arc 的 Alex。
en: 嗯， so next speaker is Alex, um, from the Auto Arc.

source_text: So let's welcome, 呃，下一位是来自 Auto Arc 的 Alex，啊，大家欢迎。
zh: So let's welcome, 呃，下一位是来自 Auto Arc 的 Alex，啊，大家欢迎。
en: Next up is Alex from Auto Arc. Please give him a warm welcome!

source_text: OK，直接用上面的，上面也有个话筒。
zh: OK，直接用上面的，上面也有个话筒。
en: Okay, just use the one up there. There’s a microphone up there too.

source_text: OK 好，谢谢大家。
zh: OK 好，谢谢大家。
en: Okay, thank you, everyone.

source_text: 呃，我叫 Alex，呃，我是来自无界方舟 Auto Arc 的 CTO，呃，我们公司是一家致力于做端侧 AI 模型的公司，
zh: 呃，我叫 Alex，呃，我是来自无界方舟 Auto Arc 的 CTO，呃，我们公司是一家致力于做端侧 AI 模型的公司，
en: My name is Alex, and I’m the CTO of Auto Arc. We’re a company focused on developing on-device AI models.

source_text: 然后今天很高兴能在这个舞台能给大家分享我们在端侧模型和端侧 AI 这一块所做的一些工作和我们的一些思考。
zh: 然后今天很高兴能在这个舞台能给大家分享我们在端侧模型和端侧 AI 这一块所做的一些工作和我们的一些思考。
en: I’m delighted to be here today to share some of our work and thoughts on on-device models and on-device AI.

source_text: 好，我我今天会从这三个部分来讲一下我的内容，呃，首先我们会看一下为什么现在的智能硬件需要端侧 AI，
zh: 好，我我今天会从这三个部分来讲一下我的内容，呃，首先我们会看一下为什么现在的智能硬件需要端侧 AI，
en: Today, I’ll cover three areas. First, we’ll look at why today’s smart devices need on-device AI.

source_text: 就端侧模型能够为咱们解决什么样的问题。
zh: 就端侧模型能够为咱们解决什么样的问题。
en: What problems can on-device models help us solve?

source_text: 第二块的话会分享一下我们在端侧 AI 这块所做的一些工作，呃，
zh: 第二块的话会分享一下我们在端侧 AI 这块所做的一些工作，呃，
en: Second, I’ll share some of the work we’ve done in on-device AI.

source_text: 以及我们所开源的解决方案 SDK 和各种各样的模型能够为咱们的开发者带来哪些助力，让我们能开发出更多更好玩、更有意思的一些产品。
zh: 以及我们所开源的解决方案 SDK 和各种各样的模型能够为咱们的开发者带来哪些助力，让我们能开发出更多更好玩、更有意思的一些产品。
en: I’ll also discuss how our open-source solutions, SDKs, and models can help developers build more creative and engaging products.

source_text: 然后最后呢，我会通过一个案例来简单分享一下通过端侧 AI 能够为咱们的开发带来哪些实际的好处。
zh: 然后最后呢，我会通过一个案例来简单分享一下通过端侧 AI 能够为咱们的开发带来哪些实际的好处。
en: Finally, I’ll use a case study to show some of the practical benefits on-device AI can bring to development.

source_text: 好，我们首先来看一下第一部分。
zh: 好，我们首先来看一下第一部分。
en: Okay, let’s start with the first part.

source_text: 呃，为什么智能硬件需要端侧 AI 呢？
zh: 呃，为什么智能硬件需要端侧 AI 呢？
en: Why do smart devices need on-device AI?

source_text: 呃，或者说为什么我们不直接使用云端的 API 呢？
zh: 呃，或者说为什么我们不直接使用云端的 API 呢？
en: Or, put another way, why not just use cloud-based APIs?

source_text: 呃，相信在座的有不少听众啊，应该是自己做过智能硬件或者智能软件的一些产品，或者说 personal agent 的一些产品啊，
zh: 呃，相信在座的有不少听众啊，应该是自己做过智能硬件或者智能软件的一些产品，或者说 personal agent 的一些产品啊，
en: I’m sure many of you here have worked on smart hardware or software products, or perhaps personal agents.

source_text: 比如说我们在做一款智能眼镜、智能耳机，或者说一款软件的时候，我们通常的做法是，
zh: 比如说我们在做一款智能眼镜、智能耳机，或者说一款软件的时候，我们通常的做法是，
en: For example, when we’re developing smart glasses, smart earbuds, or an app, the usual approach is to…

source_text: 当我完成这款硬件的开发之后呢，我们会选择调用云端大厂的一个 API，无论是音视频模型的 API 还是大语言模型的一个 API。
zh: 当我完成这款硬件的开发之后呢，我们会选择调用云端大厂的一个 API，无论是音视频模型的 API 还是大语言模型的一个 API。
en: Once we’ve built the device, we typically call an API from a major cloud provider—whether it’s for an audio or video model, or a large language model.

source_text: 那通过这种方式呢，能够为我们的产品带来包括 AI 对话啊、智能体的一些应用，
zh: 那通过这种方式呢，能够为我们的产品带来包括 AI 对话啊、智能体的一些应用，
en: That lets us add features like AI conversations and agent-based applications to our products.

source_text: 包括会议纪要、智能转录等各种各样的一些需求。但是呢，通过这种调用云端 API 的形式，会带来哪些缺点呢？
zh: 包括会议纪要、智能转录等各种各样的一些需求。但是呢，通过这种调用云端 API 的形式，会带来哪些缺点呢？
en: That includes features like meeting summaries and smart transcription. But what are the drawbacks of relying on cloud APIs?

source_text: 我们来看一下。
zh: 我们来看一下。
en: Let’s take a look.

source_text: 好，首先我们来看一下成本方面。
zh: 好，首先我们来看一下成本方面。
en: First, let’s look at the cost.

source_text: 那假设我们现在做了一款智能硬件，它非常的成功，
zh: 那假设我们现在做了一款智能硬件，它非常的成功，
en: Suppose we’ve built a smart device and it’s a huge success.

source_text: 它的年销量达到了 100 万台，同时呢，咱们的用户它的粘性又非常好，它每天能够跟 AI 对话、
zh: 它的年销量达到了 100 万台，同时呢，咱们的用户它的粘性又非常好，它每天能够跟 AI 对话、
en: It sells a million units a year, and our users are highly engaged—they talk to the AI every day…

source_text: 交互 20 次以上。
zh: 交互 20 次以上。
en: …interacting with it more than 20 times a day.

source_text: 那么根据我们现在能拿到的公开的大厂的 API token 的成本呢，我们可以轻松的算出来，如果说一款年销 100 万台的设备，
zh: 那么根据我们现在能拿到的公开的大厂的 API token 的成本呢，我们可以轻松的算出来，如果说一款年销 100 万台的设备，
en: Based on the publicly available token pricing from major providers, we can easily calculate the cost for a device that sells a million units a year.

source_text: 并且每天每个用户交互 20 次的话，它的年成本可以轻松达到，
zh: 并且每天每个用户交互 20 次的话，它的年成本可以轻松达到，
en: And if each user interacts with it 20 times a day, the annual API cost could easily reach…

source_text: 呃，10 亿元。
zh: 呃，10 亿元。
en: …one billion yuan.

source_text: 那么这就会带来一个非常尴尬的一个情况，就是说，呃，我们用产品的时候呢，我们的产品销量越高，我们反而越赔钱。
zh: 那么这就会带来一个非常尴尬的一个情况，就是说，呃，我们用产品的时候呢，我们的产品销量越高，我们反而越赔钱。
en: That puts us in an awkward position: the more units we sell, the more money we lose.

source_text: 这是现在很多做 AI 应用公司所面临的一个困境。
zh: 这是现在很多做 AI 应用公司所面临的一个困境。
en: This is the dilemma many AI application companies face today.

source_text: 那第二点呢，就是可用性了，
zh: 那第二点呢，就是可用性了，
en: The second point is availability.

source_text: 就是如果说我们一罐产品依赖云端 API 的形式来完成的话呢，那也就意味着它必须要在网络环境稳定的情况下去使用。
zh: 就是如果说我们一罐产品依赖云端 API 的形式来完成的话呢，那也就意味着它必须要在网络环境稳定的情况下去使用。
en: If our product relies entirely on cloud APIs, it can only be used when the internet connection is stable.

source_text: 如果说一旦遇到断网和无网的环境，我们整个的核心体验会迅速下降，甚至于达到不可用的情况。
zh: 如果说一旦遇到断网和无网的环境，我们整个的核心体验会迅速下降，甚至于达到不可用的情况。
en: If the connection drops or there’s no internet access, the core experience deteriorates rapidly—and the product may even become unusable.

source_text: 那么这一对于我们用户体验的延续来说是非常难以接受的。
zh: 那么这一对于我们用户体验的延续来说是非常难以接受的。
en: That’s a serious problem for delivering a consistent user experience.

source_text: 第三点呢，就是隐私的问题。
zh: 第三点呢，就是隐私的问题。
en: The third point is privacy.

source_text: 啊，随着现在咱们 AI 的功能在普通消费者这边的渗透率越来越高，我们会发现呢，
zh: 啊，随着现在咱们 AI 的功能在普通消费者这边的渗透率越来越高，我们会发现呢，
en: As AI features become more widespread among everyday consumers, we’re finding that…

source_text: 就是用户对于隐私的关注也越来越强。
zh: 就是用户对于隐私的关注也越来越强。
en: Users are becoming increasingly concerned about privacy.

source_text: 当然在日常生活过程中，咱们跟 AI 进行对话的时候，可能觉得还好，但是在一旦到了职场，
zh: 当然在日常生活过程中，咱们跟 AI 进行对话的时候，可能觉得还好，但是在一旦到了职场，
en: Of course, chatting with AI in everyday life may feel fine, but once we bring it into the workplace…

source_text: 比如说像咱们的医疗、投资、法律这些场景，呃，我们核心的录音，呃，视频，核心的数据结论文件等，
zh: 比如说像咱们的医疗、投资、法律这些场景，呃，我们核心的录音，呃，视频，核心的数据结论文件等，
en: For example, in healthcare, investment, and legal settings, we’re dealing with sensitive recordings, videos, data, and reports.

source_text: 一旦调用云端 API，这也就意味着你的数据会迅速的传递给我们的模型的 provider，从而带来数据的泄露。
zh: 一旦调用云端 API，这也就意味着你的数据会迅速的传递给我们的模型的 provider，从而带来数据的泄露。
en: Once you call a cloud API, your data is sent directly to the model provider, creating a risk of data leakage.

source_text: 那么在这些情况下，如果咱们做的一款产品是专门 target 这些，呃，非常专业的，呃，工作领域的话，你就会很快的遇到合规的问题。
zh: 那么在这些情况下，如果咱们做的一款产品是专门 target 这些，呃，非常专业的，呃，工作领域的话，你就会很快的遇到合规的问题。
en: So if you’re building a product for these highly specialized professional fields, you’ll quickly run into compliance issues.

source_text: 那么，呃，端侧 AI 呢，就是很好的解决这件事情的一个方法。所谓什么是端侧 AI 呢？
zh: 那么，呃，端侧 AI 呢，就是很好的解决这件事情的一个方法。所谓什么是端侧 AI 呢？
en: On-device AI is a great way to address this. So what exactly is on-device AI?

source_text: 我们简单给出一个定义。
zh: 我们简单给出一个定义。
en: Let’s start with a simple definition.

source_text: 啊，端侧 AI 它其实指的就是说在咱们的硬件本身上利用这个硬件本体的算力去运行咱们的模型，
zh: 啊，端侧 AI 它其实指的就是说在咱们的硬件本身上利用这个硬件本体的算力去运行咱们的模型，
en: On-device AI means running models directly on the hardware, using the device’s own computing power.

source_text: 从而完全避免对云端 API 的一个调用。
zh: 从而完全避免对云端 API 的一个调用。
en: This eliminates the need to call a cloud API altogether.

source_text: 利用端侧 AI 呢，它带来的优势是显而易见的。
zh: 利用端侧 AI 呢，它带来的优势是显而易见的。
en: The benefits of on-device AI are clear.

source_text: 啊，首先就是及时响应，因为我们的整个模型是跑在我们的硬件本体上的，
zh: 啊，首先就是及时响应，因为我们的整个模型是跑在我们的硬件本体上的，
en: First, it responds instantly because the entire model runs on the device itself.

source_text: 这也就意味着我们可以做到所有的 AI 功能在毫秒级别的响应。
zh: 这也就意味着我们可以做到所有的 AI 功能在毫秒级别的响应。
en: That means all our AI features can respond in milliseconds.

source_text: 啊，而无需通过云端去调用云端的 API，自然也不会受到云端网络波动的影响。
zh: 啊，而无需通过云端去调用云端的 API，自然也不会受到云端网络波动的影响。
en: There’s no need to call a cloud API, so performance isn’t affected by fluctuations in the network connection.

source_text: 那其次呢，就是可用性。
zh: 那其次呢，就是可用性。
en: Second, there’s availability.

source_text: 如果咱们的产品在无网弱网的环境下，通过调用云端模型的话呢，它自然就不会遇到任何体验方面的一些问题。
zh: 如果咱们的产品在无网弱网的环境下，通过调用云端模型的话呢，它自然就不会遇到任何体验方面的一些问题。
en: If our product relies on a cloud model, users will naturally run into problems when there’s no connection or the network is weak.

source_text: 那无论是在高铁、飞机、电梯以及各种弱网无网的环境，它的 AI 的功能体验都可以得以延续。
zh: 那无论是在高铁、飞机、电梯以及各种弱网无网的环境，它的 AI 的功能体验都可以得以延续。
en: So whether you’re on a high-speed train, a plane, or in an elevator—or anywhere with a weak or nonexistent connection—the AI features keep working.

source_text: 那第三点呢，就是隐私了，这个很好理解，因为我们所有的核心数据都在我们的设备本身上去完成。
zh: 那第三点呢，就是隐私了，这个很好理解，因为我们所有的核心数据都在我们的设备本身上去完成。
en: Third is privacy. It’s straightforward: all our core data is processed on the device itself.

source_text: 那么我们的核心的隐私数据是不出域的，这自然而然就带来了它的一个优势。
zh: 那么我们的核心的隐私数据是不出域的，这自然而然就带来了它的一个优势。
en: That means sensitive data never leaves the device, which naturally gives us a privacy advantage.

source_text: 好，最后呢，就是零成本了，因为我们的模型不需要调用云端的 API，那自然就不会带来任何 token 的一个成本。
zh: 好，最后呢，就是零成本了，因为我们的模型不需要调用云端的 API，那自然就不会带来任何 token 的一个成本。
en: Finally, there’s zero API cost. Since our model doesn’t call a cloud API, there are no token fees.

source_text: 从行业趋势来看呢，大家其实也可以发现啊，现在云端的端侧 AI 已经出现了一个爆发的趋势。
zh: 从行业趋势来看呢，大家其实也可以发现啊，现在云端的端侧 AI 已经出现了一个爆发的趋势。
en: Looking at industry trends, you can see that on-device AI is now taking off.

source_text: 一方面呢，随着咱们模型本身的尺寸和架构和训练方法在持续升级，1B 到 7B 这个规模的模型，它的智力水平也持续进步，
zh: 一方面呢，随着咱们模型本身的尺寸和架构和训练方法在持续升级，1B 到 7B 这个规模的模型，它的智力水平也持续进步，
en: On one hand, as model sizes, architectures, and training methods continue to improve, the capabilities of models in the 1B-to-7B parameter range are steadily advancing.

source_text: 基本上已经能够接近前几年旗舰大模型的一个水平。
zh: 基本上已经能够接近前几年旗舰大模型的一个水平。
en: They’re now approaching the performance of flagship large models from just a few years ago.

source_text: 那第二呢，随着咱们芯片本身的算力也在加强，我们有越来越多的嵌入式芯片和手机芯片开始带上 NPU，
zh: 那第二呢，随着咱们芯片本身的算力也在加强，我们有越来越多的嵌入式芯片和手机芯片开始带上 NPU，
en: Second, as chips become more powerful, more embedded and smartphone chips are coming equipped with NPUs.

source_text: 我们的算力也从零点几个 tops 到 1 tops、10 tops，甚至几百几千 tops，
zh: 我们的算力也从零点几个 tops 到 1 tops、10 tops，甚至几百几千 tops，
en: Computing power has also grown from fractions of a TOPS to 1 TOPS, 10 TOPS, and even hundreds or thousands of TOPS.

source_text: 这天然为我们的端侧模型的部署和运行创造了非常良好的一个条件。
zh: 这天然为我们的端侧模型的部署和运行创造了非常良好的一个条件。
en: This creates ideal conditions for deploying and running our models on-device.

source_text: 当然在呃，部署端侧模型的时候也不完全是免费的，对于一款智能硬件而言，
zh: 当然在呃，部署端侧模型的时候也不完全是免费的，对于一款智能硬件而言，
en: Of course, deploying an on-device model isn’t entirely free. For a smart device,

source_text: 它天然会受到包括内存啊、电量、续航各方面的一些限制，这天然阻碍了我们把无脑把最大的模型放到我们的硬件上去。
zh: 它天然会受到包括内存啊、电量、续航各方面的一些限制，这天然阻碍了我们把无脑把最大的模型放到我们的硬件上去。
en: It’s inherently constrained by memory, power consumption, and battery life, so we can’t simply put the largest model we can find on the device.

source_text: 其次呢，就是我们每一个平台，像以前我们做云端模型的时候，我们通常只需要适配像 NVIDIA 的 CUDA 生态，
zh: 其次呢，就是我们每一个平台，像以前我们做云端模型的时候，我们通常只需要适配像 NVIDIA 的 CUDA 生态，
en: Second, there’s the challenge of supporting different platforms. When we built cloud-based models, we usually only needed to support NVIDIA’s CUDA ecosystem.

source_text: 或者说像华为这种国产卡的算力新算力生态就可以了。
zh: 或者说像华为这种国产卡的算力新算力生态就可以了。
en: Or a newer domestic accelerator ecosystem, such as Huawei’s.

source_text: 但是在端侧，我们有各种各样的一些平台，
zh: 但是在端侧，我们有各种各样的一些平台，
en: But on-device, we have to deal with a wide variety of platforms.

source_text: 比如像 FreeRTOS、Arm、Linux 啊、ESP32 啊、iOS、Android，各种各样的一些平台，
zh: 比如像 FreeRTOS、Arm、Linux 啊、ESP32 啊、iOS、Android，各种各样的一些平台，
en: For example, there’s FreeRTOS, Arm, Linux, ESP32, iOS, Android—a whole range of platforms.

source_text: 每一个平台每一个编程语言都需要重新去写这个端侧模型的部署逻辑。对于工程化来说是极大的一个成本。
zh: 每一个平台每一个编程语言都需要重新去写这个端侧模型的部署逻辑。对于工程化来说是极大的一个成本。
en: For every platform and programming language, we have to rewrite the logic for deploying the on-device model. That’s a huge engineering cost.

source_text: 当然，虽然存在这些问题啊，我们依然认为端侧 AI 是我们接下来发展的一个重心，
zh: 当然，虽然存在这些问题啊，我们依然认为端侧 AI 是我们接下来发展的一个重心，
en: Of course, despite these challenges, we still believe on-device AI will be a major focus for us going forward.

source_text: 也也是我们接下来 AI 模型和 AI 产品发展的一个重心。
zh: 也也是我们接下来 AI 模型和 AI 产品发展的一个重心。
en: It will also be a major focus for our AI models and products going forward.

zh: 有一个很严重的问题就是说，我们 MOE 大模型在做每一个 Token 解码的时候，
en: There’s a major challenge: every time an MoE model decodes a token,

source_text: 它下一个 Token 和这个 Token 所需的参数有可能完全不一样。
zh: 它下一个 Token 和这个 Token 所需的参数有可能完全不一样。
en: The parameters needed for the next token could be completely different from those needed for the current one.

source_text: 那么如果说我们在每一次 Token 解码的时候，
zh: 那么如果说我们在每一次 Token 解码的时候，
en: So if, every time we decode a token,

source_text: 再把我们的参数从 SSD 加载到内存，我们的整个的解码速度会非常慢，有可能会达到好几秒吐一个 Token，
zh: 再把我们的参数从 SSD 加载到内存，我们的整个的解码速度会非常慢，有可能会达到好几秒吐一个 Token，
en: we have to load the required parameters from the SSD into memory, decoding would be extremely slow—potentially taking several seconds to generate a single token.

source_text: 这显然是不满足咱们实际使用需求的。
zh: 这显然是不满足咱们实际使用需求的。
en: That clearly wouldn’t meet the needs of real-world use.

source_text: 那么就为了解决这一点呢，我们也创新性的提出了 pre-router，就是一个参数的预加载技术，
zh: 那么就为了解决这一点呢，我们也创新性的提出了 pre-router，就是一个参数的预加载技术，
en: To address this, we developed an innovative technique called the pre-router, which preloads the parameters.

source_text: 通过预训练的一个模块加载到我们的 LM 里面去，让我们的 LM 在每一座一个 Token 推理的时候，
zh: 通过预训练的一个模块加载到我们的 LM 里面去，让我们的 LM 在每一座一个 Token 推理的时候，
en: By integrating a pretrained module into our language model, we can, each time it generates a token,

source_text: 我们可以实时的去预测下一个 Token 下下个 Token 和后面几个 Token 所需要的专家参数，
zh: 我们可以实时的去预测下一个 Token 下下个 Token 和后面几个 Token 所需要的专家参数，
en: predict in real time which expert parameters the next token, the token after that, and several subsequent tokens will need.

source_text: 并且把这些参数通过后台异步的形式加载到我们的内存，从而当我们在解码每一个 Token 的时候，
zh: 并且把这些参数通过后台异步的形式加载到我们的内存，从而当我们在解码每一个 Token 的时候，
en: We then load those parameters into memory asynchronously in the background, so that when we decode each token,

source_text: 它相关的参数已经准备好了。
zh: 它相关的参数已经准备好了。
en: the parameters it needs are already in place.

source_text: 通过这种形式，我们能实现数量级别的解码速度的提升，从而才能达成刚刚大家看见的录屏里面非常惊艳的一个效果。
zh: 通过这种形式，我们能实现数量级别的解码速度的提升，从而才能达成刚刚大家看见的录屏里面非常惊艳的一个效果。
en: This gives us an order-of-magnitude boost in decoding speed, making possible the impressive results you saw in the screen recording just now.

source_text: 好，呃，最后来看一下大算力设备。
zh: 好，呃，最后来看一下大算力设备。
en: Okay, finally, let’s look at the high-compute devices.

source_text: 所谓大算力设备呢，通常指的就是咱们的笔记本，比如说带独显的 Windows 笔记本、MacBook Pro、Mac mini、Mac Studio 啊，
zh: 所谓大算力设备呢，通常指的就是咱们的笔记本，比如说带独显的 Windows 笔记本、MacBook Pro、Mac mini、Mac Studio 啊，
en: By high-compute devices, we usually mean computers like laptops—for example, Windows laptops with dedicated GPUs, as well as MacBook Pros, Mac minis, and Mac Studios.

source_text: 或者像呃带独显的台式机这样的啊硬件设备。
zh: 或者像呃带独显的台式机这样的啊硬件设备。
en: Or desktop computers with dedicated GPUs—hardware like that.

zh: 对于这样的硬件设备而言呢，主打的需求就是 Vibe Coding 啊，
en: For devices like these, the main use case is vibe coding.

zh: 那么在这一块呢，我们也是第一次发布啊一个 preview，就是我们即将开源 150B 的端侧 MOE 多模态大模型。

zh: 能够实现最高轻松实现超过 1,000 的 profile 的 Token 的每秒的速度和超过 100 的解码的速度。
en: It can easily reach prefill speeds of over 1,000 tokens per second and decoding speeds of over 100 tokens per second.

en: Its capabilities are close to those of Flash-class models. You can use it for video production, software development, and even 3D modeling by having it control Blender through computer use.

source_text: 啊，这些场景都是可以通过我们的端侧模型，在你自己的笔记本和电脑上去完成的，不需要调用云端 API，也不会有任何 Token 费用。

source_text: And defining sandbox as like in this broad definition, like an isolated compute environment, is pretty general and there's no, let's say, precise mathematical definition of what sandbox is. And the reason behind that is that things are changing really fast.

source_text: Uh,

en: Uh,

source_text: they can do pretty cool stuff, especially in the reinforcement learning space, like evals, benchmark, post-training, model fine-tuning, etc.

source_text: these computer use agents which are let's say can be considered like general purpose knowledge workers started to emerge.

source_text: And they required some compute level requirements.

source_text: Now back to the Kubernetes.

source_text: As I said previously, Kubernetes is exceptional for the task it was designed to do.
zh: 正如我之前所说，Kubernetes 非常擅长完成它最初设计要解决的任务。
en: As I said previously, Kubernetes is exceptional for the task it was designed to do.

source_text: So it was released in 2014 and it's its main objective was to run a containers on scale and run them reliably.
zh: 它于 2014 年发布，主要目标是大规模、可靠地运行容器。
en: So it was released in 2014 and it's its main objective was to run a containers on scale and run them reliably.

source_text: So recovering them from errors and failures, also letting you update running containers without downtime. And it's ideal for running low long running web stateless services.
zh: 也就是说，容器发生错误或故障时，它能帮助恢复运行，还能让你在不中断服务的情况下更新容器。它非常适合运行长期在线的无状态 Web 服务。
en: So recovering them from errors and failures, also letting you update running containers without downtime. And it's ideal for running low long running web stateless services.

source_text: But the thing is with the agents, the requirements are completely opposite.
zh: 但问题是，智能体的需求恰恰相反。
en: But the thing is with the agents, the requirements are completely opposite.

source_text: So agents need number one statefulness, uh, to preserve their work where you, for example, when you stop agent work and resume it after two days,
zh: 首先，智能体需要有状态，能够保存工作进度。比如，你暂停了它的工作，两天后还能接着做。
en: So agents need number one statefulness, uh, to preserve their work where you, for example, when you stop agent work and resume it after two days,

source_text: you want everything preserved in the sandbox.
zh: 你希望沙箱里的一切都能保留下来。

source_text: And most of the task that agent do are short-lived.
zh: 而且，智能体执行的大多数任务都是短期任务。
en: And most of the task that agent do are short-lived.

source_text: So agents often spin up these sandboxes on demand do some stuff inside it and shut them down.
zh: 所以，智能体通常会按需启动沙箱，在里面完成一些任务，然后将其关闭。
en: So agents often spin up these sandboxes on demand do some stuff inside it and shut them down.

source_text: So yeah, here we see complete completely opposite requirements and definitions between these two architecture types.
zh: 所以可以看到，这两种架构的需求和设计理念截然相反。
en: So yeah, here we see complete completely opposite requirements and definitions between these two architecture types.

source_text: And yeah, that's the test that we took at Daytona to basically rebuild the infra layer for agents.
zh: 这也正是我们在 Daytona 接受的挑战：为智能体重新构建基础设施层。
en: And yeah, that's the test that we took at Daytona to basically rebuild the infra layer for agents.

source_text: Uh, so we decided to divide features at every sandbox provider should implement into, let's say, three pillars.
zh: 所以，我们决定把每家沙箱服务商都应该具备的功能划分为三个方面。
en: Uh, so we decided to divide features at every sandbox provider should implement into, let's say, three pillars.

source_text: First pillar, infrastructure pillar is related to performance, throughput, and concurrency.
zh: 第一大支柱是基础设施，涉及性能、吞吐量和并发能力。
en: First pillar, infrastructure pillar is related to performance, throughput, and concurrency.

source_text: Second one,
zh: 第二个是，
en: Second one,

source_text: we call it primitive, is mostly regarding the features that are coupled with the infrastructure layer, like forking, snapshotting, etc.
zh: 我们称之为“基础能力”，主要指与基础设施层紧密相关的功能，比如分叉、创建快照等。
en: we call it primitive, is mostly regarding the features that are coupled with the infrastructure layer, like forking, snapshotting, etc.

source_text: Third one is the tools.
zh: 第三个是工具。
en: Third one is the tools.

source_text: So since the agent moved inside the sandbox, uh,
zh: 所以，既然智能体已经进入沙箱，呃，
en: So since the agent moved inside the sandbox, uh,

source_text: your goal as a sandbox provider is to enable tools to the agent so that the agent can do its task in the most optimal way.
zh: 作为沙箱服务商，你的目标是为智能体提供工具，让它以最高效的方式完成任务。
en: your goal as a sandbox provider is to enable tools to the agent so that the agent can do its task in the most optimal way.

source_text: And on the other hand, you also need to prevent the agent from doing dumb things such as leaking your secrets, etc.
zh: 另一方面，你还得防止智能体干出泄露密钥之类的蠢事。
en: And on the other hand, you also need to prevent the agent from doing dumb things such as leaking your secrets, etc.

source_text: So this is what it takes you to spin up a sandbox using Daytona. And on the right is what it takes you to spin up the sandbox Kubernetes from ground zero.
zh: 这就是用 Daytona 启动一个沙箱所需的步骤。右边则是从零开始用 Kubernetes 搭建沙箱所需的步骤。
en: So this is what it takes you to spin up a sandbox using Daytona. And on the right is what it takes you to spin up the sandbox Kubernetes from ground zero.

source_text: So yeah,
zh: 所以，是的，
en: So yeah,

source_text: based on this slide, we're not going into the details, but the question emerges like, why do you want to do this?
