source_text: So you can get a perfect HTTP 200 request from upstream, initially, and still get it wrong in the middle.
zh: 也就是说，上游一开始可能返回了正常的 HTTP 200，但中间环节仍然可能出错。
en: So you can get a perfect HTTP 200 request from upstream, initially, and still get it wrong in the middle.

source_text: We've seen countless issues like that.
zh: 这类问题我们已经遇到过无数次了。
en: We've seen countless issues like that.

source_text: You can have a request that started streaming nicely and suddenly stalled halfway, and the user stopped receiving the rest of the response.
zh: 请求一开始可能流式传输得很顺畅，却突然在中途卡住，用户也就收不到后续的回复了。
en: You can have a request that started streaming nicely and suddenly stalled halfway, and the user stopped receiving the rest of the response.

source_text: Uh, we have seen that because we are doing translation of protocols, that sometimes you have broken cache in the middle, that you should have a nice cache rate, a high cache rate,
zh: 呃，我们发现，由于我们在做协议转换，有时候中间的缓存机制会出问题；按理说缓存命中率应该很高，
en: Uh, we have seen that because we are doing translation of protocols, that sometimes you have broken cache in the middle, that you should have a nice cache rate, a high cache rate,

source_text: basically, uh, equal to saving money for you.
zh: 基本上，呃，这就相当于帮你省钱。
en: basically, uh, equal to saving money for you.

source_text: Because you are paying one, usually one-tenth of the cost for cache request.
zh: 因为缓存命中的请求，费用通常只有普通请求的十分之一。
en: Because you are paying one, usually one-tenth of the cost for cache request.

source_text: But if your cache is broken due to something is wrong in the middle, then you can see from the cost, it doubles,
zh: 但如果中间某个环节出了问题，导致缓存失效，你就会发现成本翻倍了，
en: But if your cache is broken due to something is wrong in the middle, then you can see from the cost, it doubles,

source_text: triples, quickly.
zh: 甚至很快涨到三倍。
en: triples, quickly.

source_text: Uh, we have also seen silent failures.
zh: 呃，我们也遇到过一些不易察觉的故障。
en: Uh, we have also seen silent failures.

source_text: This one is recent, that, um, it won't show up anywhere in your monitoring system.
zh: 这是最近才遇到的一个问题，嗯，它不会出现在你的任何监控系统里。
en: This one is recent, that, um, it won't show up anywhere in your monitoring system.

source_text: So we found in one, some of our requests that Anthropic thinking block, which is nowadays they no longer send in clear text, that they send encrypted signatures.
zh: 我们发现，在部分请求中，Anthropic 的思考内容块如今已不再以明文发送，而是以加密签名的形式发送。
en: So we found in one, some of our requests that Anthropic thinking block, which is nowadays they no longer send in clear text, that they send encrypted signatures.

source_text: Which is actually the thinking content itself, with a summary.
zh: 其实就是思考内容本身，外加一段摘要。
en: Which is actually the thinking content itself, with a summary.

source_text: So in certain cases, we noticed that the response is actually silently dropping these thinking blocks.
zh: 所以我们注意到，在某些情况下，响应会悄悄丢掉这些思考内容块。
en: So in certain cases, we noticed that the response is actually silently dropping these thinking blocks.

source_text: So this is scary, because you don't see it in the gateway, but what happens is user will still see the response in their request, but in the next request, because actually thinking chain is broken,
zh: 这就很可怕，因为网关里看不出异常。用户这次请求仍能收到响应，但到了下一次请求，由于思考链实际上已经断了，
en: So this is scary, because you don't see it in the gateway, but what happens is user will still see the response in their request, but in the next request, because actually thinking chain is broken,

source_text: so the gateway or upstream provider need to do more work to regenerate these thinking blocks.
zh: 网关或上游服务商就得做更多工作，重新生成这些思考内容块。
en: so the gateway or upstream provider need to do more work to regenerate these thinking blocks.

source_text: So in the end, increased latency, and increased the cost.
zh: 结果就是延迟增加，成本也随之上升。
en: So in the end, increased latency, and increased the cost.

source_text: So one of our user found this with their agent, that detected that this anomaly in the response.
zh: 我们的一位用户通过自己的智能体发现了这个问题：它检测到了响应中的异常。
en: So one of our user found this with their agent, that detected that this anomaly in the response.

source_text: But, uh, they let us know and we found it's actually a bug in translating the protocol from Anthropic to OpenAI.
zh: 不过，他们把这个情况告诉了我们，我们发现这其实是将 Anthropic 协议转换为 OpenAI 协议时的一个 bug。
en: But, uh, they let us know and we found it's actually a bug in translating the protocol from Anthropic to OpenAI.

source_text: So I think they were calling Anthropic models from an OpenAI compatible harness, right?
zh: 所以，我理解他们当时是通过兼容 OpenAI 的调用框架来调用 Anthropic 的模型，对吧？
en: So I think they were calling Anthropic models from an OpenAI compatible harness, right?

source_text: So as we.
zh: 所以，我们……
en: So as we.

source_text: Can see, many of these issues eventually they attribute to the fact that we are translating between harness protocols.
zh: 可以看到，很多这类问题归根结底都与我们在不同调用框架的协议之间进行转换有关。
en: Can see, many of these issues eventually they attribute to the fact that we are translating between harness protocols.

source_text: So this make us start thinking what we should do about it.
zh: 这让我们开始思考该怎么解决这个问题。
en: So this make us start thinking what we should do about it.

source_text: Okay, so assuming now that you solved the translation problem,
zh: 好的，假设现在你们已经解决了协议转换的问题，
en: Okay, so assuming now that you solved the translation problem,

source_text: you educated your user that never call Anthropic model from OpenAI harnesses and don't do the other way around as well, uh, other things can fail. So upstream providers, they are not perfect.
zh: 你们已经提醒用户，不要通过兼容 OpenAI 的调用框架来调用 Anthropic 模型，反过来也不要这么做，因为还可能出其他问题。再说，上游模型提供商也并非十全十美。
en: you educated your user that never call Anthropic model from OpenAI harnesses and don't do the other way around as well, uh, other things can fail. So upstream providers, they are not perfect.

source_text: Should it be AWS, should it be Anthropic, every provider's nowadays they are certain period of time that they can fail.
zh: 无论是 AWS 还是 Anthropic，如今任何服务提供商都可能偶尔发生故障。
en: Should it be AWS, should it be Anthropic, every provider's nowadays they are certain period of time that they can fail.

source_text: They can fail for certain requests that they can fail for even extended period of time. But business cannot be stopped by this.
zh: 它们可能在处理某些请求时出错，甚至长时间无法恢复。但业务不能因此停摆。
en: They can fail for certain requests that they can fail for even extended period of time. But business cannot be stopped by this.

source_text: So the lessons learned from here is that for every important language models that we are using, we will try to get at least the two providers and failover between them.
zh: 所以，我们从中吸取的教训是：对于每个关键的大语言模型，都要尽量接入至少两家服务提供商，并在一家出故障时切换到另一家。
en: So the lessons learned from here is that for every important language models that we are using, we will try to get at least the two providers and failover between them.

source_text: So user won't notice or won't need to do anything in case one broke down.
zh: 这样，即使其中一家服务商出了故障，用户也不会察觉，更不需要采取任何操作。
en: So user won't notice or won't need to do anything in case one broke down.

source_text: But how we do failover, this is not, again, this is I'm comparing this with a typical web proxy.
zh: 但故障切换该怎么做呢？这和普通的 Web 代理不太一样。
en: But how we do failover, this is not, again, this is I'm comparing this with a typical web proxy.

source_text: That you cannot simply load balance between them.
zh: 不能简单地在它们之间做负载均衡。
en: That you cannot simply load balance between them.

source_text: Because the nature of LM request is stateful.
zh: 因为大语言模型的请求是有状态的。
en: Because the nature of LM request is stateful.

source_text: So we.
zh: 所以，我们……
en: So we.

source_text: Have a clear boundary here on how we handle the failover.
zh: 我们需要明确故障切换的处理边界。
en: Have a clear boundary here on how we handle the failover.

source_text: If the user haven't seen the response yet, like you send a request to one provider and it immediately give you a 429 that's you are rate limited or 529 that server is busy,
zh: 如果用户还没看到回复，比如你向一家服务商发送请求后，它立刻返回 429，表示请求受到限流；或者返回 529，表示服务器繁忙。
en: If the user haven't seen the response yet, like you send a request to one provider and it immediately give you a 429 that's you are rate limited or 529 that server is busy,

source_text: you can try the second provider.
zh: 这时可以尝试切换到第二家服务商。
en: you can try the second provider.

source_text: And continue serving users request.
zh: 然后继续处理用户的请求。
en: And continue serving users request.

source_text: But in case that streaming already started,
zh: 但如果流式输出已经开始，
en: But in case that streaming already started,

source_text: what your user will see is they started seeing the response coming up on their screen and something went wrong in the middle,
zh: 用户看到的就是，回复已经开始出现在屏幕上，但中途出了问题，
en: what your user will see is they started seeing the response coming up on their screen and something went wrong in the middle,

source_text: which do happen as well.
zh: 这种情况也确实会发生。
en: which do happen as well.

source_text: Uh, well, we have no choice but to surface the error to the user.
zh: 呃，那我们别无选择，只能把错误提示给用户。
en: Uh, well, we have no choice but to surface the error to the user.

source_text: So they will see an error and they can choose to retry or do something else.
zh: 这样用户会看到错误提示，可以选择重试或采取其他操作。
en: So they will see an error and they can choose to retry or do something else.

source_text: Yeah?
zh: 是吗？
en: Yeah?

source_text: Uh, I am aware that now we have some more advanced gateway that can failover midstream.
zh: 呃，我知道现在有一些更先进的网关，可以在流式输出进行到一半时切换到备用服务商。
en: Uh, I am aware that now we have some more advanced gateway that can failover midstream.

source_text: Like for example, they can continue streaming using the response returned by a second provider.
zh: 比如，它们可以切换到第二家服务提供商，利用其返回的响应继续流式输出。
en: Like for example, they can continue streaming using the response returned by a second provider.

source_text: But we evaluated the complexity and we decided we'll probably not do it for now and we'll stick with the simpler option to just fail it early and let the user decide what they want to do. Okay?
zh: 但我们评估了实现难度，决定暂时不这么做，还是采用更简单的方案：尽早报错，让用户自行决定下一步怎么办。好吗？
en: But we evaluated the complexity and we decided we'll probably not do it for now and we'll stick with the simpler option to just fail it early and let the user decide what they want to do. Okay?

source_text: But in certain cases, you will see that one provider simply broke.
zh: 但有些情况下，你会发现某家服务提供商直接出故障了。
en: But in certain cases, you will see that one provider simply broke.

source_text: That it doesn't serve that it doesn't want to serve requests at all.
zh: 也就是说，它完全不愿意处理任何请求。
en: That it doesn't serve that it doesn't want to serve requests at all.

source_text: While the other one is acting perfectly fine.
zh: 而另一家服务提供商却运行得好好的。
en: While the other one is acting perfectly fine.

source_text: So in this case,
zh: 所以在这种情况下，
en: So in this case,

source_text: another important mechanism we have is a circuit breaker.
zh: 我们还有一个重要机制，就是熔断器。
en: another important mechanism we have is a circuit breaker.

source_text: So we have threshold set for different type of errors.
zh: 所以，我们针对不同类型的错误设置了不同的阈值。
en: So we have threshold set for different type of errors.

source_text: And we decide to we can our gateway can decide to stop sending requests to one provider altogether. For a period of time, if the circuit breaker is tripped.
zh: 如果触发了熔断器，我们的网关就可以决定在一段时间内完全停止向某家服务提供商发送请求。
en: And we decide to we can our gateway can decide to stop sending requests to one provider altogether. For a period of time, if the circuit breaker is tripped.

source_text: All right,
zh: 好的，
en: All right,

source_text: so now you have two providers, everything should be fine, right?
zh: 现在有两家服务提供商了，一切应该都没问题了，对吧？
en: so now you have two providers, everything should be fine, right?

source_text: And you also know you.
zh: 而且你也知道，你……
en: And you also know you.

source_text: Should be failing over between them.
zh: 应该在两家服务提供商之间进行故障切换。
en: Should be failing over between them.

source_text: But things can still go wrong.
zh: 但还是可能出问题。
en: But things can still go wrong.

source_text: Again, this is back to this is back to the nature of LM is stateful.
zh: 这又回到了语言模型有状态这一特性。
en: Again, this is back to this is back to the nature of LM is stateful.

source_text: So one thing we noticed that if you simply splitting your traffic between two providers, even if they serve the same model, you can easily break your cache.
zh: 我们发现，如果只是把流量分给两家服务提供商，即使它们提供的是同一个模型，也很容易导致缓存失效。
en: So one thing we noticed that if you simply splitting your traffic between two providers, even if they serve the same model, you can easily break your cache.

source_text: Again,
zh: 再说一次，
en: Again,

source_text: you pay much less when things are cached, right?
zh: 命中缓存时，费用会低很多，对吧？
en: you pay much less when things are cached, right?

source_text: So a few lessons we learned here, one thing is if you do want to failover your request,
zh: 所以，我们从中总结了几点经验。首先，如果你确实想在请求失败时切换服务提供商，
en: So a few lessons we learned here, one thing is if you do want to failover your request,

source_text: normally you would keep the session sticky.
zh: 通常会让同一个会话始终由同一家服务提供商处理。
en: normally you would keep the session sticky.

source_text: So even if you have two providers behind the same model ID, one thing you should do is make sure that single session from single user always hit one model.
zh: 所以，即使同一个模型 ID 背后接了两家服务提供商，也要确保同一用户的同一个会话始终发往同一家。
en: So even if you have two providers behind the same model ID, one thing you should do is make sure that single session from single user always hit one model.

source_text: Even if you want the actual traffic to split between the two.
zh: 即使你想把整体流量分配给这两家服务提供商，也要这样做。
en: Even if you want the actual traffic to split between the two.

source_text: You can have two sessions calling two different models, but never one session across the two models.
zh: 可以让两个会话分别调用两个不同的模型，但不要让同一个会话跨两个模型。
en: You can have two sessions calling two different models, but never one session across the two models.

source_text: In some cases, for some model, like some Anthropic models, they also have
zh: 有些情况下，某些模型，比如 Anthropic 的部分模型，还会有……
en: In some cases, for some model, like some Anthropic models, they also have

source_text: Certain featuresets which is not always supported on all providers.
zh: 某些功能并非所有服务提供商都支持。
en: Certain featuresets which is not always supported on all providers.

source_text: Like on the Anthropic first party, they may support beta features which hides behind beta flags.
zh: 比如 Anthropic 官方服务可能支持一些需要通过 Beta 标志开启的测试功能。
en: Like on the Anthropic first party, they may support beta features which hides behind beta flags.

source_text: Sometimes it can be super helpful, like the tool search can massively save our tokens in MCP tool.
zh: 有时候这非常有用。比如，工具搜索功能能大幅减少使用 MCP 工具时消耗的 token。
en: Sometimes it can be super helpful, like the tool search can massively save our tokens in MCP tool.

source_text: And there are other features as well that we might want to use.
zh: 此外，我们可能还想使用其他功能。
en: And there are other features as well that we might want to use.

source_text: But they may not be supported on AWS bedrock for the moments,
zh: 但目前 AWS Bedrock 可能还不支持这些功能。
en: But they may not be supported on AWS bedrock for the moments,

source_text: right?
zh: 对吧？
en: right?

source_text: Compatibility or features are changing every day.
zh: 兼容性和功能每天都在变化。
en: Compatibility or features are changing every day.

source_text: And one thing we learned is if you want to have two models serving on the same model ID, that you need to hide this complexity from the users.
zh: 我们还发现，如果想让两个模型共用同一个模型 ID，就得对用户屏蔽其中的复杂性。
en: And one thing we learned is if you want to have two models serving on the same model ID, that you need to hide this complexity from the users.

source_text: And you need to get feature parity between them.
zh: 而且，你得确保它们在功能上保持一致。
en: And you need to get feature parity between them.

source_text: So if a feature doesn't work on both providers, just disable them.
zh: 所以，如果某项功能无法在两家服务商的平台上都正常使用，那就直接禁用它。
en: So if a feature doesn't work on both providers, just disable them.

source_text: And have the common feature sets for the user to use.
zh: 只向用户提供两家服务商都支持的功能。
en: And have the common feature sets for the user to use.

source_text: Okay?
zh: 明白吗？
en: Okay?

source_text: The third lesson we learned from provider failover is that you.
zh: 我们从服务商故障切换中学到的第三个经验是，你……
en: The third lesson we learned from provider failover is that you.

source_text: Should keep your fallback in exercise.
zh: 要定期启用备用方案，确保它随时可用。
en: Should keep your fallback in exercise.

source_text: So this is the one thing is backup always breaks when you need it.
zh: 因为备用方案往往一到关键时刻就掉链子。
en: So this is the one thing is backup always breaks when you need it.

source_text: So if you heard about this one,
zh: 所以，如果你听说过这个说法，
en: So if you heard about this one,

source_text: that we shouldn't start sending requests to the fallback only when the primary fails.
zh: 我们不应该等到主服务商出故障时，才开始向备用服务商发送请求。
en: that we shouldn't start sending requests to the fallback only when the primary fails.

source_text: We should keep exercising it even when everything is working fine.
zh: 即使一切运行正常，我们也应该持续测试备用方案。
en: We should keep exercising it even when everything is working fine.

source_text: So the way we deal with it is we always split 10% of the traffic or sessions to the secondary model provider here.
zh: 所以，我们的做法是始终将 10% 的流量或会话分配给备用模型服务商。
en: So the way we deal with it is we always split 10% of the traffic or sessions to the secondary model provider here.

source_text: So that give us valuable data and metrics to help us understand how this secondary provider is working even when we don't need it at the moment.
zh: 这样，即使暂时用不上备用服务商，我们也能持续获得有价值的数据和指标，了解它的运行情况。
en: So that give us valuable data and metrics to help us understand how this secondary provider is working even when we don't need it at the moment.

source_text: Okay,
zh: 好的，
en: Okay,

source_text: so all the external matters have been sorted.
zh: 所以，所有外部事宜都已经处理妥当。
en: so all the external matters have been sorted.

source_text: Now we know that we can handle request level issues.
zh: 现在我们知道，请求级别的问题也能处理了。
en: Now we know that we can handle request level issues.

source_text: We can handle provider level failover.
zh: 我们可以处理服务商级别的故障切换。
en: We can handle provider level failover.

source_text: Now the problem comes back to ourselves. Right?
zh: 现在，问题又回到我们自己身上了，对吧？
en: Now the problem comes back to ourselves. Right?

source_text: So I mentioned earlier that we are serving LM gateways across four regions or four data centers.
zh: 我前面提到过，我们在四个区域，也就是四个数据中心，部署了语言模型网关。
en: So I mentioned earlier that we are serving LM gateways across four regions or four data centers.

source_text: We have one problem.
zh: 我们遇到了一个问题。
en: We have one problem.

source_text: Is that because we have a requirement that we want access control to be centrally managed,
zh: 这是因为我们要求对访问权限进行集中管理吗？
en: Is that because we have a requirement that we want access control to be centrally managed,

source_text: we want to have a single set of credentials and permissions for all the users.
zh: 我们希望为所有用户统一管理凭证和权限。
en: we want to have a single set of credentials and permissions for all the users.

source_text: So if they can access the model in one region,
zh: 所以，如果他们能在一个区域访问某个模型，
en: So if they can access the model in one region,

source_text: they should be able to do so from all the regions.
zh: 他们就应该能在所有区域访问这个模型。
en: they should be able to do so from all the regions.

source_text: This is important because many of our applications are deployed globally.
zh: 这一点很重要，因为我们的许多应用都部署在全球各地。
en: This is important because many of our applications are deployed globally.

source_text: And we can't rely on user to manage the complexity like they have to keep four API keys to depending on where they're calling. We want things to be simple for them.
zh: 我们不能让用户自己应对这种复杂性，比如根据调用的区域保管四个不同的 API 密钥。我们希望让他们用起来尽可能简单。
en: And we can't rely on user to manage the complexity like they have to keep four API keys to depending on where they're calling. We want things to be simple for them.

source_text: Like you have one API key and it works everywhere.
zh: 比如，只需要一个 API 密钥，就能在所有区域使用。
en: Like you have one API key and it works everywhere.

source_text: But this comes with a cost.
zh: 但这也有代价。
en: But this comes with a cost.

source_text: Our initial architecture here was naive that we kept a single Postgres database to keep all these data here.
zh: 我们最初的架构设计比较简单，用一个 PostgreSQL 数据库存储所有这些数据。
en: Our initial architecture here was naive that we kept a single Postgres database to keep all these data here.

source_text: And what makes the matter worse is because our compliance requirement asked us to keep track of all the prompt logs.
zh: 更糟的是，合规要求还规定，我们必须记录所有的提示词日志。
en: And what makes the matter worse is because our compliance requirement asked us to keep track of all the prompt logs.

source_text: Basically everything we get, we send and we get back from the upstream provider.
zh: 基本上，我们收到的所有内容、发给上游服务提供商的内容，以及从他们那里收到的回复，都要记录下来。
en: Basically everything we get, we send and we get back from the upstream provider.

source_text: We choose to just flip on a switch in this open source gateway to say store this in Postgres.
zh: 我们当时只是在这个开源网关里打开一个开关，让它把这些日志存进 PostgreSQL。

source_text: So two things we did.
zh: 所以我们做了两件事。
en: So two things we did.

source_text: One thing is we immediately turned off the prompt logging in the database.
zh: 第一件事，我们立即关闭了数据库中的提示词日志记录。
en: One thing is we immediately turned off the prompt logging in the database.

source_text: Just don't send this massive amount of data back to Postgres.

zh: 我们改为从各个区域直接把数据发送到 S3 对象存储。

source_text: So it does give us a few seconds delay in propagating permission change or new API key created.

source_text: But it help us to drop the authentication latency from two seconds to 20 milliseconds.

en: But it help us to drop the authentication latency from two seconds to 20 milliseconds.

source_text: Okay?

source_text: And we want to control and cap the usage if they goes over the limits.
zh: 如果用量超过限额，我们还希望能够加以控制并限制其继续使用。
en: And we want to control and cap the usage if they goes over the limits.

source_text: But on this part we choose to do eventual consistency.
zh: 但在这方面，我们选择采用最终一致性。
en: But on this part we choose to do eventual consistency.

source_text: That does mean that if you are over the limit for a few minutes, that's fine as long as we can stop you eventually if you are misbehaving, for example.
zh: 这意味着，即使短时间内超出限额几分钟也没关系；比如，如果你持续滥用，我们最终还是能阻止你。
en: That does mean that if you are over the limit for a few minutes, that's fine as long as we can stop you eventually if you are misbehaving, for example.

source_text: It's a trade off here.
zh: 这是一种权衡。
en: It's a trade off here.

source_text: So between having accounting in the hot paths versus eventual consistency, we picked eventual consistency. Okay?
zh: 所以，在把用量统计放进关键路径和采用最终一致性之间，我们选择了最终一致性。明白吧？
en: So between having accounting in the hot paths versus eventual consistency, we picked eventual consistency. Okay?

source_text: Yeah.
zh: 对。
en: Yeah.

source_text: So after we have done all of this, you would think that now it's the end of the story.

en: So after we have done all of this, you would think that now it's the end of the story.

source_text: Previously we already have metrics and logs.

source_text: Right?

source_text: Metrics helps you understand overall gateway health.

source_text: You answer questions like how many well, what's the latency?

en: You answer questions like how many well, what's the latency?

source_text: How many requests?

source_text: What's the error rate?

source_text: But one thing we're missing is tracing.
zh: 但我们还缺少一项：链路追踪。
en: But one thing we're missing is tracing.

source_text: So we want to understand for every given request what's the path it has been through.

en: So we want to understand for every given request what's the path it has been through.

source_text: What tool is it calling?

source_text: How long it takes and so on.

This is a question we hear all the time in customer interviews. We work with many companies building agents, both for online and offline use. They often ask, “How can we turn these materials into a review workspace that the team can use together tomorrow and keep editing afterward?”

That request carries a big promise. The customer won’t be sitting at their computer the whole time, so the agent needs to keep the work moving on its own. A colleague will pick it up tomorrow, which means the code and materials need to persist. And the workspace needs to go live and keep running.

en:
For a database, the first thing an agent typically needs to store is its metadata. Everything the agent does is recorded in two tables: agent session snapshots and agent session events.

A session snapshot captures the agent’s context, plan, and tool-call history. These records can be quite large—40 to 80 KB each is common. The event records are even larger because they preserve the full sequence of activity at the data level. As a result, metadata can easily grow from a few terabytes to hundreds of terabytes, or even petabytes.

Agents can move quickly between sandboxes while access is controlled by least-privilege permissions. We can also set and manage quotas for each project. TideDB takes on the burden of managing file systems at that scale, so the agent platform only needs to use them correctly. Right.

en:
Traditionally, if the platform maintains these databases itself, it quickly runs into problems. We’re not talking about creating just one or two applications. If hundreds of thousands, millions, or even tens of millions of users each create one, two, or perhaps ten applications, the scale changes completely.

At that point, managing all those applications raises questions: if database creation times out, was the database actually created? Will retrying create a duplicate? When an application is removed, are its resources fully reclaimed? Behind those questions lie ongoing responsibilities for provisioning, scaling, backups, upgrades, and failure recovery. The platform managing these databases has to take all of that on.

So the faster we generate code, the more we need a database service that can keep pace with application delivery. Right.

en:
Once we’ve identified something worth improving, how do we tell whether changing the model, prompt, or tools actually made it better? If we rerun everything from scratch, the inputs, tool responses, or files may have changed. Then it’s hard to tell whether a different result came from our changes or from changes in the environment.

So we need a common starting point: preserve the metadata, files, essential inputs, and configuration from the original run. Then we can create independent branches and evaluate them against the same criteria. A trace tells us what happened, but to optimize effectively, we also need checkpoints or snapshots that let us recreate the original conditions.

That gives us a reliable starting point for optimization. Right.

source_text: basically paying for Claude Code, Kiro from AWS, or Ollama as an AI inference, and there's a paper token, which basically most companies use nowadays,

source_text: right?

en: this is just to save you guys time from reading a very long research paper, this is the math behind it.

source_text: The numerator is basically the cost for running provisioning a GPU, and the denominator is basically cost for paper token.

en: The numerator is basically the cost for running provisioning a GPU, and the denominator is basically cost for paper token.

source_text: And to give you guys a perspective and a real example of how we apply this math, this is basically the biggest question nowadays, right?

en: And to give you guys a perspective and a real example of how we apply this math, this is basically the biggest question nowadays, right?

source_text: Should we now host GLM 5.3?
zh: 我们现在应该自行部署 GLM 5.3 吗？
en: Should we now host GLM 5.3?

source_text: We have run a lot of experiments set up, such as running with B200 on AWS, or even H200, but B200 nowadays provides the best cost efficiency, and maximum token output.
zh: 我们做了大量实验，测试过在 AWS 上用 B200、H200 等 GPU 运行模型。就目前来看，B200 的成本效益最高，Token 输出量也最大。
en: We have run a lot of experiments set up, such as running with B200 on AWS, or even H200, but B200 nowadays provides the best cost efficiency, and maximum token output.

source_text: And if you guys have a chance to grab your hand on B300, that would be awesome, but it's quite not there yet, right?
zh: 如果大家有机会用上 B300，那当然更好，不过目前还不太容易拿到，对吧？
en: And if you guys have a chance to grab your hand on B300, that would be awesome, but it's quite not there yet, right?

source_text: It's not available for most people.
zh: 大多数人还用不上。
en: It's not available for most people.

source_text: So with B200, the AWS flat price is roughly $140 per hour, and with this setup, we'll now go into a real example, right?
zh: 使用 B200 时，AWS 的固定费用大约是每小时 140 美元。接下来，我们就用这个配置来看一个实际案例，好吗？
en: So with B200, the AWS flat price is roughly $140 per hour, and with this setup, we'll now go into a real example, right?

source_text: If your company runs 67 billion tokens per month,

source_text: should I be switching?

en: On the right-hand side, you see the cost for running paper token, basically the effective blended cost is $2.

source_text: To break it down, $2 means GLM 5.3 nowadays charges around $1 per million input, and $5 per million output, right?
zh: 具体来说，这 2 美元是综合成本：目前 GLM 5.3 的价格大约是每百万输入 Token 1 美元、每百万输出 Token 5 美元，对吧？
en: To break it down, $2 means GLM 5.3 nowadays charges around $1 per million input, and $5 per million output, right?

source_text: And normally your organization input and output ratio should be around 4 to 1 for general purpose, and for heavy use case like tool calling, MCP,
zh: 一般来说，通用场景下，你们公司的输入与输出 Token 比例大约是 4 比 1；而对于工具调用、MCP 这类高负载场景，
en: And normally your organization input and output ratio should be around 4 to 1 for general purpose, and for heavy use case like tool calling, MCP,

source_text: RAG agent, the ratio can range from 10 to 1 to 15 to 1.
zh: RAG 智能体的输入与输出 Token 比例可能在 10 比 1 到 15 比 1 之间。
en: RAG agent, the ratio can range from 10 to 1 to 15 to 1.

source_text: So the left-hand side is basically the cost for paper token on an organization level.
zh: 左边显示的，基本上是企业层面每个 Token 的成本。
en: So the left-hand side is basically the cost for paper token on an organization level.

source_text: And the right-hand side is the cost for provisioning.
zh: 右边则是资源配置成本。
en: And the right-hand side is the cost for provisioning.

source_text: So we will provision 2 nodes of AWS 8B200 GPUs, basically 16 B200 GPUs, and that will cost around $166K per month.
zh: 所以我们会部署两个 AWS 节点，每个节点配备 8 张 B200 GPU，总共 16 张，每月费用约为 16.6 万美元。
en: So we will provision 2 nodes of AWS 8B200 GPUs, basically 16 B200 GPUs, and that will cost around $166K per month.

source_text: So with this number, it's very evident that you should not be switching, right?
zh: 从这些数字来看，很明显，你们不该切换，对吧？
en: So with this number, it's very evident that you should not be switching, right?

source_text: Because you are running a 3K deficit for your organization.
zh: 因为这样一来，你们公司每月会亏损约 3000 美元。
en: Because you are running a 3K deficit for your organization.

source_text: So now begs the question, when should I be switching?
zh: 那么问题来了：我应该什么时候切换？
en: So now begs the question, when should I be switching?

source_text: Basically now you have all the number, the ingredient to calculate.
zh: 现在，你基本上已经掌握了计算所需的所有数据。
en: Basically now you have all the number, the ingredient to calculate.

source_text: $166K to provision the model,
zh: 部署这个模型需要 16.6 万美元，
en: $166K to provision the model,

source_text: $2 effective cost per million token, so you can calculate the token point that you should be switching, which we call it the efficiency point.
zh: 每百万个 Token 的实际成本是 2 美元，因此你可以算出应该切换的 Token 用量临界点，我们称之为“效率临界点”。
en: $2 effective cost per million token, so you can calculate the token point that you should be switching, which we call it the efficiency point.

source_text: So the efficiency point is around 83 million.
zh: 所以，效率临界点大约是 8300 万个 Token。
en: So the efficiency point is around 83 million.

source_text: What does this mean?
zh: 这意味着什么？
en: What does this mean?

source_text: So if your organization consumes more than 83 million tokens per month, you should consider switching, and that is the point where you start gaining efficiency.
zh: 也就是说，如果你们机构每月使用超过 8300 万个 Token，就可以考虑切换；从这个用量开始，切换才会更划算。
en: So if your organization consumes more than 83 million tokens per month, you should consider switching, and that is the point where you start gaining efficiency.

source_text: Below this point, you actually run a deficit because your GPU is not at the efficient consumption rate, and you actually pay for the full price of the GPU because you basically are renting it, right?
zh: 低于这个用量，你实际上会亏钱，因为 GPU 的利用率还没达到经济高效的水平，但你仍要支付它的全部费用——毕竟你相当于是在租用它，对吧？
en: Below this point, you actually run a deficit because your GPU is not at the efficient consumption rate, and you actually pay for the full price of the GPU because you basically are renting it, right?

source_text: One.
zh: 一。
en: One.

source_text: Problem that we see in real practice is that provisioning the model is limited by the concurrency unit,
zh: 我们在实际应用中遇到的问题是，模型部署受到并发能力的限制，
en: Problem that we see in real practice is that provisioning the model is limited by the concurrency unit,

source_text: right?
zh: 对吧？
en: right?

source_text: CCU.
zh: 并发用户数（CCU）。
en: CCU.

source_text: So there's a lot of CCU setup that we have tried, for now we still strongly believe that GLM 5.3 at 8 at one node with 8 B200 is the best setup.
zh: 我们尝试过很多种 CCU 配置。目前我们仍然坚信，在一台配备 8 张 B200 的服务器上部署 GLM 5.3，支持 8 个并发用户，是最合适的方案。
en: So there's a lot of CCU setup that we have tried, for now we still strongly believe that GLM 5.3 at 8 at one node with 8 B200 is the best setup.

source_text: And this is basically the whole presentation in just one slide, with the chart is quite clear.
zh: 这一页基本概括了整场演示，图表也很清楚。
en: And this is basically the whole presentation in just one slide, with the chart is quite clear.

source_text: Below the efficiency point, you run a very big deficit, and above the efficiency point, you will gain a lot of efficiency in cost quite dramatically.
zh: 低于这个用量门槛，成本会高出很多；一旦超过，成本效率就会显著提升。
en: Below the efficiency point, you run a very big deficit, and above the efficiency point, you will gain a lot of efficiency in cost quite dramatically.

source_text: And during our practice, we found that this is basically the path to gain best efficiency in cost.
zh: 在实际应用中，我们发现这基本上是实现最佳成本效益的路径。
en: And during our practice, we found that this is basically the path to gain best efficiency in cost.

source_text: It's quite a no-brainer for you to switch from credit-based to paper token, right?
zh: 所以，从按额度计费切换到按 Token 计费，对你们来说是个显而易见的选择，对吧？
en: It's quite a no-brainer for you to switch from credit-based to paper token, right?

source_text: Because most of us, we run Claude Code with 200 credit plans, and it's just not enough, and we run into overage.

en: Because most of us, we run Claude Code with 200 credit plans, and it's just not enough, and we run into overage.

source_text: And overage cost is quite high, and just switching to paper token using GLM is much more efficient.
zh: 超额使用的费用很高，改用 GLM 按 Token 计费，成本效益要高得多。
en: And overage cost is quite high, and just switching to paper token using GLM is much more efficient.

source_text: And when you should consider for to switch from paper token to provisioning is when you reach the efficiency point.
zh: 当使用量达到这个成本效益门槛时，就该考虑从按 Token 计费切换到预置容量了。
en: And when you should consider for to switch from paper token to provisioning is when you reach the efficiency point.

source_text: And when you start in the provisioning mode, you should really consider when you should be scaling up.
zh: 进入预置容量模式后，就要认真考虑什么时候该扩容。
en: And when you start in the provisioning mode, you should really consider when you should be scaling up.

source_text: If you reach maximum concurrency,

en: If you reach maximum concurrency,

source_text: right?

source_text: Right?

en: We expected and we strongly believe that a 30 to 50 percent cost efficiency is quite achievable, and this is an example math.

en: So that is 58 percent cost efficiency.

en: And more on top of that, we have seen that the cost efficiency can be more than just 50 percent due to the enterprise nature.

source_text: Because this is influenced a lot due to the saving plans that you guys have, because you guys rent EC2 from hyperscalers such as AWS, GCP,

en: So that can influence the price quite a lot.

source_text: But on the left-hand right-hand side, the operational staff cost, the cost to maintain auto scaling is also worth considering.
zh: 但另一方面，运维人员的成本，以及维护自动扩缩容的成本，也值得考虑。
en: But on the left-hand right-hand side, the operational staff cost, the cost to maintain auto scaling is also worth considering.

source_text: So three problem statements before you guys can consider switching between this model, paper token to provisioning.
zh: 所以，在考虑从按 Token 计费模式切换到预置容量模式之前，你们需要先解决三个问题。
en: So three problem statements before you guys can consider switching between this model, paper token to provisioning.

source_text: GPU is actually quite scarce, right?
zh: GPU 资源其实相当紧缺，对吧？
en: GPU is actually quite scarce, right?

source_text: You for some company is quite hard for you to get your hand on GPUs.
zh: 对一些公司来说，想要拿到 GPU 资源相当困难。
en: You for some company is quite hard for you to get your hand on GPUs.

source_text: So it you need to plan ahead and deal with the hyperscaler to get the GPUs.
zh: 所以你们需要提前规划，并与大型云服务商协调，确保拿到所需的 GPU 资源。
en: So it you need to plan ahead and deal with the hyperscaler to get the GPUs.

source_text: So basically that is the biggest blocker now.
zh: 所以，这基本上是目前最大的障碍。
en: So basically that is the biggest blocker now.

source_text: Secondly, because if we set up auto scaling for us, we have seen that cases we need to grow from 12 GPUs to 15 GPUs due to peak time traffic.
zh: 第二，我们发现，如果启用自动扩缩容，高峰时段的流量可能会让 GPU 需求从 12 块增加到 15 块。
en: Secondly, because if we set up auto scaling for us, we have seen that cases we need to grow from 12 GPUs to 15 GPUs due to peak time traffic.

source_text: So we best to keep the paper token as a fallback rather than removing it completely.
zh: 所以，最好保留按 Token 计费的模式作为备用方案，而不是完全取消它。
en: So we best to keep the paper token as a fallback rather than removing it completely.

source_text: So usually in our setup,
zh: 所以，通常在我们的配置中，
en: So usually in our setup,

source_text: Databricks provide Unity AI Gateway, so it is quite achieved like as a platform, right?
zh: Databricks 提供了 Unity AI Gateway，所以它作为一个平台已经相当成熟了，对吧？
en: Databricks provide Unity AI Gateway, so it is quite achieved like as a platform, right?

source_text: In the platform, we can set up fallback, GLM provision as a main model, and GLM paper token as a fallback.
zh: 在这个平台上，我们可以设置故障切换：以预置资源的 GLM 模型为主，按 Token 计费的 GLM 模型作为备用。
en: In the platform, we can set up fallback, GLM provision as a main model, and GLM paper token as a fallback.

source_text: When we run trial, it's usually we see that 10 percent of the time the paper token model is invoked, and the customer does not realize any difference between provisioning or paper token, right?
zh: 在试运行时，我们通常会发现，大约 10% 的请求会调用按 Token 计费的备用模型，而客户并不会察觉它与预置资源模型有什么区别，对吧？
en: When we run trial, it's usually we see that 10 percent of the time the paper token model is invoked, and the customer does not realize any difference between provisioning or paper token, right?

source_text: And thirdly, the number are quite the flaw numbers, right?
zh: 第三，这些数字也只是大致的估算，对吧？
en: And thirdly, the number are quite the flaw numbers, right?

source_text: Because it's influenced a lot by the enterprise nature,
zh: 因为这在很大程度上受到企业自身特点的影响，
en: Because it's influenced a lot by the enterprise nature,

source_text: such as if you guys have deals with the hyperscalers, enterprise discount, saving plans. So it can change the number quite drastically.
zh: 比如，你们是否与大型云服务商签有协议、享有企业折扣或采用节省计划，这些都会让实际数字发生很大变化。
en: such as if you guys have deals with the hyperscalers, enterprise discount, saving plans. So it can change the number quite drastically.

source_text: So lastly,
zh: 最后，
en: So lastly,

source_text: we also strongly believe that switching from paper token to provisioning is not the only way to achieve cost efficiency.
zh: 我们也坚信，从按 Token 计费切换到预置资源，并不是实现成本效益的唯一途径。
en: we also strongly believe that switching from paper token to provisioning is not the only way to achieve cost efficiency.

source_text: We are now adopting semantic model routing and linguistic model routing as well, using the newly released OpenJev.
zh: 我们现在也开始采用语义模型路由和语言模型路由，并使用新发布的 OpenJev。
en: We are now adopting semantic model routing and linguistic model routing as well, using the newly released OpenJev.

source_text: Because due to our new with our new IPS research paper, on tokenization tags,
zh: 因为根据我们新发表的 IPS 研究论文中关于分词标签的研究，
en: Because due to our new with our new IPS research paper, on tokenization tags,

source_text: we found that linguistic model routing and semantic model routing can save the cost by also like 40 to 50 percent, right?
zh: 我们发现，语言模型路由和语义模型路由也能将成本降低约 40% 到 50%，对吧？
en: we found that linguistic model routing and semantic model routing can save the cost by also like 40 to 50 percent, right?

source_text: Give you an example, some model is not as efficient in Vietnamese and Chinese as with other models.
zh: 举个例子，有些模型处理越南语和中文时，效率不如其他模型。
en: Give you an example, some model is not as efficient in Vietnamese and Chinese as with other models.

source_text: So we pay attention to tokenization tags very deeply.
zh: 所以我们非常关注分词标签。
en: So we pay attention to tokenization tags very deeply.

source_text: And that will be the end of the meeting.
zh: 那么，今天的会议就到这里。
en: And that will be the end of the meeting.

source_text: Just to recap for you guys, I leave you guys two bullet points.
zh: 最后简单总结一下，我给大家留两点要点。
en: Just to recap for you guys, I leave you guys two bullet points.

source_text: The first one is there is an efficiency point in which your company can use the formula to calculate at this point, I should consider switching from paper token to provisioning.
zh: 第一点是，存在一个效率临界点。贵公司可以用这个公式计算：到了什么阶段，就该考虑从按量购买 token 转向预留资源。
en: The first one is there is an efficiency point in which your company can use the formula to calculate at this point, I should consider switching from paper token to provisioning.

source_text: Secondly,
zh: 第二，
en: Secondly,

source_text: the output of this method,
zh: 这种方法的结果，
en: the output of this method,

source_text: we strongly believe that a 30 percent to 50 percent cost optimization is quite achievable.
zh: 我们坚信，实现 30% 到 50% 的成本优化完全可行。
en: we strongly believe that a 30 percent to 50 percent cost optimization is quite achievable.

source_text: So thank you guys again. I'm TA from Techcombank. Hope you guys have a wonderful evening ahead.
zh: 再次感谢大家。我是来自 Techcombank 的 TA。祝大家今晚愉快。
en: So thank you guys again. I'm TA from Techcombank. Hope you guys have a wonderful evening ahead.

source_text: Thank you, TA, for Techcombank.
zh: 感谢来自 Techcombank 的 TA。
en: Thank you, TA, for Techcombank.

source_text: 谢谢TA的分享。
zh: 谢谢TA的分享。
en: Thank you, TA, for sharing your insights.

source_text: 然后下一位是来自谷歌的Timsley。
zh: 然后下一位是来自谷歌的Timsley。
en: Next up is Timsley from Google.

source_text: So the next one our guest is Timsley from Google. Let's welcome.
zh: 接下来有请来自谷歌的嘉宾 Timsley，大家欢迎！
en: So the next one our guest is Timsley from Google. Let's welcome.

source_text: 大家欢迎。
zh: 大家欢迎。
en: Please give them a warm welcome.

source_text: 啊大家好。 大家下午好。
zh: 啊大家好。 大家下午好。
en: Hello, everyone. Good afternoon.

source_text: 我是来自谷歌Agent Infra的产品经理。我叫诗婷。
zh: 我是来自谷歌Agent Infra的产品经理。我叫诗婷。
en: I’m Shiting, a product manager on Google’s Agent Infrastructure team.

source_text: 今天我们来谈一下。
zh: 今天我们来谈一下。
en: Today, we’re going to talk about…

source_text: 首先强化学习或训练应该是个非常热门的话题。
zh: 首先强化学习或训练应该是个非常热门的话题。
en: First, reinforcement learning and training are very hot topics right now.

source_text: 在做有多少同学是目前在做强化学习或者试图学习强化学习的？
zh: 在做有多少同学是目前在做强化学习或者试图学习强化学习的？
en: How many of you are currently working on reinforcement learning or trying to learn about it?

source_text: 有的话举个手好吗？
zh: 有的话举个手好吗？
en: If so, could you raise your hand?

source_text: Okay.
zh: 好的。
en: Okay.

source_text: 还挺多的。
zh: 还挺多的。
en: Quite a few of you.

source_text: 那我感觉我今天的难度可能给大家上点难度。
zh: 那我感觉我今天的难度可能给大家上点难度。
en: Looks like I might need to make today’s talk a bit more challenging for you all.

source_text: 有点有点干货。
zh: 有点有点干货。
en: I’ll share some practical insights.

source_text: Okay.
zh: 好的。
en: Okay.

source_text: 我们开始讲一下。
zh: 我们开始讲一下。
en: Let’s get started.

source_text: 首先为什么我今天讲的是百万量级？
zh: 首先为什么我今天讲的是百万量级？
en: First, why am I focusing on the million-scale level today?

source_text: 就是今天如果大家去看强化学习对模型的训练有多重要，你会看到比如说Kimi K3、DeepSeek V4、Flash、GLM。
zh: 就是今天如果大家去看强化学习对模型的训练有多重要，你会看到比如说Kimi K3、DeepSeek V4、Flash、GLM。
en: If you look at how important reinforcement learning is to training models today, you’ll see it in models like Kimi K3, DeepSeek V4, Flash, and GLM.

source_text: 强化学习的后训练在比如说coding特定的任务上，它对模型效果提升是巨大的。
zh: 强化学习的后训练在比如说coding特定的任务上，它对模型效果提升是巨大的。
en: In post-training, reinforcement learning can dramatically improve a model’s performance on specific tasks, such as coding.

source_text: 而且持续增长。
zh: 而且持续增长。
en: And the gains keep growing.

source_text: 那么今天这些所有的前沿实验室都在强化学习训练，并且规模越来越大。
zh: 那么今天这些所有的前沿实验室都在强化学习训练，并且规模越来越大。
en: So today, all the leading AI labs are using reinforcement learning to train their models, and they’re doing it at an ever-larger scale.

source_text: 但是很多时候，当我们跟研究员聊的时候，他其实发现了一个很大的问题是说，我的可能很大一部分的程度我想持续的训练，
zh: 但是很多时候，当我们跟研究员聊的时候，他其实发现了一个很大的问题是说，我的可能很大一部分的程度我想持续的训练，
en: But when we talk to researchers, a major problem often comes up: they want to keep training their models, often at a much larger scale.

source_text: 但是我会block在基础设施。
zh: 但是我会block在基础设施。
en: But I get blocked by the infrastructure.

source_text: 这个基础设施是什么？
zh: 这个基础设施是什么？
en: What is this infrastructure?

source_text: 其实是如何持续调度大规模的沙箱。
zh: 其实是如何持续调度大规模的沙箱。
en: The real challenge is how to continuously orchestrate sandboxes at scale.

source_text: 我们首先从最简单的一个RL的loop我们来讲起。
zh: 我们首先从最简单的一个RL的loop我们来讲起。
en: Let’s start with the simplest reinforcement learning loop.

source_text: 比方说我们要做一个训练，这个task是让这个AI输出一个hello world。
zh: 比方说我们要做一个训练，这个task是让这个AI输出一个hello world。
en: Suppose we want to train an AI to output “Hello, world.”

source_text: 那我们这个任务就叫输出hello world，用python写。
zh: 那我们这个任务就叫输出hello world，用python写。
en: So the task is to write a Python program that prints “Hello, world.”

source_text: 那一般来说我们会给它一个镜像。
zh: 那一般来说我们会给它一个镜像。
en: Generally, we’d give it a container image.

source_text: 镜像里面打包了一个基础的python库。
zh: 镜像里面打包了一个基础的python库。
en: The image comes with the basic Python libraries installed.

source_text: 你可以这个agent里面写。
zh: 你可以这个agent里面写。
en: You can write it in this agent.

source_text: 那首先你要准备好这个镜像，在这个沙箱里。
zh: 那首先你要准备好这个镜像，在这个沙箱里。
en: First, you need to have the image ready in the sandbox.

source_text: 那因为它是需要执行这个工作，有一些脱扣，它不再是像单纯的对话。
zh: 那因为它是需要执行这个工作，有一些脱扣，它不再是像单纯的对话。
en: Because it needs to execute the task and use some tools, it’s no longer just a simple conversation.

source_text: 那么你就需要这些不可信的执行的code放在sandbox里。
zh: 那么你就需要这些不可信的执行的code放在sandbox里。
en: So you need to run this untrusted code in a sandbox.

source_text: 也就是说每一次的这个LLM思考完了以后，这个东西都会放到sandbox里去执行。
zh: 也就是说每一次的这个LLM思考完了以后，这个东西都会放到sandbox里去执行。
en: In other words, after each time the LLM finishes thinking, its output is sent to the sandbox for execution.

source_text: 执行完了之后呢，你就会去看，哎，执行完它写的是不是到底是hello world，
zh: 执行完了之后呢，你就会去看，哎，执行完它写的是不是到底是hello world，
en: Once it’s run, you check whether it actually prints “Hello, world.”

source_text: 还是说hello今天的hello AI engineer伤害，对吧？
zh: 还是说hello今天的hello AI engineer伤害，对吧？
en: Or does it say, “Hello, AI engineer,” or something else? Right?

source_text: 那结束完了之后呢，我们会进行一个评分，可以是LLM作为judge评分，哎，这个是对的还是这个是错的。
zh: 那结束完了之后呢，我们会进行一个评分，可以是LLM作为judge评分，哎，这个是对的还是这个是错的。
en: Once it’s done, we score it. We can use an LLM as a judge to decide whether the result is right or wrong.

source_text: 这个是大体的整个每次RL的强化学习的rollout的流程。
zh: 这个是大体的整个每次RL的强化学习的rollout的流程。
en: That’s roughly how each rollout works in RL training.

source_text: 那么你会发现沙箱在每一步，每一个条轨迹上都必须要执行。
zh: 那么你会发现沙箱在每一步，每一个条轨迹上都必须要执行。
en: So you’ll notice that the sandbox has to run at every step of every rollout.

source_text: 但是当我们在实践中的时候，你会发现出现了很多问题。
zh: 但是当我们在实践中的时候，你会发现出现了很多问题。
en: But in practice, you’ll find that a lot of problems come up.

source_text: 首先我刚才说的只是一个非常简单的一个过程，但实际上通常来说，前沿实验室对一个任务你会让LLM产生比如说16个16个任务，
zh: 首先我刚才说的只是一个非常简单的一个过程，但实际上通常来说，前沿实验室对一个任务你会让LLM产生比如说16个16个任务，
en: First, what I just described was a very simple process. In practice, frontier labs typically have the LLM generate, say, 16 attempts for a single task.

source_text: 而且每一个任务它的难度都指数级的上升。
zh: 而且每一个任务它的难度都指数级的上升。
en: And the difficulty of each task increases exponentially.

source_text: 那么今天你去看比如说小米它有一个实时直播的RL dashboard，
zh: 那么今天你去看比如说小米它有一个实时直播的RL dashboard，
en: If you look at Xiaomi’s real-time RL dashboard today, for example,

source_text: 它上面会说，哎，我一次单个的任务它就要执行1000个1000个task，并且每个task都要做16次的这个rollout。
zh: 它上面会说，哎，我一次单个的任务它就要执行1000个1000个task，并且每个task都要做16次的这个rollout。
en: It shows that a single training run involves 1,000 tasks, with 16 rollouts for each task.

source_text: 也就是说我单次这个沙箱的起停就要满足16000次。
zh: 也就是说我单次这个沙箱的起停就要满足16000次。
en: That means the sandbox needs to start and stop 16,000 times in a single run.

source_text: 这是一个非常常见的数字在前沿实验室。
zh: 这是一个非常常见的数字在前沿实验室。
en: That’s a very common number at frontier labs.

source_text: 但是对于我们普通的比如说agent serving和inference，你很少能够达到并发量这么大的一个量级。
zh: 但是对于我们普通的比如说agent serving和inference，你很少能够达到并发量这么大的一个量级。
en: But with ordinary agent serving and inference, you rarely see concurrency at anything like that scale.

source_text: 首先这就对我们基础设施，比如说传统的容器infra产生巨大的挑战。
zh: 首先这就对我们基础设施，比如说传统的容器infra产生巨大的挑战。
en: First, this poses a huge challenge for our infrastructure, including traditional container infrastructure.

source_text: 因为没有见过这么大的吞吐量。
zh: 因为没有见过这么大的吞吐量。
en: Because it’s never had to handle throughput on this scale.

source_text: 第二点，我们的这个随着我们比如说code agent这些task，它也会变得越来越难。
zh: 第二点，我们的这个随着我们比如说code agent这些task，它也会变得越来越难。
en: Second, tasks for agents like coding agents are also becoming increasingly difficult.

source_text: 那今天这些前沿实验室训练的时候，它拿的这个数据都会经常打包成一个镜像。
zh: 那今天这些前沿实验室训练的时候，它拿的这个数据都会经常打包成一个镜像。
en: So when frontier labs train their models today, they often package the data into an image.

source_text: 比如说拿一个GitHub的仓库，打包成一个镜像，像sweet bench，然后这些镜像也安装了各种依赖包。
zh: 比如说拿一个GitHub的仓库，打包成一个镜像，像sweet bench，然后这些镜像也安装了各种依赖包。
en: For example, they’ll package a GitHub repository into an image, as with SWE-bench, and install all the necessary dependencies in that image.

source_text: 你会发现它的这个size非常的大，基本上每一个镜像都会超过一个GB，基本上是几个GB不等。
zh: 你会发现它的这个size非常的大，基本上每一个镜像都会超过一个GB，基本上是几个GB不等。
en: You’ll find these images are quite large. Almost every one is over a gigabyte, and many are several gigabytes.

source_text: 这样的一个挑战，而且他们在训练的超大数据规模，如果你去看Kimi K3的这个技术报告，
zh: 这样的一个挑战，而且他们在训练的超大数据规模，如果你去看Kimi K3的这个技术报告，
en: That’s one challenge. And the scale of their training data is enormous—if you look at the Kimi K3 technical report,

source_text: 他们训练了超过150万个镜像。
zh: 他们训练了超过150万个镜像。
en: They trained on more than 1.5 million images.

source_text: 那在这样大的体量下，
zh: 那在这样大的体量下，
en: At that scale,

source_text: 我们的网络存储怎么把这个镜像拉取、解析，能够快速的执行，不影响这个整体的训练流程，其实是个非常大的挑战。
zh: 我们的网络存储怎么把这个镜像拉取、解析，能够快速的执行，不影响这个整体的训练流程，其实是个非常大的挑战。
en: Getting our network storage to pull and unpack these images quickly enough to run them without slowing down the overall training process is a major challenge.

source_text: 啊第三点其实是影响到的数据质量。
zh: 啊第三点其实是影响到的数据质量。
en: The third challenge is data quality.

source_text: 因为在你整个过程中，我们会发现这个研究员经常说在传统的这个情况下，我们的沙箱大概要等它几分钟，
zh: 因为在你整个过程中，我们会发现这个研究员经常说在传统的这个情况下，我们的沙箱大概要等它几分钟，
en: Because throughout the process, researchers often tell us that, with the traditional setup, they have to wait several minutes for a sandbox to start up.

source_text: 比如说把这些镜像准备好等等等等。
zh: 比如说把这些镜像准备好等等等等。
en: For example, the system has to prepare the images and so on.

source_text: 但是如果在实际的训练过程中，
zh: 但是如果在实际的训练过程中，
en: But during the actual training process,

source_text: 这些情况就有可能被你的reward的这个评估评估为，哎，这个任务没有完成。
zh: 这些情况就有可能被你的reward的这个评估评估为，哎，这个任务没有完成。
en: These delays could cause the reward evaluator to mark the task as incomplete.

source_text: 有比如说内存溢出啊，或者超时等等。
zh: 有比如说内存溢出啊，或者超时等等。
en: For example, it might run out of memory or time out.

source_text: 那么这个你的整体的训练数据其实是被污染了，它没有正确的评定这个任务是否真的完成，而是是因为基础设施的问题而被评判为了没有完成。这会影响到最终模型的权重输出。
zh: 那么这个你的整体的训练数据其实是被污染了，它没有正确的评定这个任务是否真的完成，而是是因为基础设施的问题而被评判为了没有完成。这会影响到最终模型的权重输出。
en: That means your training data is effectively contaminated. The task is marked as incomplete not because it actually failed, but because of an infrastructure issue. That, in turn, affects the model’s final weights.

source_text: 啊更大的一个问题是说，哎，今天我们其实是去看这些沙箱的过程中，它其实我们发现80%的时间它都是空的，

source_text: 只有只有15%的时间它是在真正工作。

source_text: 它80%的时间是在等这个模型产生，哎，我要写什么code，或者下一步的计划，等它的这个思维链的思考啊。

en: For 80% of the time, the sandbox is waiting for the model to decide what code to write or what to do next—waiting for it to work through its chain of thought.

source_text: 对于一个前沿实验室来说，它要适应比如说每天百万量级的这样一个轨迹，那这样对他们来说资源是一个极大的浪费。

source_text: 而且这些等待的过程也使得我们非常昂贵的GPU啊，可能是百万美元的GPU集群就在那等几分钟，这其实是巨大巨大的一个浪费。

en: And we ran this test using 300,000 large container images from public datasets, such as SWE-bench and others widely available.

source_text: 啊第三点是，在传统的过程中你会发现这个啊，这个控制平面的infra它会经常的崩溃或者超时，

en: The second issue is network identity: as you scale exponentially, you start running into problems there too.

source_text: 比如说你是一个批量处理的任务X乘以16，这非常大量，非常容易使得你的网络的identity也是指数级上升，
zh: 比如说你是一个批量处理的任务X乘以16，这非常大量，非常容易使得你的网络的identity也是指数级上升，
en: For example, if a batch job scales by a factor of 16, that’s a huge increase, and the number of network identities can grow exponentially too.

source_text: 这大大大部分的情况下你是会遇到各种各样的问题。
zh: 这大大大部分的情况下你是会遇到各种各样的问题。

source_text: 所以呢我们进对这个网络的identity也进行了简化，使得你如果产生1万个沙箱，你也你也最多只需要512个identity，这样大规大幅的降低了整体集群的压力。

en: So we simplified network identity as well. Even if you create 10,000 sandboxes, you need at most 512 identities, which greatly reduces the load on the cluster.

source_text: 啊第三就是我们的这个镜像的分发，其实超大规模的镜像分发是，在每一个这个呃场景下都会产生呃挑战。

source_text: 那最终我们实现的情形是，我们还能够提升非常高的密度，在一个节点上你能够部署60个沙箱，这个对于超大规模的训练来说是非常重要的，
zh: 那最终我们实现的情形是，我们还能够提升非常高的密度，在一个节点上你能够部署60个沙箱，这个对于超大规模的训练来说是非常重要的，
en: Ultimately, we were able to achieve very high density: you can deploy 60 sandboxes on a single node. That’s crucial for training at a massive scale.

source_text: 你能够提升你的利用率。
zh: 你能够提升你的利用率。
en: You can improve resource utilization.

source_text: 它能够通过呃snapshot快照和快速起停的方式完成，使得你每一步的这个优化都通过快照恢复，呃低于亚秒级的方式，

source_text: 好，OK。

en: Okay.

zh: 就整个那个今年就是在Personal Agent这一块的一些关键时间节点，然后Tom和那个Instant的，
en: These are some of the key milestones in the Personal Agent space this year, including Tom and Instant.

source_text: 其实是今年6月份和和8月份就已经有了，他们去连接邮箱，然后连接Slack，做一些就是像那机率这一块，
zh: 其实是今年6月份和和8月份就已经有了，他们去连接邮箱，然后连接Slack，做一些就是像那机率这一块，
en: They actually had that back in June and August this year: connecting to email and Slack, and doing things like scheduling.

source_text: 其实发展很快。
zh: 其实发展很快。
en: Things have moved really fast.

zh: 然后还有一一个点，其实是今年6月6月23号，是那个Claude Tag，就在这不知道有没有用，
en: And another milestone was June 23 this year, when Claude launched Tasks. I’m not sure if anyone here has tried it.

source_text: 其实它也是我觉得是一个看起来是企业级的一个一个Agent，但实际上它在就是那个人性上，就是它知道是什么时候跟你聊天，什么时候不跟你聊天，

en: It may look like an enterprise-grade agent, but what makes it feel human is that it knows when to talk to you—and when to leave you alone.

source_text: 就是目前那Claude Tag的话，是我自己有用过将近那两个月，是体感最好的。
zh: 就是目前那Claude Tag的话，是我自己有用过将近那两个月，是体感最好的。
en: I’ve been using Claude Tasks for almost two months now, and so far, it’s given me the best experience.

source_text: 其实它是让6月份就有了，然后再往下的话，就可能是最近大家在9月份和11期间有接触的，像那Global Vault，然后Muse，
zh: 其实它是让6月份就有了，然后再往下的话，就可能是最近大家在9月份和11期间有接触的，像那Global Vault，然后Muse，
en: It was actually available back in June. Moving down the timeline, there are the ones people may have come across more recently, between September and November, like Global Vault and Muse.

source_text: 然后包括像那俊元他们有在做那Today，然后还有一系列产品，包括就包括Minus有发表，有Q，还还有那个Dose，
zh: 然后包括像那俊元他们有在做那Today，然后还有一系列产品，包括就包括Minus有发表，有Q，还还有那个Dose，
en: And Junyuan’s team has been working on Today, along with a whole series of products, including ones announced by Minus, like Q and Dose.

source_text: 就相信在座的应该就是投屏里面的这些PA有用过的，能够举个手吧。大概看一下有多少人有实际用过。
zh: 就相信在座的应该就是投屏里面的这些PA有用过的，能够举个手吧。大概看一下有多少人有实际用过。
en: If you’ve used any of the personal agents shown on the screen, could you raise your hand? I’d like to get a sense of how many people have tried them.

source_text: OK，比我想象中要少呀，虽然只有可能1/5的人有用过。对，这个但都大家都包应该都用过吧。
zh: OK，比我想象中要少呀，虽然只有可能1/5的人有用过。对，这个但都大家都包应该都用过吧。
en: Okay, fewer than I expected—maybe only about a fifth of you have tried them. But I assume everyone’s used Doubao, right?

source_text: OK，用过豆包就算用过Agent，所以也没啥。
zh: OK，用过豆包就算用过Agent，所以也没啥。
en: Okay, if you’ve used Doubao, that counts as having used an agent, so that’s fine.

source_text: OK，我们就往下，就是我们看这些从从年底去年年底到现在，真的是全面那个下场，
zh: OK，我们就往下，就是我们看这些从从年底去年年底到现在，真的是全面那个下场，
en: Okay, let’s move on. Looking at everything from the end of last year to now, it really feels like everyone has jumped in.

source_text: 非常非常多的那Personal Agent，然后都在做这些事情，就非这真的是那非常有意思。
zh: 非常非常多的那Personal Agent，然后都在做这些事情，就非这真的是那非常有意思。
en: There are so many personal agents doing these things now, and it’s really fascinating.

source_text: 然后我们去那掰开看，看它那工程的一些那个技术细节的话，我们发现那基础上基本上就大家都在做这几件事情。
zh: 然后我们去那掰开看，看它那工程的一些那个技术细节的话，我们发现那基础上基本上就大家都在做这几件事情。
en: When we break them down and look at the technical details, we find that, fundamentally, everyone is doing the same few things.

source_text: 第一块是那Memory，就是在做一些就是那个记忆，然后包括基于各种你的资料，你的记忆，尝试去那理解你，然后帮你去建那Profile，
zh: 第一块是那Memory，就是在做一些就是那个记忆，然后包括基于各种你的资料，你的记忆，尝试去那理解你，然后帮你去建那Profile，
en: The first area is memory: using your data and past interactions to understand you and build a profile of you.

source_text: 然后往上的话，然后通过各种那连接器，就是能够把你的那个Gmail呀，还有就各种信息能够拿到，就是其实实际上感知你的话，
zh: 然后往上的话，然后通过各种那连接器，就是能够把你的那个Gmail呀，还有就各种信息能够拿到，就是其实实际上感知你的话，
en: Then, on top of that, they use various connectors to access your Gmail and other information, so they can actually get a sense of who you are.

source_text: 相当于是一个传感器，就通过各种方式，让那个Agent能够看见你看见的世界，能够读到读的你，
zh: 相当于是一个传感器，就通过各种方式，让那个Agent能够看见你看见的世界，能够读到读的你，
en: It’s essentially a sensor: it gives the agent different ways to see the world as you see it and read what you read.

source_text: 你要读过的资料。
zh: 你要读过的资料。
en: The materials you’ve read.

source_text: 然后然后再往上的话，就是这一件那PA里面，就是在整个那个主动性，会比会比那Coding Agent会更加主动，
zh: 然后然后再往上的话，就是这一件那PA里面，就是在整个那个主动性，会比会比那Coding Agent会更加主动，
en: And beyond that, personal agents are much more proactive than coding agents.

source_text: 就是再很多情况下会会有Schedule，然后你可以设各种地区任务，然后它会主动那个触达你。
zh: 就是再很多情况下会会有Schedule，然后你可以设各种地区任务，然后它会主动那个触达你。
en: In many cases, they have scheduling features. You can set up recurring tasks, and the agent will proactively reach out to you.

source_text: 所以在这块也是很好玩的，然后包括当然有一块是绕不开的，甚至在目前可能真的做好的也不多，就是目前全全线和那隐私这一块，
zh: 所以在这块也是很好玩的，然后包括当然有一块是绕不开的，甚至在目前可能真的做好的也不多，就是目前全全线和那隐私这一块，
en: That’s another interesting area. And, of course, there’s one issue we can’t avoid—one that few have really solved so far: security and privacy.

source_text: 所以从工程技术上来看的话，其实整个那Personal Agent可以说能力上是差不多的，其实大家从从纯粹那工程上，
zh: 所以从工程技术上来看的话，其实整个那Personal Agent可以说能力上是差不多的，其实大家从从纯粹那工程上，
en: So, from an engineering perspective, personal agents are all fairly similar in what they can do. Purely on the technical side, everyone is...

source_text: 我觉得都是在做在做最这些事情吧。
zh: 我觉得都是在做在做最这些事情吧。
en: I think everyone is working on pretty much the same things.

source_text: 核心区别是那场景，然后回到场景的话，我觉得这边比较有意思了，就是每个Personal Agent那主打的场景可能都会有些不一样，
zh: 核心区别是那场景，然后回到场景的话，我觉得这边比较有意思了，就是每个Personal Agent那主打的场景可能都会有些不一样，
en: The key difference is the use case. And that’s where things get interesting: each personal agent may focus on a slightly different set of use cases.

source_text: 像那Tom的话，像那Tom AI其实核心让它把那个Gmail给连接之后，
zh: 像那Tom的话，像那Tom AI其实核心让它把那个Gmail给连接之后，
en: For example, with Tom AI, the key is connecting it to Gmail first.

source_text: 你发现真的是感觉Tom AI做了一个比Gmail还好的邮件客户端，真的把你的邮件管得很好。
zh: 你发现真的是感觉Tom AI做了一个比Gmail还好的邮件客户端，真的把你的邮件管得很好。
en: You realize Tom AI has built an email client that feels even better than Gmail. It really does a great job of managing your inbox.

source_text: 对，然后像那Global Vault也是，就总之在这里面，大家如果有尝试过的，
zh: 对，然后像那Global Vault也是，就总之在这里面，大家如果有尝试过的，
en: Right, and Global Vault is similar. Anyway, if any of you have tried these...

source_text: 基本上目前的Personal Agent都在帮你处理很多生活杂事，帮你在看邮件，然后做会议纪要，然后简报或者写周报之类的，
zh: 基本上目前的Personal Agent都在帮你处理很多生活杂事，帮你在看邮件，然后做会议纪要，然后简报或者写周报之类的，
en: Right now, personal agents mainly help with everyday tasks: managing your email, taking meeting notes, and putting together briefings or weekly reports.

source_text: 就总之很多很多事情都在做。
zh: 就总之很多很多事情都在做。
en: In short, they’re doing all sorts of things.

source_text: 然后还有一些比较比较有趣的，比如说在关注你的身体健康，它会根据一些健康数据，然后给你提醒，
zh: 然后还有一些比较比较有趣的，比如说在关注你的身体健康，它会根据一些健康数据，然后给你提醒，
en: And there are some more interesting uses, too. For example, an agent can keep track of your health data and send you reminders based on it.

source_text: 然后会非常多的就是一些那场景。
zh: 然后会非常多的就是一些那场景。
en: And there are many more use cases like that.

source_text: 对，对，就上面这些场景看起来很多，那我觉得很有意思，就是之前跟一个朋友在聊天，
zh: 对，对，就上面这些场景看起来很多，那我觉得很有意思，就是之前跟一个朋友在聊天，
en: Right, right. There seem to be a lot of use cases here. Something interesting came up when I was talking to a friend recently.

source_text: 我们说这么多场景里面，真的去细掰的话，会发现可能就两类场景，一个是把我们日常不想干的事情，
zh: 我们说这么多场景里面，真的去细掰的话，会发现可能就两类场景，一个是把我们日常不想干的事情，
en: We were saying that if you really break down all these use cases, they probably fall into two categories. One is taking care of the everyday tasks we don’t want to do.

source_text: 通过那Agent去去我们干掉，就是这是在解决我们的烦恼。
zh: 通过那Agent去去我们干掉，就是这是在解决我们的烦恼。
en: We use an agent to take those tasks off our hands—that’s one way it solves our everyday frustrations.

source_text: 比如说有些订阅，不知道有没有取消，通过Agent帮你去取消，其实那个这这个场景还是真的是一个烦恼。
zh: 比如说有些订阅，不知道有没有取消，通过Agent帮你去取消，其实那个这这个场景还是真的是一个烦恼。
en: For example, you might have subscriptions you’re not sure you’ve canceled. Having an agent check and cancel them for you would solve a real headache.

source_text: 一旦帮你解解决之后的话，是挺方便的，包括定像一些订票呀，然后就是邮件啊，就是就这是一块，帮你解决你不想干的事情，
zh: 一旦帮你解解决之后的话，是挺方便的，包括定像一些订票呀，然后就是邮件啊，就是就这是一块，帮你解决你不想干的事情，
en: Once an agent takes care of those things, it’s really convenient—booking tickets, handling email, and so on. That’s one category: doing the things you don’t want to do.

source_text: 是解决烦恼。
zh: 是解决烦恼。
en: It’s about taking care of hassles.

source_text: 然后第二块的话，其实就是也是目前在那自媒体圈会比较比较流行，有了那Personal Agent之后，
zh: 然后第二块的话，其实就是也是目前在那自媒体圈会比较比较流行，有了那Personal Agent之后，
en: The second category is something that’s also quite popular in the creator community right now: once you have a personal agent…

source_text: 就终于可以开始做内容自动化工厂，
zh: 就终于可以开始做内容自动化工厂，
en: …you can finally build an automated content creation pipeline.

source_text: 然后让自己的各种碎片时间无缝那个利用起来，然后尝试去涨粉，去涨流量，
zh: 然后让自己的各种碎片时间无缝那个利用起来，然后尝试去涨粉，去涨流量，
en: It lets you make the most of every spare moment and try to grow your following and traffic.

source_text: 其实一定很多是满足内心里想被更多人关注的一个欲望。
zh: 其实一定很多是满足内心里想被更多人关注的一个欲望。
en: A lot of it really comes down to the desire to be noticed by more people.

source_text: 甚至通过这种那流获取流量的方式，能够去挣钱。
zh: 甚至通过这种那流获取流量的方式，能够去挣钱。
en: You can even make money by generating traffic this way.

source_text: 所以那这是一个那欲望满足，但是无论是烦恼还是欲望，我觉得这都是很正常的一个一个需求吧，
zh: 所以那这是一个那欲望满足，但是无论是烦恼还是欲望，我觉得这都是很正常的一个一个需求吧，
en: So that’s about fulfilling a desire. But whether it’s solving a hassle or satisfying a desire, I think both are perfectly normal needs.

source_text: 其实能解决也都也都是那个很好的。
zh: 其实能解决也都也都是那个很好的。
en: And if these agents can meet those needs, that’s a good thing.

source_text: 但是真的去想的话，
zh: 但是真的去想的话，
en: But if you really think about it,

source_text: 又发现那这两类其实更多是那向外的。
zh: 又发现那这两类其实更多是那向外的。
en: You realize that both of these are actually more outward-facing.

source_text: 回到我们那内心里，我们真的有这么多烦恼吗？
zh: 回到我们那内心里，我们真的有这么多烦恼吗？
en: But if we look inward, do we really have that many worries?

source_text: 这么真的有这么多那欲望吗？
zh: 这么真的有这么多那欲望吗？
en: Do we really have that many desires?

source_text: 是不是有个那Agent能够帮你去解决一些不太不太一样的东西？
zh: 是不是有个那Agent能够帮你去解决一些不太不太一样的东西？
en: Could an agent help you with something a little different?

source_text: 我们来看那第一块，就是就是前面是那Muse的，是那个Art的王，他的一句话，通过那Muse让AI能够把一些让自己很烦的事情，
zh: 我们来看那第一块，就是就是前面是那Muse的，是那个Art的王，他的一句话，通过那Muse让AI能够把一些让自己很烦的事情，
en: Let’s look at the first point. It’s a quote from Art Wang of Muse: with Muse, AI can take care of some of the things that really bother you.

source_text: 把它去那做到了，然后后续呢，你就能够把时间花在想做的事情上，
zh: 把它去那做到了，然后后续呢，你就能够把时间花在想做的事情上，
en: Once it takes care of those things, you can spend your time on what you actually want to do.

source_text: 这是一个那Muse的一个美好那愿景。
zh: 这是一个那Muse的一个美好那愿景。
en: That’s the vision behind Muse.

source_text: 但是实际上我们无论看中国还是海外，
zh: 但是实际上我们无论看中国还是海外，
en: But in reality, whether we look at China or the rest of the world,

source_text: 就发现很多事情，
zh: 就发现很多事情，
en: we find that a lot of things...

source_text: 目前这个时代，第一个可能日常杂事，对于绝大部分人来说也没那么多，然后其实我们有很多时间，
zh: 目前这个时代，第一个可能日常杂事，对于绝大部分人来说也没那么多，然后其实我们有很多时间，
en: These days, most people don’t have that many everyday chores to deal with, and we actually have quite a lot of free time.

source_text: 但我们真正把这些时间真的真的会花在想做的事情上吧。
zh: 但我们真正把这些时间真的真的会花在想做的事情上吧。
en: But do we actually spend that time doing what we really want to do?

source_text: 对，
zh: 对，
en: Right.

source_text: 可能不一定是我们的主观那个能东西，更多是各种环境，使得我们真正的时间去刷短剧了，去刷短视频了，或者去看那个TikTok了。
zh: 可能不一定是我们的主观那个能东西，更多是各种环境，使得我们真正的时间去刷短剧了，去刷短视频了，或者去看那个TikTok了。
en: Maybe it’s not entirely a conscious choice. Our surroundings play a bigger role, and we end up spending that time watching short dramas, scrolling through short videos, or browsing TikTok.

source_text: 对，就整个其实哪怕有人把时间省下来，各种那Personal Agent发挥到极致，
zh: 对，就整个其实哪怕有人把时间省下来，各种那Personal Agent发挥到极致，
en: Right. Even if personal agents did everything they could to save people time,

source_text: 真的能让我们把各种那烦恼的事情和那欲望都满足掉之后，我们真的会去干我们想做的事情吗？
zh: 真的能让我们把各种那烦恼的事情和那欲望都满足掉之后，我们真的会去干我们想做的事情吗？
en: If they really could take care of all our hassles and satisfy all our desires, would we actually go and do what we truly want to do?

source_text: 这答案肯定是那否定的。
zh: 这答案肯定是那否定的。
en: The answer is definitely no.

source_text: 对，然后包括就是为什么我们很多时候，很多人无论熬夜到几点，包括我自己有段时间，可能哪怕一看一两点了，很困了，那这就是有点睡不着，
zh: 对，然后包括就是为什么我们很多时候，很多人无论熬夜到几点，包括我自己有段时间，可能哪怕一看一两点了，很困了，那这就是有点睡不着，
en: Right. And that’s part of why so many of us stay up late. I went through a period when, even at one or two in the morning, I’d be exhausted but still couldn’t quite fall asleep.

source_text: 然后会打开手机，还要去可能刷刷短剧，或者看看那个X。为什么？
zh: 然后会打开手机，还要去可能刷刷短剧，或者看看那个X。为什么？
en: Then I’d pick up my phone and scroll through short dramas or check X. Why?

source_text: 就是为什么人明明困了，还会想去在睡前花个半个小时一个小时，去刷各种媒体，其实这这这这里面，从心理学上来讲，
zh: 就是为什么人明明困了，还会想去在睡前花个半个小时一个小时，去刷各种媒体，其实这这这这里面，从心理学上来讲，
en: Why do we still spend half an hour or an hour scrolling through social media before bed when we’re clearly tired? Psychologically speaking, there’s something going on here.

source_text: 很大程度上是那补偿机制，就因为白天白天很多事情是身不由己，所以到了睡前，终于你就有了一些那自主权，所以你想去刷，
zh: 很大程度上是那补偿机制，就因为白天白天很多事情是身不由己，所以到了睡前，终于你就有了一些那自主权，所以你想去刷，
en: To a large extent, it’s a way of compensating. So much of your day is out of your control that, when bedtime comes, you finally have a bit of freedom to choose what you do. So you want to scroll.

source_text: 其实其实深夜刷手机是一种人的自由，是人在夺回自己那个选择权。
zh: 其实其实深夜刷手机是一种人的自由，是人在夺回自己那个选择权。
en: Scrolling on your phone late at night is, in a way, an act of freedom—a way to reclaim your sense of choice.

source_text: 但是你看我们的Personal Agent能够帮我们夺回那主动权吗？
zh: 但是你看我们的Personal Agent能够帮我们夺回那主动权吗？
en: But can our personal agents really help us reclaim that sense of control?

source_text: 你想感觉是那做不到的。
zh: 你想感觉是那做不到的。
en: It doesn’t seem like they can.

source_text: 所以就是怎么说呢，就是有没有那个Personal Agent，那个Personal Agent最重要的不是Agent，
zh: 所以就是怎么说呢，就是有没有那个Personal Agent，那个Personal Agent最重要的不是Agent，
en: So, how should I put it? Whether or not you have a personal agent, the most important part isn’t the “agent.”

source_text: 是前面那个Person，是Person是人，人的主动性如何在这一届Personal Agent里面有没有人去关注，让更多人更加关注自己的那个主动性。
zh: 是前面那个Person，是Person是人，人的主动性如何在这一届Personal Agent里面有没有人去关注，让更多人更加关注自己的那个主动性。
en: It’s the “person” part—the human being. Is anyone in this wave of personal agents paying attention to human agency and helping people become more aware of their own power to choose?

source_text: OK，就是所以回到这点，我觉得可能在座的像参加线下会议，一定程度上都不是说想着天天刷抖音的，而是一定在内心里，
zh: OK，就是所以回到这点，我觉得可能在座的像参加线下会议，一定程度上都不是说想着天天刷抖音的，而是一定在内心里，
en: Okay, so coming back to that point, I think those of us here at an in-person event probably don’t want to spend all day scrolling through Douyin. Deep down, we must all...

source_text: 除了烦恼和欲望之外，还是想学会，
zh: 除了烦恼和欲望之外，还是想学会，
en: Beyond our worries and desires, we still want to learn how to…

source_text: 比如说学会更好的创业，然后来来会场去教一些朋友，在内心里会有想做的事情，想去比如说无论是OPC还是创业，想把自己的那作品给做出来，
zh: 比如说学会更好的创业，然后来来会场去教一些朋友，在内心里会有想做的事情，想去比如说无论是OPC还是创业，想把自己的那作品给做出来，
en: For example, you might want to learn how to build a better business, or come to an event like this to share what you know with friends. Deep down, there’s something you want to do—whether it’s starting a one-person company or a larger venture, you want to bring your own work to life.

source_text: 在内心里一定是有自己想做的。
zh: 在内心里一定是有自己想做的。
en: Deep down, there’s something you want to do.

source_text: 但这跟小素描，我觉得是一定程度上是本质最本质最足的。
zh: 但这跟小素描，我觉得是一定程度上是本质最本质最足的。
en: But I think this is, in a sense, the most fundamental thing.

source_text: 其实我们每个人都有这个能力，我们除了烦恼和欲望之外，我们的本心其实都是非常之好。
zh: 其实我们每个人都有这个能力，我们除了烦恼和欲望之外，我们的本心其实都是非常之好。
en: The truth is, we all have this capacity. Beneath our worries and desires, we’re fundamentally good at heart.

source_text: 对，我们我们更需要的，可能需要一些东西，一些环境，
zh: 对，我们我们更需要的，可能需要一些东西，一些环境，
en: Right. What we may need more than anything is the right kind of support and environment.

source_text: 来把我们本心的这个东西给点燃。
zh: 来把我们本心的这个东西给点燃。
en: To ignite that spark within us.

source_text: 对，然后点燃的方式之一的话，我我自己两三年的一个时间，我觉得就是创作，就是AI，我们叫在国内叫AI GC，是生成式内容，生成的话，
zh: 对，然后点燃的方式之一的话，我我自己两三年的一个时间，我觉得就是创作，就是AI，我们叫在国内叫AI GC，是生成式内容，生成的话，
en: Right. And one way to ignite that spark, I’ve come to feel over the past two or three years, is through creating with AI. In China, we call it AIGC—AI-generated content, or generative content.

source_text: 其实是让这种生成能力，是让我们在座的每一个人在内容创作这一块，可能都有了一种更更好的那个选择权。
zh: 其实是让这种生成能力，是让我们在座的每一个人在内容创作这一块，可能都有了一种更更好的那个选择权。
en: It gives everyone here a much wider range of options when it comes to creating content.

source_text: 我们之前在门户时代，在报纸时代，是看那个别人去编辑好，选择好的东西，然后到那搜索时代，内容极大丰富，
zh: 我们之前在门户时代，在报纸时代，是看那个别人去编辑好，选择好的东西，然后到那搜索时代，内容极大丰富，
en: In the days of newspapers and web portals, we read what others had edited and selected for us. Then came the age of search, when content became vastly more abundant.

source_text: 我们通过谷歌可以去搜索，然后到了到了金融头条，到到抖音，然后到了红果，我们其实一直被那个推荐给牵走，彼此带走。
zh: 我们通过谷歌可以去搜索，然后到了到了金融头条，到到抖音，然后到了红果，我们其实一直被那个推荐给牵走，彼此带走。
en: We could search for things on Google, but then came news feeds, Douyin, and later Hongguo. Ever since, recommendation algorithms have been leading us from one thing to the next.

source_text: 其实消费侧，我们那被动消费，我们丧失选择权的消费，其实已经已经到了尽头。
zh: 其实消费侧，我们那被动消费，我们丧失选择权的消费，其实已经已经到了尽头。
en: On the consumption side, passive consumption—where we’ve lost the power to choose—has reached its limit.

source_text: 所以我们一定程度上我个人会觉得，目前有个小趋势，有个那未来，就是我们可能在这个时代，更多的情况下，应该要从从那种消费侧逐步去走向那个创作侧。
zh: 所以我们一定程度上我个人会觉得，目前有个小趋势，有个那未来，就是我们可能在这个时代，更多的情况下，应该要从从那种消费侧逐步去走向那个创作侧。
en: So personally, I see an emerging trend—and perhaps a glimpse of the future: in this era, we may need to move gradually from consuming content to creating it.

source_text: 对，然后整个UMA的要做的事情，就基于那上面的一一个一个想法，
zh: 对，然后整个UMA的要做的事情，就基于那上面的一一个一个想法，
en: Right. And everything UMA is trying to do is built on that idea.

source_text: 就是更更多想做的，可能不是那Personal Agent，而而真正需要的，就是其实创造一种环境，
zh: 就是更更多想做的，可能不是那Personal Agent，而而真正需要的，就是其实创造一种环境，
en: What we really want to build may not be a personal agent, but an environment that makes creation possible.

source_text: 因为人是人是环境的反应器。
zh: 因为人是人是环境的反应器。
en: Because people respond to their environment.

source_text: 对，无论是微信，还是UMA的，还是任何一个产品，它都在营造一个环境。
zh: 对，无论是微信，还是UMA的，还是任何一个产品，它都在营造一个环境。
en: Right. Whether it’s WeChat, UMA, or any other product, each one creates an environment.

source_text: 所以UMA的想做的，就是你和AI和你的那个很多那个Agent一起，更好的去去创作。
zh: 所以UMA的想做的，就是你和AI和你的那个很多那个Agent一起，更好的去去创作。
en: So what UMA aims to do is help you create better work together with AI and your many agents.

source_text: 而且这个创作更多是给自己看的，这边我分享一个数据，就是目前的UMA的大概已经有上千名，
zh: 而且这个创作更多是给自己看的，这边我分享一个数据，就是目前的UMA的大概已经有上千名，
en: And a lot of that creation is just for yourself. Here’s one data point: UMA currently has over a thousand users...

source_text: 是那个Max的那个付费用户，就一个月那付100刀的，然后在那Max用户群里面，每周每个月平均会做15个PPT。
zh: 是那个Max的那个付费用户，就一个月那付100刀的，然后在那Max用户群里面，每周每个月平均会做15个PPT。
en: They’re Max subscribers paying $100 a month, and on average, each of them makes 15 presentations a month.

source_text: 对，我当时很好奇，当时以为UMA的在在进军那PPT界，在在和Gamma和那JazzBug在竞争。
zh: 对，我当时很好奇，当时以为UMA的在在进军那PPT界，在在和Gamma和那JazzBug在竞争。
en: Right. I was curious at the time—I thought UMA was getting into the presentation business and competing with Gamma and JazzBug.

source_text: 对，我说完蛋了，因为那Gamma可能和JazzBug都还是有，就是资金雄厚度会比我多。
zh: 对，我说完蛋了，因为那Gamma可能和JazzBug都还是有，就是资金雄厚度会比我多。
en: Right, I thought, “We’re in trouble,” because Gamma and JazzBug probably have much deeper pockets than we do.

source_text: 如果如果真的做PPT的话，可能那没机会。
zh: 如果如果真的做PPT的话，可能那没机会。
en: If we were really trying to compete on presentations, we probably wouldn’t stand a chance.

source_text: 但是我后来发现，这个用户访谈又发现，就是很很有意思，很多人在UMA的做PPT是做给自己看的，中间做15个PPT里面，
zh: 但是我后来发现，这个用户访谈又发现，就是很很有意思，很多人在UMA的做PPT是做给自己看的，中间做15个PPT里面，
en: But then, through user interviews, I discovered something interesting: many people make presentations in UMA just for themselves. Of the 15 presentations they make...

source_text: 一个月平均两天做一个PPT，中间15个里面，只有一两个会给别人看。
zh: 一个月平均两天做一个PPT，中间15个里面，只有一两个会给别人看。
en: They make about one presentation every two days, but out of those 15 in a month, they only share one or two with other people.

source_text: 所以所以在在这个里面，是就真的那很有意思。
zh: 所以所以在在这个里面，是就真的那很有意思。
en: So that’s what makes this really interesting.

source_text: 就包括海外有个产品是谷歌有做那个Notebook LM，就它里面也有一个很很好玩的东西，很多人在上面做播客，做视频概览，
zh: 就包括海外有个产品是谷歌有做那个Notebook LM，就它里面也有一个很很好玩的东西，很多人在上面做播客，做视频概览，
en: Google has a product called NotebookLM, and there’s something really interesting happening there too: lots of people use it to create podcasts and video overviews.

source_text: 做PPT，做信息图，其实都是那给自己看，其实并不是给别人看的。
zh: 做PPT，做信息图，其实都是那给自己看，其实并不是给别人看的。
en: They make presentations and infographics mainly for themselves, not to show other people.

source_text: 所以给自己看的需求，能够能够越级，就是在ToB ToC之外，还有ToM，能够让自己有所不一样，有所成长，其实也是一个很大的市场。
zh: 所以给自己看的需求，能够能够越级，就是在ToB ToC之外，还有ToM，能够让自己有所不一样，有所成长，其实也是一个很大的市场。
en: So there’s a real demand for things people make for themselves. Beyond B2B and B2C, there’s also “To Me”—helping people grow and become a better version of themselves. That’s a huge market too.

source_text: OK，然后整个UMA的从功能上，其实我觉得跟大家都差不多，就是那Memory啊，Scale啊，这些东西。
zh: OK，然后整个UMA的从功能上，其实我觉得跟大家都差不多，就是那Memory啊，Scale啊，这些东西。
en: Okay, in terms of features, I think UMA is pretty similar to everyone else—memory, scale, and things like that.

source_text: 所以这个我觉得是几乎做从工程去解构的话，任何Personal Agent产品都差不多，大同小异。
zh: 所以这个我觉得是几乎做从工程去解构的话，任何Personal Agent产品都差不多，大同小异。
en: So I think if you break it down from an engineering perspective, pretty much every personal agent product is built along similar lines.

source_text: 但最终还是回到场景，回到场景上，目前UMA的核核心答案，能够两个场景，第一个场景的话，是那Create to Learn，
zh: 但最终还是回到场景，回到场景上，目前UMA的核核心答案，能够两个场景，第一个场景的话，是那Create to Learn，
en: But ultimately, it comes back to use cases. Right now, UMA focuses on two core scenarios. The first is “Create to Learn.”

source_text: 就是通过学习的方式去创作，是那费曼学习法，就是你得把东西给能够通过自己的方式讲出来，或者做成PPT，或者写成一篇那文章。
zh: 就是通过学习的方式去创作，是那费曼学习法，就是你得把东西给能够通过自己的方式讲出来，或者做成PPT，或者写成一篇那文章。
en: It’s about creating as a way to learn—the Feynman technique. You need to explain something in your own words, whether that’s by making a presentation or writing an article.

source_text: 在在这个过程中，
zh: 在在这个过程中，
en: In this process,

source_text: 你对一个主题，然后对自己的一个那好奇，你会那学的更多。
zh: 你对一个主题，然后对自己的一个那好奇，你会那学的更多。
en: As you explore a topic you’re curious about, you end up learning more.

source_text: 对，这之前之前有个朋友开玩笑说，说UMA的其实是全球第一个第一个那个费曼Agent。
zh: 对，这之前之前有个朋友开玩笑说，说UMA的其实是全球第一个第一个那个费曼Agent。
en: Right. A friend once joked that UMA was the world’s first Feynman agent.

source_text: 对，
zh: 对，
en: Right.

source_text: 这个确实没有人做过，而且我感觉也确实很贴切，就是如果大家对费曼学习法有有听过的话，想实践的话，
zh: 这个确实没有人做过，而且我感觉也确实很贴切，就是如果大家对费曼学习法有有听过的话，想实践的话，
en: No one’s really done this before, and I think the description fits. If you’ve heard of the Feynman technique and want to put it into practice,

source_text: UMA的应该是一个不错的工具。
zh: UMA的应该是一个不错的工具。
en: UMA should be a great tool for that.

source_text: 然后这是第一块，是Create to Learn，然后第二块我觉得也很重要，因为纯粹乐，就是学习和创作，
zh: 然后这是第一块，是Create to Learn，然后第二块我觉得也很重要，因为纯粹乐，就是学习和创作，
en: So that’s the first area: Create to Learn. The second is also important, because learning and creating can simply be fun.

source_text: 创作和学习，如果不能正循环也不行。
zh: 创作和学习，如果不能正循环也不行。
en: Creating and learning need to reinforce each other in a positive cycle.

source_text: 如果在这种情况下，
zh: 如果在这种情况下，
en: If that’s the case,

source_text: 还可以那Create to Learn，就就然后这个乐，当然包括去变现，通过就是各种方式去接商单，成为那自媒体，然后这是一种乐。
zh: 还可以那Create to Learn，就就然后这个乐，当然包括去变现，通过就是各种方式去接商单，成为那自媒体，然后这是一种乐。
en: There’s also Create to Learn, where the fun can include making money—taking on brand deals through different channels and becoming a content creator. That’s one kind of reward.

source_text: 然后这个乐的话，
zh: 然后这个乐的话，
en: And as for the fun part,

source_text: 我觉得去迎娶，通过AI工具去迎娶你内心的一个喜悦和成长，也是一种非常重要的，一个乐。

source_text: 是需要经过刻意练习的。

zh: 这几万小时在AI时代，通过AI工具，可以把这个刻意练习的10万小时可以急剧的加剧，
en: In the age of AI, AI tools can dramatically speed up the tens of thousands of hours of deliberate practice it takes to develop a skill.

source_text: 可以迅速让你之前没有做过拍过影视，那个没有做过那个音乐，通过AI你是可以快速去那加快这个进程。

en: Even if you’ve never made a film or created music before, AI can help you learn and progress much faster.

source_text: 对，哎，

en: Right, yeah.

zh: 然后你再产出的话，你就可以不断的去跟他去做交流，把这个PPT不断按照你的想法去做出你想要的样子，

source_text: 然后整个PPT做完的过程，其实既是做PPT，更多其实是也是我自己的一个思路的那梳理，是一种那个学习和成长，是那这一块。

en: So making the slides wasn’t just about creating a deck. More importantly, it helped me organize my thoughts. It was a process of learning and growth for me.

source_text: 还挺有意思的，就是并且就每一轮那个下来之后，就他都会那更加懂我，因为把记忆和偏好在每一轮那交互里面，其实在UMA里面都沉下来了，
zh: 还挺有意思的，就是并且就每一轮那个下来之后，就他都会那更加懂我，因为把记忆和偏好在每一轮那交互里面，其实在UMA里面都沉下来了，

source_text: 就比如说像因为这这个PPT改的比较多，他第一版的时候，他其实PPT里面有带那个页脚，因为目前这个是那个图图片法，

zh: 然后然后更好玩的就是，在这个PPT里面，关于UMA的理解，其实他是把我过往一年多跟他的那个交互，那所有的一些资料，一些记忆，
en: And what’s even more interesting is that, for the part of the presentation about UMA, it drew on all the materials and memories from more than a year of our interactions.

source_text: 他都记住了，就他可能比我还懂那个UMA的，但他懂的是UMA的过去和当下，但是我知道的是UMA的未来，
zh: 他都记住了，就他可能比我还懂那个UMA的，但他懂的是UMA的过去和当下，但是我知道的是UMA的未来，
en: It remembered all of that. It may even understand UMA better than I do—but it understands UMA’s past and present, while I know where UMA is headed.

source_text: 所以我跟他就会形成一种很好的那互补关系，就我会告诉他UMA的应该去往何方，然后他知道UMA的之前那经历过什么，所以他就会和我一起去把这个Slides给做出来。
