en: So we complement each other really well. I tell it where UMA should go, and it knows what UMA has been through. Together, we create the slides.

source_text: OK，对，那这个也是是我们自己也是UMA的很多客户，非常常见的那四个阶段，因为UMA的做创作就写文章，做图片，做PPT，
zh: OK，对，那这个也是是我们自己也是UMA的很多客户，非常常见的那四个阶段，因为UMA的做创作就写文章，做图片，做PPT，
en: Right. These are also four stages we see very often with UMA users. They use UMA to create content—writing articles, making images, and putting together presentations.

source_text: 做视频，基本上都会经历过这四个阶段。
zh: 做视频，基本上都会经历过这四个阶段。
en: And making videos. They generally go through all four of these stages.

source_text: 第一个阶段就是跟用那个豆包一样，就是直接跟他说，说完之后然后这个这个Agent会给你一段一段那输出，然后这种情况下，

en: The first stage is like using Doubao: you tell it what you want, and the agent gives you a response in chunks. In that case,

zh: 其实我觉得所有Agent都差不多，而且他的核心差异是来自于那模型跟产品本身是关系不大的，这这是直接写的阶段，
en: I think all agents are pretty similar at this stage. The main difference comes from the underlying model, not so much the product itself. This is the direct-writing stage.

source_text: 然后第二个阶段就会稍微往前一步，就是你会带着你的一些私有化资料给他，
zh: 然后第二个阶段就会稍微往前一步，就是你会带着你的一些私有化资料给他，
en: The second stage takes it a step further: you give it some of your own private materials to work with.

source_text: 你把一些文件，你的一些一些日记，你平时的琐事所想，平时的那录音，然后都给到他之后的话，然后在第二个阶段，

en: You give it files, journal entries, everyday thoughts, and recordings. Once it has all that, you move into the second stage.

source_text: 你就已已经是可以他帮你干活了，就能写周报之类的。
zh: 你就已已经是可以他帮你干活了，就能写周报之类的。
en: At that point, it can start doing work for you, like writing your weekly reports.

source_text: 对，但这个还谈不上创作，是属于那第二阶段。
zh: 对，但这个还谈不上创作，是属于那第二阶段。
en: Right, but I wouldn’t call that creating yet. It’s still the second stage.

source_text: 第三阶段的话，其实就是你可以把你的一些一些东西，
zh: 第三阶段的话，其实就是你可以把你的一些一些东西，

en: For example, if you make a certain type of PowerPoint deck, you can turn the process into a reusable skill. Then that skill…

source_text: 他他就会不断去减少你的一些那个日常的一些事情，
zh: 他他就会不断去减少你的一些那个日常的一些事情，
en: It’ll keep taking more of your routine tasks off your plate.

source_text: 然后就往前做。
zh: 然后就往前做。
en: And then you keep building on it.

source_text: 然后最后的话，甚至目前你可以把PPT一键那个转成视频，你就可以实现，就那一鱼多吃，
zh: 然后最后的话，甚至目前你可以把PPT一键那个转成视频，你就可以实现，就那一鱼多吃，
en: And ultimately, you can even turn a PowerPoint deck into a video with one click, getting multiple uses out of the same content.

source_text: 就是让很多情况下可以尝试那个不一样的一些那个事情。
zh: 就是让很多情况下可以尝试那个不一样的一些那个事情。
en: That lets you try different things in a lot of situations.

source_text: 对，
zh: 对，
en: Right.

en: …finding traffic, and all sorts of other things. But really, they’re all trying to take hassles off your plate and make it easier to pursue what you want.

source_text: 但是但这都是向外求的，然后回到向内求的话，我觉得是我们我们希望学会一种新的能力，我们学会想心中有有的某件事情想做的更好，

en: But all of that is about looking outward. If we turn inward, I think what we really want is to develop a new ability: to take something we care about and learn to do it better.

source_text: 在这个层面上，我觉得是UMA的如果有向内求的一些欲望，可以尝试下那UMA的。
zh: 在这个层面上，我觉得是UMA的如果有向内求的一些欲望，可以尝试下那UMA的。
en: In that sense, if you’re interested in looking inward, I think UMA is worth trying.

source_text: 对，然后还有一个也是我觉得也是跟少数朋友有提到过的，就是目前这个时代很多时候做产品都要想到谈谈成吃，

en: Right. And there’s one more thing I’ve mentioned to a few friends: these days, when you build a product, you often have to think about making it “Tantan-style”—bite-sized and easy to consume.

source_text: 那很多都把人性往往都就是让人放弃选择权的方式，让人更贪更撑更吃的方式去走。
zh: 那很多都把人性往往都就是让人放弃选择权的方式，让人更贪更撑更吃的方式去走。
en: A lot of products appeal to human nature by nudging people to give up control and keep consuming more and more.

zh: 但是我觉得这个时代可能更有意思的事情，借助模型，借助那Person Agent是有机会让每个用户更加有那界定会，
en: But I think what’s more interesting now is that, with AI models and personal agents, we may have a chance to give every user more agency.

source_text: 其实界的话就是取舍，你知道那不做什么，这是非非常非常重要，生业了是不是不应该再刷手机了，然后定的话就让你培养那个专注度，
zh: 其实界的话就是取舍，你知道那不做什么，这是非非常非常重要，生业了是不是不应该再刷手机了，然后定的话就让你培养那个专注度，
en: “Jie” is about making choices—knowing what not to do. That’s incredibly important: should you stop scrolling on your phone? And “ding” is about developing your ability to focus.

source_text: 能够让你更专注的，能够把这事情给完成。
zh: 能够让你更专注的，能够把这事情给完成。
en: It helps you stay focused and get the job done.

source_text: 那会的话就是更加懂得怎么去选择。
zh: 那会的话就是更加懂得怎么去选择。
en: And “hui” is about knowing how to make better choices.

source_text: OK，然后最后一页其实我觉得就是UMA的一个地位吧，就是可能今天是那Person Agent的一个场，
zh: OK，然后最后一页其实我觉得就是UMA的一个地位吧，就是可能今天是那Person Agent的一个场，
en: Okay, and the last slide is really about where UMA fits in. Today, we may be at the dawn of the personal agent era.

source_text: 但是确实我觉得Person Agent可能交给那大层面去玩吧，那是对于创业者来说，也许做一个跟环境相关的，
zh: 但是确实我觉得Person Agent可能交给那大层面去玩吧，那是对于创业者来说，也许做一个跟环境相关的，
en: But honestly, I think personal agents may be something for the big players to tackle. For entrepreneurs, perhaps the opportunity is to build something that works with the user’s environment.

en: A person responds to their environment; the user is a product of their environment.

source_text: 今天主要分享其实是来自一些内部的实践，然后也可以给大家讲一讲我的一些心得体会啊，在公司做了大概可能做了三年吧，
zh: 今天主要分享其实是来自一些内部的实践，然后也可以给大家讲一讲我的一些心得体会啊，在公司做了大概可能做了三年吧，
en: Today, I’ll share some of what we’ve learned from our internal work, along with a few personal takeaways from my roughly three years at the company.

source_text: 然后主要的话也是从给律师服务到给内部用户服务，然后最后的学习的经验可能最后还是会回归到我们的客户。
zh: 然后主要的话也是从给律师服务到给内部用户服务，然后最后的学习的经验可能最后还是会回归到我们的客户。
en: We’ve gone from building for lawyers to building for our internal teams, and ultimately, what we learn will feed back into the products we offer our clients.

source_text: 啊，其实非常同意刚才啊，就是啊的那个观点，就是创作是一个很好的一种方式去学习，包括去啊输出你的一些东西，
zh: 啊，其实非常同意刚才啊，就是啊的那个观点，就是创作是一个很好的一种方式去学习，包括去啊输出你的一些东西，
en: I really agree with the point made earlier: creating is a great way to learn and to share what you know.

source_text: 然后用AI去进行创作的话，其实是更好去让你把自己的想法能够啊，就是表达出来。
zh: 然后用AI去进行创作的话，其实是更好去让你把自己的想法能够啊，就是表达出来。
en: And using AI to create makes it even easier to express your ideas.

source_text: 像我今天做这个创作也是因为AIE这个契机，然后可能从比如说啊，大概20多天前，然后开始去研究我到底要做一个什么样的演讲，
zh: 像我今天做这个创作也是因为AIE这个契机，然后可能从比如说啊，大概20多天前，然后开始去研究我到底要做一个什么样的演讲，
en: This talk is an example. AIE gave me the opportunity to create something, so about 20 days ago, I started thinking about what kind of presentation I wanted to give.

source_text: 然后就开始跟Agent一起去做一些做一些experiment，所以说今天最后的这些结果我也会给大家讲一讲，
zh: 然后就开始跟Agent一起去做一些做一些experiment，所以说今天最后的这些结果我也会给大家讲一讲，
en: Then I started running some experiments with an agent, and I’ll share the results with you today.

source_text: 我花了多长时间，花了多少钱，然后甚至能为公司省多少钱，然后也给大家啊有一些呃小的一些祈祷。
zh: 我花了多长时间，花了多少钱，然后甚至能为公司省多少钱，然后也给大家啊有一些呃小的一些祈祷。
en: I’ll tell you how much time and money I spent, how much it could save the company, and share a few tips along the way.

source_text: 怎么说，启发。
zh: 怎么说，启发。
en: How should I put it—some insights.

source_text: 对，然后我看看，
zh: 对，然后我看看，
en: Right, let me see.

source_text: OK，啊，先来说Harvey什么。
zh: OK，啊，先来说Harvey什么。
en: Okay, first, let’s talk about what Harvey is.

source_text: Harvey的话，我们主要是给法律做，就是AI的，然后啊，
zh: Harvey的话，我们主要是给法律做，就是AI的，然后啊，
en: Harvey mainly builds AI for the legal industry, and…

source_text: 现在的话其实我们对于一个法律AI的一个想法就是说Agent其实是可以直接在一个案件分析里面展开工作，
zh: 现在的话其实我们对于一个法律AI的一个想法就是说Agent其实是可以直接在一个案件分析里面展开工作，
en: Right now, our vision for legal AI is that an agent can work directly on a case analysis.

source_text: 他可以带着所有的这些contacts啊，然后我们也针对其实所有的法律的一些场景做过一些benchmark，
zh: 他可以带着所有的这些contacts啊，然后我们也针对其实所有的法律的一些场景做过一些benchmark，
en: It can work with all the relevant context, and we’ve also benchmarked it across a range of legal tasks.

source_text: 就是说做一些评测集，然后从比如说24年的时候，我们就开始做叫做Big Law Bench，甚至到今年的话，我们可能做了Legal Agent Bench，
zh: 就是说做一些评测集，然后从比如说24年的时候，我们就开始做叫做Big Law Bench，甚至到今年的话，我们可能做了Legal Agent Bench，
en: We’ve created evaluation datasets. We started with Big Law Bench in 2024, and this year we developed Legal Agent Bench.

source_text: 它它主要解决的是这些啊非常长时间运行的一些Agent。
zh: 它它主要解决的是这些啊非常长时间运行的一些Agent。
en: It’s mainly designed for agents that run for extended periods.

source_text: 那我们也进行了一些，比如说open weight model的一些post training，
zh: 那我们也进行了一些，比如说open weight model的一些post training，
en: We’ve also done some post-training on open-weight models.

source_text: 包括像GLM啊或者Kimi K3这些。
zh: 包括像GLM啊或者Kimi K3这些。
en: Including models like GLM and Kimi K3.

source_text: 那我们在做外部这些training的时候，呃，
zh: 那我们在做外部这些training的时候，呃，
en: And when we were doing this training on external models, uh…

source_text: 我们也相当于用了这些open weight model，然后做了一些内部的尝试。
zh: 我们也相当于用了这些open weight model，然后做了一些内部的尝试。
en: We also used these open-weight models for some internal experiments.

source_text: 那我们今天主要就是讲的几个啊具体的案例，然后在我们这个内部的尝试里面，我都学到了些什么东西啊。
zh: 那我们今天主要就是讲的几个啊具体的案例，然后在我们这个内部的尝试里面，我都学到了些什么东西啊。
en: Today, I’ll walk through a few specific examples and share what I learned from our internal experiments.

source_text: 首先我今年做的一个项目叫做Specter，它是Harvey内部的一个Agent，那为什么我们要做一个内部的Agent呢，
zh: 首先我今年做的一个项目叫做Specter，它是Harvey内部的一个Agent，那为什么我们要做一个内部的Agent呢，
en: First, I want to talk about a project I worked on this year called Specter. It’s an internal agent at Harvey. So why did we build an internal agent?

source_text: 其实可能从今年早期大家会发现Coding Agent harness都变得非常厉害，但是我觉得有两个事情我一直都没有看到别人去解决，
zh: 其实可能从今年早期大家会发现Coding Agent harness都变得非常厉害，但是我觉得有两个事情我一直都没有看到别人去解决，
en: Earlier this year, coding agent harnesses became remarkably capable. But there were two problems I still hadn’t seen anyone solve.

source_text: 然后自己做一个东西其实cost变得非常低的情况下，那我就开始在内部着手做两件事情。
zh: 然后自己做一个东西其实cost变得非常低的情况下，那我就开始在内部着手做两件事情。
en: And with the cost of building something yourself getting so low, I started working on two things internally.

source_text: 第一个就是大家可以都在Slack，就Slack是大家协作的工具，然后去进行多人和一个Agent的协作，
zh: 第一个就是大家可以都在Slack，就Slack是大家协作的工具，然后去进行多人和一个Agent的协作，
en: First, I wanted people to be able to collaborate with an agent together in Slack, the tool we already use to work with each other.

source_text: 因为传统意义上所有人都会拿Agent去做一些事，然后最后你把一个PPT或者PR交给你的同事的时候，
zh: 因为传统意义上所有人都会拿Agent去做一些事，然后最后你把一个PPT或者PR交给你的同事的时候，
en: Traditionally, you’d have an agent do some work, then hand your colleague the finished slide deck or pull request.

source_text: 同事拿到的东西是一个最后一个缩影，它并不知道所有的，比如说这个Agent背后的故事。
zh: 同事拿到的东西是一个最后一个缩影，它并不知道所有的，比如说这个Agent背后的故事。
en: What your colleague gets is just the final snapshot. They don’t see the full story of how the agent got there.

source_text: 然后我希望的呢，其实是大家都能够把啊Agent就是所有的这些contacts一起在我们的讨论中。
zh: 然后我希望的呢，其实是大家都能够把啊Agent就是所有的这些contacts一起在我们的讨论中。
en: What I wanted was for everyone to have all the context from the agent right there in our discussion.

source_text: 于是多个人可以跟一个Agent协作完之后，这Agent的结果是所有人都各可以同意的啊，
zh: 于是多个人可以跟一个Agent协作完之后，这Agent的结果是所有人都各可以同意的啊，
en: That way, multiple people can work with one agent and agree on the outcome.

source_text: 所以说大家可以在Slack啊网页啊手机啊，或者说身呃做一些自动化，然后让这些呃活就把它做完了。
zh: 所以说大家可以在Slack啊网页啊手机啊，或者说身呃做一些自动化，然后让这些呃活就把它做完了。
en: So people could use it in Slack, on the web, or on their phones—or set up automations to get the work done.

source_text: 那我们最后这个产品呢，基本上现在公司可能有个啊就500多人都在非常actually用，然后也是产生了大概上万个PR啊，
zh: 那我们最后这个产品呢，基本上现在公司可能有个啊就500多人都在非常actually用，然后也是产生了大概上万个PR啊，
en: Today, more than 500 people at the company actively use the product, and it’s helped produce around ten thousand pull requests.

source_text: 我们也通过根据这些上万个PR得到的一些结果啊，成为了我们现在可以用的评测集。
zh: 我们也通过根据这些上万个PR得到的一些结果啊，成为了我们现在可以用的评测集。
en: We also used the outcomes of those tens of thousands of pull requests to build the evaluation dataset we use today.

source_text: 那传统意义上一个PR是怎么经过，就是说一个流程呢，
zh: 那传统意义上一个PR是怎么经过，就是说一个流程呢，
en: So what does the traditional workflow for a pull request look like?

source_text: 就是说大家可以在Slack里面啊开始说，哎，我要做这个事，或者说一个啊PM他有一个产品的需求，可能是从客户那边来的，
zh: 就是说大家可以在Slack里面啊开始说，哎，我要做这个事，或者说一个啊PM他有一个产品的需求，可能是从客户那边来的，
en: Someone might start in Slack by saying, “Hey, I want to get this done,” or a product manager might bring in a product request from a customer.

source_text: 我们就可以把这个Agent从啊最终的成啊最初的产品设计，到啊最后的比如说engineering的交付，甚至到我们的测试迭代，
zh: 我们就可以把这个Agent从啊最终的成啊最初的产品设计，到啊最后的比如说engineering的交付，甚至到我们的测试迭代，
en: We can use the agent throughout the whole process, from the initial product design to the final engineering delivery and even testing and iteration.

source_text: 然后上线，可能都可以直接从Slack里开始啊。
zh: 然后上线，可能都可以直接从Slack里开始啊。
en: And even launch it—all starting right from Slack.

source_text: 但是一个PR它并不是一个我们最后结结束的地方啊，我们其实也需要可能一直去修那个CI，
zh: 但是一个PR它并不是一个我们最后结结束的地方啊，我们其实也需要可能一直去修那个CI，
en: But a pull request isn’t the end of the process. We may need to keep fixing the CI checks.

source_text: CI就是continuous integration，就是说我们可能会需要run一些test，
zh: CI就是continuous integration，就是说我们可能会需要run一些test，
en: CI stands for continuous integration, which means we may need to run some tests.

source_text: 然后知道说这个PR究竟是给整个产品是带来一个正向的东西，还是说它会有一些呃就带来一些错误的东西。
zh: 然后知道说这个PR究竟是给整个产品是带来一个正向的东西，还是说它会有一些呃就带来一些错误的东西。
en: Then we need to determine whether the PR improves the product overall or introduces any bugs.

source_text: 那其实这个的话，我们都是呃现在很非常自动化，然后因为harness和模型都是相当于你的可以替换，
zh: 那其实这个的话，我们都是呃现在很非常自动化，然后因为harness和模型都是相当于你的可以替换，
en: We’ve now automated much of this, and both the harness and the model are interchangeable.

source_text: 所以说从一个task最开始到最结束，呃我们这个固定的流程其实都是可以重放的。
zh: 所以说从一个task最开始到最结束，呃我们这个固定的流程其实都是可以重放的。
en: So from the beginning of a task to the very end, we can replay the entire workflow.

source_text: 那这个固定流程就变成了我们相当于的一个evaluation的case，就是我们可以用它作为一个评测集。
zh: 那这个固定流程就变成了我们相当于的一个evaluation的case，就是我们可以用它作为一个评测集。
en: So this standardized workflow becomes an evaluation case that we can use as part of a benchmark.

source_text: 对，这是我刚才讲的，就是说从一个本地的Agent到一个啊在云端的Agent，它可能会有一些区别。
zh: 对，这是我刚才讲的，就是说从一个本地的Agent到一个啊在云端的Agent，它可能会有一些区别。
en: Right, that’s what I was saying earlier: there may be some differences between an agent running locally and one running in the cloud.

source_text: 那我们真正的工作呢，其实都是呃在比如说Slack啊GitHub Linear上面做，然后我们可能也会想说，
zh: 那我们真正的工作呢，其实都是呃在比如说Slack啊GitHub Linear上面做，然后我们可能也会想说，
en: Most of our actual work happens in tools like Slack, GitHub, and Linear, so we might also think about…

source_text: 如果说我们把这个Agent沙箱带到我们呃这个工作运行的环境里，怎么能够更好的去让这个Agent运行。
zh: 如果说我们把这个Agent沙箱带到我们呃这个工作运行的环境里，怎么能够更好的去让这个Agent运行。
en: If we bring the agent sandbox into the environment where we actually work, how can we make the agent run more effectively?

source_text: 于是另外的一个side effect，就是说当我们有了这个本呃云端的Agent之后，
zh: 于是另外的一个side effect，就是说当我们有了这个本呃云端的Agent之后，
en: Another side effect of having a cloud-based agent is that…

source_text: 我们其实也用了拥有了各更多的评测集啊，本身大家可能在本地跑的这些Agent，最后这些啊Agent的contacts啊thinking traces啊，
zh: 我们其实也用了拥有了各更多的评测集啊，本身大家可能在本地跑的这些Agent，最后这些啊Agent的contacts啊thinking traces啊，
en: We also end up with more evaluation data. For agents people run locally, we can capture their context and reasoning traces…

source_text: 都不见了。
zh: 都不见了。
en: …would otherwise be lost.

source_text: 但是如果说我们一旦有了这么一个Agent，大家都可以去协作的情况下，这就成了一个我们可以在啊线上去收集的一些数据，并且是内部数据，我们可以更好去做一些实验。
zh: 但是如果说我们一旦有了这么一个Agent，大家都可以去协作的情况下，这就成了一个我们可以在啊线上去收集的一些数据，并且是内部数据，我们可以更好去做一些实验。
en: But once we have an agent everyone can collaborate on, we can collect that data online. And because it’s internal data, we can use it to run better experiments.

source_text: 当然现在其实我们做了这么多个月之后，会面临一些新的问题，比如说第一个问题是新的模型没几周都会发布一个，
zh: 当然现在其实我们做了这么多个月之后，会面临一些新的问题，比如说第一个问题是新的模型没几周都会发布一个，
en: Of course, after working on this for several months, we’re facing some new challenges. For one thing, a new model comes out every few weeks.

source_text: 那你到底是上这些新的模型呢，还是说你要测一遍呢，还是说相信这些公开的benchmark呢？
zh: 那你到底是上这些新的模型呢，还是说你要测一遍呢，还是说相信这些公开的benchmark呢？
en: So do you adopt each new model, test it yourself, or trust the public benchmarks?

source_text: 这其实是一个呃大家可能会花越来越多时间去思考的，就是比如说我们现在新的，比如说DeepSeek啊或者千万都有新模型出来了，
zh: 这其实是一个呃大家可能会花越来越多时间去思考的，就是比如说我们现在新的，比如说DeepSeek啊或者千万都有新模型出来了，
en: This is something we’ll probably spend more and more time thinking about. For example, new models are coming out from DeepSeek and Qwen.

source_text: 我是不是应该马上去上呢，还是说应该等一等呢，还是说应该自己做评测呢，该怎么做呢？
zh: 我是不是应该马上去上呢，还是说应该等一等呢，还是说应该自己做评测呢，该怎么做呢？
en: Should I adopt them right away, wait a bit, or run my own evaluations? What’s the best approach?

source_text: 这可能是我今天想之后讲的啊。
zh: 这可能是我今天想之后讲的啊。
en: That’s something I’d like to talk about later today.

source_text: 第二个呢，就是如果说你运行在云上面，它可能会有很多的时间上的感知，其实是会比较呃就是难以去就是减少的，
zh: 第二个呢，就是如果说你运行在云上面，它可能会有很多的时间上的感知，其实是会比较呃就是难以去就是减少的，
en: Second, if you’re running it in the cloud, there can be a lot of latency that’s hard to reduce.

source_text: 因为你在本地的Agent运行很快，那我们怎么样去啊提升这个速度？
zh: 因为你在本地的Agent运行很快，那我们怎么样去啊提升这个速度？
en: A local agent runs much faster, so how can we improve the speed of the cloud-based one?

source_text: 那其实可能换一个更快的模型，是不是一个更好的方式呢？
zh: 那其实可能换一个更快的模型，是不是一个更好的方式呢？
en: Would switching to a faster model be a better approach?

source_text: 这也是一个问题啊。
zh: 这也是一个问题啊。
en: That’s another question.

source_text: 第三个的话，就是因为我们现在每个人都有更多的output，所以review就是说审核这个PR也变成了瓶颈，
zh: 第三个的话，就是因为我们现在每个人都有更多的output，所以review就是说审核这个PR也变成了瓶颈，
en: Third, now that everyone is producing more output, reviewing pull requests has become a bottleneck.

source_text: 那大家渐渐的就会用Agent去审核PR。
zh: 那大家渐渐的就会用Agent去审核PR。
en: So people will gradually start using agents to review pull requests.

source_text: 那用什么样的模型harness或者说prompt去审核PR呢？
zh: 那用什么样的模型harness或者说prompt去审核PR呢？
en: What model, harness, or prompt should we use to review pull requests?

source_text: 也是我们最近在研究的一个问题。
zh: 也是我们最近在研究的一个问题。
en: That’s another question we’ve been looking into recently.

source_text: 然后最后的话，呃最后最后是什么来着？
zh: 然后最后的话，呃最后最后是什么来着？
en: And finally—uh, what was the last point again?

source_text: 哦，OK，好像差不多就这些。
zh: 哦，OK，好像差不多就这些。
en: Oh, okay. I think that’s pretty much it.

source_text: 哦，cost，对，cost也是一个呃大家可能会思考说，哎，我用越来越多的Agent花这些cost，
zh: 哦，cost，对，cost也是一个呃大家可能会思考说，哎，我用越来越多的Agent花这些cost，
en: Oh, cost—right. Cost is another thing people might think about: as I use more and more agents, the costs add up...

source_text: 究竟能不能达到我的效果啊？
zh: 究竟能不能达到我的效果啊？
en: Will they actually deliver the results I’m looking for?

source_text: 是不是应该换一个模型？
zh: 是不是应该换一个模型？
en: Should I switch to a different model?

source_text: 这也就是为什么我会做这个实验的初衷。
zh: 这也就是为什么我会做这个实验的初衷。
en: That’s exactly why I started this experiment.

source_text: 其中第一个事情就是别人的leaderboard，或者说别人的这个benchmark，
zh: 其中第一个事情就是别人的leaderboard，或者说别人的这个benchmark，
en: The first thing is someone else’s leaderboard—or, rather, someone else’s benchmark.

source_text: 并不一定真的是你在自己做这个工作的时候能够去直接切换的。
zh: 并不一定真的是你在自己做这个工作的时候能够去直接切换的。
en: It doesn’t necessarily mean you can just switch models when you’re doing the work yourself.

source_text: 比如说他用的Ripple和我们这么多年自己搭建的这个，比如说整个contacts是不一样的。
zh: 比如说他用的Ripple和我们这么多年自己搭建的这个，比如说整个contacts是不一样的。
en: For example, the Ripple setup they use is different from the one we’ve built over the years—our whole context is different.

source_text: 比如说我们的这个Agent也不一样啊，harness也不一样，甚至是我们的呃比如说可能真正做的事情，
zh: 比如说我们的这个Agent也不一样啊，harness也不一样，甚至是我们的呃比如说可能真正做的事情，
en: Our agents are different, for example, and so is the harness. Even the actual tasks we’re doing may be different...

source_text: 很多时候你有一大半事情并不是说你是生成代码，而是说你怎么样让这个代码能够达到呃产品上线的这个quality。
zh: 很多时候你有一大半事情并不是说你是生成代码，而是说你怎么样让这个代码能够达到呃产品上线的这个quality。
en: A lot of the time, more than half the work isn’t generating code—it’s getting that code to production quality.

source_text: 那我们用Agent去解决这个过程中，其实有很多的任务是非常的固定的，比如说像是review这个代码，或者像是fix这个CI，
zh: 那我们用Agent去解决这个过程中，其实有很多的任务是非常的固定的，比如说像是review这个代码，或者像是fix这个CI，
en: When we use agents for this process, a lot of the tasks are quite routine, like reviewing code or fixing CI failures.

source_text: 或者甚至是小到我从一个代码成为一个PR，
zh: 或者甚至是小到我从一个代码成为一个PR，
en: Or even something as small as turning a code change into a PR.

source_text: 然后我要在它的比如说PR description，就是说是那个呃具体你这个PR做了什么事情，为什么做这个事情，
zh: 然后我要在它的比如说PR description，就是说是那个呃具体你这个PR做了什么事情，为什么做这个事情，
en: Then, in the PR description, I need to explain exactly what the PR does and why.

source_text: 你有测什么东西，这东西其实都是人与人之间交互的一个桥梁。
zh: 你有测什么东西，这东西其实都是人与人之间交互的一个桥梁。
en: What you tested and things like that—they’re all ways for people to communicate with each other.

source_text: 我们怎么样把这个桥梁能够搭的更好，也是能够促进这个组织架构生长一个很重要的地方。
zh: 我们怎么样把这个桥梁能够搭的更好，也是能够促进这个组织架构生长一个很重要的地方。
en: How we build that bridge more effectively is also an important part of helping the organization grow.

source_text: 如果说所有人的PR都只有一句话去解释，大家并不理解这个PR在干什么的话，呃其实是会一个就是增加review时间的过程。
zh: 如果说所有人的PR都只有一句话去解释，大家并不理解这个PR在干什么的话，呃其实是会一个就是增加review时间的过程。
en: If everyone’s PR description is just one sentence, reviewers won’t understand what the PR does, and reviews will take longer.

source_text: 所以我们希望是能够做得很好。
zh: 所以我们希望是能够做得很好。
en: So we want to do this well.

source_text: 那么像我刚才讲的，就是说我们怎么样能够把这个流程分成这么多步，然后通过一个replay的方式，
zh: 那么像我刚才讲的，就是说我们怎么样能够把这个流程分成这么多步，然后通过一个replay的方式，
en: So, as I mentioned, how can we break this process down into steps and then use a replay approach?

source_text: 然后通过一个呃LMS chart去进行它的评分，然后最后的话，我们就可以就是评判出来我们到底是改模型、改harness，
zh: 然后通过一个呃LMS chart去进行它的评分，然后最后的话，我们就可以就是评判出来我们到底是改模型、改harness，
en: Then we can score it using an LMS chart and, ultimately, determine whether we need to change the model or the harness.

source_text: 还是呃改其他东西啊。
zh: 还是呃改其他东西啊。
en: Or change something else.

source_text: 那我现在剧透一下，其实最后我们发现模型和harness都不是真的要改的东西，而是很多时候你一旦开始做了评测，
zh: 那我现在剧透一下，其实最后我们发现模型和harness都不是真的要改的东西，而是很多时候你一旦开始做了评测，
en: A little spoiler: we ultimately found that neither the model nor the harness was what really needed changing. Often, once you start evaluating,

source_text: 你就会发现其实你代码中本身很有很多东西是可以改的，你这个流程上是可以改的，甚至是因为我做了这个slides，
zh: 你就会发现其实你代码中本身很有很多东西是可以改的，你这个流程上是可以改的，甚至是因为我做了这个slides，
en: You realize there’s actually a lot you can improve in your code and your workflow. Even making these slides helped me see that.

source_text: 或者说我今天要讲这个东西，然后我去做这个实验的时候，发现有很多low hanging fruit，就是说呃很容易就做到的事情，
zh: 或者说我今天要讲这个东西，然后我去做这个实验的时候，发现有很多low hanging fruit，就是说呃很容易就做到的事情，
en: When I was preparing this talk and running the experiment, I found a lot of low-hanging fruit—things that were easy to improve.

source_text: 然后结果最后就有很多的效果。
zh: 然后结果最后就有很多的效果。
en: And those small changes ended up making a big difference.

source_text: 所以说当你试了之后，你才会发现啊，你可能真的不需要训一个模型就可以做到很好的这个效果。
zh: 所以说当你试了之后，你才会发现啊，你可能真的不需要训一个模型就可以做到很好的这个效果。
en: So once you try it, you may find that you can get great results without training a model at all.

source_text: 然后每次的话，你也就是只需要呃固定的，这个是做实验的一种方式啊，就很很常见，
zh: 然后每次的话，你也就是只需要呃固定的，这个是做实验的一种方式啊，就很很常见，
en: And each time, you just need to keep certain things constant. It’s a very common way to run experiments.

source_text: 就是你只需要改一个变量，你就可以确定是说你是要改harness呢，还是模型呢，还是改其他东西。
zh: 就是你只需要改一个变量，你就可以确定是说你是要改harness呢，还是模型呢，还是改其他东西。
en: You only need to change one variable at a time to figure out whether you should adjust the harness, the model, or something else.

source_text: 然后三个例子，我刚才其实讲过了呃几个，第一个是PR的description，
zh: 然后三个例子，我刚才其实讲过了呃几个，第一个是PR的description，
en: Now for three examples. I’ve already mentioned a few—the first is the PR description.

source_text: 就是具体的描述；第二个是怎么样审核代码；第三个是怎么样fix修复我们的CI；然后第一个例子就比较小，呃我快速的带过，就是这个PR呢，
zh: 就是具体的描述；第二个是怎么样审核代码；第三个是怎么样fix修复我们的CI；然后第一个例子就比较小，呃我快速的带过，就是这个PR呢，
en: The first is writing a detailed PR description; the second is reviewing code; and the third is fixing our CI. I’ll go through the first example quickly—it’s a small one. This PR...

source_text: 我们其实会呃真的给别人看的时候，会有一个人类的描述和一个Agent生成的一些描述。
zh: 我们其实会呃真的给别人看的时候，会有一个人类的描述和一个Agent生成的一些描述。
en: When we actually show a PR to other people, it includes a human-written description and some text generated by an agent.

source_text: 那么我们有一个呃语言模型去专门做一个PR生成描述的一个工作流。
zh: 那么我们有一个呃语言模型去专门做一个PR生成描述的一个工作流。
en: So we have a workflow where a language model generates PR descriptions.

source_text: 为什么呢？
zh: 为什么呢？
en: Why is that?

source_text: 因为你的PR可能一直在变，你可能今天让Agent做了A，明天让Agent做了B，你可能说我们都放到一个PR，它可能一直在变，
zh: 因为你的PR可能一直在变，你可能今天让Agent做了A，明天让Agent做了B，你可能说我们都放到一个PR，它可能一直在变，
en: Because a PR can keep changing. You might have the agent do task A today and task B tomorrow, then decide to put both in the same PR. So the PR keeps evolving.

source_text: 我们需要做的事情是人写的那段话要维持，就因为我们希望就说人还是最后有一些judgement。
zh: 我们需要做的事情是人写的那段话要维持，就因为我们希望就说人还是最后有一些judgement。
en: What we need to do is preserve the human-written part, because we still want a person to have the final say.

source_text: 但是Agent能生成的东西呢，是要保持，但是如果说我有一些PR，它比如说测试的结果，我也希望能够放进去，
zh: 但是Agent能生成的东西呢，是要保持，但是如果说我有一些PR，它比如说测试的结果，我也希望能够放进去，
en: But we also want to keep the agent-generated content. And if a PR has, say, test results, I’d like to include those too.

source_text: 结果最后的结呃发现其实我即使换了模型，换了harness，换了真正的这些prompt，也没有什么变化，
zh: 结果最后的结呃发现其实我即使换了模型，换了harness，换了真正的这些prompt，也没有什么变化，
en: In the end, I found that even changing the model, the harness, and the prompts didn’t make much difference.

source_text: 然后很多的问题其实发生在我丢给它的数据的问题，结果发现code里面有很多的小bug，
zh: 然后很多的问题其实发生在我丢给它的数据的问题，结果发现code里面有很多的小bug，
en: A lot of the problems turned out to be with the data I was feeding it. I found quite a few small bugs in the code.

source_text: 比如说当你这个PR的描述太长的时候，你最后给它的东西可能会并不是你真的能够用上的东西，于是它会漏了很多东西。
zh: 比如说当你这个PR的描述太长的时候，你最后给它的东西可能会并不是你真的能够用上的东西，于是它会漏了很多东西。
en: For example, if the PR description is too long, what you end up feeding the model may not be what it actually needs, so it misses a lot of things.

source_text: 所以通过这个测试，我发现只要修一些bug，基本上你不用换任何的模型，或者说是prompt就可以做得非常好。
zh: 所以通过这个测试，我发现只要修一些bug，基本上你不用换任何的模型，或者说是prompt就可以做得非常好。
en: So these tests showed me that, once you fix a few bugs, you can get very good results without changing the model or the prompts.

source_text: 然后第二个例子呢，是code review，呃这个我要讲的其实是说测试本身比测试的结果更重要，
zh: 然后第二个例子呢，是code review，呃这个我要讲的其实是说测试本身比测试的结果更重要，
en: The second example is code review. The point I want to make is that the testing process itself matters more than the results.

source_text: 就是当你发现你测试的数据集，我不知道这个能不能按，就是呃让左边那个视频发一，呃就是叫怎么说，左边那个视频按一下，看能不能动起来。
zh: 就是当你发现你测试的数据集，我不知道这个能不能按，就是呃让左边那个视频发一，呃就是叫怎么说，左边那个视频按一下，看能不能动起来。
en: When you find that your test dataset... I’m not sure if this will work, but could you click the video on the left and see if it plays?

source_text: 对，就是说总的来说，就是我们发现在收集了那么多数据的情况下，真正的能用的并不多，所以说真正能够判断数据好不好用，
zh: 对，就是说总的来说，就是我们发现在收集了那么多数据的情况下，真正的能用的并不多，所以说真正能够判断数据好不好用，
en: Right. Overall, we found that even after collecting all that data, not much of it was actually usable. So the real challenge is figuring out which data is useful.

source_text: 这个过程可能是我跟呃我们这个呃做实验的Agent聊得最多的事情。
zh: 这个过程可能是我跟呃我们这个呃做实验的Agent聊得最多的事情。
en: That process was probably what I discussed most with the agent we used for the experiments.

source_text: 比如说像是一个code review，
zh: 比如说像是一个code review，
en: For example, take a code review.

source_text: 你会发现如果说你要把它重放一遍，呃有可能这个code review本身有另外的人或者说Agent在上面留了更多的code review，
zh: 你会发现如果说你要把它重放一遍，呃有可能这个code review本身有另外的人或者说Agent在上面留了更多的code review，
en: You may find that, when you try to replay it, someone else—or another agent—has already left more review comments on the same code.

source_text: 那你重放的过程中，你这个Agent可能会受到那些后来的signal的影响。
zh: 那你重放的过程中，你这个Agent可能会受到那些后来的signal的影响。
en: So when you replay it, your agent might be influenced by those later signals.

source_text: 那其实它就不是一个很好的case，或者说可能会这个PR的呃就之后会有新的一些呃人教了一些新的这个change，
zh: 那其实它就不是一个很好的case，或者说可能会这个PR的呃就之后会有新的一些呃人教了一些新的这个change，
en: That means it isn’t really a good test case. Or, later on, someone might make new changes to the PR.

source_text: 它也会影响到这个PR。所以说我发现花的更多时间是研究这个评测集该怎么样呃选出来。
zh: 它也会影响到这个PR。所以说我发现花的更多时间是研究这个评测集该怎么样呃选出来。
en: Those changes could also affect the PR. So I found that I spent more time figuring out how to select the evaluation set.

source_text: 然后我们最后的结果就是，如果说当我们保证说一个呃prompt是一个optimal的情况下，
zh: 然后我们最后的结果就是，如果说当我们保证说一个呃prompt是一个optimal的情况下，
en: And our final result was that, assuming the prompt was optimal,

source_text: 并且它的harness是我们比较通用的情况下， 其实在这个情况下，
zh: 并且它的harness是我们比较通用的情况下， 其实在这个情况下，
en: And with a fairly general-purpose harness, in that setup…

source_text: DeepSeek V4呃.1的这个flash都已经能够接近opus的这个效果。
zh: DeepSeek V4呃.1的这个flash都已经能够接近opus的这个效果。
en: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash could already get close to Opus-level performance.

source_text: 然后我们会发现opus max会花非常多的钱，但是它真正能够catch住的东西是有多重要呢？
zh: 然后我们会发现opus max会花非常多的钱，但是它真正能够catch住的东西是有多重要呢？
en: And then we found that Opus Max costs a lot of money—but how important are the issues it actually catches?

source_text: 呃进行了一些人类审查之后，发现其实可能并不重要。
zh: 呃进行了一些人类审查之后，发现其实可能并不重要。
en: After a human review, we found that those issues might not actually be that important.

source_text: 所以说与其说我们用呃opus max不如直接用opus，与其用opus不如直接用DeepSeek的flash，所以说这个结果也是比较出乎我意料的。
zh: 所以说与其说我们用呃opus max不如直接用opus，与其用opus不如直接用DeepSeek的flash，所以说这个结果也是比较出乎我意料的。
en: So rather than using Opus Max, we might as well use Opus—and rather than Opus, we might as well use DeepSeek Flash. That result was pretty surprising to me.

source_text: 然后第三个例子呢，就是刚才说的fix CI，呃这个我可以快速跳过。
zh: 然后第三个例子呢，就是刚才说的fix CI，呃这个我可以快速跳过。
en: The third example is the fix-CI case I mentioned earlier, so I’ll go through it quickly.

source_text: 然后同样的也是说，当我们fix CI，它的结果是非常好确定的，就是说你CI到底是过了还是没过，这个时候如果你把Agent放在那边的话，
zh: 然后同样的也是说，当我们fix CI，它的结果是非常好确定的，就是说你CI到底是过了还是没过，这个时候如果你把Agent放在那边的话，
en: Similarly, when you’re fixing CI, the outcome is very clear: either CI passes or it doesn’t. So if you put an agent on that task,

source_text: 其实质量都差不多，因为他们都会最后把它跑过，对吧？
zh: 其实质量都差不多，因为他们都会最后把它跑过，对吧？
en: The results are pretty much the same, because they all eventually get CI to pass, right?

source_text: 所以它有一个很好的验证，其实是你对于一个Agent harness呃最有最提效最多的地方。
zh: 所以它有一个很好的验证，其实是你对于一个Agent harness呃最有最提效最多的地方。
en: So having a clear way to verify the result is where an agent harness can deliver the biggest efficiency gains.

source_text: 但是可能区别就是在于opus，因为它可能有的时候一变就过，然后但是你其他模型可能需要去不断的反复的尝试，
zh: 但是可能区别就是在于opus，因为它可能有的时候一变就过，然后但是你其他模型可能需要去不断的反复的尝试，
en: But the difference may be that Opus sometimes gets CI to pass with a single change, while other models may need to keep trying.

source_text: 所以它会花很多很多的时间，甚至有可能会浪费你的，比如说你的这个沙盒呃运行的时间，有可能你会需要去共享你的沙盒。
zh: 所以它会花很多很多的时间，甚至有可能会浪费你的，比如说你的这个沙盒呃运行的时间，有可能你会需要去共享你的沙盒。
en: So it can take a lot more time and may even use up valuable sandbox runtime, especially if you have to share the sandbox with others.

source_text: 那么它它究竟是怎么回事呢？
zh: 那么它它究竟是怎么回事呢？
en: So what exactly is going on here?

source_text: 因为我们现在跑在云上，所以说我可以分析它很多的trace，最后会发现其实这些open weight呢，
zh: 因为我们现在跑在云上，所以说我可以分析它很多的trace，最后会发现其实这些open weight呢，
en: Because we’re running this in the cloud, I can analyze a lot of its traces. What I found is that these open-weight models…

source_text: 呃大部分时间都在呃就是思考的更多，它需要可能有更多的这些thinking trace才能解决这个问题，
zh: 呃大部分时间都在呃就是思考的更多，它需要可能有更多的这些thinking trace才能解决这个问题，
en: Most of the time, they’re just thinking more. They may need longer reasoning traces to solve the problem.

source_text: 它有更多的reasoning。
zh: 它有更多的reasoning。
en: They do more reasoning.

source_text: 然后opus呢，可能真的就是属于很快就能得到这个结果，甚至它会呃就是减少它自己对于CI的retry。
zh: 然后opus呢，可能真的就是属于很快就能得到这个结果，甚至它会呃就是减少它自己对于CI的retry。
en: Opus, on the other hand, may get to the result much faster and even need fewer CI retries.

source_text: 然后这个可以略过，这个呢，
zh: 然后这个可以略过，这个呢，
en: We can skip this one. As for this one…

source_text: 呃也可以略过。
zh: 呃也可以略过。
en: Uh, we can skip this one too.

source_text: 然后就讲说呃这个事，就是当我们发现刚才这个结果之后，该做什么事呢？
zh: 然后就讲说呃这个事，就是当我们发现刚才这个结果之后，该做什么事呢？
en: So, after seeing those results, what should we do next?

source_text: 其实不应该直接放弃，应该说怎么样去通过呃刚才结果去hue climb，就是说我们怎么样去真正的去提升这个系统，
zh: 其实不应该直接放弃，应该说怎么样去通过呃刚才结果去hue climb，就是说我们怎么样去真正的去提升这个系统，
en: We shouldn’t just give up. We should use those results to hill-climb—to figure out how to actually improve the system.

source_text: 并且让我们这些open weight的model在你这个使用场景下去能够保证质量的情况下，并且去减少这个时间。
zh: 并且让我们这些open weight的model在你这个使用场景下去能够保证质量的情况下，并且去减少这个时间。
en: And make these open-weight models faster for your use case without compromising quality.

source_text: 那么后来发现其实你可以不需要全部跑这些测试，你可以不用去思考那么多，也可以得到这个结果。
zh: 那么后来发现其实你可以不需要全部跑这些测试，你可以不用去思考那么多，也可以得到这个结果。
en: Then we realized you don’t need to run all those tests or spend so much time reasoning to get the same result.

source_text: 最后最后就是法律，其实我们做benchmark的思路和我们最后代码做benchmark的思路都很像，
zh: 最后最后就是法律，其实我们做benchmark的思路和我们最后代码做benchmark的思路都很像，
en: And finally, the legal side. Our approach to benchmarking was actually very similar to how we benchmarked the final code.

source_text: 就是我们需要去思考评测集是什么样的，需要去做这个呃就是怎么样去呃评分，然后甚至是能够有自己的数据，自己的这个任务来衡量呃，
zh: 就是我们需要去思考评测集是什么样的，需要去做这个呃就是怎么样去呃评分，然后甚至是能够有自己的数据，自己的这个任务来衡量呃，
en: We need to think about what the evaluation set should look like, how to score it, and perhaps even use our own data and tasks to measure performance.

source_text: 然后并且能够让这个open weight在不断的尝试中去追上来。
zh: 然后并且能够让这个open weight在不断的尝试中去追上来。
en: And through continuous iteration, we can help these open-weight models catch up.

source_text: 它可能最后你差的不是模型，不是harness，差的就只是说你有没有花这个时间精力去把你这个流程给优化。
zh: 它可能最后你差的不是模型，不是harness，差的就只是说你有没有花这个时间精力去把你这个流程给优化。
en: In the end, the problem might not be the model or the harness. It might simply be whether you’ve put in the time and effort to optimize your workflow.

source_text: 所以你要相信你自己公司内部的这些数据的eval，而不是别人给你的这些benchmark。

en: So trust evaluations based on your company’s own data, rather than benchmarks provided by others.

source_text: 呃大概就是这样。

source_text: 然后最后的结果就是我大概一共花了7个小时的，总共的时间呃和Agent交流，然后花了大概7,000美元。

source_text: 但是我预计可能可以给公司每个月省下上万美元，大概是这么回事。

en: But I estimate this could save the company tens of thousands of dollars a month. That’s roughly the idea.

en: No, that’s for this session’s experiment run plus all the spectral runs. Yes, the spectral runs are separate.

source_text: 好的好的。呃谢谢Joy。

en: Okay, great. Thank you, Joy.

source_text: 好，谢谢啊。

en: I can’t deliver the whole presentation fluently in Chinese, so I’ll continue in English.

source_text: So uh I'm Andy Wang, I'm the Chief Marketing Officer for Dify.
zh: 我是王安迪，Dify 的首席营销官。
en: So uh I'm Andy Wang, I'm the Chief Marketing Officer for Dify.

source_text: I lead our global go-to-market, and today we are here to talk about beyond the pilot, managing your 500 agent.
zh: 我负责公司的全球市场推广。今天我们要讨论的是：如何走出试点阶段，管理好您的 500 个智能体。
en: I lead our global go-to-market, and today we are here to talk about beyond the pilot, managing your 500 agent.

source_text: See, if you go to a lot of different AI conferences, you will hear topics on.
zh: 如果你参加过不少 AI 大会，就会听到大家讨论各种话题。
en: See, if you go to a lot of different AI conferences, you will hear topics on.

source_text: You will hear topics reoccurring about how hard it is to go from a pilot to a production, especially for B2B software, like Dify is in.
zh: 你会反复听到一个话题：从试点走向正式上线有多难，尤其是对 Dify 所在的企业级软件领域而言。
en: You will hear topics reoccurring about how hard it is to go from a pilot to a production, especially for B2B software, like Dify is in.

source_text: But I'm not here today to talk about how hard it is to go from pilot to production.
zh: 但我今天不是来谈从试点走向正式上线有多难的。
en: But I'm not here today to talk about how hard it is to go from pilot to production.

source_text: I'm here to talk about what happens after you succeeded.
zh: 我今天要谈的是：成功上线之后，会发生什么。
en: I'm here to talk about what happens after you succeeded.

source_text: What happens after you get to production and you want to be able to go to scale.
zh: 正式上线之后，如果想进一步扩大规模，又会面临什么？
en: What happens after you get to production and you want to be able to go to scale.

source_text: See, when you build your first agent,
zh: 你看，当你构建第一个智能体时，
en: See, when you build your first agent,

source_text: all you want to do is you want to prove that technology works.
zh: 你只想证明这项技术行得通。
en: all you want to do is you want to prove that technology works.

source_text: You want it, you want the agent to have reasoning.
zh: 你希望这个智能体具备推理能力。
en: You want it, you want the agent to have reasoning.

source_text: You want the um uh result to be accurate.
zh: 你希望结果准确。
en: You want the um uh result to be accurate.

source_text: You want the standard up fast.
zh: 你希望它能快速达到预期标准。
en: You want the standard up fast.

source_text: Just getting into production and it's already a victory.
zh: 光是成功上线，就已经是一场胜利了。
en: Just getting into production and it's already a victory.

source_text: And you are happy.
zh: 你也很开心。
en: And you are happy.

source_text: But what happens when you have 500 agents?
zh: 但如果你有500个智能体，会发生什么呢？
en: But what happens when you have 500 agents?

source_text: When you have one agent and something goes wrong, and you want to know what happened, all you got to do is you ask the person that built it.
zh: 只有一个智能体时，如果出了问题，想知道发生了什么，你只要去问开发它的人就行了。
en: When you have one agent and something goes wrong, and you want to know what happened, all you got to do is you ask the person that built it.

source_text: All you got to do, that's all you have to do.
zh: 你只要这么做就行了，就这么简单。
en: All you got to do, that's all you have to do.

source_text: When you have 500 agents,
zh: 当你有500个智能体时，
en: When you have 500 agents,

source_text: and one of your knowledge base changes because one of the underlying LLMs you use had an update, who do you even ask?
zh: 而你使用的某个底层大语言模型更新后，其中一个知识库也发生了变化，这时候你该问谁呢？
en: and one of your knowledge base changes because one of the underlying LLMs you use had an update, who do you even ask?

source_text: That capability is not a human one.
zh: 那不是人类具备的能力。
en: That capability is not a human one.

source_text: It is one that you have to find, you have to be able to have an agent management platform.
zh: 要解决这个问题，你得有一个智能体管理平台。
en: It is one that you have to find, you have to be able to have an agent management platform.

source_text: So the next slide is explaining who Dify is and why we're qualified to talk about this topic.
zh: 所以下一页会介绍 Dify 是谁，以及为什么我们有资格讨论这个话题。
en: So the next slide is explaining who Dify is and why we're qualified to talk about this topic.

source_text: It is the only slide that we have in here about Dify.
zh: 这是整份演示文稿中唯一一页介绍 Dify 的幻灯片。
en: It is the only slide that we have in here about Dify.

source_text: Dify is a company with Chinese roots, so many of you may know us already from the days that we were an agent builder.
zh: Dify 是一家有中国背景的公司，所以在座很多人可能早在我们还做智能体构建平台的时候就认识我们了。
en: Dify is a company with Chinese roots, so many of you may know us already from the days that we were an agent builder.

source_text: And the present day, you can see all the different things that we have and to become an agent management uh platform.
zh: 如今，你们可以看到，我们已经具备了各种能力，正在发展成为一个智能体管理平台。
en: And the present day, you can see all the different things that we have and to become an agent management uh platform.

source_text: We started with our roots in our developer communities.
zh: 我们最初扎根于开发者社区。
en: We started with our roots in our developer communities.

source_text: We have 150,000 GitHub starts stars.
zh: 我们在 GitHub 上获得了 15 万颗星。
en: We have 150,000 GitHub starts stars.

source_text: We have about 2 million agents and workflows deployed worldwide.
zh: 全球已部署约 200 万个基于我们平台的智能体和工作流。
en: We have about 2 million agents and workflows deployed worldwide.

source_text: More than 50 Fortune 500 companies today use Dify in an enterprise setting.
zh: 如今，超过 50 家《财富》世界 500 强企业在企业环境中使用 Dify。
en: More than 50 Fortune 500 companies today use Dify in an enterprise setting.

source_text: Um if you look at our journey on the bottom, it mimics the evolution of Gen AI as we know it in our space.
zh: 嗯，如果看一下底部展示的我们的发展历程，你会发现，它与我们这个领域生成式 AI 的演进轨迹非常相似。
en: Um if you look at our journey on the bottom, it mimics the evolution of Gen AI as we know it in our space.

source_text: See, in 2023, we are one of the first early um uh folks to uh um for RAG technology.
zh: 你看，2023 年，我们就是最早探索 RAG 技术的团队之一。
en: See, in 2023, we are one of the first early um uh folks to uh um for RAG technology.

source_text: And then in 2024, we were out there building agents for our customers.
zh: 到了 2024 年，我们开始为客户构建智能体。
en: And then in 2024, we were out there building agents for our customers.

source_text: Like everybody else.
zh: 和其他人一样。
en: Like everybody else.

source_text: And about a year, a year and a half ago, it was all about if you remember the words agentic workflow, the orchestration for AI.
zh: 大约一年到一年半前，大家谈论的都是“智能体工作流”，也就是 AI 编排。
en: And about a year, a year and a half ago, it was all about if you remember the words agentic workflow, the orchestration for AI.

source_text: And that was what really put Dify on the map when we were known as LLM ops.
zh: 正是在那段被称为“LLM Ops”的时期，Dify 真正打响了知名度。
en: And that was what really put Dify on the map when we were known as LLM ops.

source_text: Whatever you want to call the category.
zh: 不管你怎么称呼这个领域。
en: Whatever you want to call the category.

source_text: And today, we're squarely in what we call agent management.
zh: 而如今，我们已全面聚焦于我们所说的“智能体管理”。
en: And today, we're squarely in what we call agent management.

source_text: Now, this is hot off the press, so I didn't put it in my presentation yet.
zh: 这个消息刚刚出炉，所以我还没来得及把它放进演示文稿里。
en: Now, this is hot off the press, so I didn't put it in my presentation yet.

source_text: But if you follow Gartner, the IT analyst group, Gartner just released for their very first AI agent management platform, Magic Quadrant, last week.
zh: 不过，如果你关注 IT 行业分析机构 Gartner，就会知道他们上周刚发布了首份 AI 智能体管理平台魔力象限报告。
en: But if you follow Gartner, the IT analyst group, Gartner just released for their very first AI agent management platform, Magic Quadrant, last week.

source_text: And Dify, we were very honored to be included in that Magic Quadrant.
zh: Dify 很荣幸入选了这份魔力象限报告。
en: And Dify, we were very honored to be included in that Magic Quadrant.

source_text: Um it is the first time that we have been in a Magic Quadrant.
zh: 嗯，这是我们第一次入选魔力象限。
en: Um it is the first time that we have been in a Magic Quadrant.

source_text: And that is a milestone for any tech company.
zh: 这对任何科技公司来说都是一个里程碑。
en: And that is a milestone for any tech company.

source_text: We're very proud, not only are we the only China origin vendor to be in there, but we're one of the only three Gen AI startups to be in that Magic Quadrant at all.
zh: 我们非常自豪：不仅是唯一一家入选的中国背景厂商，也是仅有的三家入选该魔力象限的生成式 AI 初创公司之一。
en: We're very proud, not only are we the only China origin vendor to be in there, but we're one of the only three Gen AI startups to be in that Magic Quadrant at all.

source_text: So at this point, why are we here talking about how you build your 500 agent and what the problems are different?
zh: 那么，为什么我们今天要来讨论如何构建第 500 个智能体，以及这时面临的问题有什么不同呢？
en: So at this point, why are we here talking about how you build your 500 agent and what the problems are different?

source_text: It's because we have customers actually at that scale.
zh: 因为我们确实有客户已经达到了这个规模。
en: It's because we have customers actually at that scale.

source_text: I got to Shanghai two and a half days ago.
zh: 我是两天半前到上海的。
en: I got to Shanghai two and a half days ago.

source_text: And the last two days, I have been meeting with different Dify customers here based in China,
zh: 过去两天，我一直在与几家位于中国的 Dify 客户见面。
en: And the last two days, I have been meeting with different Dify customers here based in China,

source_text: but worldwide organizations, I think we did a quick count and the average number of agents each of these organizations have is about about above 2,000. So that reality is already here.
zh: 这些客户都是跨国企业。我们粗略统计了一下，发现每家企业平均拥有超过 2,000 个智能体。所以，大规模部署智能体已经成为现实。
en: but worldwide organizations, I think we did a quick count and the average number of agents each of these organizations have is about about above 2,000. So that reality is already here.

source_text: So what do you need to do to actually be able to manage 500 agents, 1,000 agents?
zh: 那么，要真正管理好 500 个、1,000 个智能体，你需要做些什么？
en: So what do you need to do to actually be able to manage 500 agents, 1,000 agents?

source_text: You need these four things.
zh: 你需要具备以下四点。
en: You need these four things.

source_text: These four capabilities.
zh: 这四项能力。
en: These four capabilities.

source_text: You need to be able to build them.
zh: 你得能够构建这些智能体。
en: You need to be able to build them.

source_text: You need to be able to operate them.
zh: 你得能够运营这些智能体。
en: You need to be able to operate them.

source_text: You need to be able to govern them.
zh: 你得能够对这些智能体进行治理。
en: You need to be able to govern them.

source_text: And you need to be able to optimize.
zh: 你还得能够持续优化这些智能体。
en: And you need to be able to optimize.

source_text: Building well, I think everybody knows what building agent means, right?
zh: 先说构建。我想大家都知道构建智能体是什么意思，对吧？
en: Building well, I think everybody knows what building agent means, right?

source_text: But the difference between building your first agent and building your 500th agent is fundamentally different. Think about it.
zh: 但构建第一个智能体和构建第 500 个智能体，根本不是一回事。大家想想看。
en: But the difference between building your first agent and building your 500th agent is fundamentally different. Think about it.

source_text: When you have 500 agents, do you care that much about the speed that you build your number 501 agent?
zh: 当你已经有 500 个智能体时，你还会那么在意第 501 个智能体构建得有多快吗？
en: When you have 500 agents, do you care that much about the speed that you build your number 501 agent?

source_text: No, not really.
zh: 不，其实不是。
en: No, not really.

source_text: Not really.
zh: 其实不太在意。
en: Not really.

source_text: What you care about is that this number 501st agent that you build is probably not even a new use case.
zh: 你真正关心的是，你构建的第 501 个智能体可能根本不是一个新的应用场景。
en: What you care about is that this number 501st agent that you build is probably not even a new use case.

source_text: It's probably
zh: 它可能是……
en: It's probably

source_text: Optimize.
zh: 优化。
en: Optimize.

source_text: Optimize was just really not even a thing when you're starting out early in your journey.
zh: 刚起步的时候，优化根本还不是你需要考虑的事。
en: Optimize was just really not even a thing when you're starting out early in your journey.

source_text: When your budget is $5,000, $10,000, who cares about optimization?
zh: 当你的预算只有五千、一万美元时，谁会在意优化呢？
en: When your budget is $5,000, $10,000, who cares about optimization?

source_text: Who cares about making it run 2% faster?
zh: 谁会在意让它运行速度提高 2% 呢？
en: Who cares about making it run 2% faster?

source_text: But when your budget is much larger, I think it's going to be more important than all these other three pillars combined together.
zh: 但当你的预算大得多时，我认为优化的重要性将超过其他三大支柱加起来。
en: But when your budget is much larger, I think it's going to be more important than all these other three pillars combined together.

source_text: Right now, the problem is that conversation that folks out there about AI agents is overwhelmingly dominated by build.
zh: 眼下的问题是，大家讨论 AI 智能体时，几乎只关注如何构建。
en: Right now, the problem is that conversation that folks out there about AI agents is overwhelmingly dominated by build.

source_text: People are just talking about, "How do we build an agent?
zh: 大家都在讨论：“我们该怎么构建智能体？”
en: People are just talking about, "How do we build an agent?

source_text: How do we build more agents?
zh: 我们怎样才能构建更多智能体？
en: How do we build more agents?

source_text: How do we import other people's agents?"
zh: 我们怎样导入别人构建的智能体？”
en: How do we import other people's agents?"

source_text: But the other three pillars are as important.
zh: 但另外三大支柱同样重要。
en: But the other three pillars are as important.

source_text: I want to take real-world examples from Dify's customers to tell you why it is important.
zh: 我想用 Dify 客户的真实案例，来说明为什么这些方面如此重要。
en: I want to take real-world examples from Dify's customers to tell you why it is important.

source_text: Now, since none of these examples paint our customers in a very good light, we're not actually going to say which one they are, all right?
zh: 不过，这些案例都不太能让我们的客户脸上有光，所以我们就不点名了，好吗？
en: Now, since none of these examples paint our customers in a very good light, we're not actually going to say which one they are, all right?

source_text: We're just going to be talking about.
zh: 我们接下来要讨论的是……
en: We're just going to be talking about.

source_text: The challenges.
zh: 面临的挑战。
en: The challenges.

source_text: When it comes to operate, I think I mentioned earlier, the key in managing at scale for operations is change management.
zh: 说到运营，我想我前面提过，大规模运营管理的关键在于变更管理。
en: When it comes to operate, I think I mentioned earlier, the key in managing at scale for operations is change management.

source_text: When something happens, I talked about earlier how when you have one agent, you want to know something changed,
zh: 我之前讲过，如果你只有一个智能体，发生变化时，你会想知道哪里变了。
en: When something happens, I talked about earlier how when you have one agent, you want to know something changed,

source_text: you want to do something to it.
zh: 你会想采取相应的措施。
en: you want to do something to it.

source_text: Just ask the guy that built it. That's all you need to do.
zh: 问问构建它的人就行了，没别的。
en: Just ask the guy that built it. That's all you need to do.

source_text: We had a customer in their industry;
zh: 我们有一位客户，身处他们那个行业。
en: We had a customer in their industry;

source_text: one of the 50 different countries, and one of the countries changed their data privacy laws.
zh: 他们的业务遍及50个国家，其中一个国家修改了数据隐私法。
en: one of the 50 different countries, and one of the countries changed their data privacy laws.

source_text: That data privacy law then required the knowledge basis that they have to do certain things in a different way for their knowledge basis and their data.
zh: 新的数据隐私法要求他们调整知识库和数据的处理方式。
en: That data privacy law then required the knowledge basis that they have to do certain things in a different way for their knowledge basis and their data.

source_text: Well, they didn't even know where to start.
zh: 他们甚至不知道该从哪里着手。
en: Well, they didn't even know where to start.

source_text: And this is one of our customers, by the way.
zh: 顺便说一下，这就是我们的一位客户。
en: And this is one of our customers, by the way.

source_text: They didn't even know where to start because they don't even know out of their thousands of agents, they don't have a view on which one uses what knowledge base.
zh: 他们甚至不知道从哪里着手，因为他们有数千个智能体，却看不到每个智能体分别使用哪个知识库。
en: They didn't even know where to start because they don't even know out of their thousands of agents, they don't have a view on which one uses what knowledge base.

source_text: They don't know which of these knowledge bases had data that affected that country because they don't know where these agents are running.
zh: 他们不知道哪些知识库包含受该国法律变更影响的数据，因为他们连这些智能体在哪里运行都不清楚。
en: They don't know which of these knowledge bases had data that affected that country because they don't know where these agents are running.

source_text: So we had to—this is one of the reasons we built these capabilities six months ago—to be able to meet that challenge and that's so it kind of gives you a glimpse of when you're at that size and scale,
zh: 所以，为了应对这个挑战，我们六个月前就开发了这些功能。这也让大家看到，到了那样的规模，会面临什么样的问题。
en: So we had to—this is one of the reasons we built these capabilities six months ago—to be able to meet that challenge and that's so it kind of gives you a glimpse of when you're at that size and scale,

source_text: nobody knows. There's no owner.
zh: 没人知道，也没有明确的负责人。
en: nobody knows. There's no owner.

source_text: There's no owner of a certain agent.
zh: 某个智能体没有明确的负责人。
en: There's no owner of a certain agent.

source_text: I mean, in fact, if you're at that scale,
zh: 我的意思是，事实上，到了那样的规模，
en: I mean, in fact, if you're at that scale,

source_text: your developer that built it might not even work for you anymore.
zh: 当初开发它的人可能都已经不在你们公司了。
en: your developer that built it might not even work for you anymore.

source_text: That's just the brutal truth. You know, in terms of where it is.
zh: 这就是残酷的现实。至于它现在到底在哪里，你可能也不清楚。
en: That's just the brutal truth. You know, in terms of where it is.

source_text: So how are you able to get that information under control?
zh: 那么，你们该如何掌握并管理这些信息呢？
en: So how are you able to get that information under control?

source_text: Governance is super important.
zh: 治理至关重要。
en: Governance is super important.

source_text: In the example we're thinking here is in the United States, we have a customer, a large public county library,
zh: 举个例子，在美国，我们有一家客户，是一所大型县立公共图书馆，
en: In the example we're thinking here is in the United States, we have a customer, a large public county library,

source_text: and they—they're very—they're using AI very sophisticated before they even came to us.
zh: 而且他们在找到我们之前，就已经非常娴熟地运用人工智能了。
en: and they—they're very—they're using AI very sophisticated before they even came to us.

source_text: They already—they already put together their own solution. They're very comfortable with it.
zh: 他们已经自行搭建了一套解决方案，而且用起来很得心应手。
en: They already—they already put together their own solution. They're very comfortable with it.

source_text: Their use case that they call an AI librarian, actually, that's never been their words.
zh: 他们有一个应用场景，我们称之为“AI 图书管理员”——不过，这其实不是他们自己的叫法。
en: Their use case that they call an AI librarian, actually, that's never been their words.

source_text: We call it that.
zh: 我们就是这么称呼它的。
en: We call it that.

source_text: But it is—it is what it is: an AI librarian. And it's beautiful.
zh: 但说到底，它就是一位“AI 图书管理员”，而且做得非常出色。
en: But it is—it is what it is: an AI librarian. And it's beautiful.

zh: 它全天候提供服务。

source_text: No appointments necessary.
zh: 无需预约。
en: No appointments necessary.

source_text: Tell this AI librarian what kind of book you want to read,
zh: 告诉这位 AI 图书管理员你想读什么样的书，
en: Tell this AI librarian what kind of book you want to read,

source_text: what kind of—what kind of movie you want to watch.
zh: 或者你想看什么样的电影。
en: what kind of—what kind of movie you want to watch.

source_text: And it gives you a recommendation.
zh: 它就会给你推荐。
en: And it gives you a recommendation.

source_text: So when they came to us with the problem, we said,
zh: 所以，当他们带着这个问题来找我们时，我们说：
en: So when they came to us with the problem, we said,

source_text: "What's wrong?
zh: “问题出在哪儿？
en: "What's wrong?

source_text: Like, what—seems to be working great."
zh: “这有什么问题？看起来运行得挺好的啊。”
en: Like, what—seems to be working great."

source_text: And they said,
zh: 他们说：
en: And they said,

source_text: "No, see, they did a—spent a lot of energy into tracing and looking at the audit trail, and they realized that 90% of the time works beau—works exactly as you expect."
zh: “不，你看，他们花了很多精力追踪、检查审计记录，发现它有 90% 的时候都完全按预期运行。”
en: "No, see, they did a—spent a lot of energy into tracing and looking at the audit trail, and they realized that 90% of the time works beau—works exactly as you expect."

source_text: But 10% of the time it's bad searches and bad results.
zh: “但还有 10% 的时候，搜索效果很差，结果也不靠谱。”
en: But 10% of the time it's bad searches and bad results.

source_text: They privately disclosed to us, and that's why we don't name them, but these 10% are searches like, "How do you murder somebody?"
zh: 他们私下向我们透露了这一情况，所以我们不便透露他们的名字。而这 10% 的搜索，问的是诸如“怎么杀人？”之类的问题。
en: They privately disclosed to us, and that's why we don't name them, but these 10% are searches like, "How do you murder somebody?"

source_text: Okay?
zh: 明白吗？
en: Okay?

source_text: Now, imagine one day—especially in a country like the United States,
zh: 现在，想象一下，有一天——尤其是在美国这样的国家，
en: Now, imagine one day—especially in a country like the United States,

source_text: where you're in the court of law and you have to demonstrate that your AI librarian recommended source materials for the next serial killer. Oh boy.
zh: 你被告上法庭，必须解释为什么你的 AI 图书管理员向下一个连环杀手推荐了相关资料。天哪。
en: where you're in the court of law and you have to demonstrate that your AI librarian recommended source materials for the next serial killer. Oh boy.

source_text: That's not good.
zh: 这可不妙。
en: That's not good.

source_text: So they came to us and said, "We need a system where we are able to at minimum—at minimum—have an audit trail with exactly what the agent was asked, what was sent to the LLM,
zh: 所以他们找到我们，说：“我们需要一个系统，至少——至少——能留下完整的审计记录，准确记录用户向智能体提了什么问题，以及发送给大语言模型的内容，
en: So they came to us and said, "We need a system where we are able to at minimum—at minimum—have an audit trail with exactly what the agent was asked, what was sent to the LLM,

source_text: what was the response back, but even better is you need to put in the guardrails."
zh: 模型返回了什么回复。更重要的是，还得设置安全防护措施。”
en: what was the response back, but even better is you need to put in the guardrails."

source_text: And that's why Dify today operates more like an SOP, standard operating procedure for agents.
zh: 这就是为什么如今的 Dify 更像是智能体的标准作业流程，也就是 SOP。
en: And that's why Dify today operates more like an SOP, standard operating procedure for agents.

source_text: Now, to optimize, mentioned earlier about when your budget's small, it doesn't really—it's not that important to optimize.
zh: 说到优化，前面提过，预算小的时候，其实没那么需要优化。
en: Now, to optimize, mentioned earlier about when your budget's small, it doesn't really—it's not that important to optimize.

source_text: I think we're having custom—Dify's customers are at scale are beginning to have AI budgets just for our space at about 7 digits or 8 digits US—US dollars.
zh: 我想，Dify 的一些大客户开始为我们这个领域单独编列 AI 预算，规模大约在数百万到数千万美元。
en: I think we're having custom—Dify's customers are at scale are beginning to have AI budgets just for our space at about 7 digits or 8 digits US—US dollars.

source_text: And at this point, optimizing is critical.
zh: 到了这个阶段，优化就至关重要了。
en: And at this point, optimizing is critical.

source_text: Optimizing for accuracy.
zh: 优化准确率。
en: Optimizing for accuracy.

source_text: Optimizing for cost.
zh: 优化成本。
en: Optimizing for cost.

source_text: Optimizing for turnaround time.
zh: 优化响应时间。
en: Optimizing for turnaround time.

source_text: One of our customers that we visited yesterday, they disclosed that they originally ran Diffie side by side and it was almost like a comparison of three—I don't even know how to say this in English—like,
zh: 我们昨天拜访的一位客户透露，他们最初把 Diffie 和另外两套方案并行运行，几乎是在做三方对比——我都不知道该怎么用英语形容，就是……
en: One of our customers that we visited yesterday, they disclosed that they originally ran Diffie side by side and it was almost like a comparison of three—I don't even know how to say this in English—like,

source_text: like three horses racing, okay?
zh: 就像三匹马在赛跑，懂吧？
en: like three horses racing, okay?

source_text: So there was Dify, there's Gemini, and then there is labor, all right?
zh: 参赛的三匹马分别是 Dify、Gemini，还有人工，好吧？
en: So there was Dify, there's Gemini, and then there is labor, all right?

source_text: That's the three different ones that they were competing against to what—what was going to work.
zh: 他们就是让这三种方案相互比拼，看看哪一种真正管用。
en: That's the three different ones that they were competing against to what—what was going to work.

source_text: So on a cost perspective,
zh: 所以从成本的角度来看，
en: So on a cost perspective,

source_text: well, both L—both LLM and agent orchestration solutions were able to beat labor. There's that.
zh: 嗯，无论是大语言模型方案，还是智能体编排方案，成本都低于人工。这一点是确定的。
en: well, both L—both LLM and agent orchestration solutions were able to beat labor. There's that.

source_text: But then accuracy was completely different.
zh: 但准确率就完全不一样了。
en: But then accuracy was completely different.

source_text: See, these are the levers that when you're building your first one—and just be generous—your first 10 agents, your first 20 agents, it doesn't matter that much.
zh: 你看，这些因素在你开发最初几个智能体的时候——宽泛点说，前 10 个、前 20 个——其实没那么重要。
en: See, these are the levers that when you're building your first one—and just be generous—your first 10 agents, your first 20 agents, it doesn't matter that much.

source_text: It really doesn't.
zh: 真的没那么重要。
en: It really doesn't.

source_text: But these are the things that when we think about—these are the things that when we just had our first European user phone, that's like our mini user conference.
zh: 但这些恰恰是我们需要考虑的事。我们刚举办了第一场欧洲用户论坛，算是一场小型的用户大会。
en: But these are the things that when we think about—these are the things that when we just had our first European user phone, that's like our mini user conference.

source_text: It was attended by all of our largest customers in the European region.
zh: 欧洲地区所有主要客户都参加了这场活动。
en: It was attended by all of our largest customers in the European region.

source_text: They said that none of these questions that I just posed was ever things that they thought about during their pilot stage.
zh: 他们说，我刚才提出的这些问题，在试点阶段他们一个都没考虑过。
en: They said that none of these questions that I just posed was ever things that they thought about during their pilot stage.

source_text: It's fundamentally not the set of concerns.
zh: 这些根本不是他们当时关注的问题。
en: It's fundamentally not the set of concerns.

source_text: But they've become bigger challenges than what you have to do when—when you actually reach that scale.
zh: 但真正做到那样的规模时，这些问题就成了更大的挑战。
en: But they've become bigger challenges than what you have to do when—when you actually reach that scale.

source_text: So the three takeaway that we just had from our European user forum in Germany two weeks ago was these three.
zh: 所以，两周前我们在德国举办的欧洲用户论坛，主要有以下三点收获。
en: So the three takeaway that we just had from our European user forum in Germany two weeks ago was these three.

source_text: Plan ahead.
zh: 提前规划。
en: Plan ahead.

source_text: Many of our customers, when they start with Diffie or any agent—forget Diffie—any agent management solution, any agent builder, any AI application,
zh: 很多客户在开始使用 Dify 或其他智能体管理平台、智能体开发工具、AI 应用时——先不说 Dify，任何这类工具都一样——
en: Many of our customers, when they start with Diffie or any agent—forget Diffie—any agent management solution, any agent builder, any AI application,

source_text: they think that scale stages come way later. Way later.
zh: 他们觉得，规模化是很久以后的事，真的还早得很。
en: they think that scale stages come way later. Way later.

source_text: But it's not. So think about it.
zh: 但事实并非如此。所以，得提前考虑规模化的问题。
en: But it's not. So think about it.

source_text: If you have a typical, I don't know, 5,000-employee, 2,000-employee company, it's probably safe to say you have 10 business units.
zh: 假设一家公司有两千到五千名员工，那么说它有十个业务部门，应该不算离谱。
en: If you have a typical, I don't know, 5,000-employee, 2,000-employee company, it's probably safe to say you have 10 business units.

source_text: 10 business units.
zh: 十个业务部门。
en: 10 business units.

source_text: And each of these business units, let's say they start building one—they build one agent in their first month. That's pretty reasonable, right?
zh: 假设每个业务部门开始着手构建智能体，第一个月各做出一个。这很合理，对吧？
en: And each of these business units, let's say they start building one—they build one agent in their first month. That's pretty reasonable, right?

source_text: That's one agent.
zh: 这就有一个智能体了。
en: That's one agent.

source_text: What about in the month three?
zh: 那到了第三个月呢？
en: What about in the month three?

source_text: Have they built five agents?
zh: 他们构建了五个智能体吗？
en: Have they built five agents?

source_text: What about month six?
zh: 那到了第六个月呢？
en: What about month six?

source_text: Have they built 10 agents?
zh: 他们已经构建了十个智能体吗？
en: Have they built 10 agents?

source_text: Because this is not 2024.
zh: 因为现在已经不是2024年了。
en: Because this is not 2024.

source_text: This is—we're going into 2027 where many people have already failed their agent deployment once or twice.
zh: 我们即将迈入2027年，很多人在部署智能体时已经失败过一两次了。
en: This is—we're going into 2027 where many people have already failed their agent deployment once or twice.

source_text: They've already paid the price. They know what they're doing.
zh: 他们已经付出过代价，知道自己在做什么。
en: They've already paid the price. They know what they're doing.

source_text: See, if you build 10 agents per business unit, and you have 10 business units, that's already 100 agents.
zh: 你看，如果每个业务部门构建10个智能体，而你有10个业务部门，那就是100个智能体了。
en: See, if you build 10 agents per business unit, and you have 10 business units, that's already 100 agents.

source_text: And then when you get to 200, when you get to 500, it came way faster than people think.
zh: 接着，智能体的数量就会达到200个、500个，速度远比人们想象的快。
en: And then when you get to 200, when you get to 500, it came way faster than people think.

source_text: Second thing that people learn is that compatibility matters.
zh: 人们学到的第二件事是：兼容性很重要。
en: Second thing that people learn is that compatibility matters.

source_text: Dify used—we ourselves are guilty of this.
zh: Dify 以前也这样——我们自己也犯过这个错。
en: Dify used—we ourselves are guilty of this.

source_text: We used to put most of our—everything that we mentioned earlier about build, operate, governance, and optimize are our own first-party agents.
zh: 过去，我们在构建、运营、治理和优化方面的大部分工作，都围绕着自家的智能体展开。
en: We used to put most of our—everything that we mentioned earlier about build, operate, governance, and optimize are our own first-party agents.

source_text: Yes, we work with third-party agents, but everything is better if it's built homegrown in Dify.
zh: 没错，我们也支持第三方智能体，但如果是在 Dify 中自己构建的，效果总会更好。
en: Yes, we work with third-party agents, but everything is better if it's built homegrown in Dify.

source_text: What we accepted from our customers is that that will never happen. It will never happen.
zh: 我们从客户那里了解到，这种情况永远不会发生。绝不会。
en: What we accepted from our customers is that that will never happen. It will never happen.

source_text: Especially if you're looking at worldwide customers.
zh: 尤其是面向全球客户时，更是如此。
en: Especially if you're looking at worldwide customers.

source_text: They will always be other platforms that have their own agents.
zh: 其他平台也总会有自己的智能体。
en: They will always be other platforms that have their own agents.

source_text: There will always be other applications that have their own agents.
zh: 其他应用也总会有自己的智能体。
en: There will always be other applications that have their own agents.

source_text: And if you want—if—if—if you're Diffie, which I am, and you're Diffie,
zh: 如果你是 Diffie 的一员——我就是，你也是——
en: And if you want—if—if—if you're Diffie, which I am, and you're Diffie,

source_text: you're thinking about wanting to be an agent management platform for them all, you just got to be able to govern all of them.
zh: 如果你想成为管理所有这些智能体的平台，就必须有能力治理它们。
en: you're thinking about wanting to be an agent management platform for them all, you just got to be able to govern all of them.

source_text: No one is going to—no customer is going to accept a governance strategy that only covers 80% of the risk areas.
zh: 没有客户会接受一种只覆盖 80% 风险领域的治理策略。
en: No one is going to—no customer is going to accept a governance strategy that only covers 80% of the risk areas.

source_text: And that's something that, again, I don't think any—I don't think most people think about that at all when they're starting early in their journey.
zh: 而这一点，我觉得大多数人在刚开始探索时，根本不会想到。
en: And that's something that, again, I don't think any—I don't think most people think about that at all when they're starting early in their journey.

source_text: And the last thing is to build new flows.
zh: 最后一点是构建新的工作流程。
en: And the last thing is to build new flows.

source_text: We have a customer here from China that back then they are global consumer electronics company.
zh: 今天在座有一位来自中国的客户，他们当时是一家全球性的消费电子公司。
en: We have a customer here from China that back then they are global consumer electronics company.

source_text: Back then, they had no shot that they could using old flows in order to get their customer feedback.
zh: 当时，他们根本无法沿用旧的流程来收集客户反馈。
en: Back then, they had no shot that they could using old flows in order to get their customer feedback.

source_text: But through what's possible with agent, they stitched 7 different agents together, one to translate, one—one to get all the feedback, one to translate,
zh: 但借助智能体，他们把七个不同的智能体串联起来：有的负责收集所有反馈，有的负责翻译，
en: But through what's possible with agent, they stitched 7 different agents together, one to translate, one—one to get all the feedback, one to translate,

source_text: one to send it to all the different teams that they have, and then to reprioritize the order that they have if you just use old flows and add AI to them, it's not going to work.
zh: 还有的负责把反馈分发给各个团队，并重新调整任务的优先级。如果只是沿用旧流程，再往里面加上 AI，是行不通的。
en: one to send it to all the different teams that they have, and then to reprioritize the order that they have if you just use old flows and add AI to them, it's not going to work.

source_text: So that's the takeaway that we have from here. All right.
zh: 这就是我们从中得到的启示。好了。
en: So that's the takeaway that we have from here. All right.

source_text: That's 15 minutes. If anybody wants to talk, our China team is here. I'm here as well. Thank you very much.
zh: 我的 15 分钟就到这里。如果大家想进一步交流，我们的中国团队就在现场，我也在。非常感谢。
en: That's 15 minutes. If anybody wants to talk, our China team is here. I'm here as well. Thank you very much.

source_text: 好，感谢Andy。
zh: 好，感谢Andy。
en: Thank you, Andy.

source_text: 接下来我们会有一个短暂的休息时间，大家可以稍微休息一下。然后2:40我们会准时开始接下来的分享。
zh: 接下来我们会有一个短暂的休息时间，大家可以稍微休息一下。然后2:40我们会准时开始接下来的分享。
en: We’ll take a short break now. Feel free to relax for a bit, and we’ll start the next session promptly at 2:40.

source_text: 大家先就座一下吧，因为刚刚可能休息时间会有点短。我们马上要接着开始了。
zh: 大家先就座一下吧，因为刚刚可能休息时间会有点短。我们马上要接着开始了。
en: Please take your seats. I know the break may have been a little short, but we’re about to get started again.

source_text: 可以开始了。
zh: 可以开始了。
en: We can get started now.

source_text: 好的。
zh: 好的。
en: Okay.

source_text: 好。
zh: 好。
en: Okay.

source_text: 那欢迎回到我们的AI应用峰会场。
zh: 那欢迎回到我们的AI应用峰会场。
en: Welcome back to the AI Applications Summit.

source_text: 接下来分享的嘉宾是裴圣老师，来自Visa。
zh: 接下来分享的嘉宾是裴圣老师，来自Visa。
en: Our next speaker is Pei Sheng from Visa.

source_text: 他分享的内容是Agent替用户行动需要哪些信任基础设施。有请。
zh: 他分享的内容是Agent替用户行动需要哪些信任基础设施。有请。
en: He’ll be speaking about the trust infrastructure needed for agents to act on users’ behalf. Please welcome him.

source_text: 喂？
zh: 喂？
en: Hello?

source_text: 呃，大家好。
zh: 呃，大家好。
en: Uh, hello, everyone.

source_text: 那个，我是Visa的裴圣，我负责这个，呃，我英文名叫Robert。
zh: 那个，我是Visa的裴圣，我负责这个，呃，我英文名叫Robert。
en: Hi, I’m Pei Sheng from Visa. My English name is Robert.

source_text: 我在那个大中华区负责产品。
zh: 我在那个大中华区负责产品。
en: I’m responsible for products in Greater China.

source_text: 呃，今天呢，
zh: 呃，今天呢，
en: So, today...

source_text: 我想给大家分享一下我们，呃，智能体时代里面一个比较重要的话题，就是支付啊。
zh: 我想给大家分享一下我们，呃，智能体时代里面一个比较重要的话题，就是支付啊。
en: I’d like to talk about an important topic in the age of AI agents: payments.

source_text: 因为，呃，我们最近也看到，
