en: Then you give the agent a budget, but how it actually spends that budget…

source_text: 甚至可能是由agent决定的。
zh: 甚至可能是由agent决定的。
en: might even be up to the agent.

source_text: 那么在这个时候，假设他买错了怎么办，或者说当然买超是不会，因为我们会做限额，但他如果买错了，或者他产生一些纠纷的时候怎么办。
zh: 那么在这个时候，假设他买错了怎么办，或者说当然买超是不会，因为我们会做限额，但他如果买错了，或者他产生一些纠纷的时候怎么办。
en: So what happens if the agent buys the wrong thing? Overspending shouldn’t be an issue, of course, because we’ll set spending limits. But what if it makes a bad purchase, or a dispute arises?

source_text: 这就是我们在这个，这个network里面需要，需要这个解决的问题。
zh: 这就是我们在这个，这个network里面需要，需要这个解决的问题。
en: That’s the problem we need to solve within this network.

source_text: 那么我也看到刚才提到说，呃，就是除了最后的购买的这个行为以外，
zh: 那么我也看到刚才提到说，呃，就是除了最后的购买的这个行为以外，
en: I also noticed you mentioned earlier that, beyond the final purchase itself,

source_text: 实际上在我们的discovery，包括我们的这个刚才最核心的这个决策啊，就是购买决策的这部分，
zh: 实际上在我们的discovery，包括我们的这个刚才最核心的这个决策啊，就是购买决策的这部分，
en: the discovery process—and, most importantly, the purchase decision itself—

source_text: 实际上已经开始由agent来帮这个我们的人类去，呃，去代劳啊。
zh: 实际上已经开始由agent来帮这个我们的人类去，呃，去代劳啊。
en: are already starting to be handled by agents on our behalf.

source_text: 那么这里面就面临了好几个问题啊。
zh: 那么这里面就面临了好几个问题啊。
en: That raises several questions.

source_text: 呃，第一个就是智能体的身份和信任的问题，就是说，呃，尤其是啊，就是我们所谓的open source agent，
zh: 呃，第一个就是智能体的身份和信任的问题，就是说，呃，尤其是啊，就是我们所谓的open source agent，
en: The first is the question of an agent’s identity and trustworthiness, especially with what we call open-source agents.

source_text: 就是比如说企业做的agent，像比如说最近比较火的instinct，或者是Muse、Grobot、personal agent的这些，
zh: 就是比如说企业做的agent，像比如说最近比较火的instinct，或者是Muse、Grobot、personal agent的这些，
en: For example, there are agents built by companies, like the recently popular Instinct, Muse, Grobot, and various personal agents.

source_text: 由公司建立的agent比较好办，对吧。
zh: 由公司建立的agent比较好办，对吧。
en: Agents built by companies are easier to deal with, right?

source_text: 那我们去找他去担一些责任，就像你这个，这个，这个robotaxi一样，那是这个平台，它可以担一些责。
zh: 那我们去找他去担一些责任，就像你这个，这个，这个robotaxi一样，那是这个平台，它可以担一些责。
en: We can hold the company accountable, just as we can hold a robotaxi platform responsible for its vehicles.

source_text: 但如果是个人的agent，就是我自己装一个harness，我用这个，这个，这个MS，或者我用什么，什么open cloud，
zh: 但如果是个人的agent，就是我自己装一个harness，我用这个，这个，这个MS，或者我用什么，什么open cloud，
en: But if it’s a personal agent—say I set up my own harness and use something like MS or OpenClaw—

source_text: 那么拿着我的卡出去买东西，那如果买错了，这个，这个，或者甚至是这个agent本身就是一个我，我这个，这个，这个人，他本身做了，
zh: 那么拿着我的卡出去买东西，那如果买错了，这个，这个，或者甚至是这个agent本身就是一个我，我这个，这个，这个人，他本身做了，
en: and it goes shopping with my credit card—what happens if it buys the wrong thing? Or what if the person behind the agent deliberately...

source_text: 做了一些恶意的行为的时候，那么我们的卡组怎么去和我们的银行，包括我们的商户怎么去杜绝这种行为，这是智能体身份和信任的问题。
zh: 做了一些恶意的行为的时候，那么我们的卡组怎么去和我们的银行，包括我们的商户怎么去杜绝这种行为，这是智能体身份和信任的问题。
en: ...does something malicious? How can card networks, banks, and merchants prevent that kind of behavior? That’s the question of agent identity and trust.

source_text: 那么一部分的智能体，它不是可以信任的。
zh: 那么一部分的智能体，它不是可以信任的。
en: So, some agents simply can’t be trusted.

source_text: 第二就是刚才说的这个意图和授权的问题。
zh: 第二就是刚才说的这个意图和授权的问题。
en: The second is the question of intent and authorization that I mentioned earlier.

source_text: 那么我们的意图会越来越模糊，因为人会越来越懒，因为agent会越来越强大。
zh: 那么我们的意图会越来越模糊，因为人会越来越懒，因为agent会越来越强大。
en: Our intent will become increasingly unclear as people grow more reliant on agents and the agents become more capable.

source_text: 那么我跟他说的这句话，他最后做了以后，呃，买了东西以后，你不认账怎么办，对吧。这是意图和授权。
zh: 那么我跟他说的这句话，他最后做了以后，呃，买了东西以后，你不认账怎么办，对吧。这是意图和授权。
en: So what if I give an agent an instruction, it buys something, and then I deny authorizing the purchase? That’s the issue of intent and authorization.

source_text: 呃，还有就是刚才提到的一些生态系统的成熟度啊，包括商户以后是不是也会被拖没，对吧。
zh: 呃，还有就是刚才提到的一些生态系统的成熟度啊，包括商户以后是不是也会被拖没，对吧。
en: And there’s also the maturity of the ecosystem, as I mentioned earlier—including whether merchants might eventually get pushed out altogether, right?

source_text: 就是说来的都是机器人，买了就走。
zh: 就是说来的都是机器人，买了就走。
en: I mean, they’re all bots—they just buy what they need and leave.

source_text: 那么我们传统商户所谓的这些loyalty怎么办，对吧，积分怎么办，
zh: 那么我们传统商户所谓的这些loyalty怎么办，对吧，积分怎么办，
en: So what happens to traditional merchants’ loyalty programs? What happens to their rewards points?

source_text: 然后我的这个常客的挽留怎么办，这些都是些需要解决的问题啊。
zh: 然后我的这个常客的挽留怎么办，这些都是些需要解决的问题啊。
en: And how do I retain my regular customers? These are all issues we need to address.

source_text: 所以我们在这个，呃，我们看到的这个，我就用刚才的那个例子哈，就比如说我这个engineer晚上睡觉前，
zh: 所以我们在这个，呃，我们看到的这个，我就用刚才的那个例子哈，就比如说我这个engineer晚上睡觉前，
en: So, to use the example I mentioned earlier, say I’m an engineer and, before going to bed...

source_text: 我把这笔交易丢给，呃，把这个任务就交给这个agent去做以后呢，实际上我们在今天的商业社会面临几个问题啊。
zh: 我把这笔交易丢给，呃，把这个任务就交给这个agent去做以后呢，实际上我们在今天的商业社会面临几个问题啊。
en: Once I hand that transaction—well, that task—over to an agent, we face several challenges in today’s business environment.

source_text: 第一个就是能不能通信的问题，就是说我们今天，比如说大家知道Cloudflare，Cloudflare，
zh: 第一个就是能不能通信的问题，就是说我们今天，比如说大家知道Cloudflare，Cloudflare，
en: The first is whether they can communicate. For example, take Cloudflare, which many of you know.

source_text: 那么它实际上上来有可能你到一个网站以后，它先问你你是不是个bot。
zh: 那么它实际上上来有可能你到一个网站以后，它先问你你是不是个bot。
en: When you visit a website, Cloudflare may first ask whether you’re a bot.

source_text: 那如果我的agent去的话，它肯定诚实的说我是个bot，那，
zh: 那如果我的agent去的话，它肯定诚实的说我是个bot，那，
en: But if my agent visits the site, it’ll honestly say, “I’m a bot,” and then...

source_text: 那你连网站的页面都retrieve不了，你就被block，对吧。
zh: 那你连网站的页面都retrieve不了，你就被block，对吧。
en: Then you can’t even retrieve the webpage—you just get blocked, right?

source_text: 那你还做什么shopping。
zh: 那你还做什么shopping。
en: So how are you supposed to shop?

source_text: 所以，所以这个infrastructure level呢，我们需要有一个tunnel，有一个通道呢，
zh: 所以，所以这个infrastructure level呢，我们需要有一个tunnel，有一个通道呢，
en: So at the infrastructure level, we need a tunnel—a channel...

source_text: 能让这个agent能够，能够，尤其是我们在白名单或者在我们认证过的这些好的智智能体，是可以进到这个网站里面的，
zh: 能让这个agent能够，能够，尤其是我们在白名单或者在我们认证过的这些好的智智能体，是可以进到这个网站里面的，
en: ...that lets agents—especially trusted ones we’ve whitelisted or verified—access the website.

source_text: 包括这个智能体刚才提到的这个认证的问题，包括就是说这个智能体背后的用户是谁，还有就是这个商户是否合法，
zh: 包括这个智能体刚才提到的这个认证的问题，包括就是说这个智能体背后的用户是谁，还有就是这个商户是否合法，
en: That includes the agent authentication issue I just mentioned: who the user behind the agent is, and whether the merchant is legitimate.

source_text: 包括是怎么去接入的。
zh: 包括是怎么去接入的。
en: And how they connect to the system.

source_text: 那这些每一笔交易里面都有这些问题。
zh: 那这些每一笔交易里面都有这些问题。
en: These questions come up in every transaction.

source_text: 那么包括我们跟我们的生态系统里面，比如说我们的这张，这张卡是银行发的，呃，实际上呃，人和机器的交易是不一样的，
zh: 那么包括我们跟我们的生态系统里面，比如说我们的这张，这张卡是银行发的，呃，实际上呃，人和机器的交易是不一样的，
en: And that extends to our ecosystem. For example, this card is issued by a bank, but transactions involving people and transactions involving machines aren’t the same.

source_text: 还是刚才那个例子啊，你比如大半夜突然我们的银行收到好好好多笔一分钱、两分钱的这种交易的时候，
zh: 还是刚才那个例子啊，你比如大半夜突然我们的银行收到好好好多笔一分钱、两分钱的这种交易的时候，
en: Take that same example: if a bank suddenly sees a flood of one- and two-cent transactions in the middle of the night...

source_text: 在我们传统的信用卡的这个风控模型里面，这肯定是被盗了，对吧。
zh: 在我们传统的信用卡的这个风控模型里面，这肯定是被盗了，对吧。
en: Under a traditional credit card fraud detection model, that would definitely be flagged as a stolen card, right?

source_text: 但实际上是因为我们，我们的engineer去睡觉了，然后让，让我们的agent在帮他半夜再再再build一个小app，
zh: 但实际上是因为我们，我们的engineer去睡觉了，然后让，让我们的agent在帮他半夜再再再build一个小app，
en: But in reality, our engineer went to bed and left the agent building a small app for him overnight.

source_text: 然后再买图片。
zh: 然后再买图片。
en: And then it buys images.

source_text: 那这这时候我们的这个，我们就要区分出来，哎，这个东西到底这笔交易是人发生的，
zh: 那这这时候我们的这个，我们就要区分出来，哎，这个东西到底这笔交易是人发生的，
en: So at that point, we need to distinguish whether the transaction was made by a person...

source_text: 还是机器发生的，人跟机器的这个，甚至作息和这个，这个行为模式是不一样的。
zh: 还是机器发生的，人跟机器的这个，甚至作息和这个，这个行为模式是不一样的。
en: ...or by a machine. People and machines have different schedules and patterns of behavior.

source_text: 第二个是说，包括它的上下文，包括它的这个执行速度，呃，很多我们以前的风控规则是要改的，否则我们没有办法去适应这个机器时代的这种，这种，
zh: 第二个是说，包括它的上下文，包括它的这个执行速度，呃，很多我们以前的风控规则是要改的，否则我们没有办法去适应这个机器时代的这种，这种，
en: Second, we need to account for the context and speed of these transactions. Many of our existing fraud detection rules will have to change; otherwise, we won’t be able to adapt to this new era of machine-driven transactions.

source_text: 这种交易频率和它的这个交易的这个，这个，这个pattern啊。
zh: 这种交易频率和它的这个交易的这个，这个，这个pattern啊。
en: The frequency and patterns of these transactions.

source_text: 当然反过来呢，我们可能也需要教育我们的消费者，就是说，呃，这个智能体到底，比如说我们，我们下了一个新的这个personal agent，
zh: 当然反过来呢，我们可能也需要教育我们的消费者，就是说，呃，这个智能体到底，比如说我们，我们下了一个新的这个personal agent，
en: Of course, we also need to educate consumers—for example, if you download a new personal agent...

source_text: 那么它到底能干什么，不能干什么，我能给给它授权什么，不能授权什么，这些可能都是一些我们需要去，呃，去推进的，在生态系统里面啊，需要解决的问题。
zh: 那么它到底能干什么，不能干什么，我能给给它授权什么，不能授权什么，这些可能都是一些我们需要去，呃，去推进的，在生态系统里面啊，需要解决的问题。
en: What exactly can it do, and what can’t it do? What can I authorize it to do, and what should I keep off-limits? These are issues we’ll need to tackle across the ecosystem.

source_text: 所以围绕这个呢，我们Visa提出来的这个intelligent commerce，给大家简单介绍一下它的几个核心的这个，呃，
zh: 所以围绕这个呢，我们Visa提出来的这个intelligent commerce，给大家简单介绍一下它的几个核心的这个，呃，
en: With that in mind, let me briefly introduce the key elements of Visa’s Intelligent Commerce initiative.

source_text: 思路啊。
zh: 思路啊。
en: ...ideas.

source_text: 第一个就是说，呃，所有的agent本质上，我今天是不可能直接给agent发一张卡的，因为agent它不是一个实体，
zh: 第一个就是说，呃，所有的agent本质上，我今天是不可能直接给agent发一张卡的，因为agent它不是一个实体，
en: First, an agent isn’t a legal entity, so I can’t just issue it a card.

source_text: 它背后挂的还是一个人。
zh: 它背后挂的还是一个人。
en: There’s still a person behind it.

source_text: 所以呢，我们每个人手上的一个账户，银行账户也好，信用卡也好，借记卡也好啊，那么怎么能够安全的、有控制的，呃，
zh: 所以呢，我们每个人手上的一个账户，银行账户也好，信用卡也好，借记卡也好啊，那么怎么能够安全的、有控制的，呃，
en: So how can each of us securely and with appropriate controls...

source_text: 叫叫有效的付给这个agent，这是一个核心问题，对吧。
zh: 叫叫有效的付给这个agent，这是一个核心问题，对吧。
en: ...make our bank accounts or cards available to the agent so it can pay on our behalf? That’s a core issue, right?

source_text: 那么我们，我们提出的一个概念就是，一个是说它是一个tokenize的一个，就是你不会把卡号直接给到这个，这个，这个智能体。
zh: 那么我们，我们提出的一个概念就是，一个是说它是一个tokenize的一个，就是你不会把卡号直接给到这个，这个，这个智能体。
en: So one concept we’re proposing is tokenization: you wouldn’t give the agent your actual card number.

source_text: 另外呢，是说它可能是一个scope的一个，呃，一个，一个token。
zh: 另外呢，是说它可能是一个scope的一个，呃，一个，一个token。
en: And the token could also have a defined scope.

source_text: 那么就是说它可能在今天晚上就失效了，它的这个上限是多少，那么这些是可以进行控制的啊。
zh: 那么就是说它可能在今天晚上就失效了，它的这个上限是多少，那么这些是可以进行控制的啊。
en: For example, you could set it to expire tonight or put a spending limit on it. Those are things you can control.

source_text: 第二个是控制权的问题，就是说刚才提到的，那么这个token拿去消费的时候，一定要匹配这个用户的意图和他的授权，
zh: 第二个是控制权的问题，就是说刚才提到的，那么这个token拿去消费的时候，一定要匹配这个用户的意图和他的授权，
en: The second issue is control. When the token is used to make a purchase, that purchase must match the user’s intent and what they’ve authorized.

source_text: 而且我们在这个阶段是要明确的授权的，而且在刚开始的时候，因为human in the loop，
zh: 而且我们在这个阶段是要明确的授权的，而且在刚开始的时候，因为human in the loop，
en: And at this stage, we need explicit authorization, especially at the outset, when a human is still in the loop.

source_text: 那就是每一笔交易我都用户需要进行一次确认。
zh: 那就是每一笔交易我都用户需要进行一次确认。
en: That means the user needs to confirm every transaction.

source_text: 那么之后有可能在一些小额场景里面，我们可能变成像刚才提到的这种，就是用户只要只要在，比如说我今天晚上最高20块钱，
zh: 那么之后有可能在一些小额场景里面，我们可能变成像刚才提到的这种，就是用户只要只要在，比如说我今天晚上最高20块钱，
en: Later, for small purchases, we might move to a model where the user simply sets a limit—say, a maximum of $20 for tonight.

source_text: 那么agent问你确认吗，他确认了以后，那么这我们认为也是一个明确的授权啊。
zh: 那么agent问你确认吗，他确认了以后，那么这我们认为也是一个明确的授权啊。
en: If the agent asks, “Do you confirm?” and the user says yes, we’d consider that explicit authorization too.

source_text: 其再再次就是我们所谓的生态的信任，那么就是刚才提到的，我们的这个智能体跟这个商户之间，
zh: 其再再次就是我们所谓的生态的信任，那么就是刚才提到的，我们的这个智能体跟这个商户之间，
en: The third issue is what we call trust in the ecosystem—specifically, trust between the agent and the merchant, as I mentioned earlier.

source_text: 实际上是要有一个mapping的啊。
zh: 实际上是要有一个mapping的啊。
en: There needs to be a way to map the agent to the merchant.

source_text: 那么它不是一个任何的智能体在任何的商户都可以，呃，是同样的这个信任level。
zh: 那么它不是一个任何的智能体在任何的商户都可以，呃，是同样的这个信任level。
en: Not every agent has the same level of trust with every merchant.

source_text: 所以我们做了一些这个，呃，一些一些这个行业跟生态伙伴一起的一些工作啊，呃，包括说，
zh: 所以我们做了一些这个，呃，一些一些这个行业跟生态伙伴一起的一些工作啊，呃，包括说，
en: So we’ve been working with industry and ecosystem partners on this, including...

source_text: 呃，我们提到一个叫trusty agent protocol，那么在这个里面呢，这个一个是说我们对agent会进行一个认证，第二个呢，
zh: 呃，我们提到一个叫trusty agent protocol，那么在这个里面呢，这个一个是说我们对agent会进行一个认证，第二个呢，
en: We mentioned something called the Trusted Agent Protocol. Under this protocol, we first authenticate the agent, and second...

source_text: 是我们的这个商户呢，是需要有个tunnel能够跟这个agent进行握手。
zh: 是我们的这个商户呢，是需要有个tunnel能够跟这个agent进行握手。
en: Merchants need a channel through which they can establish a handshake with the agent.

source_text: 那么握手以后呢，确认它是一个好的agent啊，呃，第二个是说我们也对商户做一些enablement，
zh: 那么握手以后呢，确认它是一个好的agent啊，呃，第二个是说我们也对商户做一些enablement，
en: After the handshake, we can confirm that it’s a trusted agent. We also give merchants the tools they need to support this.

source_text: 那么我们在旧金山有一个合作伙伴，那在帮这个商户打分，这个分实际上你也可以想象，当年的这个page rank一样，对吧，
zh: 那么我们在旧金山有一个合作伙伴，那在帮这个商户打分，这个分实际上你也可以想象，当年的这个page rank一样，对吧，

source_text: So basically like by making the app observable we providing an engineer's view to the agent so agent can operate the app much more efficiently more like a developer instead of a normal user so here's another example that I take from our like real world example uh so basically in this case we are trying to set the speed over a certain value video to 2 2x and to set it to 2x we basically need to adjust the slider like for actual user is easy it's basically you drag this knob here and it is 2x but for agent is surprisingly difficult because it has no idea like how the slider percentage map to the actual speed value so in reality we found out the agent will keep guessing it will do those like left and right it might slide a bit left and light speed right left then right then left then right and doing like you are in our in our experience usually ends up with like maybe 10 around 10 two calls and it costs lots of tokens and screenshots it can get there but usually take a very long time make it like usually is for the actual for useful validation so how do we fix this we expose the semantics on this slider so this is this is a code snippet from the Android Jetpack compose but what it does is to provide a semantics of this slider basically telling the agent that if you scroll to this percentage and what it's mapping speed here and by exposing the semantics here the agent knows how to do the proper scrolling it can use one two call instead of maybe nine or ten and it directly like it is working out of the box and by our evaluation it's like save the two calls reduce the two calls by average of 38 to nine and reduce the tokens by over 90%.

简单来说，让应用的内部状态可观测，就是给智能体提供一个工程师视角。这样，它就能更高效地操作应用，更像开发者，而不只是普通用户。

再举一个我们在实际场景中遇到的例子：把视频速度设为 2 倍速。对用户来说很简单，拖动滑块就行；但对智能体来说却出乎意料地难，因为它不知道滑块的位置与实际速度是怎么对应的。我们发现，它往往只能反复猜测，一会儿向左拖、一会儿向右拖，通常要调用工具大约十次，还会消耗大量 token、截取很多屏幕画面。最后也许能调对，但耗时太长，不利于实际验证。

怎么解决呢？我们为滑块提供语义信息。这段 Android Jetpack Compose 代码，就是告诉智能体滑块位置与速度值之间的映射关系。有了这些信息，它就知道该怎么拖动，原本可能需要九到十次工具调用，现在一两次就能完成。根据我们的评估，平均工具调用次数从 38 次降到了 9 次，token 消耗减少了 90% 以上。
en: So basically like by making the app observable we providing an engineer's view to the agent so agent can operate the app much more efficiently more like a developer instead of a normal user so here's another example that I take from our like real world example uh so basically in this case we are trying to set the speed over a certain value video to 2 2x and to set it to 2x we basically need to adjust the slider like for actual user is easy it's basically you drag this knob here and it is 2x but for agent is surprisingly difficult because it has no idea like how the slider percentage map to the actual speed value so in reality we found out the agent will keep guessing it will do those like left and right it might slide a bit left and light speed right left then right then left then right and doing like you are in our in our experience usually ends up with like maybe 10 around 10 two calls and it costs lots of tokens and screenshots it can get there but usually take a very long time make it like usually is for the actual for useful validation so how do we fix this we expose the semantics on this slider so this is this is a code snippet from the Android Jetpack compose but what it does is to provide a semantics of this slider basically telling the agent that if you scroll to this percentage and what it's mapping speed here and by exposing the semantics here the agent knows how to do the proper scrolling it can use one two call instead of maybe nine or ten and it directly like it is working out of the box and by our evaluation it's like save the two calls reduce the two calls by average of 38 to nine and reduce the tokens by over 90%.

source_text: So combining the discoverability and the semantic actions we build our verification agent so the verification agent is a combination of the features and the LM so by features I mean the deterministic stuff for example when doing a mobile app verification we need to do some like free stuff for example we need to build the app we need to install login and prepare the test media and making sure all the gating is working and those setups we do not need LM because those are deterministic and we don't want to waste the tokens here and what what needs LM here is uh to understand the prompt once we finish the setup we have the LM interpret the prompt into the CLI and the discoverability stuff we just built for example the prompt here which is create a project a video editing project from 2 1080p clips and export it at 1080p 30 fps and the agents will the LM agent will interpret this and calling the call responding CLI actions like the create select two videos and set up the export configuration and start exporting and for each step the agent will actually check the response from each CLI to make sure that each step is proceeding correctly and once finished the LM execution we're doing we are doing the teardown stuff which is like which is also deterministic so to make sure that each verification run is isolated without interfering with each other and.
zh:
结合可发现性和语义化操作，我们构建了一个验证智能体。它由确定性流程和大语言模型两部分组成。

以移动应用验证为例，构建应用、安装、登录、准备测试素材，以及确认各项准入条件都正常，这些准备工作都是确定性的，不需要动用大语言模型、浪费 token。需要大语言模型的是理解任务要求：准备完成后，它会根据要求，使用我们构建的命令行工具和可发现性信息来操作应用。

比如任务要求是：“用两个 1080p 视频片段创建一个视频剪辑项目，并以 1080p、30 帧每秒导出。”智能体会将其转化为相应的命令行操作：创建项目、选择两个视频、设置导出参数并开始导出。每执行一步，它都会检查工具的返回结果，确保流程正常推进。

大语言模型执行完毕后，我们再运行确定性的清理流程，确保每次验证相互隔离、互不干扰。

en:
Hi, everyone. I’m Devon. My Chinese name is Dong Yongchao—the “chao” is the same character as in “superhero.” Here’s a fun fact to help you remember me: Yongchao abbreviates to YC, and my friends have called me YC since I was little. Then I moved to the US in 2013 and to the Bay Area at the end of 2015, and I thought, “Oh no—how can I go around calling myself YC when that’s Y Combinator?” So around 2015 or 2016, I adopted the English name Devon. Please call me Devon now. I don’t dare call myself YC anymore.

A little about us: I followed a fairly typical path—undergraduate studies in China, then graduate school in the US. I joined Instagram quite early, when it had around a hundred employees. Later I worked at Tencent in Shenzhen and TikTok in Singapore before starting my own company. For the first seven years of my ten-year career, I worked on consumer products across product, operations, growth, and monetization. For the past three years, I’ve worked on B2B marketing.

Our CTO is also a veteran of Meta and Airbnb, and spent three years building voice agents at his own startup. Our CRO came from Nielsen and has many years of experience. We’re a US company that has raised about $7.3 million. We’re headquartered in San Francisco and have a small office in Singapore.

What we do is a very old business: user interviews. Say a consumer brand wants to know why you bought its product—or why you didn’t. It invites you to its office or meets you online, pays you for your time, and asks how you made your decision and what you were thinking. This has been around for centuries. Before the pandemic, these were mostly moderated in-person sessions.

And importantly, an interview is often many-to-one, not one-to-one. The moderator asks the questions, while people from the business sit behind a one-way mirror, observing what the participant says and how they react, and suggesting follow-up questions.

Then the pandemic—and later AI—pushed interviews online, creating an opportunity. Our company is essentially trying to bring the full in-person interview experience online. The short version is that we’ve probably achieved only about half the effectiveness of an in-person session so far, but the whole industry is working toward that goal. I’ll get into the many challenges shortly.

en: It’s that our model needs to see the person in two ways. First, this is a video interview.

source_text: 所以需要模型能看到这个人在呃，镜头面前，他到底是，在开小差呢，玩手机呢，还是在认真地回答，然后他高兴了，然后他思考了，对吧？
zh: 所以需要模型能看到这个人在呃，镜头面前，他到底是，在开小差呢，玩手机呢，还是在认真地回答，然后他高兴了，然后他思考了，对吧？
en: So the model needs to see whether the person on camera is distracted, playing with their phone, or answering thoughtfully—and whether they’re happy or thinking something over, right?

source_text: 他不耐烦了等等等等。
zh: 他不耐烦了等等等等。
en: Whether they’re getting impatient, and so on.

source_text: 另外呢，就是说我们很多时候是需要这个受访者去共享他的屏幕的，呃，然后我们的AI还要去一边看着他的脸，
zh: 另外呢，就是说我们很多时候是需要这个受访者去共享他的屏幕的，呃，然后我们的AI还要去一边看着他的脸，
en: Also, we often need the interviewee to share their screen, and our AI needs to watch their face at the same time.

source_text: 一边看着他分享的屏幕，然后呢，去追问一些问题，就比如说，
zh: 一边看着他分享的屏幕，然后呢，去追问一些问题，就比如说，
en: While also watching the screen they’re sharing, so it can ask follow-up questions. For example,

source_text: 哎，你刚才做了这个操作，能不能跟我解释一下，这是为什么？
zh: 哎，你刚才做了这个操作，能不能跟我解释一下，这是为什么？
en: Hey, you just did that—could you walk me through why?

source_text: 然后还要继续追问。
zh: 然后还要继续追问。
en: And then it needs to keep asking follow-up questions.

source_text: 所以这个对呃，context window对于这个实时的效果是要求很高的。
zh: 所以这个对呃，context window对于这个实时的效果是要求很高的。
en: So this places heavy demands on the context window for real-time performance.

source_text: 另外一个要求呢，是刚才我提到这是一个多对一的访谈，所以我们还需要去允许有observer，就是不是提问，
zh: 另外一个要求呢，是刚才我提到这是一个多对一的访谈，所以我们还需要去允许有observer，就是不是提问，
en: Another requirement is that, as I mentioned, this is a many-to-one interview, so we also need to allow observers—people who aren’t asking questions—

source_text: 但是坐在边上偷偷看着的那些observer，他要能继续地呃，向这个AI，比如说塞个小纸条说，
zh: 但是坐在边上偷偷看着的那些observer，他要能继续地呃，向这个AI，比如说塞个小纸条说，
en: But those observers watching quietly from the sidelines need to be able to pass the AI a little note, so to speak, saying,

source_text: 哎，刚才那个人回答这个问题的时候，我觉得非常有意思，你能不能再问一个问题，呃，这个呃，挖得更深入一点，
zh: 哎，刚才那个人回答这个问题的时候，我觉得非常有意思，你能不能再问一个问题，呃，这个呃，挖得更深入一点，
en: That person’s answer just now was really interesting. Could you ask a follow-up question and dig a little deeper?

source_text: 或者，哎，刚才有一个点我可能没有听清，能不能请这位受访者再解释一下。
zh: 或者，哎，刚才有一个点我可能没有听清，能不能请这位受访者再解释一下。
en: Or, “I might have missed something they said just now. Could you ask the interviewee to explain it again?”

source_text: 所以这个AI它不仅要实时地思考，不仅要实时地提问，它还要实时地听到背后这个这个这个researcher啊，
zh: 所以这个AI它不仅要实时地思考，不仅要实时地提问，它还要实时地听到背后这个这个这个researcher啊，
en: So the AI not only has to think and ask questions in real time; it also has to listen to the researcher behind the scenes in real time.

source_text: 或者是业务方提过来的诉求。
zh: 或者是业务方提过来的诉求。
en: Or requests coming from the business team.

source_text: 好，所以这里面有比较多的差异化的能力，呃，当我们仔细研究之后发现跟AI客服还是不太一样的，呃，我我这里就不细讲了，呃，大家大大概能想象。
zh: 好，所以这里面有比较多的差异化的能力，呃，当我们仔细研究之后发现跟AI客服还是不太一样的，呃，我我这里就不细讲了，呃，大家大大概能想象。
en: So this requires quite a few specialized capabilities. When we looked into it closely, we found it’s quite different from AI customer service. I won’t go into the details here, but you can probably imagine why.

source_text: 好，呃，那我们走过很多弯路哈，第一条弯路呢，就是大家所有人的脑子里第一想法就是，好，那我用大小模型配合不就行了吗？
zh: 好，呃，那我们走过很多弯路哈，第一条弯路呢，就是大家所有人的脑子里第一想法就是，好，那我用大小模型配合不就行了吗？
en: Okay, so we went down quite a few wrong paths. The first was what everyone thought of right away: “Why not just use a large model together with a smaller one?”

source_text: 那个呃，包括那个呃，GPT live，包括那个thinking machine的那个interactive model，
zh: 那个呃，包括那个呃，GPT live，包括那个thinking machine的那个interactive model，
en: You know, things like GPT Live and Thinking Machines’ interactive model.

source_text: 不都是大小模型配合吗？
zh: 不都是大小模型配合吗？
en: Aren’t they all using large and small models together?

source_text: 听上去super works but in reality it doesn't optimize for our like long term goal for the insight per minute。为什么呢？
zh: 听上去super works but in reality it doesn't optimize for our like long term goal for the insight per minute。为什么呢？
en: It sounds like it would work really well, but in reality it doesn’t optimize for our long-term goal of maximizing insights per minute. Why is that?

source_text: 是因为那个大模型它的思考，为什么它大，就是就是它太慢了。
zh: 是因为那个大模型它的思考，为什么它大，就是就是它太慢了。
en: Because the large model takes too long to think. That’s the problem: it’s too slow.

source_text: 所以呢，就是说大模型思考出来说，我下一个问题应该问什么，是不是应该跳过，是不是应该结束的时候，小模型早就在聊下一个话题了。
zh: 所以呢，就是说大模型思考出来说，我下一个问题应该问什么，是不是应该跳过，是不是应该结束的时候，小模型早就在聊下一个话题了。
en: So by the time the large model has figured out what question to ask next, whether to skip ahead, or whether to wrap up, the smaller model has already moved on to the next topic.

source_text: 然后很多时候大模型会被小模型带偏，你不管怎么调，这东西我们就是调不好。
zh: 然后很多时候大模型会被小模型带偏，你不管怎么调，这东西我们就是调不好。
en: And a lot of the time, the smaller model leads the larger one astray. No matter how we tuned it, we just couldn’t get it to work reliably.

source_text: 如果有人能帮我们调好的话，我们愿意出一十万美金吧，不说一百万美金，十万美金帮我们调一调，
zh: 如果有人能帮我们调好的话，我们愿意出一十万美金吧，不说一百万美金，十万美金帮我们调一调，
en: If someone can help us get it working, we’d pay $100,000. I won’t say a million dollars, but we’d pay $100,000 to help us tune it.

source_text: 但是我们目前为止没有特别好的解法。
zh: 但是我们目前为止没有特别好的解法。
en: But so far, we haven’t found a particularly good solution.

source_text: 嗯，好，然后呢，第二个呢，就是很所有人都能想象，对吧，端到端的模型，对吧，特别牛逼，
zh: 嗯，好，然后呢，第二个呢，就是很所有人都能想象，对吧，端到端的模型，对吧，特别牛逼，
en: Okay, so the second approach is one everyone can imagine: an end-to-end model. It sounds incredibly powerful, right?

source_text: 现在各种开源的、闭源的项目都很牛逼，但是，在这个场景下，他不work。为什么呢？
zh: 现在各种开源的、闭源的项目都很牛逼，但是，在这个场景下，他不work。为什么呢？
en: There are some incredibly impressive open-source and closed-source projects out there right now, but they don’t work for this use case. Why not?

source_text: 他没有办法做屏幕共享，没有办法做各个这个复杂的多模态的音频的输入，对吧，呃，这个文字的输入，然后呢，那个复杂的指令遵循你也做不到。
zh: 他没有办法做屏幕共享，没有办法做各个这个复杂的多模态的音频的输入，对吧，呃，这个文字的输入，然后呢，那个复杂的指令遵循你也做不到。
en: It can’t handle screen sharing or complex multimodal inputs like audio and text. And it can’t reliably follow complex instructions, either.

source_text: 所以就是说实时模型的thinking的能力，它确实比较差，所以就做不到。
zh: 所以就是说实时模型的thinking的能力，它确实比较差，所以就做不到。
en: So the real-time model just isn’t very good at reasoning, and that’s why it can’t do it.

source_text: 那怎么办呢？
zh: 那怎么办呢？
en: So what do we do?

source_text: 大家肯定听过Jeff，大家肯定听过呃，那个decisions API，对吧，这个东西是我们最后发现work的方式，
zh: 大家肯定听过Jeff，大家肯定听过呃，那个decisions API，对吧，这个东西是我们最后发现work的方式，
en: You’ve probably all heard of Jeff, and you’ve probably heard of the Decisions API, right? That’s the approach we eventually found that works.

source_text: 就是说把判断这件事情和下一步应该要做什么的actions，以及是具体怎么回的这个response，
zh: 就是说把判断这件事情和下一步应该要做什么的actions，以及是具体怎么回的这个response，
en: Basically, we separate the decision-making—what action to take next—from the response—what exactly to say.

source_text: 这三个东西拆开来，拆成三个，就是三大类的子agent，每一大类的子agent都给一堆的最好的模型，最快的模型，
zh: 这三个东西拆开来，拆成三个，就是三大类的子agent，每一大类的子agent都给一堆的最好的模型，最快的模型，
en: We split those three things into three main categories of sub-agents, each with a range of the best and fastest models.

source_text: 然后让它去本质上这东西是集连的。
zh: 然后让它去本质上这东西是集连的。
en: Then we let them work together—essentially, they’re connected in a pipeline.

source_text: 但为什么集连效果可能比前面的反而更好呢？
zh: 但为什么集连效果可能比前面的反而更好呢？
en: But why might this pipeline actually work better than the earlier approach?

source_text: 因为它是集连，所以它不太容易串信息，其次是你前面这两个能够做得很快很快很快，你可以做很多很多的优化来让它变得很快很快很快。
zh: 因为它是集连，所以它不太容易串信息，其次是你前面这两个能够做得很快很快很快，你可以做很多很多的优化来让它变得很快很快很快。
en: Because they’re chained together, information is less likely to get mixed up. And you can make the first two stages extremely fast through a lot of optimization.

source_text: 其中有一个最傻最笨的办法，是我们可以给大家share的，就是同一个模型，你完全一样的那个输入去call它，
zh: 其中有一个最傻最笨的办法，是我们可以给大家share的，就是同一个模型，你完全一样的那个输入去call它，
en: One of the simplest tricks we can share is to call the same model with exactly the same input.

source_text: 它的那个那个latency是不一样的。
zh: 它的那个那个latency是不一样的。
en: You’ll get different latency each time.

source_text: 我们因为成本不受限制，所以我可以同一个模型我就call五次，我就看谁最快，
zh: 我们因为成本不受限制，所以我可以同一个模型我就call五次，我就看谁最快，
en: Since cost isn’t a constraint for us, I can call the same model five times and just use whichever response comes back first.

source_text: 对吧，我甚至可以call多家的同一个API，我就call五次，每一家我都call五次，我call我看谁最快。
zh: 对吧，我甚至可以call多家的同一个API，我就call五次，每一家我都call五次，我call我看谁最快。
en: Right? I could even call the same API through multiple providers—five times per provider—and use whichever response comes back fastest.

source_text: 就类似于这种方式，我们可以去解决很多很多的，比如说模型突然抽风了，它的那个输出的那个JSON格式不对了，就导致后面的很多东西不不好计算啊，
zh: 就类似于这种方式，我们可以去解决很多很多的，比如说模型突然抽风了，它的那个输出的那个JSON格式不对了，就导致后面的很多东西不不好计算啊，
en: With an approach like this, we can handle a lot of issues. For example, if a model suddenly glitches and outputs malformed JSON, that can make it hard for downstream stages to process the result.

source_text: 或者是速度慢啦等等等等，就这里面有好多问题，你都是暴力可以解决这个问题。
zh: 或者是速度慢啦等等等等，就这里面有好多问题，你都是暴力可以解决这个问题。
en: Or it might just be slow. There are all sorts of problems like that, and you can solve many of them by brute force.

source_text: 但下一步还有，就是这个访谈的场景下，什么叫做有效的insight？
zh: 但下一步还有，就是这个访谈的场景下，什么叫做有效的insight？
en: But the next question is: in an interview setting, what counts as a useful insight?

source_text: 我们跟很多的优秀的researcher、academia、researchers，
zh: 我们跟很多的优秀的researcher、academia、researchers，
en: We’ve spoken with many excellent researchers, including academics.

source_text: 特别是social science，还有像尼尔森的这些优秀的user researcher们讨论过，
zh: 特别是social science，还有像尼尔森的这些优秀的user researcher们讨论过，
en: We’ve discussed this with excellent researchers, especially in the social sciences, as well as user researchers at companies like Nielsen.

source_text: 人人类对于好的insight的定义是很不一样的。
zh: 人人类对于好的insight的定义是很不一样的。
en: People have very different ideas about what makes a good insight.

source_text: 所以我们怎么样对我们的这个AI访谈员问出来的这个有效的insight，这东西是比较难定义到底好不好的。
zh: 所以我们怎么样对我们的这个AI访谈员问出来的这个有效的insight，这东西是比较难定义到底好不好的。
en: So it’s hard to define what counts as a good, useful insight from our AI interviewer.

source_text: 就算你问同一个，就是你把同一个问题问两个不同的user researchers，他们对于这个好的定义都不一样。
zh: 就算你问同一个，就是你把同一个问题问两个不同的user researchers，他们对于这个好的定义都不一样。
en: Even if you ask two different user researchers the exact same question, they’ll have different ideas about what makes an insight good.

source_text: 所以我们在我们在呃，就是去定benchmark的时候，就很难呢，我们工程方面就很难去做到说，哎，我这次prompt调了一下，
zh: 所以我们在我们在呃，就是去定benchmark的时候，就很难呢，我们工程方面就很难去做到说，哎，我这次prompt调了一下，
en: So when we’re setting benchmarks, it’s hard from an engineering perspective to say, “Okay, I tweaked the prompt this time…”

source_text: 那边harness调了一下，这个模型优化一下，或者那个场景优化一下，它就是能让这个业务真的变得更好吗？
zh: 那边harness调了一下，这个模型优化一下，或者那个场景优化一下，它就是能让这个业务真的变得更好吗？
en: “…tweaked the harness, improved the model, or optimized that scenario—but does any of that actually make the business better?”

source_text: 很多时候是我们觉得更好，但是客户不一定觉得更好。
zh: 很多时候是我们觉得更好，但是客户不一定觉得更好。
en: A lot of the time, we think it’s better, but the customer doesn’t necessarily agree.

source_text: 有的时候客户觉得好了，但我们觉得，哎，好像不太对。
zh: 有的时候客户觉得好了，但我们觉得，哎，好像不太对。
en: Sometimes the customer thinks it’s better, but we feel like something’s not quite right.

source_text: 所以就是我们现在怎么办呢？
zh: 所以就是我们现在怎么办呢？
en: So what do we do now?

source_text: 我们可我做了个很笨的办法，就是我们把历史以来，要么是客户觉得不好，要么是我们自己觉得不好的所有场景，全部把它抓下来。
zh: 我们可我做了个很笨的办法，就是我们把历史以来，要么是客户觉得不好，要么是我们自己觉得不好的所有场景，全部把它抓下来。
en: We’ve taken a pretty simple, brute-force approach: we’ve collected every past case where either the customer or we ourselves felt the result wasn’t good enough.

source_text: 那个场景细到什么程度？
zh: 那个场景细到什么程度？
en: How granular are those scenarios?

source_text: 就是一个30分钟的访谈，其中在第15分钟、20秒的时候，人类回了一句话，然后AI问了那个问题，
zh: 就是一个30分钟的访谈，其中在第15分钟、20秒的时候，人类回了一句话，然后AI问了那个问题，
en: Take a 30-minute interview: at 15 minutes and 20 seconds, the participant gave an answer, and then the AI asked a follow-up question.

source_text: 然后那个问题客户觉得你问的好像不太对。
zh: 然后那个问题客户觉得你问的好像不太对。
en: And the customer felt the AI’s question wasn’t quite right.

source_text: 好，我们把所有这种场景全部抓下来，历史以来我们可能积累了几千个这样的案例，然后我们把这样的样例做成我们的benchmark，
zh: 好，我们把所有这种场景全部抓下来，历史以来我们可能积累了几千个这样的案例，然后我们把这样的样例做成我们的benchmark，
en: So we collected every case like that. Over time, we’ve built up thousands of them, and we’ve turned those examples into our benchmark.

source_text: 诚然每一次的优化就是就是就像打地鼠一样，你这里优化，对吧，这个东西好了，那个东西就下去了。
zh: 诚然每一次的优化就是就是就像打地鼠一样，你这里优化，对吧，这个东西好了，那个东西就下去了。
en: Every optimization is like a game of whack-a-mole: you fix one thing, and something else gets worse.

source_text: 但是呢，整体来说，我们再给它一个大概的weight，然后呢，再让它测很多次，所以综合来看，
zh: 但是呢，整体来说，我们再给它一个大概的weight，然后呢，再让它测很多次，所以综合来看，
en: But overall, we assign each case a rough weight and run the tests many times, so when you look at the results as a whole…

source_text: 能够得到一个相对来讲就是大家能align说，啊，这样调一下好像是更好的。
zh: 能够得到一个相对来讲就是大家能align说，啊，这样调一下好像是更好的。
en: We can reach a rough consensus that, yes, this adjustment seems to make things better.

source_text: 那我们后来呢，演进到了所谓的半自动的RSI，因为你看啊，
zh: 那我们后来呢，演进到了所谓的半自动的RSI，因为你看啊，
en: Later, we moved toward what we call semi-automated RSI, because, you see…

source_text: 一个好的reward，一个好的benchmark，看上去有了，然后呢，呃，一个能够自动去找问题的能力，好像也有了。
zh: 一个好的reward，一个好的benchmark，看上去有了，然后呢，呃，一个能够自动去找问题的能力，好像也有了。
en: We seemed to have a good reward function and a good benchmark, as well as a way to automatically identify problems.

source_text: 所以呢，它就能自己转起来，但这东西是一个很危险的方式，因为它很容易去呃，优化到一个局部的最优，
zh: 所以呢，它就能自己转起来，但这东西是一个很危险的方式，因为它很容易去呃，优化到一个局部的最优，
en: So the system can run on its own. But that’s risky, because it can easily optimize its way into a local optimum.

source_text: 然后那个局部最优可能是一个很奇怪的一种方式。
zh: 然后那个局部最优可能是一个很奇怪的一种方式。
en: And that local optimum might take a very strange form.

source_text: 但是这里面有一个我们能够呃，
zh: 但是这里面有一个我们能够呃，
en: But there’s one thing here that we can, uh…

source_text: 这个leverage的一个好的优势是什么呢？
zh: 这个leverage的一个好的优势是什么呢？
en: So what’s the key advantage we can leverage here?

source_text: 我们的对话虽然发生在实时，也就是说模型在此时此刻的1.3秒之内，你就得要想出来到底要问什么问题，还是要结束这个对话。
zh: 我们的对话虽然发生在实时，也就是说模型在此时此刻的1.3秒之内，你就得要想出来到底要问什么问题，还是要结束这个对话。
en: Even though the conversation is happening in real time, the model has just 1.3 seconds to decide what question to ask next—or whether to end the conversation.

source_text: 但是整个访谈结束之后，比如说30分钟、1个小时的访谈结束之后，

en:
Yes, I think that’s really important! Let’s give him a round of applause. Really, no applause? Okay.

I think you’ve all made great points, but for me, the biggest one is **context**. All the information we generate is incredibly valuable. One habit I have is to keep all our community information in a knowledge base. If it can go in the cloud, put it in the cloud rather than on your own device. That way, we can access it from anywhere.

Since 2023, I’ve also made a habit of recording everything as we go. Sorry—I’ve brought my recording device today, too! The idea is to capture all that information. Our community has essentially grown up in Feishu Docs, which gave us a great starting point. Everything we’ve done—events, plans, proposals, meetings—we’ve saved as context. It’s become our most important asset.

Now, if I need to organize an event next month, I can tell the AI: “Pull together all the relevant information, draft a plan, and help me identify everyone I need to contact.” Because we’ve archived our community information, people’s details, and everything we’ve done, we can turn that context into workflows.

We have meeting transcripts, group chats, and recordings. How do we bring them together? Through AI workflows. First, I archive everything as context. The system identifies what a meeting was about and, say, which client it was with, then files it under that client.

But today’s meeting might be in my documents, while tomorrow’s is in someone else’s. So we give everyone a skill that automatically archives the information after a conversation into shared context that the whole team can read. I want it all to be transparent. People often raise questions about access permissions, but I think, when it comes to context, sharing matters more.

Then we distill that information. AI also writes far too much these days—lots of AI slop that’s hard for humans to read. So I’d recommend a skill called the ADHD skill. Does anyone here have ADHD? Could you raise your hand?

Oh, there are a few of us! I think the AI era is actually quite ADHD-friendly, but complicated documents can still be a headache for us. The ADHD skill helps make content more structured and visual.

I’ve added one more instruction: present the document on a canvas. Let me quickly show you. You just add that line to your `agent.md` file. If you’re using Feishu Docs, the agent knows what a canvas is. Tell it to use one, and it can draw the content in SVG, making the structure easier to see. You can spot the key points and follow the flow.

I put these instructions in my `CLAUDE.md` or `agent.md`: use the ADHD skill to make the output easier to understand. If there’s a lot of text or the subject is complicated, explain it plainly and simply. Present it on a canvas, and whenever you save a Markdown file locally, upload it to the cloud and put a copy in Feishu Docs. That way, everyone can share and build on the same context.

en:
We’ve also found some interesting ways to work. Our rule is that once you’ve done something more than twice, you turn it into an SOP. For example, we turn what we’ve learned through team discussions into a workspace that’s more visual, easier to navigate, and easier for everyone to reuse.

We’ve run a lot of hackathons, so we built a hackathon workspace. It contains logos from major companies we’ve worked with and all the other materials we’ve accumulated. With that workspace, you could organize an entire hackathon from start to finish.

We did the same for trade shows. We kept running into questions about display-board dimensions and print files: Have the fonts been converted to outlines? Is there enough bleed? I didn’t know about any of that before, so we created a trade-show workspace. Now anyone preparing for an event can find the documents, design assets, and talking points for on-site conversations in one place.

That’s made us much more efficient, especially since so much of our communication is remote. We actually encourage remote work. In an office, I could just tap someone on the shoulder, point at my screen, and ask for help—and that would be it. Remotely, we have to get on a call, which means all that information becomes part of the recorded context. In the AI era, many small teams, including teams of around ten people, are spread across the globe.

So that’s the idea: once you’ve done something twice, make it an SOP and build a visual workspace the whole team can reuse. That’s what I’ve been explaining here. You can also find skills like “I Have ADHD” directly on GitHub.

We’ve taken this further, too. For example, I created a skill that everyone installs for what happens after a meeting. You can add it as an automation to whichever work agent you use. Once the meeting ends and Feishu Minutes has finished transcribing it, AI summarizes the discussion. It sends the action items to your task workspace and files customer-related information in each customer’s folder, with the appropriate access permissions. You just need to specify the rules.

source_text: Um, so I'm talking about how we rebuilt Atlas.

en: Um, so I'm talking about how we rebuilt Atlas.

source_text: Atlas is an open source application which is developed by Odyssey, which is a, um, organization in the observational health, uh, data research.
zh: Atlas 是一款由 Odyssey 开发的开源应用。Odyssey 是一家从事观察性健康数据研究的机构。
en: Atlas is an open source application which is developed by Odyssey, which is a, um, organization in the observational health, uh, data research.

source_text: And, um,
zh: 然后，嗯……
en: And, um,

source_text: the talk is not about the application itself, but about how we used agents to build application and to verify the correctness of the application.
zh: 这次分享的重点不是应用本身，而是我们如何利用智能体来构建应用，并验证它的正确性。
en: the talk is not about the application itself, but about how we used agents to build application and to verify the correctness of the application.

source_text: So basically to, to look into the problem of how do you actually verify the generated code without basically reviewing every single line of the code.
zh: 所以，核心问题是：怎样才能在不逐行审查生成代码的情况下，验证它是否正确？
en: So basically to, to look into the problem of how do you actually verify the generated code without basically reviewing every single line of the code.

source_text: And, um, just to give a little bit of a background, what is Atlas, um, so on the left side you're seeing here the, um, the Atlas version two, um,
zh: 先简单介绍一下背景：Atlas 是什么？大家现在看到左边的是 Atlas 2.0 版本。
en: And, um, just to give a little bit of a background, what is Atlas, um, so on the left side you're seeing here the, um, the Atlas version two, um,

source_text: which is the old version of Atlas which was developed with knockout JS.
zh: 这是用 Knockout.js 开发的旧版 Atlas。
en: which is the old version of Atlas which was developed with knockout JS.

source_text: And, um, yeah, in the last, I mean, was used about a decade.
zh: 嗯，对，这个版本用了大约十年。
en: And, um, yeah, in the last, I mean, was used about a decade.

source_text: And, um, we basically rebuilt it from scratch in Vue.js.
zh: 后来，我们用 Vue.js 从零开始重建了它。
en: And, um, we basically rebuilt it from scratch in Vue.js.

source_text: Uh, and we not only basically exchange the text stack, but the idea was, I mean, one of the challenges was that the application was, uh, especially for new users,
zh: 我们不只是更换了技术栈。当时的一大挑战是，这款应用对新用户来说尤其……
en: Uh, and we not only basically exchange the text stack, but the idea was, I mean, one of the challenges was that the application was, uh, especially for new users,

source_text: hard to use.
zh: 很难上手。
en: hard to use.

source_text: And so we wanted to as well, um, yeah, change the visual design and as well the user flow and user experience.
zh: 因此，我们也希望改进视觉设计、用户操作流程和整体体验。
en: And so we wanted to as well, um, yeah, change the visual design and as well the user flow and user experience.

source_text: And to just go one more level deeper of, of basically understanding Atlas, so basically the researcher he would like to, um, answer research questions.
zh: 为了再深入了解一下 Atlas：研究人员会用它来解答研究问题。
en: And to just go one more level deeper of, of basically understanding Atlas, so basically the researcher he would like to, um, answer research questions.

source_text: So looking at health records and basically building a patient cohort.
zh: 也就是查阅健康档案，并据此建立患者队列。
en: So looking at health records and basically building a patient cohort.

source_text: So a group of patients.
zh: 也就是一组患者。
en: So a group of patients.

source_text: And so he, he can then visually in the Atlas UI create these filters.
zh: 然后，研究人员就可以在 Atlas 的界面中以可视化的方式设置这些筛选条件。
en: And so he, he can then visually in the Atlas UI create these filters.

source_text: The Atlas UI is sending a JSON to the backends in the web API, and that's translated to SQL and queries the database.
zh: Atlas 界面会将 JSON 数据发送到 Web API 后端，后端再将其转换为 SQL，查询数据库。
en: The Atlas UI is sending a JSON to the backends in the web API, and that's translated to SQL and queries the database.

source_text: So each, basically, I mean,
zh: 所以，每个……我是说，
en: So each, basically, I mean,

source_text: if there's basically a bug which is, um, yeah, changing the JSON, it immediately leans in the wrong patient cohort, and so the research question cannot be reliably analyzed.
zh: 如果有个 bug 导致 JSON 发生变化，就会直接筛选出错误的患者队列，研究问题也就无法得到可靠的分析。
en: if there's basically a bug which is, um, yeah, changing the JSON, it immediately leans in the wrong patient cohort, and so the research question cannot be reliably analyzed.

source_text: Um, what we did here,
zh: 嗯，我们在这里所做的是……
en: Um, what we did here,

source_text: we, uh, yeah, rebuilt Atlas from scratch in Vue, and we as well renewed the text stack of web API.
zh: 我们用 Vue 从头重建了 Atlas，也更新了 Web API 的技术栈。
en: we, uh, yeah, rebuilt Atlas from scratch in Vue, and we as well renewed the text stack of web API.

source_text: Um, I will talk here especially about the rewrite of the Atlas UI, as I think that's, I think the more challenging part, as it involves the UI and not only basically, uh, yeah, well-defined backend.
zh: 嗯，我会重点讲讲 Atlas 界面的重写，因为我觉得这部分更有挑战性：它涉及用户界面，而不只是定义相对明确的后端。
en: Um, I will talk here especially about the rewrite of the Atlas UI, as I think that's, I think the more challenging part, as it involves the UI and not only basically, uh, yeah, well-defined backend.

source_text: Um, and so if you look at what changed.
zh: 嗯，接下来我们看看有哪些变化。
en: Um, and so if you look at what changed.

source_text: So basically, um, when we rewrote it, it's, it's roughly, I mean, 300, I mean, nearly 300 PRs, 150 lines of, um, source code,
zh: 所以，重写过程中，我们大概提交了将近 300 个 PR，写了约 15 万行源代码。
en: So basically, um, when we rewrote it, it's, it's roughly, I mean, 300, I mean, nearly 300 PRs, 150 lines of, um, source code,

source_text: 150, 1,000 lines of, um, test code.
zh: 还有 15 万行测试代码。
en: 150, 1,000 lines of, um, test code.

source_text: And it was a small team, so it was basically I started the rewrite and one other engineer, um, joined me in doing the rewrite.
zh: 而且团队很小，基本上是我先开始重写，后来另一位工程师加入，和我一起完成。
en: And it was a small team, so it was basically I started the rewrite and one other engineer, um, joined me in doing the rewrite.

source_text: And so by that, it was basically yeah, at the end, too much basically code to really basically manually review every line.
zh: 所以到最后，代码量实在太大，根本没法逐行人工审查。
en: And so by that, it was basically yeah, at the end, too much basically code to really basically manually review every line.

source_text: And so what does it mean?
zh: 那么，这意味着什么呢？
en: And so what does it mean?

source_text: So, um, so in Atlas two, I mean, actually it didn't have basically a large test code.
zh: 所以，Atlas 2 其实并没有大量的测试代码。
en: So, um, so in Atlas two, I mean, actually it didn't have basically a large test code.

source_text: So that basically as well needed to be developed.
zh: 因此，测试代码也需要同步编写。
en: So that basically as well needed to be developed.

source_text: Atlas two just had five utility tests.
zh: Atlas 2 只有五个工具类测试。
en: Atlas two just had five utility tests.

source_text: So therefore we needed to develop the harness as well.
zh: 所以，我们还得开发测试框架。
en: So therefore we needed to develop the harness as well.

source_text: And that was basically done along basically building the actual product.
zh: 这项工作基本上是和产品本身的开发同步进行的。
en: And that was basically done along basically building the actual product.

source_text: And of course we used basically the agents as well to write the tests.
zh: 当然，我们也用智能体来编写测试。
en: And of course we used basically the agents as well to write the tests.

source_text: And so I will now start talking about basically what is actually the harness we built for, um, yeah, rewriting the application.
zh: 接下来我会讲讲，为了重写这个应用，我们构建了什么样的测试框架。
en: And so I will now start talking about basically what is actually the harness we built for, um, yeah, rewriting the application.

source_text: So I think there are two parts to this. One is around the agent.
zh: 我认为这可以分成两部分，一部分是关于智能体的。
en: So I think there are two parts to this. One is around the agent.

source_text: So we have the instructions of skills, permissions, and sub-agents.
zh: 我们为智能体设定了操作指令、技能、权限和子智能体。
en: So we have the instructions of skills, permissions, and sub-agents.

source_text: Here we used mostly basically existing open source software and, and other software like cloud code and skill frameworks.
zh: 在这方面，我们主要使用了现有的开源软件，以及 Claude Code 和技能框架等工具。
en: Here we used mostly basically existing open source software and, and other software like cloud code and skill frameworks.

source_text: But and then it is, I mean, especially for verification, I think you need to basically have the harness around the code.
zh: 但尤其是在验证方面，我认为还需要围绕代码搭建一套测试框架。
en: But and then it is, I mean, especially for verification, I think you need to basically have the harness around the code.

source_text: And then as well a visual verification via screenshots.

source_text: So you first basically look into the specs, you define basically what you would like to do,

source_text: So one is basically, yeah, check it against the, um, the previous application Atlas two, to basically, um, yeah, have the tests to, to, yeah, check the correctness and as well to do a, um, uh,

source_text: visual validation.

en: visual validation.

source_text: Um,
zh: 嗯，
en: Um,

source_text: yeah, before basically then the human, I mean, yeah, does the final check.

en: yeah, before basically then the human, I mean, yeah, does the final check.

source_text: So now I go into the a little bit more detail regarding these four gates.

en: So now I go into the a little bit more detail regarding these four gates.

source_text: I mean, the specs, I mean, I think it's nothing, um, new.

source_text: I think nowadays with, with, um, newer LLMs, I think it's mostly about really well-defining what needs to be done, what needs to be achieved, what is basically actually, um, yeah, considered done for the, I mean,
zh: 我觉得现在有了更新的大语言模型，关键更多在于清楚地定义要做什么、要达到什么目标，以及怎样才算真正完成……
en: I think nowadays with, with, um, newer LLMs, I think it's mostly about really well-defining what needs to be done, what needs to be achieved, what is basically actually, um, yeah, considered done for the, I mean,

source_text: so basically an acceptance test. What is considered done for the task.
zh: 也就是验收标准：怎样才算完成了这项任务。
en: so basically an acceptance test. What is considered done for the task.

source_text: As we are, um,
zh: 既然我们，嗯，
en: As we are, um,

source_text: did the rewrite and really changed the whole UI, it actually starts a little bit before the spec.

source_text: Because on one side, I think you by that can basically make sure that actually, I mean, it's really basically um, the definition, I mean,
zh: 因为一方面，我觉得这样可以确保，嗯，也就是说，定义确实……
en: Because on one side, I think you by that can basically make sure that actually, I mean, it's really basically um, the definition, I mean,

source_text: what you wanted to change is really basically looks like where you want.
zh: 看看你想改的地方，最终呈现出来是不是你想要的样子。
en: what you wanted to change is really basically looks like where you want.

source_text: And on the other side, it gives you basically possibility in the way the AI is basically as well um, bringing ideas in basically how the usability can be improved.
zh: 另一方面，AI 也能提出一些改进易用性的想法，给你更多选择。
en: And on the other side, it gives you basically possibility in the way the AI is basically as well um, bringing ideas in basically how the usability can be improved.

source_text: So then basically, I mean, you had now the specs, you had basically the mockups.
zh: 这样一来，你就有了规格说明和界面原型。
en: So then basically, I mean, you had now the specs, you had basically the mockups.

source_text: So then basically you give that to the agents to generate the code.
zh: 然后把这些交给 AI 智能体，让它们生成代码。
en: So then basically you give that to the agents to generate the code.

source_text: And now it's about, yeah, validating that actually what, what implemented is correct.
zh: 接下来就是验证实现的内容是否正确。
en: And now it's about, yeah, validating that actually what, what implemented is correct.

source_text: Or is what you wanted.
zh: 或者说，是否符合你的预期。
en: Or is what you wanted.

source_text: And so there basically, I mean, the first component there is, um, comparing it to the existing system.
zh: 所以这里的第一步，就是把它和现有系统进行对比。
en: And so there basically, I mean, the first component there is, um, comparing it to the existing system.

source_text: So, I mean, this is one example what we did.

en: So, I mean, this is one example what we did.

en: Um, so we had basically there's a,

source_text: And so we took these uploaded them into the basically the front end and then imported it, exported it, ensured that basically it's, um, still correct.

en: And so we took these uploaded them into the basically the front end and then imported it, exported it, ensured that basically it's, um, still correct.

source_text: And that's where basically um,

en: And that's where basically um,

source_text: then loaded basically modified it in a way.
zh: 然后把它加载进来，做了一些修改。
en: then loaded basically modified it in a way.

source_text: And by that basically, um, yeah, ensured that the Atlas two and Atlas three are basically coming to the same result.

en: And by that basically, um, yeah, ensured that the Atlas two and Atlas three are basically coming to the same result.

source_text: So why did we do that?
zh: 那我们为什么要这么做呢？
en: So why did we do that?

source_text: And,
zh: 然后，
en: And,

source_text: um, what did we find by doing that?
zh: 嗯，我们通过这样做发现了什么？
en: um, what did we find by doing that?

source_text: So actually, I mean, it started with that we had a bug in the converter.
zh: 其实，最初是因为我们的转换器出了一个问题。
en: So actually, I mean, it started with that we had a bug in the converter.

source_text: I mean, that basically it was not the same.
zh: 我的意思是，转换后的结果其实并不一致。
en: I mean, that basically it was not the same.

source_text: And instead of basically just solving, um, that specific issue, we uh, thought about, okay, how can we ensure that in the future the agents are um,
zh: 我们没有只解决这个具体问题，而是开始思考：怎样才能确保今后这些智能体……
en: And instead of basically just solving, um, that specific issue, we uh, thought about, okay, how can we ensure that in the future the agents are um,

source_text: detecting these kind of issues automatically.
zh: 能够自动检测出这类问题。
en: detecting these kind of issues automatically.

source_text: And so, um, yeah, by running that, we basically discovered additional bugs in the converter, but as well basically additional um, problem in actually how uh, the how the basically structure was represented in the front end.

en: And so, um, yeah, by running that, we basically discovered additional bugs in the converter, but as well basically additional um, problem in actually how uh, the how the basically structure was represented in the front end.

source_text: Okay, then the next component is the, the testing framework.
zh: 好，接下来的组件是测试框架。
en: Okay, then the next component is the, the testing framework.

source_text: So here we have basically our CI gates in a way.
zh: 这里基本上就是我们的 CI 检查关卡。
en: So here we have basically our CI gates in a way.

source_text: So you have um, you can think like a type checks,

source_text: And so
zh: 所以，
en: And so

en: I think in addition to that, because the agent as well wrote the tests, we as well looked into how do we actually ensure that the tests are actually testing the source code correctly.

source_text: So they had on one side some static checks where we noticed that the agents are sometimes in a way cheating and basically creating tests which are always true.
zh: 因此，我们一方面设置了静态检查，因为我们发现智能体有时会“作弊”，编写出无论如何都会通过的测试。
en: So they had on one side some static checks where we noticed that the agents are sometimes in a way cheating and basically creating tests which are always true.

source_text: And on the other side, um, we did mutation testing.
zh: 另一方面，我们还做了变异测试。
en: And on the other side, um, we did mutation testing.

source_text: And so what is mutation testing?
zh: 那么，什么是变异测试呢？
en: And so what is mutation testing?

source_text: Mutation testing means that um,
zh: 变异测试是指，嗯，
en: Mutation testing means that um,

source_text: you modify actually the source code.
zh: 你会实际修改源代码。
en: you modify actually the source code.

source_text: Um, you make small modifications, you introduce small bugs,
zh: 嗯，就是对源代码做些小改动，引入一些小错误，
en: Um, you make small modifications, you introduce small bugs,

source_text: and check um, whether the tests are failing if these bugs are introduced.
zh: 然后检查引入这些错误后，测试是否会失败。
en: and check um, whether the tests are failing if these bugs are introduced.

source_text: And so here is one example on the left side that for one component we had, we had a test coverage of nearly 90%.

en: And so here is one example on the left side that for one component we had, we had a test coverage of nearly 90%.

source_text: So it looked like that's great.
zh: 所以看起来，效果很不错。
en: So it looked like that's great.

source_text: But um, then we basically did the mutation testing.
zh: 但后来，我们又做了变异测试。
en: But um, then we basically did the mutation testing.

source_text: We noticed that only, I mean, less than 15% actually of the modifications were caught by the tests.

en: We noticed that only, I mean, less than 15% actually of the modifications were caught by the tests.

source_text: And so we use that to again basically um, that's a, I mean, via the agents improve basically the testing and now, I mean,

en: And so we use that to again basically um, that's a, I mean, via the agents improve basically the testing and now, I mean,

source_text: the whole repository we have there, I mean, around 98% code coverage and as well above 70% of the mutation tests are succeeding.

en: the whole repository we have there, I mean, around 98% code coverage and as well above 70% of the mutation tests are succeeding.

source_text: Okay, then um, the last component,
zh: 好的，接下来是最后一个组件，
en: Okay, then um, the last component,

source_text: that's like the visual check.

en: that's like the visual check.

source_text: So I think here, um, I mean, once the tests are, I mean,

en: So I think here, um, I mean, once the tests are, I mean,

source_text: passing, I mean, you are somewhat confident that is correct, but there are still certain class of, of problems you might not catch.
zh: 通过了，你会对结果的正确性有一定信心，但仍有一些问题可能检测不出来。
en: passing, I mean, you are somewhat confident that is correct, but there are still certain class of, of problems you might not catch.

source_text: And so for that, we basically let agents basically really go through the application, do screenshots, and then interpret the screenshots and check whether that's um, in the screenshot is actually what we expect.
zh: 所以为了解决这个问题，我们让智能体实际操作整个应用、截取屏幕画面，再分析截图，检查画面是否符合预期。
en: And so for that, we basically let agents basically really go through the application, do screenshots, and then interpret the screenshots and check whether that's um, in the screenshot is actually what we expect.

source_text: And so what does it mean?
zh: 那么，这具体是什么意思呢？
en: And so what does it mean?

source_text: So what basically stays on the human side and what can be done by the harness?

en: So what basically stays on the human side and what can be done by the harness?

source_text: So what stays human is the intent.

en: So what stays human is the intent.

source_text: So you need to basically clearly specify what you would like to do.
zh: 所以，你需要清楚地说明自己想做什么。
en: So you need to basically clearly specify what you would like to do.

source_text: And um, and yeah, what's basically, I mean, when is it considered done.
zh: 还有，什么情况下才算完成。
en: And um, and yeah, what's basically, I mean, when is it considered done.

source_text: Then you have choices.
zh: 然后，你就可以做出选择。
en: Then you have choices.

source_text: So I mean, especially if you look at UI code, I think it's a lot about as well about taste.
zh: 尤其是用户界面代码，我觉得很大程度上也取决于审美品位。
en: So I mean, especially if you look at UI code, I think it's a lot about as well about taste.

source_text: There's not something like which is wrong and something which is correct.
zh: 并不是说某个选择是错的，另一个就是对的。
en: There's not something like which is wrong and something which is correct.

source_text: And so therefore, I mean, there we for example use the mockups as well I think for architectural um,

en: And so therefore, I mean, there we for example use the mockups as well I think for architectural um,

source_text: you can basically let the agents suggest options and then choose.

en: you can basically let the agents suggest options and then choose.

source_text: Yeah,

en: Yeah,

source_text: the user experience is another part.

en: the user experience is another part.

source_text: I mean, I already mentioned this.

en: I mean, I already mentioned this.

source_text: I mean, I think UI, I think has a lot of um, yeah,
zh: 我觉得，用户界面这方面有很多……嗯，是的……
en: I mean, I think UI, I think has a lot of um, yeah,

source_text: taste and component.

en: taste and component.

source_text: I think for us it was as well the case that we still took some influence on the shape of the source code.

source_text: Where we noticed that um, yeah,

zh: 智能体提出的某些建议可能不太经得起未来变化的考验，所以我们也做了一些调整。
en: certain suggestions of the agent were basically maybe not that future proof and we um, yeah, influenced it.

source_text: I think what the harness owns is, is um, yeah, the contracts.

en: I think what the harness owns is, is um, yeah, the contracts.

source_text: Like, I mean, the lints, uh, linting, type checks, all that can be automatically handled.

source_text: Um, this basically our comparison to the legacy system, I think we can basically do these fidelity checks.

en: Um, this basically our comparison to the legacy system, I think we can basically do these fidelity checks.

source_text: Then, I mean, the testing and as well basically checking that the tests are actually meaningful.

en: Then, I mean, the testing and as well basically checking that the tests are actually meaningful.

source_text: That can be done by the harness.

en: That can be done by the harness.

source_text: And as well visual verification.
zh: 还有视觉效果的验证。
en: And as well visual verification.

source_text: And so what did we, um, yeah, catch with our, I mean, were basically our harness more successful and which are basically still gaps we are having.

en: And so what did we, um, yeah, catch with our, I mean, were basically our harness more successful and which are basically still gaps we are having.

source_text: So, I mean,

source_text: we are having basically now, I mean, we detect basically if a test checks and which sometimes with AI happens.

en: we are having basically now, I mean, we detect basically if a test checks and which sometimes with AI happens.

source_text: And as well even more important, I mean, the mutation tests were basically the test is still basically, I mean, working is still doing something, but it's really doing, I mean,

en: And as well even more important, I mean, the mutation tests were basically the test is still basically, I mean, working is still doing something, but it's really doing, I mean,

source_text: it's not really um, completely checking the application.

en: it's not really um, completely checking the application.

source_text: I mean, in Vue.js, we have as well basically compiler macros.

en: I mean, in Vue.js, we have as well basically compiler macros.

source_text: So that's basically situations which we cannot do the mutation testing.
zh: 所以，遇到这种情况，我们就无法进行变异测试。
en: So that's basically situations which we cannot do the mutation testing.

source_text: So that's at least something we highlight.
zh: 所以，这至少是我们会特别指出的一点。
en: So that's at least something we highlight.

source_text: And then,
zh: 然后，
en: And then,

source_text: I mean, for new code, we basically, I mean, yeah, via code coverage reports basically ensure that um,
zh: 对于新代码，我们基本上会通过代码覆盖率报告来确保……
en: I mean, for new code, we basically, I mean, yeah, via code coverage reports basically ensure that um,

source_text: new code always um, gets tested.
zh: 新代码总是会经过测试。
en: new code always um, gets tested.

source_text: Yeah, what our harness is still missing and still currently,

en: Yeah, what our harness is still missing and still currently,

source_text: I mean, manual is um, environment assumptions.

en: I mean, manual is um, environment assumptions.

source_text: So I mean, we had bugs where basically the time zone played a role or, I mean, different browsers have different results.

en: So I mean, we had bugs where basically the time zone played a role or, I mean, different browsers have different results.

zh: 在这里我有两个非常好的呃方法可以分享给大家。
en: I have two really useful ways to do that, and I’d like to share them with you.

source_text: 第一个是我觉得大家可以经常去看社媒上的use case。
zh: 第一个是我觉得大家可以经常去看社媒上的use case。
en: First, I think you should regularly look at examples of how people are using AI on social media.

source_text: 就其实我经常看的社媒是X，因为我觉得在X上有很多很多的大佬会去分享他们可能是一些拿到内测名单，
zh: 就其实我经常看的社媒是X，因为我觉得在X上有很多很多的大佬会去分享他们可能是一些拿到内测名单，
en: I mostly use X, because a lot of experts there share what they’re doing with new tools they’ve gotten early access to.

source_text: 他们会分享他们在提前做的use case use case。
zh: 他们会分享他们在提前做的use case use case。
en: They share examples of what they’re doing with those tools before they’re widely available.

source_text: 就比如说最近有一个这个视频特别火，你们也看到，就是我当时截图的时候在浏览量是130万，就FIBO 5.5做的一个视频。
zh: 就比如说最近有一个这个视频特别火，你们也看到，就是我当时截图的时候在浏览量是130万，就FIBO 5.5做的一个视频。
en: For example, there’s a video that’s been going viral recently—you may have seen it. When I took this screenshot, it had 1.3 million views. It was made with Veo 5.5.

source_text: 那在这个时候我就会有一个印象说现在FIBO 5.5能做这么厉害的视频了吗？
zh: 那在这个时候我就会有一个印象说现在FIBO 5.5能做这么厉害的视频了吗？
en: That’s when I start to think, “Wow, can Veo 5.5 make videos this good now?”

source_text: 所以如果当这个我可以使用FIBO 5.5的时候，我也会第一时间去尝试说用FIBO 5.5去做这样的case。
zh: 所以如果当这个我可以使用FIBO 5.5的时候，我也会第一时间去尝试说用FIBO 5.5去做这样的case。
en: So as soon as I get access to Veo 5.5, I’ll try using it to make something like that myself.

source_text: 那比如说Opus 5.5的时候，我当时就看到这样的一些例子，
zh: 那比如说Opus 5.5的时候，我当时就看到这样的一些例子，
en: For example, when Opus 5.5 came out, I saw examples like these.

source_text: 然后这时我也知道就是说Opus 5.5通过它的中等的effort都能做这么好的一个case，
zh: 然后这时我也知道就是说Opus 5.5通过它的中等的effort都能做这么好的一个case，
en: And that showed me that Opus 5.5 could produce something this good even at a medium effort setting.

source_text: 那我觉得其实在AI的3D呃能力上是有所突破的。
zh: 那我觉得其实在AI的3D呃能力上是有所突破的。
en: So I think that represents a real breakthrough in AI’s 3D capabilities.

source_text: 第二个就是我觉得在新模型发布的第一瞬间，我都会用各种的提示词去进行测试。
zh: 第二个就是我觉得在新模型发布的第一瞬间，我都会用各种的提示词去进行测试。
en: Second, whenever a new model is released, I immediately test it with a variety of prompts.

source_text: 不管是从3D前端还是代码，我都有自己的提示词去进行测试，然后分享一个当时我测试的case。
zh: 不管是从3D前端还是代码，我都有自己的提示词去进行测试，然后分享一个当时我测试的case。
en: Whether it’s 3D, front-end development, or coding, I have my own prompts for testing. Let me share one example from a test I ran at the time.

source_text: 在GPT-6 Astra出来的时候，当时我的第一瞬第一时间也是用我自己的提示词去进行了case。
zh: 在GPT-6 Astra出来的时候，当时我的第一瞬第一时间也是用我自己的提示词去进行了case。
en: When GPT-6 Astra came out, the first thing I did was test it with my own prompts.

source_text: 嗯，去测试，然后我发现它在3D能力上是有所突破的，而且很强。
zh: 嗯，去测试，然后我发现它在3D能力上是有所突破的，而且很强。
en: I tested it and found that it had made a real breakthrough in 3D—and that it was very capable.

source_text: 所以当时我就尝试去复刻了一个移民员的这种3D场景。
zh: 所以当时我就尝试去复刻了一个移民员的这种3D场景。
en: So I tried to recreate a 3D scene featuring an immigration officer.

source_text: 这其实这个场景是我当时直接一个提示词直接出的。
zh: 这其实这个场景是我当时直接一个提示词直接出的。
en: I actually generated this entire scene with a single prompt.

source_text: 所以当时做出了这个use case后我就明白说现在GPT-6 Astra是代表了AI可以做3D的一个零件点。
zh: 所以当时做出了这个use case后我就明白说现在GPT-6 Astra是代表了AI可以做3D的一个零件点。
en: So after creating that use case, I realized GPT-6 Astra marked a turning point for AI-generated 3D.

source_text: 所以以前的话就是大家用AI去生成的3D建模都是全是slop，做的很差。
zh: 所以以前的话就是大家用AI去生成的3D建模都是全是slop，做的很差。
en: Before that, the 3D models people generated with AI were mostly slop—they were really poorly made.

source_text: 但现在我觉得在GPT-6 Astra出来那一瞬间，我就知道现在嗯是AI是完全可以完成3D建模。
zh: 但现在我觉得在GPT-6 Astra出来那一瞬间，我就知道现在嗯是AI是完全可以完成3D建模。
en: But the moment GPT-6 Astra came out, I knew AI could now handle 3D modeling on its own.

source_text: 所以当时才有了后续的《小王子》这个游戏。
zh: 所以当时才有了后续的《小王子》这个游戏。
en: That’s what led me to create The Little Prince game.

source_text: 所以我是完全知道在做《小王子》的时候它是能做出来，只是我需要花时间去打磨。
zh: 所以我是完全知道在做《小王子》的时候它是能做出来，只是我需要花时间去打磨。
en: So when I started making The Little Prince, I knew it was possible. I just needed to put in the time to polish it.

source_text: 第二个我觉得很重要的一个能能力是具备审美的能力。
zh: 第二个我觉得很重要的一个能能力是具备审美的能力。
en: The second ability I think is really important is having an eye for aesthetics.

source_text: 就你需要知道什么是好的审美，什么是不好的审美，这也可以分享一个比较有意思的题外话，
zh: 就你需要知道什么是好的审美，什么是不好的审美，这也可以分享一个比较有意思的题外话，
en: You need to know what looks good and what doesn’t. That reminds me of an interesting side story.

source_text: 就是其实我在大学的时候很多同学会吐槽我说我的审美能力不太行。
zh: 就是其实我在大学的时候很多同学会吐槽我说我的审美能力不太行。
en: Actually, back in college, a lot of my classmates would tease me for not having a very good eye for design.

source_text: 确实我也觉得我当时的审美能力不太行，但是我觉得所有的能力都是你可以培养的。
zh: 确实我也觉得我当时的审美能力不太行，但是我觉得所有的能力都是你可以培养的。
en: Honestly, I agree that my eye for design wasn’t very good back then. But I believe any skill can be developed.

source_text: 然后其实在我做自媒体的嗯这个阶段的时候，我就发现只要有审美的作品都会被大家去嗯就是会受到大家喜欢，
zh: 然后其实在我做自媒体的嗯这个阶段的时候，我就发现只要有审美的作品都会被大家去嗯就是会受到大家喜欢，
en: Then, when I started creating content online, I noticed that people really responded to work that looked good.

source_text: 也会被大家就是会很有很很好的浏览，很高的浏览量。
zh: 也会被大家就是会很有很很好的浏览，很高的浏览量。
en: And it would get a lot of views, too.

source_text: 那我也会给大家分享一个我怎么去嗯培养我平时审美的方法。
zh: 那我也会给大家分享一个我怎么去嗯培养我平时审美的方法。
en: So I’d like to share how I’ve developed my eye for design.

source_text: 就是我自己会帮所有我认为好的审美的case记在Lotion数据库中，但这都其实是agent帮我去整理，然后发的。
zh: 就是我自己会帮所有我认为好的审美的case记在Lotion数据库中，但这都其实是agent帮我去整理，然后发的。
en: I save every example of good design I come across in a Notion database, though an AI agent actually organizes and posts them for me.

source_text: 然后这只是我放的一个小的片段啊，它就会定期给我整理，然后我也会定期去看里面的一些好的case。
zh: 然后这只是我放的一个小的片段啊，它就会定期给我整理，然后我也会定期去看里面的一些好的case。
en: This is just a small sample. The agent organizes them for me regularly, and I go back from time to time to look through some of the good examples.

source_text: 那这些都是其实大家就是在嗯社媒上一些我觉得做的比较好的case，然后就放进来。
zh: 那这些都是其实大家就是在嗯社媒上一些我觉得做的比较好的case，然后就放进来。
en: These are all examples I’ve found on social media that I think are particularly well done, so I save them here.

source_text: 其实这有两个好处，第一个就是说它可以培养我的审美能力。
zh: 其实这有两个好处，第一个就是说它可以培养我的审美能力。
en: There are two benefits to this. First, it helps me develop my eye for design.

source_text: 其实你们可以看从这个截图上都可以去知道这些其实是非常好的审美case。
zh: 其实你们可以看从这个截图上都可以去知道这些其实是非常好的审美case。
en: You can tell from this screenshot that these are all great examples of good design.

source_text: 第二个就是我也可以从中获得特别多的灵感来源。
zh: 第二个就是我也可以从中获得特别多的灵感来源。
en: Second, I can draw a lot of inspiration from them.

source_text: 就我觉得一个人如果是从0到1的创新是特别难的，但如果说你经常去看一些大家好的这种case，你是其实可以获得特别多的灵感的。
zh: 就我觉得一个人如果是从0到1的创新是特别难的，但如果说你经常去看一些大家好的这种case，你是其实可以获得特别多的灵感的。
en: I think creating something entirely from scratch is really hard. But if you regularly look at great examples of other people’s work, you can find a lot of inspiration.

source_text: 然后第三个我觉得就是呃一个比较重要的是你需要懂社媒，因为我觉得在AI时代到来的时候，
zh: 然后第三个我觉得就是呃一个比较重要的是你需要懂社媒，因为我觉得在AI时代到来的时候，
en: And third, I think it’s important to understand social media, because as we enter the age of AI...

source_text: 其实就有很多人去提出要building public。我觉得这个非常重要。
zh: 其实就有很多人去提出要building public。我觉得这个非常重要。
en: A lot of people are talking about “building in public,” and I think that’s really important.

source_text: 而building public的关键就是你需要去懂嗯社交媒体。
zh: 而building public的关键就是你需要去懂嗯社交媒体。
en: And the key to building in public is understanding social media.

source_text: 就你就要需要大家喜欢什么，什么人什么会愿意让人转发什么的内容汇报。
zh: 就你就要需要大家喜欢什么，什么人什么会愿意让人转发什么的内容汇报。
en: You need to understand what people like and what kinds of content they’re willing to share.

source_text: 我也可以在这里又给大家分享一个题外话，就是当时我在前一天和朋友吃饭的时候，然后我要就是后一天我要发布《小王子》，
zh: 我也可以在这里又给大家分享一个题外话，就是当时我在前一天和朋友吃饭的时候，然后我要就是后一天我要发布《小王子》，
en: Here’s a quick aside: I was having dinner with a friend the day before I was going to publish *The Little Prince*.

source_text: 朋友说你觉得你的《小王子》能跑多少万的流量？
zh: 朋友说你觉得你的《小王子》能跑多少万的流量？
en: My friend asked, “How many tens of thousands of views do you think your *Little Prince* post will get?”

source_text: 然后我说我可以跑300万的流量在X上，并且嗯就是刚我们一开始看到的时候有在微信公众号有抖音有小红书的转发，
zh: 然后我说我可以跑300万的流量在X上，并且嗯就是刚我们一开始看到的时候有在微信公众号有抖音有小红书的转发，
en: I said, “I think it can get three million views on X.” And as we saw at the beginning, it was also shared on WeChat, Douyin, and Xiaohongshu.

source_text: 其实这些我都不是很意外，因为其实我是非常懂这个社媒的传播机制的，我是非常相信X上的好的东西会被社媒去国内的社媒转发，
zh: 其实这些我都不是很意外，因为其实我是非常懂这个社媒的传播机制的，我是非常相信X上的好的东西会被社媒去国内的社媒转发，
en: None of that really surprised me, because I understand how things spread on social media. I was confident that something good on X would get picked up and shared on Chinese platforms.

source_text: 因为它整个的传播机制就是这样。
zh: 因为它整个的传播机制就是这样。
en: Because that’s how the whole sharing ecosystem works.

source_text: 因为很多的AI的一手新闻都是在X诞生，所有国内的相关的媒体它都会关注X上的一些爆款内容去作为他们的选题。
zh: 因为很多的AI的一手新闻都是在X诞生，所有国内的相关的媒体它都会关注X上的一些爆款内容去作为他们的选题。
en: A lot of breaking AI news originates on X, so Chinese media outlets watch for viral posts there and use them as story ideas.

source_text: 所以其实在《小王子》发布的第二天，就有很多国内的这种媒体或者KOL去嗯进行转发。
zh: 所以其实在《小王子》发布的第二天，就有很多国内的这种媒体或者KOL去嗯进行转发。
en: So the day after I published *The Little Prince*, a lot of Chinese media outlets and influencers shared it.

source_text: 所以我觉得在这个时所以当时看到有这么多的人的喜欢和曝光，其实这其实有有点意料之内吧。
zh: 所以我觉得在这个时所以当时看到有这么多的人的喜欢和曝光，其实这其实有有点意料之内吧。
en: So when I saw how much people liked it and how much exposure it got, it was more or less what I’d expected.

source_text: 对，
zh: 对，
en: Right.

source_text: 就是在我的一个意料之内。
zh: 就是在我的一个意料之内。
en: It was pretty much what I expected.

source_text: 所以我觉得懂什么是社媒也非常重要，因为你不能只做出产品，但你也需要让啊大家知道你的就是大家你知道你的产品是什么样子。
zh: 所以我觉得懂什么是社媒也非常重要，因为你不能只做出产品，但你也需要让啊大家知道你的就是大家你知道你的产品是什么样子。
en: So I think understanding social media is really important. You can’t just build a product; you also need to let people know what it is and what it can do.

source_text: 我觉得这个挺重要的。
zh: 我觉得这个挺重要的。
en: I think that’s really important.

source_text: 然后我觉得就讲完了一些理论部分，就是为什么我可以做出《小王子》，那我们就进入一些实操部分。
zh: 然后我觉得就讲完了一些理论部分，就是为什么我可以做出《小王子》，那我们就进入一些实操部分。
en: Now that I’ve covered the theory behind how I was able to create *The Little Prince*, let’s move on to the practical side.

source_text: 就整体的游戏制作流程是什么样的，然后你也可以通过这个实操流程去尝试做你的第一款AI 3D游戏。
zh: 就整体的游戏制作流程是什么样的，然后你也可以通过这个实操流程去尝试做你的第一款AI 3D游戏。
en: I’ll walk you through the full game development process, so you can follow the steps and try making your first AI-powered 3D game.

source_text: 然后我觉得在游戏制作流程中有两个比较重要板块，一个是场景设计和角色制作。
zh: 然后我觉得在游戏制作流程中有两个比较重要板块，一个是场景设计和角色制作。
en: In the game development process, I think two areas are especially important: environment design and character creation.

source_text: 那我们先讲我先讲解一下当时我做《小王子》的时候的一个整体流程。
zh: 那我们先讲我先讲解一下当时我做《小王子》的时候的一个整体流程。
en: Let me start by walking you through the overall process I followed when making *The Little Prince*.

source_text: 呃就在这里的话我是让FIBO 5.1去负责了整体的设计，Opus 5.5编写了整体的代码，呃然后Codex是进行了一个迭代，
zh: 呃就在这里的话我是让FIBO 5.1去负责了整体的设计，Opus 5.5编写了整体的代码，呃然后Codex是进行了一个迭代，
en: Here, I had FIBO 5.1 handle the overall design, Opus 5.5 write the code, and Codex refine it through further iterations.

source_text: 然后你也会使用到3D的生成模型去生成一些资产。
zh: 然后你也会使用到3D的生成模型去生成一些资产。
en: You’ll also use 3D generation models to create some assets.

source_text: 在这里我使用的是Triple，但你会要同时下载Blender CI和Unity CI。
zh: 在这里我使用的是Triple，但你会要同时下载Blender CI和Unity CI。
en: I used Triple here, but you’ll also need to download Blender CI and Unity CI.

source_text: 然后就到产品制作流程，第一个步骤是你需要去生成对应的参考图。
zh: 然后就到产品制作流程，第一个步骤是你需要去生成对应的参考图。
en: Now let’s move on to the production workflow. The first step is to generate the reference images you need.

source_text: 在生成参考图的时候，我可以有两点我可以给大家嗯我觉得需要注意一下，就第一个是在俯视图的时候是特别重要的，
zh: 在生成参考图的时候，我可以有两点我可以给大家嗯我觉得需要注意一下，就第一个是在俯视图的时候是特别重要的，
en: When generating reference images, there are two things I think you should keep in mind. First, the top-down view is especially important.

source_text: 因为俯视图AI可以详细的参考你的俯视图去了解整个场景的一个布置，这样的话你的嗯制作整个流程会事半功倍。
zh: 因为俯视图AI可以详细的参考你的俯视图去了解整个场景的一个布置，这样的话你的嗯制作整个流程会事半功倍。
en: A top-down view lets the AI see exactly how the scene is laid out. That makes the rest of the production process much more efficient.

source_text: 第二个大家也可以像我这样去生成一个完整的参考图，就这是我觉得方便文献管理。
zh: 第二个大家也可以像我这样去生成一个完整的参考图，就这是我觉得方便文献管理。
en: Second, you can generate a complete reference sheet like I did. I find it makes the references easier to organize.

source_text: 然后我也帮我提示词放在上面，
zh: 然后我也帮我提示词放在上面，
en: I’ve also put my prompt up there for you.

source_text: 就是让AI就生成一个全面的全面参考图片，但是也包括了场景的一些细节。
zh: 就是让AI就生成一个全面的全面参考图片，但是也包括了场景的一些细节。
en: The idea is to have the AI generate a comprehensive reference image that also shows some of the scene’s details.

source_text: 然后第二个就是其实要制作3D资产，其实因为我是一个完全不懂建模的人，
zh: 然后第二个就是其实要制作3D资产，其实因为我是一个完全不懂建模的人，
en: The second step is creating the 3D assets. Since I don’t know how to model at all,

source_text: 其实我也不知道哪些资产需要用专业的3D模型去生成，哪些资产是直接通过Blender就可以完成的。
zh: 其实我也不知道哪些资产需要用专业的3D模型去生成，哪些资产是直接通过Blender就可以完成的。
en: I wasn’t sure which assets needed to be generated as professional 3D models and which ones I could create directly in Blender.

source_text: 所以其实我也是就是这也是我当时总结一个提示词，因为我觉得就是帮你的技术路线告诉他，然后呃让他去分析参考图，
zh: 所以其实我也是就是这也是我当时总结一个提示词，因为我觉得就是帮你的技术路线告诉他，然后呃让他去分析参考图，
en: So I put together a prompt that explains my technical approach and asks the AI to analyze the reference image.

source_text: 他就可以告诉你哪些是可以用3D资产去生成，哪些是你需要去建模。
zh: 他就可以告诉你哪些是可以用3D资产去生成，哪些是你需要去建模。
en: Then it can tell you which elements can be generated as 3D assets and which ones you’ll need to model yourself.
