source_text: So I asked Claude to check the Pipecab docs, and write a Pipecab audio simulation to simulate a Chinese speaker being really undecided when they're ordering their bubble tea. Um, this is what it generated.
zh: 所以我让 Claude 查阅 Pipecab 的文档，写一个 Pipecab 音频模拟，模拟一位说中文的顾客点奶茶时特别犹豫的情景。嗯，这就是它生成的内容。
en: So I asked Claude to check the Pipecab docs, and write a Pipecab audio simulation to simulate a Chinese speaker being really undecided when they're ordering their bubble tea. Um, this is what it generated.

source_text: Oh,
zh: 哦，
en: Oh,

source_text: there's some, some.
zh: 有一些……一些。
en: there's some, some.

source_text: Chinese you can see some of the Chinese characters there.
zh: 中文，你可以看到那里有一些汉字。
en: Chinese you can see some of the Chinese characters there.

source_text: Obviously, I'm not quite sure what this says, but luckily, I can have the success criteria,
zh: 显然，我不太确定这段中文写的是什么，不过好在我可以设定成功标准，
en: Obviously, I'm not quite sure what this says, but luckily, I can have the success criteria,

source_text: criteria written in English.
zh: 用英文写出来。
en: criteria written in English.

source_text: So I don't need necessarily need to know the test,
zh: 所以我不一定需要知道测试的具体内容，
en: So I don't need necessarily need to know the test,

source_text: but I can check double-check the success side.
zh: 不过，我可以再核对一下成功标准。
en: but I can check double-check the success side.

source_text: So we can.
zh: 所以我们可以。
en: So we can.

source_text: Run these evaluations either in a text mode or audio mode.
zh: 可以在文本模式或音频模式下运行这些评估。
en: Run these evaluations either in a text mode or audio mode.

source_text: So text mode is way faster because you don't have to generate any of the audio.
zh: 所以文本模式快得多，因为不需要生成音频。
en: So text mode is way faster because you don't have to generate any of the audio.

source_text: Uh, also means you're using very few tokens, and you use basically no tokens if you're using a local LLM as a judge.
zh: 呃，这也意味着消耗的 token 很少；如果用本地大语言模型来评判，基本就不需要消耗额外的 token。
en: Uh, also means you're using very few tokens, and you use basically no tokens if you're using a local LLM as a judge.

source_text: And audio mode uncovers issues that text mode just won't surface so.
zh: 而音频模式能发现一些文本模式根本发现不了的问题。
en: And audio mode uncovers issues that text mode just won't surface so.

source_text: So a great example is this.
zh: 这就是一个很好的例子。
en: So a great example is this.

source_text: When I was running audio mode, uh, I discovered there was a bug in the speech-to-text processor.
zh: 我在运行音频模式时，呃，发现语音转文字模块有一个 bug。
en: When I was running audio mode, uh, I discovered there was a bug in the speech-to-text processor.

source_text: Uh, sometimes when I said "chubing," which means no ice, it heard it as "too ping," which is like a weird mix of English and Chinese.
zh: 呃，有时候我说“去冰”，意思是不要冰，它却识别成“too ping”，听起来像是英语和中文混在一起的怪词。
en: Uh, sometimes when I said "chubing," which means no ice, it heard it as "too ping," which is like a weird mix of English and Chinese.

source_text: I was saying "two bottles."
zh: 我说的是“两瓶”。
en: I was saying "two bottles."

source_text: Uh,
zh: 呃，
en: Uh,

source_text: and that's an issue where a pure text mode test just would never have caught.
zh: 而这个问题，纯文本模式的测试根本发现不了。
en: and that's an issue where a pure text mode test just would never have caught.

source_text: And that's the problem number three.
zh: 这就是第三个问题。
en: And that's the problem number three.

source_text: I don't have to speak the whole call every more.
zh: 我不用再全程说话了。
en: I don't have to speak the whole call every more.

source_text: I don't have to manually test this.
zh: 我不用再手动测试这个了。
en: I don't have to manually test this.

source_text: I can run 10, 20, 100 simulations all at the same time every time I make a small change and see if that's improved my voice agent.
zh: 每次做一点小改动，我都可以同时运行 10 次、20 次甚至 100 次模拟，看看我的语音助手有没有变得更好。
en: I can run 10, 20, 100 simulations all at the same time every time I make a small change and see if that's improved my voice agent.

source_text: So here's a clip of one of the simulations. Uh, to see what it sounds like.
zh: 下面放一段模拟测试的录音，听听效果怎么样。
en: So here's a clip of one of the simulations. Uh, to see what it sounds like.

source_text: Hi Holly.
zh: 嗨，霍莉。
en: Hi Holly.

source_text: 今天想喝什么？
zh: 今天想喝什么？
en: What would you like to drink today?

source_text: 请问你刚刚说什么呢？
zh: 请问你刚刚说什么呢？
en: Sorry, what did you just say?

source_text: 请问你有推荐的奶茶吗？
zh: 请问你有推荐的奶茶吗？
en: Could you recommend a milk tea?

source_text: 我们刚为你光临，推荐奶茶的话，精品奶茶名为乌龙奶茶或珍珠奶茶。
zh: 我们刚为你光临，推荐奶茶的话，精品奶茶名为乌龙奶茶或珍珠奶茶。
en: Welcome! If you’d like a recommendation, try our oolong milk tea or bubble tea.

source_text: So this voice agent did a much better job than me, uh, on this.
zh: 所以在这件事上，这个语音助手做得比我好多了。
en: So this voice agent did a much better job than me, uh, on this.

source_text: And it could generate even more and more and more different scenarios.
zh: 而且它还能生成越来越多不同的场景。
en: And it could generate even more and more and more different scenarios.

source_text: So as Claude builds the checks,
zh: 所以，在 Claude 编写这些检查项的同时，
en: So as Claude builds the checks,

source_text: it adds new features and fixes bugs,
zh: 它还会添加新功能、修复漏洞，
en: it adds new features and fixes bugs,

source_text: which produces more checks, which adds new features and fixes bugs, which produces more checks and adds new features and fixes bugs.
zh: 这又会生成更多检查项，进而添加新功能、修复漏洞；然后再生成更多检查项，继续添加新功能、修复漏洞。
en: which produces more checks, which adds new features and fixes bugs, which produces more checks and adds new features and fixes bugs.

source_text: That's the loop.
zh: 这就形成了一个循环。
en: That's the loop.

source_text: So machines are doing the work, judges are checking the work, and then humans check the judges.
zh: 所以，机器负责干活，评判模型负责检查成果，最后由人来核查评判模型。
en: So machines are doing the work, judges are checking the work, and then humans check the judges.

source_text: So whatever you're building, I really challenge y'all to start thinking in loops.
zh: 所以，不管你们在打造什么，我都希望大家开始用循环的思维去思考。
en: So whatever you're building, I really challenge y'all to start thinking in loops.

source_text: So I've already got the bubble tea voice agent handled, so you're probably not gonna be building that.
zh: 奶茶语音助手这块我已经搞定了，所以你们大概不用再做这个了。
en: So I've already got the bubble tea voice agent handled, so you're probably not gonna be building that.

source_text: But the same ideas apply for any sort of agent where you don't have business domain expertise.
zh: 但对于任何你不具备相关业务领域专业知识的智能体，这套思路同样适用。
en: But the same ideas apply for any sort of agent where you don't have business domain expertise.

source_text: So for example, you might be building an outbound sales agent selling insurance, but you don't know anything about insurance.
zh: 比如，你可能在开发一个推销保险的外呼销售智能体，但你对保险一窍不通。
en: So for example, you might be building an outbound sales agent selling insurance, but you don't know anything about insurance.

source_text: Uh, you could have, uh, you could tell the LLM to act like an insurance agent, agent.
zh: 呃，你可以让大语言模型扮演一名保险代理人。
en: Uh, you could have, uh, you could tell the LLM to act like an insurance agent, agent.

source_text: You might be doing inbound support for an auto shop, and you don't know anything about cars or being a mechanic.
zh: 你可能在为一家汽车修理店开发来电客服，但你既不懂车，也不了解修车。
en: You might be doing inbound support for an auto shop, and you don't know anything about cars or being a mechanic.

source_text: Again, you can give it, give the LLM a scenario to act like a mechanic.
zh: 同样，你可以给大语言模型设定一个场景，让它扮演汽车维修技师。
en: Again, you can give it, give the LLM a scenario to act like a mechanic.

source_text: Or you could even build a voice agent to control a robot and go through and test simulations with that.
zh: 你甚至可以开发一个语音智能体来控制机器人，再用它运行模拟场景进行测试。
en: Or you could even build a voice agent to control a robot and go through and test simulations with that.

source_text: So as.
zh: 所以，作为……
en: So as.

source_text: My bubble tea ordering skills, I am proud to say I no longer order just Jinju Naicha.
zh: 说到点珍珠奶茶，我很自豪地说，现在我点单可不只是会说“珍珠奶茶”了。
en: My bubble tea ordering skills, I am proud to say I no longer order just Jinju Naicha.

source_text: I can no longer, I can now order Donghua Cha, Jia Qiu Qiu, Chubing,
zh: 我现在还能点冬瓜茶，加QQ，去冰。
en: I can no longer, I can now order Donghua Cha, Jia Qiu Qiu, Chubing,

source_text: Weitang, Waidai.
zh: 微糖，外带。
en: Weitang, Waidai.

source_text: So I still.
zh: 所以我还是……
en: So I still.

source_text: Can't read the whole menu, but I can order this.
zh: 虽然看不懂整份菜单，但至少我会点这个了。
en: Can't read the whole menu, but I can order this.

source_text: So build what you can't check, and then check the checkers.
zh: 所以，先构建那些你无法直接检验的东西，然后再检验负责检验它们的工具。
en: So build what you can't check, and then check the checkers.

source_text: Thanks so much. My name's James Hush. If you wanna learn about voice agents, just scan the QR code. And have a great day.
zh: 非常感谢大家！我叫詹姆斯·哈什。如果想了解语音智能体，扫一下二维码就行。祝大家今天愉快！
en: Thanks so much. My name's James Hush. If you wanna learn about voice agents, just scan the QR code. And have a great day.

source_text: Thanks, James, for a very interesting sharing.
zh: 谢谢詹姆斯带来的精彩分享。
en: Thanks, James, for a very interesting sharing.

source_text: I hope everyone knows that how to order bubble tea in different languages now.
zh: 希望大家现在都学会用不同语言点珍珠奶茶了。
en: I hope everyone knows that how to order bubble tea in different languages now.

source_text: Okay, now let's welcome Satvik from the AI Center of National University of Singapore to give us a speech about the good, the bad, and the ugly.
zh: 好，接下来有请新加坡国立大学人工智能中心的 Satvik，为我们带来题为《好、坏与丑》的演讲。
en: Okay, now let's welcome Satvik from the AI Center of National University of Singapore to give us a speech about the good, the bad, and the ugly.

source_text: 因为你在发现了这一幕。
zh: 因为你在发现了这一幕。
en: Because you discovered what was happening.

source_text: 嗯，
zh: 嗯，
en: Um.

source_text: 你只分成2026。
zh: 你只分成2026。
en: You only divided it into 2026.

source_text: All right.
zh: 好的。
en: All right.

source_text: You all must be wondering, what is this audio clip about?
zh: 大家一定在想，这段音频讲的是什么？
en: You all must be wondering, what is this audio clip about?

source_text: And why is it the first thing that I played in my talk?
zh: 为什么我一开场就播放了这段音频？
en: And why is it the first thing that I played in my talk?

source_text: So this is one of our users who's trying to practice speak Chinese by talking to our voice agent.
zh: 这是一位用户，正在通过和我们的语音智能体对话来练习说中文。
en: So this is one of our users who's trying to practice speak Chinese by talking to our voice agent.

source_text: Now, if you're a native Chinese speaker, did you hear her say the word Shanghai?
zh: 那么，如果你的母语是中文，你听到她说“上海”这个词了吗？
en: Now, if you're a native Chinese speaker, did you hear her say the word Shanghai?

source_text: I believe no, right?
zh: 我想没有，对吧？
en: I believe no, right?

source_text: Because she didn't. And I promise I didn't purposefully add in Shanghai here.
zh: 因为她根本没说。而且我保证，我不是故意在这里加上“上海”的。
en: Because she didn't. And I promise I didn't purposefully add in Shanghai here.

source_text: Apparently, the STT model knew I would be in Shanghai for this talk.
zh: 看来，语音转文字模型早就知道我会来上海做这场演讲。
en: Apparently, the STT model knew I would be in Shanghai for this talk.

source_text: Uh, hello, everyone.
zh: 呃，大家好。
en: Uh, hello, everyone.

source_text: I'm Satvik, and I've been building voice agents for more than two years now.
zh: 我是萨特维克，开发语音智能体已经两年多了。
en: I'm Satvik, and I've been building voice agents for more than two years now.

source_text: My agents deploy to production,
zh: 我开发的智能体已经部署到了生产环境，
en: My agents deploy to production,

source_text: have run thousands of real sessions,
zh: 已经完成了数千次真实用户会话，
en: have run thousands of real sessions,

source_text: and from my experience, I can say that speech-to-text is a very important component of voice agents.
zh: 根据我的经验，语音转文字是语音智能体中非常重要的一环。
en: and from my experience, I can say that speech-to-text is a very important component of voice agents.

source_text: Speech-to-text models have been around for years, and people think they're the salt part.
zh: 语音转文字模型已经问世多年，大家觉得它是比较简单的部分。
en: Speech-to-text models have been around for years, and people think they're the salt part.

source_text: But here's what we see.
zh: 但实际情况是这样的。
en: But here's what we see.

source_text: This is what the speaker was actually saying in this audio. But our speech-to-text model transcribes something entirely else.
zh: 这才是演讲者在这段音频中实际说的话，但我们的语音转文字模型却转录出了完全不同的内容。
en: This is what the speaker was actually saying in this audio. But our speech-to-text model transcribes something entirely else.

source_text: But let's go ahead and take a look at what went wrong here.
zh: 不过，我们先来看看这里到底出了什么问题。
en: But let's go ahead and take a look at what went wrong here.

source_text: So in just two sentences, our speech-to-text model came up with different kinds of errors.
zh: 短短两句话里，我们的语音转文字模型就犯了好几种不同的错误。
en: So in just two sentences, our speech-to-text model came up with different kinds of errors.

source_text: It added in foreign script, it wrote the wrong characters,
zh: 它混入了外文字符，还把字写错了，
en: It added in foreign script, it wrote the wrong characters,

source_text: and then it dropped the words that it couldn't catch.
zh: 然后，它漏掉了没听清的词。
en: and then it dropped the words that it couldn't catch.

source_text: Now, after looking.
zh: 现在，看过之后。
en: Now, after looking.

source_text: At these errors,
zh: 这些错误，
en: At these errors,

source_text: I wanted to see what is the frequency of such errors within our app. So we began to investigate, and this is what we found out.
zh: 我想看看这类错误在我们的应用中出现得有多频繁。于是我们展开了调查，结果发现了这些情况。
en: I wanted to see what is the frequency of such errors within our app. So we began to investigate, and this is what we found out.

source_text: Almost one in four of our practice sessions contained text that no one said.
zh: 我们的练习中，近四分之一的场次都出现了没人说过的文字。
en: Almost one in four of our practice sessions contained text that no one said.

source_text: This is a big number, and it directly impacts the quality of our voice agent's replies.
zh: 这个比例相当高，而且直接影响了我们语音助手的回复质量。
en: This is a big number, and it directly impacts the quality of our voice agent's replies.

source_text: So before we see how does it impact our voice agent, we need to take a look at how a voice agent works first.
zh: 所以，在看这些错误如何影响我们的语音助手之前，我们得先了解语音助手是怎么工作的。
en: So before we see how does it impact our voice agent, we need to take a look at how a voice agent works first.

source_text: So meet Lao Shi,
zh: 那么，来认识一下老史吧。
en: So meet Lao Shi,

source_text: who's our teacher and our voice agent within our app.
zh: 他是我们应用里的老师，也是我们的语音助手。
en: who's our teacher and our voice agent within our app.

source_text: She listens to our users,
zh: 她会倾听用户说话，
en: She listens to our users,

source_text: she thinks about how to respond back, and then she speaks out the response back to the user.
zh: 她会思考该如何回应，然后把回答说给用户听。
en: she thinks about how to respond back, and then she speaks out the response back to the user.

source_text: In this talk, we'll just be focusing on the listening part.
zh: 这次演讲，我们只关注“听”这个环节。
en: In this talk, we'll just be focusing on the listening part.

source_text: So what happens when a user starts speaking?
zh: 那么，用户开始说话时，会发生什么呢？
en: So what happens when a user starts speaking?

source_text: The audio.
zh: 音频。
en: The audio.

source_text: Is first passed on to a voice activity detector, which chunks the audio into segments based on the pauses the user is taking.
zh: 音频会先经过语音活动检测器，它根据用户说话时的停顿，把音频切分成多个片段。
en: Is first passed on to a voice activity detector, which chunks the audio into segments based on the pauses the user is taking.

source_text: The audio segments are then passed on to the STT model, which transcribes the audio into text and passes it further down the agent pipeline.
zh: 这些音频片段随后会传给语音转文字模型，由它将音频转写成文本，再传给智能体流程中的后续环节。
en: The audio segments are then passed on to the STT model, which transcribes the audio into text and passes it further down the agent pipeline.

source_text: Now, a question to think about is, if your transcript contains text that no one said, which one of these components should you blame?
zh: 现在请想一想：如果转写文本里出现了根本没人说过的内容，该怪哪个环节呢？
en: Now, a question to think about is, if your transcript contains text that no one said, which one of these components should you blame?

source_text: It should be the STT model, right?
zh: 应该是语音转文字模型，对吧？
en: It should be the STT model, right?

source_text: And how do you fix the errors in your transcript?
zh: 又该如何修正转写文本中的错误呢？
en: And how do you fix the errors in your transcript?

source_text: You pick a model which shows the lowest error rate. And this is what we did.
zh: 选择错误率最低的模型。我们当时就是这么做的。
en: You pick a model which shows the lowest error rate. And this is what we did.

source_text: So we went ahead to take a look at the benchmarks and find the model which shows the lowest error rate.
zh: 于是我们查看了各项基准测试，找出错误率最低的模型。
en: So we went ahead to take a look at the benchmarks and find the model which shows the lowest error rate.

source_text: But.
zh: 但是。
en: But.

source_text: This is what we saw.
zh: 结果我们看到了这样的情况。
en: This is what we saw.

source_text: All these models showed very low error rates, ranging from 2 to 7%.
zh: 这些模型的错误率都很低，在 2% 到 7% 之间。
en: All these models showed very low error rates, ranging from 2 to 7%.

source_text: But when we ran these same models on our own audio datasets, we saw that they showed error rates that were 4 to 20 times worse compared to what the benchmarks were telling us.
zh: 但当我们用自己的音频数据集测试同样的模型时，发现它们的错误率比基准测试显示的高出 4 到 20 倍。
en: But when we ran these same models on our own audio datasets, we saw that they showed error rates that were 4 to 20 times worse compared to what the benchmarks were telling us.

source_text: So why was there a discrepancy here?
zh: 那么，为什么会出现这样的差距呢？
en: So why was there a discrepancy here?

source_text: Just to let you know, the numbers here come from the fluorous benchmark, which is one of the standards for STT models.
zh: 补充说明一下，这里的数据来自 FLEURS 基准测试，它是评估语音转文字模型的标准之一。
en: Just to let you know, the numbers here come from the fluorous benchmark, which is one of the standards for STT models.

source_text: So there are two key differences here.
zh: 这里有两个关键的区别。
en: So there are two key differences here.

source_text: First, fluorous uses audio from native speakers who read prepared sentences aloud.
zh: 首先，FLEURS 使用的是母语者朗读预先准备好的句子的录音。
en: First, fluorous uses audio from native speakers who read prepared sentences aloud.

source_text: Whereas in our case, our speakers are non-native speakers who think out loud while they're speaking.
zh: 而我们这里的说话者并非母语者，他们是一边思考一边说话。
en: Whereas in our case, our speakers are non-native speakers who think out loud while they're speaking.

source_text: Secondly.
zh: 其次。
en: Secondly.

source_text: Fluorous passes in the entire audio at once.
zh: FLEURS 会一次性将整段音频输入模型。
en: Fluorous passes in the entire audio at once.

source_text: Whereas in our case, our audio flows through the pipeline that I showed you, where the VAD chunks it into segments before feeding it into the STT models.
zh: 而我们这里，音频会经过刚才展示的处理流程：先由语音活动检测模块（VAD）切分成片段，再送入语音转文字模型。
en: Whereas in our case, our audio flows through the pipeline that I showed you, where the VAD chunks it into segments before feeding it into the STT models.

source_text: So which factor was causing the discrepancy here?
zh: 那么，究竟是哪个因素造成了这里的差异？
en: So which factor was causing the discrepancy here?

source_text: Was it our speakers, or was it the way we feed these audio to our models?
zh: 是说话者的原因，还是我们向模型输入音频的方式造成的？
en: Was it our speakers, or was it the way we feed these audio to our models?

source_text: To answer this question, we did a few more things.
zh: 为了回答这个问题，我们又做了几项测试。
en: To answer this question, we did a few more things.

source_text: So we kept our same speakers and the same models and this time fed the entire audio to these models as well. And any guesses on what the results were?
zh: 于是，我们保持说话者和模型不变，这次也将整段音频一次性输入模型。大家猜猜结果如何？
en: So we kept our same speakers and the same models and this time fed the entire audio to these models as well. And any guesses on what the results were?

source_text: The results agreed with what the benchmarks were telling us.
zh: 结果与基准测试的结论一致。
en: The results agreed with what the benchmarks were telling us.

source_text: All these models showed a sharp increase in accuracy and none of them had any foreign script now.
zh: 所有这些模型的准确率都大幅提升，而且输出中再也没有出现外文文字。
en: All these models showed a sharp increase in accuracy and none of them had any foreign script now.

source_text: So this made us conclude that nothing was wrong with our speakers.
zh: 因此我们得出结论：我们的说话者并没有问题。
en: So this made us conclude that nothing was wrong with our speakers.

source_text: We did another thing.
zh: 我们还做了另一项测试。
en: We did another thing.

source_text: So we revisited the audio clip that I played in the first slide today. And we made it pass through our live pipeline where the VAD chunks it into segments.
zh: 于是，我们重新拿出今天第一张幻灯片里播放的那段音频，让它经过我们的实时处理流程，由语音活动检测器（VAD）将其切分成片段。
en: So we revisited the audio clip that I played in the first slide today. And we made it pass through our live pipeline where the VAD chunks it into segments.

source_text: Now,
zh: 现在，
en: Now,

source_text: as you can see from the audio waveform,
zh: 从音频波形中可以看到，
en: as you can see from the audio waveform,

source_text: that because the speaker was not very fluent and took a lot of pauses, the VAD chunked it into very short segments.
zh: 由于说话者不太流利，停顿也很多，VAD 就把音频切成了很短的片段。
en: that because the speaker was not very fluent and took a lot of pauses, the VAD chunked it into very short segments.

source_text: Now, what happens when you feed these very short segments to different STT models?
zh: 那么，把这些很短的片段输入不同的语音转文字模型，会发生什么呢？
en: Now, what happens when you feed these very short segments to different STT models?

source_text: You get transcriptions in different kinds of languages.
zh: 转写结果会出现各种不同的语言。
en: You get transcriptions in different kinds of languages.

source_text: But let's actually pick one of these segments and talk about it.
zh: 不过，我们还是挑其中一个片段，具体看一看。
en: But let's actually pick one of these segments and talk about it.

source_text: Say the segment where the speaker said, "Ho," I hope that was pronounced correctly.
zh: 比如说话者说“Ho”的那一段，希望我发音没错。
en: Say the segment where the speaker said, "Ho," I hope that was pronounced correctly.

source_text: Now imagine I just play this segment in front of you without telling you the language the speaker was talking in or without giving you any context about what the speaker was talking about.
zh: 现在想象一下，如果我只给你播放这段音频，不告诉你说话者说的是什么语言，也不提供谈话内容的任何背景信息。
en: Now imagine I just play this segment in front of you without telling you the language the speaker was talking in or without giving you any context about what the speaker was talking about.

source_text: Will you be able to predict what the speaker was saying?
zh: 你能判断说话者说的是什么吗？
en: Will you be able to predict what the speaker was saying?

source_text: In fact, all these different words that the STT models predicted in different languages, they sound very similar to what the speaker was saying here in this segment.
zh: 其实，语音转文字模型识别出的这些不同语言的词，听起来都和说话者在这一片段中说的内容非常相似。
en: In fact, all these different words that the STT models predicted in different languages, they sound very similar to what the speaker was saying here in this segment.

source_text: So is the STT model really at fault here?
zh: 所以，这真的是语音转文字模型的错吗？
en: So is the STT model really at fault here?

source_text: It seems like language and the size of the audio segments, which means the context we are feeding to the models.
zh: 看来，关键在于语言，以及音频片段的长度——也就是我们提供给模型的上下文信息量。
en: It seems like language and the size of the audio segments, which means the context we are feeding to the models.

source_text: Are two key settings that affect the models.
zh: 是影响模型的两个关键因素。
en: Are two key settings that affect the models.

source_text: But a question to think about here is, why should these two settings matter at all?
zh: 但这里有一个值得思考的问题：为什么这两个因素会产生影响？
en: But a question to think about here is, why should these two settings matter at all?

source_text: This is what the theory tells us.
zh: 理论是这么说的。
en: This is what the theory tells us.

source_text: So STT models are made of two components, the encoder, which listens to our audio samples, and the decoder.
zh: 语音转文字模型由两部分组成：负责处理输入音频的编码器，以及解码器。
en: So STT models are made of two components, the encoder, which listens to our audio samples, and the decoder.

source_text: The decoder is a language model that transcribes text token by token and the first token that it transcribes is the language.
zh: 解码器是一个语言模型，会逐个词元地转写文本；它转写的第一个词元是语言标识。
en: The decoder is a language model that transcribes text token by token and the first token that it transcribes is the language.

source_text: So for a very short audio segment where the language guess is incorrect, all the tokens following this language will be predicted in the wrongly guessed language.
zh: 所以，对于很短的音频片段，如果一开始判断错了语言，后续所有词元就都会按错误的语言来预测。
en: So for a very short audio segment where the language guess is incorrect, all the tokens following this language will be predicted in the wrongly guessed language.

source_text: Secondly, every token that the decoder predicts depends on the previous tokens that it predicted and the audio segment it has access to.
zh: 其次，解码器预测的每个词元，都取决于它此前预测出的词元，以及它能够获取的音频片段。
en: Secondly, every token that the decoder predicts depends on the previous tokens that it predicted and the audio segment it has access to.

source_text: So if you feed the decoder a bigger audio segment size, it has more to- it has access to more tokens and hence more context and it should be able to transcribe the audio segment accurately.
zh: 所以，如果给解码器输入更长的音频片段，它就能利用更多词元，获得更丰富的上下文，从而更准确地转写这段音频。
en: So if you feed the decoder a bigger audio segment size, it has more to- it has access to more tokens and hence more context and it should be able to transcribe the audio segment accurately.

source_text: So this is what the theory tells us, that these two settings directly affect the accuracy of these models.
zh: 因此，理论告诉我们，这两个设置会直接影响这些模型的准确率。
en: So this is what the theory tells us, that these two settings directly affect the accuracy of these models.

source_text: But let's go ahead and see them in action now.
zh: 不过，接下来我们还是实际看看它们的效果吧。
en: But let's go ahead and see them in action now.

source_text: So what we did was we varied the size of the audio segments that we had in an audio clip and see how does it affect the accuracy of these models.
zh: 我们改变了一段音频中各个片段的长度，看看这会如何影响模型的准确率。
en: So what we did was we varied the size of the audio segments that we had in an audio clip and see how does it affect the accuracy of these models.

source_text: So we varied the size ranging from live segments all the way to the entire audio recording at once.
zh: 我们调整了音频片段的长度，从实时处理的小片段，一直到一次输入整段录音。
en: So we varied the size ranging from live segments all the way to the entire audio recording at once.

source_text: And this is what we saw.
zh: 结果是这样的。
en: And this is what we saw.

source_text: The accuracy jumped from 62% in the case of live segments all the way to 82% in the case of whole recordings.
zh: 准确率从实时处理小片段时的 62%，跃升至一次处理整段录音时的 82%。
en: The accuracy jumped from 62% in the case of live segments all the way to 82% in the case of whole recordings.

source_text: That is a big 20% jump.
zh: 这可是整整提高了 20 个百分点。
en: That is a big 20% jump.

source_text: But we cannot wait for the entire audio recording to transcribe it, right?
zh: 但我们不能等整段录音结束后才开始转写，对吧？
en: But we cannot wait for the entire audio recording to transcribe it, right?

source_text: Because then our conversation no longer remains live.
zh: 因为那样一来，我们的对话就无法实时进行了。
en: Because then our conversation no longer remains live.

source_text: So how else can you increase the accuracy then?
zh: 那么，还有什么办法能提高准确率呢？
en: So how else can you increase the accuracy then?

source_text: Here comes the language part.
zh: 接下来就要谈到语言方面了。
en: Here comes the language part.

source_text: So when you tell the models the language they are supposed to transcribe in, you can regain 11% of that 20% gap.
zh: 只要告诉模型要转写的是哪种语言，就能弥补那 20 个百分点差距中的 11 个百分点。
en: So when you tell the models the language they are supposed to transcribe in, you can regain 11% of that 20% gap.

source_text: But what is the remaining 9% gap still left?
zh: 但剩下的 9 个百分点差距又是怎么回事呢？
en: But what is the remaining 9% gap still left?

source_text: That gap is the context.
zh: 剩下的差距，就在于上下文。
en: That gap is the context.

source_text: And we don't need to feed in the entire context to these models.
zh: 而且我们不需要把全部上下文都输入模型。
en: And we don't need to feed in the entire context to these models.

source_text: If you see the shaded region within this graph, where the audio segment sizes range from 2 to 8 seconds, we still see a sharp increase in accuracy for STT models.
zh: 如果看图中的阴影区域，也就是音频片段长度在 2 到 8 秒之间的部分，你会发现语音转文字模型的准确率仍在快速提升。
en: If you see the shaded region within this graph, where the audio segment sizes range from 2 to 8 seconds, we still see a sharp increase in accuracy for STT models.

source_text: But how do we land within this shaded region to still gain higher accuracy?
zh: 但我们怎样才能落在这个阴影区间内，进一步提高准确率呢？
en: But how do we land within this shaded region to still gain higher accuracy?

source_text: Remember the voice accuracy detector from before?
zh: 还记得前面提到的语音准确率检测器吗？
en: Remember the voice accuracy detector from before?

source_text: If you tune it in such a way that it waits for a longer pause before cutting the audio segment instead of cutting at the first short pause,
zh: 如果把它调整成等到较长的停顿再切分音频，而不是一遇到短暂停顿就切分，
en: If you tune it in such a way that it waits for a longer pause before cutting the audio segment instead of cutting at the first short pause,

source_text: you'll be able to accumulate bigger audio segment sizes and hence provide more context to the models to transcribe your audio better.
zh: 就能得到更长的音频片段，为模型提供更多上下文，从而提高语音转写的准确率。
en: you'll be able to accumulate bigger audio segment sizes and hence provide more context to the models to transcribe your audio better.

source_text: And if you think about it, that is how we humans function as well.
zh: 仔细想想，我们人类也是这样理解语音的。
en: And if you think about it, that is how we humans function as well.

source_text: If you miss a word in a noisy room, you fill it up with the rest of the sentence that you heard.
zh: 在嘈杂的房间里，如果你没听清某个词，就会根据听到的句子其余部分把它补出来。
en: If you miss a word in a noisy room, you fill it up with the rest of the sentence that you heard.

source_text: And that is how STT models behave as well.
zh: 语音转文字模型也是这样工作的。
en: And that is how STT models behave as well.

source_text: So if I simplify the talk into two key things that you can take away, they would be, run your models on your own users' audio,
zh: 所以，如果把这次分享归纳成两条最重要的建议，第一条就是：用你自己用户的音频来测试模型，
en: So if I simplify the talk into two key things that you can take away, they would be, run your models on your own users' audio,

source_text: tell them the language they are supposed to transcribe in, and let it hear more of the audio.
zh: 告诉模型应该用哪种语言转写，并让它听到更长的音频。
en: tell them the language they are supposed to transcribe in, and let it hear more of the audio.

source_text: This is how we build and iterate at kosher. If you found the talk interesting, you can come and check us out at kosher.ai.
zh: 这就是我们在 Kosher 开发产品并持续迭代的方式。如果你觉得这次分享有意思，欢迎访问 kosher.ai 了解我们。
en: This is how we build and iterate at kosher. If you found the talk interesting, you can come and check us out at kosher.ai.

zh: 谢谢。
en: Thank you.

source_text: Thank you very much.
zh: 非常感谢。
en: Thank you very much.

en: Now we have wrapped up all the talks in the morning.

source_text: 所以其实我就想先问问各位，就是比如说在过去一年中，你们看到在哪些赛道中模型公司的已经明显的对应用形成了严重的挤压，
zh: 所以其实我就想先问问各位，就是比如说在过去一年中，你们看到在哪些赛道中模型公司的已经明显的对应用形成了严重的挤压，
en: So I’d like to ask everyone: over the past year, which sectors have you seen model companies clearly putting serious pressure on application companies?

source_text: 以及哪些赛道中这个应用它有一定的壁垒，能够抵御住这样的大模型公司的进攻。那语森先说吧。
zh: 以及哪些赛道中这个应用它有一定的壁垒，能够抵御住这样的大模型公司的进攻。那语森先说吧。
en: And which areas have applications with enough of a moat to withstand competition from the big model companies? Yusen, why don’t you go first?

source_text: 好，谢谢比比的问题。
zh: 好，谢谢比比的问题。
en: Sure. Thanks for the question, Bibi.

source_text: 对，因为我们确实既投了 Kimi 这样的模型公司，
zh: 对，因为我们确实既投了 Kimi 这样的模型公司，
en: Right, because we’ve invested in model companies like Kimi,

source_text: 也投了 Manus、Genspark、HeyGen 一系列应用公司，我们一直觉得如果大模型它要得到广泛的应用产生价值，
zh: 也投了 Manus、Genspark、HeyGen 一系列应用公司，我们一直觉得如果大模型它要得到广泛的应用产生价值，
en: as well as application companies like Manus, Genspark, and HeyGen. We’ve always believed that for large language models to be widely adopted and create value,

source_text: 它就必须要有应用作为载体。
zh: 它就必须要有应用作为载体。
en: they need applications to bring them to users.

source_text: 其实我们看到所谓叫吞食小应用公司的，其实并不是模型本身，我认为，而是说模型公司它自己做的第一方的应用，
zh: 其实我们看到所谓叫吞食小应用公司的，其实并不是模型本身，我认为，而是说模型公司它自己做的第一方的应用，
en: What we’re seeing isn’t really the models themselves swallowing up smaller app companies. It’s the first-party applications that model companies are building.

source_text: 比如说 Claude Code、Codex、ChatGPT，它们本质上也是应用，但并且它们是第一方做的，
zh: 比如说 Claude Code、Codex、ChatGPT，它们本质上也是应用，但并且它们是第一方做的，
en: Take Claude Code, Codex, and ChatGPT, for example. They’re applications too, but they’re built by the model companies themselves.

source_text: 并且它们补贴了 20 倍的 token，对吧？
zh: 并且它们补贴了 20 倍的 token，对吧？
en: And they’re subsidizing token usage by a factor of twenty, right?

source_text: 所以它确实是一个很大的优势。
zh: 所以它确实是一个很大的优势。
en: So that does give them a significant advantage.

source_text: 但我们也发现，如果几年前模型不够强的时候，其实谁都做不出来好的应用。
zh: 但我们也发现，如果几年前模型不够强的时候，其实谁都做不出来好的应用。
en: But we’ve also found that a few years ago, when the models weren’t powerful enough, no one could build a good application.

source_text: 所以首先模型要变强，这是大家花了非常多的钱去做训练。
zh: 所以首先模型要变强，这是大家花了非常多的钱去做训练。
en: So the first step is to make the models more capable, and that’s why everyone has spent so much money training them.

source_text: 然后模型变强之后，我们看到第二个明显的趋势是推理效率不断的在提升，每年可能提高 10 倍。
zh: 然后模型变强之后，我们看到第二个明显的趋势是推理效率不断的在提升，每年可能提高 10 倍。
en: And as the models have become more capable, we’ve seen a second clear trend: inference efficiency keeps improving, perhaps by a factor of ten each year.

source_text: 所以我们可以看到是说，当智能，当 token 变得越来越便宜，智能变得越来越便宜的时候，我认为其实大家现在发现了，
zh: 所以我们可以看到是说，当智能，当 token 变得越来越便宜，智能变得越来越便宜的时候，我认为其实大家现在发现了，
en: So as tokens get cheaper and intelligence becomes more affordable, I think people are starting to realize…

source_text: 其实从模型能力到最后的商业化落地，中间的距离是挺大的。
zh: 其实从模型能力到最后的商业化落地，中间的距离是挺大的。
en: There’s actually quite a gap between what a model can do and turning that capability into a commercially viable product.

source_text: 这个距离呢，我认为是要用应用去填补。
zh: 这个距离呢，我认为是要用应用去填补。
en: I think applications are what will bridge that gap.

source_text: 只是说这个应用有可能是第一方做的，有可能是第三方做的。
zh: 只是说这个应用有可能是第一方做的，有可能是第三方做的。
en: It’s just that those applications could be built either by the model providers themselves or by third parties.

source_text: 我一直在想一个比方，就是比如说 Windows 刚出来的时候，实际上最好的几个应用可能也是第一方的，
zh: 我一直在想一个比方，就是比如说 Windows 刚出来的时候，实际上最好的几个应用可能也是第一方的，
en: I’ve been thinking of an analogy: when Windows first came out, some of the best applications were probably Microsoft’s own.

source_text: 比如说 IE 浏览器，比如说 Office，其实都是 Web 自己做的。
zh: 比如说 IE 浏览器，比如说 Office，其实都是 Web 自己做的。
en: For example, Internet Explorer and Office were both made by Microsoft itself.

source_text: 但是这上面其实也诞生了大量第三方应用生态。
zh: 但是这上面其实也诞生了大量第三方应用生态。
en: But Windows also gave rise to a huge ecosystem of third-party applications.

source_text: 所以我觉得随着模型能力越来越强，它的推理效率越来越高，那么给应用开发者其实带来了更大的机会。
zh: 所以我觉得随着模型能力越来越强，它的推理效率越来越高，那么给应用开发者其实带来了更大的机会。
en: So as models become more capable and inference becomes more efficient, I think that creates even greater opportunities for application developers.

source_text: 并且我们也看到，应用的第一波呢，首先是针对这种比较长线型的用户，其实像 Manus 当时是一个典型的，
zh: 并且我们也看到，应用的第一波呢，首先是针对这种比较长线型的用户，其实像 Manus 当时是一个典型的，
en: And we’ve seen that the first wave of applications targeted users with longer, more complex workflows. Manus was a prime example at the time.

source_text: 针对了这些比较喜欢折腾的用户，他们自己去发现它当一个应用有创新的时候会自己去使用。
zh: 针对了这些比较喜欢折腾的用户，他们自己去发现它当一个应用有创新的时候会自己去使用。
en: They targeted users who like to tinker—people who will discover and try out an innovative app on their own.

source_text: 但是现在已经有越来越多的应用已经进入到了比如说企业，或者说更加普通人的这个领域。
zh: 但是现在已经有越来越多的应用已经进入到了比如说企业，或者说更加普通人的这个领域。
en: But now, more and more applications are making their way into businesses and the lives of everyday users.

source_text: 我们在美国看到有很多在医疗、金融、法律这些领域的这个应用，其实上形成了相对大模型公司本身来讲，它自己的这个 context 也好，数据也好，
zh: 我们在美国看到有很多在医疗、金融、法律这些领域的这个应用，其实上形成了相对大模型公司本身来讲，它自己的这个 context 也好，数据也好，
en: In the U.S., we’ve seen many applications in healthcare, finance, and law develop their own context and data that the model companies themselves don’t have.

source_text: 或者是在部署上的壁垒。
zh: 或者是在部署上的壁垒。
en: Or barriers to deployment.

source_text: 那么我觉得针对普通用户的应用，最近美国 Personal Agent 也很火，
zh: 那么我觉得针对普通用户的应用，最近美国 Personal Agent 也很火，
en: I think apps for everyday users are another big opportunity. Personal agents have become very popular in the U.S. recently.

source_text: 对吧？
zh: 对吧？
en: Right?

source_text: 其实这也是体现了像 Instinct 的这样的公司，它可以通过一个好的切入点，一个很简单应用的产品形态，
zh: 其实这也是体现了像 Instinct 的这样的公司，它可以通过一个好的切入点，一个很简单应用的产品形态，
en: This also shows how companies like Instinct can start with the right entry point and a simple app format,

source_text: 也获得很多用户的关注和使用。
zh: 也获得很多用户的关注和使用。
en: and attract a lot of users and get them to try it.

source_text: 当然这些公司都还很早，但我觉得确实我们反而是看到应用是在百花齐放，有很多的形态的。
zh: 当然这些公司都还很早，但我觉得确实我们反而是看到应用是在百花齐放，有很多的形态的。
en: Of course, these companies are still at a very early stage, but we’re seeing a wide variety of applications emerge in many different forms.

source_text: 但这里面可能更大的问题是应用怎么能够挣钱。
zh: 但这里面可能更大的问题是应用怎么能够挣钱。
en: But perhaps the bigger question is how these applications can make money.

source_text: 我自己的看法是说，可能最后很多应用它是需要在模型公司的 token 上创造它的增量的价值，比如说可能像 Personal Agent 这样的应用，
zh: 我自己的看法是说，可能最后很多应用它是需要在模型公司的 token 上创造它的增量的价值，比如说可能像 Personal Agent 这样的应用，
en: My view is that many applications will ultimately need to create value beyond the model companies’ tokens. Take personal agents, for example—

source_text: 它可能最后不是靠你收订阅费用去挣钱，更多的是我帮用户省了多少钱，或者我帮用户完成了多少交易额，
zh: 它可能最后不是靠你收订阅费用去挣钱，更多的是我帮用户省了多少钱，或者我帮用户完成了多少交易额，
en: They may not ultimately make money from subscriptions. Instead, it may come down to how much money they save users or how much transaction volume they generate for them.

source_text: 从中抽取一个中间商的一个费用。
zh: 从中抽取一个中间商的一个费用。
en: and earn a fee for acting as an intermediary.

source_text: 其实这跟我们互联网公司的很多赚钱方式挺像的。
zh: 其实这跟我们互联网公司的很多赚钱方式挺像的。
en: In fact, that’s pretty similar to how many internet companies make money.

source_text: 所谓中国就是说羊毛出在猪身上嘛，这个免费的应用，但是我从中有其他的收费方式。
zh: 所谓中国就是说羊毛出在猪身上嘛，这个免费的应用，但是我从中有其他的收费方式。
en: As the Chinese saying goes, “The wool comes from the pig”: the app is free, but you make money from it in other ways.

source_text: 我觉得这些可能都还是在一个比较早的阶段，
zh: 我觉得这些可能都还是在一个比较早的阶段，
en: I think all of this is still at a fairly early stage.

source_text: 所以可能第一步就是怎么样让更多的人能够用上更好的 AI 产品。
zh: 所以可能第一步就是怎么样让更多的人能够用上更好的 AI 产品。
en: So perhaps the first step is to make better AI products available to more people.

source_text: 第二步呢，是从中找到可能 AI native 的商业模式，但我整体觉得模型变强，然后变便宜，对应用公司是好事，而不是坏事。
zh: 第二步呢，是从中找到可能 AI native 的商业模式，但我整体觉得模型变强，然后变便宜，对应用公司是好事，而不是坏事。
en: The second step is to find business models that are truly AI-native. Overall, I think stronger, cheaper models are good for application companies, not bad.

source_text: Eric 怎么看？
zh: Eric 怎么看？
en: What do you think, Eric?

source_text: 我可能在这块补充两个我们这块的思考。
zh: 我可能在这块补充两个我们这块的思考。
en: Let me add a couple of thoughts on this from our perspective.

source_text: 首先我们可能在软硬结合这块呢，思考的比较多。
zh: 首先我们可能在软硬结合这块呢，思考的比较多。
en: First, we’ve given a lot of thought to combining hardware and software.

source_text: 之所以这个也是因为你刚才提到的一个原因，我们觉得纯软的大模型能力提升的时候，
zh: 之所以这个也是因为你刚才提到的一个原因，我们觉得纯软的大模型能力提升的时候，
en: That’s partly because of the point you just raised: as the capabilities of software-only large models improve,

source_text: 的确它很容易吃掉纯应用的那些企业的边界。
zh: 的确它很容易吃掉纯应用的那些企业的边界。
en: they can indeed easily encroach on the territory of companies that only build applications.

source_text: 这种边界即使在美国也在发生，美国的那些企业的边界感相对会强一点。
zh: 这种边界即使在美国也在发生，美国的那些企业的边界感相对会强一点。
en: We’re seeing those boundaries shift even in the U.S., though American companies tend to be a bit more mindful of them.

source_text: 即使如此，
zh: 即使如此，
en: Even so,

source_text: 我觉得也在发生一些松动。
zh: 我觉得也在发生一些松动。
en: I think those boundaries are starting to blur there, too.

source_text: 那中国就不用说了，历史以来就从来没有边界这种说法。
zh: 那中国就不用说了，历史以来就从来没有边界这种说法。
en: And in China, of course, there’s never really been any notion of such boundaries.

source_text: 在这个思考下呢，我们对于软硬结合这个事呢，可能会思考的比较多一些。
zh: 在这个思考下呢，我们对于软硬结合这个事呢，可能会思考的比较多一些。
en: That’s why we’ve spent a lot of time thinking about how to combine hardware and software.

source_text: 在 AI 应用这块，的确我同意这个语森说的智能水平是在越来越高，而且价格 token 价格在越来越便宜。
zh: 在 AI 应用这块，的确我同意这个语森说的智能水平是在越来越高，而且价格 token 价格在越来越便宜。
en: When it comes to AI applications, I agree with Yusen that the models are getting smarter, while the price per token keeps falling.

source_text: 那这个指的还是在云端的。
zh: 那这个指的还是在云端的。
en: But that’s still referring to cloud-based models.

source_text: 那在于说 local AI，不管这个 local AI 是对于个人，你想想看，踩在你兜里的一个这个使用起来体验，
zh: 那在于说 local AI，不管这个 local AI 是对于个人，你想想看，踩在你兜里的一个这个使用起来体验，
en: But with local AI—whether it’s for individuals—just imagine the experience of having AI right there in your pocket...

source_text: 比起手机要方便很多的一个 IQ 在 200 以上的 Personal Agent，它能够实时的获取你的 context，
zh: 比起手机要方便很多的一个 IQ 在 200 以上的 Personal Agent，它能够实时的获取你的 context，
en: A personal agent with an IQ over 200 that’s much easier to use than a phone and can understand your context in real time.

source_text: 包括你的语音，包括你平时的这些这个各种行动，
zh: 包括你的语音，包括你平时的这些这个各种行动，
en: That includes your voice and all the things you do throughout the day.

source_text: 它的 sensor 可能会比手机的它这个 form factor 会有不一样之处。
zh: 它的 sensor 可能会比手机的它这个 form factor 会有不一样之处。
en: Its sensors and form factor might be quite different from a phone’s.

source_text: 它最后因为我认为智能可能基于三个东西，一个是大模型本身的智能，一个是中间这个 agentic。
zh: 它最后因为我认为智能可能基于三个东西，一个是大模型本身的智能，一个是中间这个 agentic。
en: Ultimately, I think intelligence may rest on three things: the intelligence of the large model itself, and then the agentic capabilities in between.

source_text: agentic 目的是为了帮你完成任务，大模型的它智能就是 next token prediction，
zh: agentic 目的是为了帮你完成任务，大模型的它智能就是 next token prediction，
en: The purpose of agentic AI is to help you complete tasks; a large model’s intelligence comes from predicting the next token.

source_text: 它就不 care 会不会说真的把你完成任务的。
zh: 它就不 care 会不会说真的把你完成任务的。
en: It doesn’t really care whether it actually gets the job done for you.

source_text: 然后在这第三层呢，就是你的 context。
zh: 然后在这第三层呢，就是你的 context。
en: And the third layer is your context.

source_text: 我觉得围绕这三层的把这个产品体验做好的这个 local AI，对于个人可能是一个很有意思的一个新的一个硬件设备。
zh: 我觉得围绕这三层的把这个产品体验做好的这个 local AI，对于个人可能是一个很有意思的一个新的一个硬件设备。
en: I think a local AI device that brings those three layers together into a great user experience could be a really interesting new piece of personal hardware.

source_text: 对于企业的话，那可能是一个这个 enterprise 的一个 box，但它是软硬可能结合的，
zh: 对于企业的话，那可能是一个这个 enterprise 的一个 box，但它是软硬可能结合的，
en: For businesses, it might be an enterprise box—a combination of hardware and software.

source_text: 里面至少能够 run 一个 DeepSeek 4.0 Flash 这种 level 的智能。
zh: 里面至少能够 run 一个 DeepSeek 4.0 Flash 这种 level 的智能。
en: It would need to be able to run a model with at least DeepSeek 4.0 Flash–level intelligence locally.

source_text: 那么对于像很多企业的 privacy，
zh: 那么对于像很多企业的 privacy，
en: That would address the privacy concerns of many businesses.

source_text: 它会我认为是可以大幅度 unleash 很多企业对于这些智能的这种使用的我可以放心的把我的 context 沉积在这个设备上。
zh: 它会我认为是可以大幅度 unleash 很多企业对于这些智能的这种使用的我可以放心的把我的 context 沉积在这个设备上。
en: I think it could dramatically expand how businesses use AI, because they could feel comfortable storing their context on the device.

source_text: 当然了，你要想要更高的，我肯定还是用云端。
zh: 当然了，你要想要更高的，我肯定还是用云端。
en: Of course, if you need more advanced capabilities, you’d still use the cloud.

source_text: 所以边云这个结合这类的这种应用，我是觉得可以借助刚才提到的 local AI。
zh: 所以边云这个结合这类的这种应用，我是觉得可以借助刚才提到的 local AI。
en: So I think applications that combine on-device and cloud AI could build on the local AI I just mentioned.

source_text: AI 这个在个体跟企业里面的这种具象化得到实现。
zh: AI 这个在个体跟企业里面的这种具象化得到实现。
en: That’s how AI could take concrete form and become useful for both individuals and businesses.

source_text: 这个呢，是在我看来是很走的，就说 X 和 Y 的话，这是 X 这个层面的。
zh: 这个呢，是在我看来是很走的，就说 X 和 Y 的话，这是 X 这个层面的。
en: To me, this is a promising direction. If we think in terms of X and Y, this falls on the X side.

source_text: 而 Y 这个面就是不同的 vertical 了，不同的 vertical 我们现在还在这方面做一些琢磨，做一些尝试。
zh: 而 Y 这个面就是不同的 vertical 了，不同的 vertical 我们现在还在这方面做一些琢磨，做一些尝试。
en: The Y side is about different verticals. We’re still exploring and experimenting with those.

source_text: 我们现在没有很好的答案，就是目前我们可能在那里看到有一个垂直的一个应用，
zh: 我们现在没有很好的答案，就是目前我们可能在那里看到有一个垂直的一个应用，
en: We don’t have a clear answer yet. So far, we may have identified one application in a specific vertical.

source_text: 比如说像 real time 的 video generation，这个实时的视频生成。
zh: 比如说像 real time 的 video generation，这个实时的视频生成。
en: For example, real-time video generation.

source_text: 因为这个跟大模型本身的它那个战场呢，有一点这个差异，相对会，
zh: 因为这个跟大模型本身的它那个战场呢，有一点这个差异，相对会，
en: Because that’s somewhat different from the main battleground for large models, it’s relatively…

source_text: 我也不能说边缘一点，因为它的这个应用方向是比较明确的，不像大模型它可能走的就是尤其语言模型就是 next token，
zh: 我也不能说边缘一点，因为它的这个应用方向是比较明确的，不像大模型它可能走的就是尤其语言模型就是 next token，
en: I wouldn’t call it more niche, either, because its applications are fairly well defined. Large models—especially language models—are different: they’re essentially built around predicting the next token.

source_text: 像那个东西主要还是基于 diffusion 的，它的目的呢，是能够把速度这个提高到原来的 20 倍以上。
zh: 像那个东西主要还是基于 diffusion 的，它的目的呢，是能够把速度这个提高到原来的 20 倍以上。
en: That technology is still mainly based on diffusion, and the goal is to make it more than 20 times faster.

source_text: 那可以说把有些特殊的一些应用展现出来。
zh: 那可以说把有些特殊的一些应用展现出来。
en: That would make certain specialized applications possible.

source_text: 所以我们也是被迫，我觉得基于这些思考，可能绕开一些主模型的主战场。
zh: 所以我们也是被迫，我觉得基于这些思考，可能绕开一些主模型的主战场。
en: So, in a sense, these considerations have pushed us to steer clear of the main battleground for foundation models.

source_text: 在某种意义上也是一种，我觉得在 Y 轴这个上面的一些尝试。这是我们可能目前的横轴纵轴的一些思考跟尝试吧。
zh: 在某种意义上也是一种，我觉得在 Y 轴这个上面的一些尝试。这是我们可能目前的横轴纵轴的一些思考跟尝试吧。
en: In a sense, I see this as another experiment along the Y axis. That’s where we are right now in our thinking and experimentation across both axes.

source_text: 我从我不但投过这个模型，还投过一些应用，但是有两个暴论，我今天看来可能也不一定完全成立，
zh: 我从我不但投过这个模型，还投过一些应用，但是有两个暴论，我今天看来可能也不一定完全成立，
en: I’ve invested not only in models but also in some applications. I had two rather bold takes, though looking back today, I’m not sure either of them entirely holds up.

source_text: 但是至少对过去三年的一个总结的话，第一个呢，是我认为尤其在中国，90%甚至99%的三年前的应用成功时都已经死了。
zh: 但是至少对过去三年的一个总结的话，第一个呢，是我认为尤其在中国，90%甚至99%的三年前的应用成功时都已经死了。
en: But if I had to sum up the past three years, my first point would be this: especially in China, 90%—perhaps even 99%—of the application startups from three years ago have already died.

source_text: 我不知道这个像语森观察的是怎样的，
zh: 我不知道这个像语森观察的是怎样的，
en: I don’t know whether that matches what Yusen has observed.

source_text: 我们也稍微统计过，至少是拿过钱的好些公司。
zh: 我们也稍微统计过，至少是拿过钱的好些公司。
en: We’ve done a rough count too, at least of the companies that raised funding.

source_text: 这是第一个。
zh: 这是第一个。
en: That’s the first point.

source_text: 然后第二个呢，就是 AI 应用，我觉得还没有完全开始爆发，当然也出现了像南慈之前也投 Genspark、Manus，
zh: 然后第二个呢，就是 AI 应用，我觉得还没有完全开始爆发，当然也出现了像南慈之前也投 Genspark、Manus，
en: And second, I don’t think AI applications have really taken off yet. Of course, there have been companies like Genspark and Manus, which Nanci invested in earlier.

source_text: 就是这些可能也不能完全叫应用层的公司。
zh: 就是这些可能也不能完全叫应用层的公司。
en: Though perhaps you can’t really call those pure application-layer companies either.

source_text: 当时因为他们确实想做通用 agent platform 这样的公司，
zh: 当时因为他们确实想做通用 agent platform 这样的公司，
en: At the time, they really wanted to build a general-purpose agent platform.

source_text: 但这些我觉得这些公司它能成是确实是现在看来就是猎奇，但是还有另外一点很重要的，
zh: 但这些我觉得这些公司它能成是确实是现在看来就是猎奇，但是还有另外一点很重要的，
en: But I think part of why these companies have succeeded is that they’re genuinely novel. There’s another important factor, though.

source_text: 我认为他们是在新的最新模型基础上的套利。
zh: 我认为他们是在新的最新模型基础上的套利。
en: I think they’re capitalizing on the capabilities of the latest models.

source_text: 就是当时这个你回顾这历史其实很清楚，就是拿着最新的模型，然后你放在某一个应用场景上，
zh: 就是当时这个你回顾这历史其实很清楚，就是拿着最新的模型，然后你放在某一个应用场景上，
en: Looking back, the pattern is clear: you take the latest model and apply it to a specific use case.

source_text: 好，用户使用通用模型不好使的，然后就用这个来去付费。
zh: 好，用户使用通用模型不好使的，然后就用这个来去付费。
en: Where a general-purpose model doesn’t work well for users, they’re willing to pay for a specialized solution.

source_text: 但这是不光有新鲜感，而且这种套利的空间随着模型延伸到应用的时候就减少了。
zh: 但这是不光有新鲜感，而且这种套利的空间随着模型延伸到应用的时候就减少了。
en: But it’s not just about novelty. As model providers expand into applications themselves, those opportunities to capitalize on the latest models shrink.

source_text: 那么继续往下看。
zh: 那么继续往下看。
en: So let’s keep going.

source_text: 沿着这个两个暴论的话，就是什么样的东西我觉得是可以了。
zh: 沿着这个两个暴论的话，就是什么样的东西我觉得是可以了。
en: If we follow these two provocative claims, what kinds of things do I think could work?

source_text: 至少在今天，就 AI native 的叫应用没有爆发，但不意味着 AI native 的方向没有出来。
zh: 至少在今天，就 AI native 的叫应用没有爆发，但不意味着 AI native 的方向没有出来。
en: At least for now, AI-native applications haven’t taken off, but that doesn’t mean promising directions for AI-native products haven’t emerged.

source_text: 我觉得是有好的方向，是已经出来，它真的，我自己特别看好的是就情绪价值这个方向。
zh: 我觉得是有好的方向，是已经出来，它真的，我自己特别看好的是就情绪价值这个方向。
en: I think some promising directions have already emerged. The one I’m especially bullish on is AI that provides emotional support and connection.

source_text: 这是其中之一，其实不管。
zh: 这是其中之一，其实不管。
en: That’s one of them. Actually, regardless...

source_text: 是男性、女性、小孩、老人，我觉得都是，这是之前的技术不能解决，而这一轮 AI 它能做到之前10倍好的体验的东西，可能更好。
zh: 是男性、女性、小孩、老人，我觉得都是，这是之前的技术不能解决，而这一轮 AI 它能做到之前10倍好的体验的东西，可能更好。
en: Whether it’s men, women, children, or older adults, I think it applies to everyone. Previous technology couldn’t really address this, but this wave of AI can deliver an experience ten times better—maybe even more.

source_text: 但现今天情绪价值还是不够，用技术来去完成它。
zh: 但现今天情绪价值还是不够，用技术来去完成它。
en: But today’s technology still isn’t good enough to truly meet people’s emotional needs.

source_text: 没准也要这时候可能是这个 Harry 讲的这样的硬件的浮肿。
zh: 没准也要这时候可能是这个 Harry 讲的这样的硬件的浮肿。
en: Maybe this is where the kind of hardware Harry was talking about comes in.

source_text: 第二个呢，是强数据相关的，我认为它是可以慢慢积累并且形成复利效应的。
zh: 第二个呢，是强数据相关的，我认为它是可以慢慢积累并且形成复利效应的。
en: The second is heavily data-driven. I think it can build up gradually and create a compounding effect.

source_text: 这个在美国表现特别明显，但在中国并不明显。
zh: 这个在美国表现特别明显，但在中国并不明显。
en: This is especially evident in the U.S., but much less so in China.

source_text: 美国的这个医疗法律，医疗是美国医疗健康是美国的第一大行业，所以它已经出现了很多这种法律，
zh: 美国的这个医疗法律，医疗是美国医疗健康是美国的第一大行业，所以它已经出现了很多这种法律，
en: Healthcare is the largest industry in the U.S., so a lot of legal issues have emerged around it.

source_text: Harvard 之类的都是非常好的。
zh: Harvard 之类的都是非常好的。
en: Harvard and others like it are all very good.

source_text: 中国还需要琢磨吧。
zh: 中国还需要琢磨吧。
en: China still needs to figure it out.

source_text: 然后第三个方向呢，我觉得就是其实就是当然就是视频了。
zh: 然后第三个方向呢，我觉得就是其实就是当然就是视频了。
en: And the third area, I think, is video, of course.

source_text: 前段时间不是看那个图片，有个上市公司说中文这个大模型。
zh: 前段时间不是看那个图片，有个上市公司说中文这个大模型。
en: I saw a graphic recently about a publicly traded company discussing Chinese-language large models.

source_text: 世界，中文 AI 世界 token 消耗55%的是短句嘛，而美国是生产力工具是 coding，这其实是代表了一个，
zh: 世界，中文 AI 世界 token 消耗55%的是短句嘛，而美国是生产力工具是 coding，这其实是代表了一个，
en: In the Chinese AI market, 55% of tokens are used for short-form content, while in the U.S., usage is centered on productivity tools like coding. That points to a broader difference...

source_text: 我觉得代表一种趋势性的东西吧。这基本上我自己的一点看法。
zh: 我觉得代表一种趋势性的东西吧。这基本上我自己的一点看法。
en: I think it reflects a broader trend. That’s basically my personal take.

source_text: 特别认可 Patrick 说情绪价值，因为我前阵子说看到一个说法说其实 AI 应用目前最大的是宏观短句，
zh: 特别认可 Patrick 说情绪价值，因为我前阵子说看到一个说法说其实 AI 应用目前最大的是宏观短句，
en: I really agree with Patrick’s point about emotional value. I recently came across the idea that the biggest use of AI right now is generating short-form content.

source_text: 就是因为其实它上面大部分都是我们用这种 AI 算力生成的。
zh: 就是因为其实它上面大部分都是我们用这种 AI 算力生成的。
en: That’s because most of the content on it is generated using AI computing power.

source_text: 那其实对于现在就是前阵子掀起过一些这个就是资本浪潮的这种 personal agent，
zh: 那其实对于现在就是前阵子掀起过一些这个就是资本浪潮的这种 personal agent，
en: So what does that mean for personal agents, which sparked a wave of investment a while back?

source_text: 不管是像是 instinct 或者像 GrokBot 这种，就前阵子激动一阵子嘛，因为确实一上来大家很觉得很新潮，然后现在很多人还在探索。我想问就是语森你对这个 personal agent 这个方向是怎么看的？
zh: 不管是像是 instinct 或者像 GrokBot 这种，就前阵子激动一阵子嘛，因为确实一上来大家很觉得很新潮，然后现在很多人还在探索。我想问就是语森你对这个 personal agent 这个方向是怎么看的？
en: Whether it’s Instinct or something like GrokBot, there was a lot of excitement around them for a while. They felt genuinely novel at first, and a lot of people are still exploring them. Yusen, what’s your take on personal agents as a direction?

source_text: 对，我觉得 personal agent 现在面临的一个问题还是它对大部分人来讲，它不是一个刚需，
zh: 对，我觉得 personal agent 现在面临的一个问题还是它对大部分人来讲，它不是一个刚需，
en: Yeah, I think the problem with personal agents right now is that, for most people, they’re not an essential need.

source_text: 不是刚需的原因是它目前主要解决还是一个把已有的任务提高效率，而这个比如说对于 VC 来讲可能确实比较忙，
zh: 不是刚需的原因是它目前主要解决还是一个把已有的任务提高效率，而这个比如说对于 VC 来讲可能确实比较忙，
en: The reason it isn’t essential is that it mainly helps people do tasks they’re already doing more efficiently. For VCs, for example, that could be useful because they’re genuinely quite busy.

source_text: 有很多这么订餐馆、订行程的事情，可能能省点效率，但实际上并不是说这事一定要 AI 去做。
zh: 有很多这么订餐馆、订行程的事情，可能能省点效率，但实际上并不是说这事一定要 AI 去做。
en: There are lots of things like booking restaurants and planning trips where AI might save you some time, but you don’t actually need AI to do them.

source_text: 所以我们看到可能像 Muse、Instinct 这些它的长期留存相对一般，就是短期内可能清了一些你的 email subscription，
zh: 所以我们看到可能像 Muse、Instinct 这些它的长期留存相对一般，就是短期内可能清了一些你的 email subscription，
en: So we’ve seen that products like Muse and Instinct tend to have fairly modest long-term retention. They might clean up some of your email subscriptions in the short term,

source_text: 帮你找了一些以前没有退的费什么的，之后呢，就发现好像你也不是天天订机票、订酒店这样，对吧？
zh: 帮你找了一些以前没有退的费什么的，之后呢，就发现好像你也不是天天订机票、订酒店这样，对吧？
en: or find a few old charges you could get refunded. But after that, you realize you’re not booking flights and hotels every day, right?

source_text: 所以我就在想，
zh: 所以我就在想，
en: So I’ve been thinking,

source_text: 从如果从移动互联网去看的话，提高个人效率，这个好像很难成为一个特别大的需求。
zh: 从如果从移动互联网去看的话，提高个人效率，这个好像很难成为一个特别大的需求。
en: If you look at the mobile internet, helping people be more productive doesn’t seem to become a particularly big market.

source_text: 比如移动互联网早期黑莓也是在提高高效率，就是那种非常繁忙的个人的效率，
zh: 比如移动互联网早期黑莓也是在提高高效率，就是那种非常繁忙的个人的效率，
en: For example, in the early days of the mobile internet, BlackBerry was all about helping very busy people work more efficiently.

source_text: 但最后移动互联网这个最大成的公司其实都是在让普通人的需求扩张，比如电商让普通人能买的东西大幅扩张，对吧？
zh: 但最后移动互联网这个最大成的公司其实都是在让普通人的需求扩张，比如电商让普通人能买的东西大幅扩张，对吧？
en: But in the end, the biggest mobile internet companies expanded what ordinary people could do. E-commerce, for example, vastly expanded what people could buy, right?

source_text: 那么不管是小红书还是字节，是让普通人的这个消磨时间的需求，娱乐的需求大幅扩张。
zh: 那么不管是小红书还是字节，是让普通人的这个消磨时间的需求，娱乐的需求大幅扩张。
en: And platforms like Xiaohongshu and ByteDance vastly expanded how ordinary people could spend their free time and enjoy entertainment.

source_text: 所以我觉得在这里面可能要真的做到一个大众市场呢，
zh: 所以我觉得在这里面可能要真的做到一个大众市场呢，
en: So I think to really reach a mass market here,

source_text: 就是得是一个新需求扩张的一个产品，而不是一个已有需求提高效率的产品。
zh: 就是得是一个新需求扩张的一个产品，而不是一个已有需求提高效率的产品。
en: it has to be a product that expands what people want to do, rather than one that just helps them do existing things more efficiently.

source_text: 因为提高效率可能大部分情况不是每个人都有的需求，所以其实刚才 Patrick 老板说的这个情感，我觉得是一个就是如果你能做得很好，对吧？
zh: 因为提高效率可能大部分情况不是每个人都有的需求，所以其实刚才 Patrick 老板说的这个情感，我觉得是一个就是如果你能做得很好，对吧？
en: Because being more efficient isn’t something everyone needs in most situations. So I think the emotional connection Patrick mentioned could be a big opportunity—if you can get it right, right?

source_text: 你可能能够提供很多人他平时没有很强的情绪价值的来源，可能发现这个是一个能够扩张的需求。
zh: 你可能能够提供很多人他平时没有很强的情绪价值的来源，可能发现这个是一个能够扩张的需求。
en: You might be able to offer emotional support to a lot of people who don’t have much of it in their everyday lives. That could turn out to be a need you can expand.

source_text: 只是说这个以什么样的形式呈现，可能是需要去思考的，要做成情绪，不要做成情色，对吧？
zh: 只是说这个以什么样的形式呈现，可能是需要去思考的，要做成情绪，不要做成情色，对吧？
en: The question is what form it should take. That’s something we need to think through: make it about emotional connection, not sexual content, right?

source_text: 然后这个，然后那比如说 personal agent 这种有没有可能作为一个需求扩张呢？
zh: 然后这个，然后那比如说 personal agent 这种有没有可能作为一个需求扩张呢？
en: So then, could something like a personal agent expand what people want to do?

source_text: 我觉得也是有可能，但是现在可能还做得不够好。
zh: 我觉得也是有可能，但是现在可能还做得不够好。
en: I think it’s possible, but the technology probably isn’t quite good enough yet.

source_text: 比如说假如这个 personal agent 它非常了解你的这个日常的这个生活习惯、身体状况，
zh: 比如说假如这个 personal agent 它非常了解你的这个日常的这个生活习惯、身体状况，
en: For example, imagine a personal agent that really understands your daily habits and health.

source_text: 那也许比如说它可以推荐你去购买之前你没有想到买的，比如说补剂，对吧？
zh: 那也许比如说它可以推荐你去购买之前你没有想到买的，比如说补剂，对吧？
en: Then it might recommend something you hadn’t thought of buying before, like a supplement, right?

source_text: 把你这个人其实这个你的各项健康指标你可能缺特定的维生素，或者有个更加 personalized 的一个健身方案、补充方案，
zh: 把你这个人其实这个你的各项健康指标你可能缺特定的维生素，或者有个更加 personalized 的一个健身方案、补充方案，
en: It could look at all your health metrics, identify specific vitamin deficiencies, and come up with a more personalized fitness and supplement plan.

source_text: 这些也许是能够扩张你的需求的。
zh: 这些也许是能够扩张你的需求的。
en: These could also create new needs you didn’t realize you had.

source_text: 当然对于已有的需求，比如说原来我在携程、我在 Expedia 去订机票，可能能切到 personal agent 来订机票，
zh: 当然对于已有的需求，比如说原来我在携程、我在 Expedia 去订机票，可能能切到 personal agent 来订机票，
en: Of course, for existing needs—like booking flights through Ctrip or Expedia—you might switch to booking them through a personal agent.

source_text: 这个是把已有场景的中间人赚的钱把它，
zh: 这个是把已有场景的中间人赚的钱把它，
en: That would take the money currently going to intermediaries in existing use cases and…

source_text: 把这个蛋糕分到了我的兜里，这个可能也是一个很大的市场，但这个的问题在于说它不是一个扩张型市场，它是一个抢别人蛋糕的事情。
zh: 把这个蛋糕分到了我的兜里，这个可能也是一个很大的市场，但这个的问题在于说它不是一个扩张型市场，它是一个抢别人蛋糕的事情。
en: …put that slice of the pie in my own pocket. That could still be a huge market, but it wouldn’t be expanding the market—it would be taking a slice of someone else’s pie.

source_text: 这个我觉得在有了领域可能会发生，但另外一步就是说能不能带来新的扩张型的需求，因为有了 personal agent，
zh: 这个我觉得在有了领域可能会发生，但另外一步就是说能不能带来新的扩张型的需求，因为有了 personal agent，
en: I think that could happen in some areas. But the next question is whether personal agents can create new demand and expand the market.

source_text: 所以我能够去买、去消费、去规划或者去做很多原来我做不了，因为我没有一个很好的智能辅助的事情。我觉得如果能把这个事情做到，那可能是一个真正的增量大机会。
zh: 所以我能够去买、去消费、去规划或者去做很多原来我做不了，因为我没有一个很好的智能辅助的事情。我觉得如果能把这个事情做到，那可能是一个真正的增量大机会。
en: So I could buy things, spend money, make plans, or do many things I couldn’t do before because I didn’t have good AI assistance. If personal agents can make that possible, I think that would be a genuinely big opportunity to create new demand.

source_text: 所以这个是我目前的一个观察吧。
zh: 所以这个是我目前的一个观察吧。
en: So that’s my take on it for now.

source_text: 但是我觉得 personal agent 呢，就是它可能也是一个需要不断的创业者不断的去尝试的过程，
zh: 但是我觉得 personal agent 呢，就是它可能也是一个需要不断的创业者不断的去尝试的过程，
en: But I think personal agents are something entrepreneurs will need to keep experimenting with.

source_text: 因为这其实也是一个可能几十年来大家都想有的东西。
zh: 因为这其实也是一个可能几十年来大家都想有的东西。
en: Because this is something people have wanted for decades.

source_text: 其实在2014、15年那波也有一波做那种叫 operator magic 那一波，那一波其实纯人工智能，人工的智能，
zh: 其实在2014、15年那波也有一波做那种叫 operator magic 那一波，那一波其实纯人工智能，人工的智能，
en: Actually, back around 2014 or 2015, there was a wave of services like Operator and Magic. They were “AI” in the sense of artificial intelligence—but really, it was human intelligence.

source_text: 可能是有人在后面真的帮你订机票那种。
zh: 可能是有人在后面真的帮你订机票那种。
en: There may have been a real person behind the scenes booking your flights for you.

source_text: 就是这个事儿是很多人一直想过，但是技术是逐渐成熟的过程，
zh: 就是这个事儿是很多人一直想过，但是技术是逐渐成熟的过程，
en: It’s something people have wanted for a long time, but the technology has taken time to mature.

source_text: 所以我们也经常看到在技术创新过程中有一些需求早就已经被发现，但是技术不够 ready，所以就每隔几年有人做一次，每隔几年有人做一次。
zh: 所以我们也经常看到在技术创新过程中有一些需求早就已经被发现，但是技术不够 ready，所以就每隔几年有人做一次，每隔几年有人做一次。
en: So in technology, we often see needs that were identified long ago, but the technology wasn’t ready yet. People keep taking another shot at them every few years.

source_text: 这次我不知道是不是就 ready 了，可能也会发现好像还这个还差点火候，但是我觉得这个大方向可能还是挺有意思的。
zh: 这次我不知道是不是就 ready 了，可能也会发现好像还这个还差点火候，但是我觉得这个大方向可能还是挺有意思的。
en: I don’t know if the technology is ready this time. We may find it still needs a little more time, but I think the overall direction is pretty interesting.

source_text: 我这个补充一个，我觉得 personal agent 这个方向是非常激动人心的，
zh: 我这个补充一个，我觉得 personal agent 这个方向是非常激动人心的，
en: Let me add one thing: I think the direction of personal agents is really exciting.

source_text: 反正我的想象就是在我的兜里有一个智商200以上，这个一个小聪明，他对我的了解甚至比我自己对自己的了解更多。
zh: 反正我的想象就是在我的兜里有一个智商200以上，这个一个小聪明，他对我的了解甚至比我自己对自己的了解更多。
en: I imagine having a little genius in my pocket, with an IQ over 200, who knows me even better than I know myself.

source_text: 其实你很多时候你说的话，你的语气其实都在不自觉的透露其实你的很多一些隐藏的一些信息，但咱们在清醒的时候，
zh: 其实你很多时候你说的话，你的语气其实都在不自觉的透露其实你的很多一些隐藏的一些信息，但咱们在清醒的时候，
en: A lot of the time, what you say and the tone you use unconsciously reveal things about yourself that you might otherwise keep hidden. But when we’re consciously aware...

source_text: 很多时候都是一种显示的感知，但其实它我们的很多感官，
zh: 很多时候都是一种显示的感知，但其实它我们的很多感官，
en: Most of the time, we’re only aware of what we consciously perceive, but many of our senses...

source_text: 它就我们说话的时候，语气、语速这些等等，隐含的一些信息，我们自己其实并没有那么清楚，但我们在表达，
zh: 它就我们说话的时候，语气、语速这些等等，隐含的一些信息，我们自己其实并没有那么清楚，但我们在表达，
en: When we speak, our tone, pace, and so on convey subtle information we may not even be fully aware of, but we’re still expressing it.

source_text: 我是觉得 AI 这些东西能够把这些信息更加全面的这个获取下来，但中间过程中把 privacy 这些去掉。
zh: 我是觉得 AI 这些东西能够把这些信息更加全面的这个获取下来，但中间过程中把 privacy 这些去掉。
en: I think AI could capture all that information more comprehensively while protecting our privacy along the way.

source_text: 但最终的目的是什么呢？
zh: 但最终的目的是什么呢？
en: But what’s the ultimate goal?

source_text: 我觉得跟大模型的区别在于，大模型其实就是 next token，
zh: 我觉得跟大模型的区别在于，大模型其实就是 next token，
en: I think the difference is that large language models are essentially just predicting the next token.

source_text: 但是这个 agent 的目的是在我看来是一个 doer，就前面那种是 talker，
zh: 但是这个 agent 的目的是在我看来是一个 doer，就前面那种是 talker，
en: But to me, the goal of an agent is to be a doer, whereas what we were talking about earlier is a talker.

source_text: 跟你聊天，这个回答你的这个问题，其实就是凑一段 token 跟你的问题的 token，这个比较和谐的。
zh: 跟你聊天，这个回答你的这个问题，其实就是凑一段 token 跟你的问题的 token，这个比较和谐的。
en: When it chats with you and answers your question, it’s essentially stringing together tokens that fit well with the tokens in your question.

source_text: 但 agent 的目的是帮你解决问题。
zh: 但 agent 的目的是帮你解决问题。
en: But an agent’s purpose is to help you solve problems.

source_text: 我觉得今天的解决问题，它的形式可能也还不够优美，
zh: 我觉得今天的解决问题，它的形式可能也还不够优美，
en: I think the way agents solve problems today may still be a bit clunky.

source_text: 它的效果也还不够优美。
zh: 它的效果也还不够优美。
en: And the results aren’t quite as elegant as they could be, either.

source_text: 如果这两个东西真能做到的话，我是觉得这个就像当年的手机一样，刚出来的时候，这个我不知道雨生，
zh: 如果这两个东西真能做到的话，我是觉得这个就像当年的手机一样，刚出来的时候，这个我不知道雨生，
en: If we can really get those two things right, I think it’ll be like the mobile phone when it first came out. I don’t know, Yusheng…

source_text: 我们当年都在 Stanford 念的书嘛，我记得有一门课上面的老师就说过，手机刚出来的时候，他认为这东西肯定没用的，
zh: 我们当年都在 Stanford 念的书嘛，我记得有一门课上面的老师就说过，手机刚出来的时候，他认为这东西肯定没用的，
en: We both studied at Stanford back then. I remember a professor saying in class that when mobile phones first came out, he was convinced they’d never be useful.

source_text: 说别人找我，你只要座机，就有门课里非常出名的一个老师叫 Diana 叫啥来着，忘掉了，那老师说，
zh: 说别人找我，你只要座机，就有门课里非常出名的一个老师叫 Diana 叫啥来着，忘掉了，那老师说，
en: He said, “If someone needs to reach me, I’ve got a landline.” There was this very well-known professor who taught one of our courses—Diana something, I forget her name—and she said…

source_text: 他说这东西怎么可能会有人用呢？
zh: 他说这东西怎么可能会有人用呢？
en: She said, “Why would anyone ever use one of these?”

source_text: 大哥大那时候，这个要带着这个出去的，然后要找到我，你就打我座机，我出门的时候，我就不想被人这个打搅，
zh: 大哥大那时候，这个要带着这个出去的，然后要找到我，你就打我座机，我出门的时候，我就不想被人这个打搅，
en: Back when mobile phones were those big, bulky bricks, she said, “Why would I carry one around? If you need me, call my landline. When I’m out, I don’t want to be disturbed.”

source_text: 就是人就那个年代的一种一个惯性的。
zh: 就是人就那个年代的一种一个惯性的。
en: That was just how people thought back then—a kind of ingrained habit.

source_text: 但这个东西发展到后来的智能手机的时候，所有人都会抛弃原来的那个惯性，那个偏见，因为这东西真的是够好，
zh: 但这个东西发展到后来的智能手机的时候，所有人都会抛弃原来的那个惯性，那个偏见，因为这东西真的是够好，
en: But once mobile phones evolved into smartphones, everyone let go of those old habits and preconceptions, because the technology had become genuinely useful.

source_text: 能够解决你随时随地，可以你要 reach 别人，别人 reach 到你，进行有必要的这个信息交换。
zh: 能够解决你随时随地，可以你要 reach 别人，别人 reach 到你，进行有必要的这个信息交换。
en: It let you reach others, and others reach you, anytime, anywhere, so you could exchange information when you needed to.

source_text: 而这次不再是信息交换，我觉得这次是一个智能的一个交互。
zh: 而这次不再是信息交换，我觉得这次是一个智能的一个交互。
en: But this time, it’s not just about exchanging information. I think it’s about interacting with intelligence.

source_text: 我觉得那个时代真的来的时候，这个东西肯定是至少在我看来可能人手一个的。
zh: 我觉得那个时代真的来的时候，这个东西肯定是至少在我看来可能人手一个的。
en: I think when that era truly arrives, everyone will probably have one of these—at least, that’s how I see it.

source_text: 所以我是觉得这个方向在这种反正我们这机构就是在这种憧憬下面，我们还是非常有兴趣看待这里面的，
zh: 所以我是觉得这个方向在这种反正我们这机构就是在这种憧憬下面，我们还是非常有兴趣看待这里面的，
en: So I think that’s where things are headed. Our organization shares that vision, and we’re very interested in exploring the opportunities here.

source_text: 不管刚才提到的这个 form factor 形式，还是说它解决问题的这个能力究竟如何。
zh: 不管刚才提到的这个 form factor 形式，还是说它解决问题的这个能力究竟如何。
en: Whether it’s the form factor we just discussed or how well it actually solves problems.

source_text: 我举个例子，instinct 跟其他有个很大不一样的，我也特别喜欢的，它就一个 session，
zh: 我举个例子，instinct 跟其他有个很大不一样的，我也特别喜欢的，它就一个 session，
en: For example, one thing I really like about Instinct that sets it apart is that it has just one session.

source_text: 它就不要你说你要我要去思考这个时候搞一个新的 bot，新的 topic，到了后面你自己都搞不清楚的，搞得人特别累。
zh: 它就不要你说你要我要去思考这个时候搞一个新的 bot，新的 topic，到了后面你自己都搞不清楚的，搞得人特别累。
en: You don’t have to think, “I need a new bot or a new topic for this.” Eventually, you can’t even keep track of them all, and it gets exhausting.

source_text: 理论上就是最近刚发布的 DeepSeek 的 super agent，它最核心的概念就是这个嘛，
zh: 理论上就是最近刚发布的 DeepSeek 的 super agent，它最核心的概念就是这个嘛，
en: In theory, that’s the core idea behind DeepSeek’s recently launched Super Agent.

source_text: 你让一个 agent 作为一个大管家，后面它可以自动去管理这个上下文，
zh: 你让一个 agent 作为一个大管家，后面它可以自动去管理这个上下文，
en: You have one agent act as your central assistant, automatically managing the context behind the scenes.

source_text: 隔离这个 session，一个任务就是一个它的 context，最后你我只要跟一个我的秘书 agent 打交道，
zh: 隔离这个 session，一个任务就是一个它的 context，最后你我只要跟一个我的秘书 agent 打交道，
en: It keeps sessions separate, with each task having its own context. In the end, you and I would only need to interact with a single agent acting as our personal assistant.

source_text: 它其他的自然帮我解决好，最后目的是把任务完成。
zh: 它其他的自然帮我解决好，最后目的是把任务完成。
en: It handles everything else for me, so the task gets done.

source_text: 我觉得这个关键点非常重要，这个就涉及到长程这类的。
zh: 我觉得这个关键点非常重要，这个就涉及到长程这类的。
en: I think this is a really important point. It ties into long-horizon tasks.

source_text: 今天的这个大模型里面的很多的训练数据，用于长程的一些垂直领域的，像 finance，甚至像 travel 里面的那些轨迹数据，
zh: 今天的这个大模型里面的很多的训练数据，用于长程的一些垂直领域的，像 finance，甚至像 travel 里面的那些轨迹数据，
en: A lot of the training data for today’s large models includes task trajectories for long-horizon work in specialized domains like finance and even travel.

source_text: 那些环境，这些数据是远远不够的。
zh: 那些环境，这些数据是远远不够的。
en: But for those environments, there’s nowhere near enough data.

source_text: 今天大模型做得好的其实就一个领域，就是 coding，
zh: 今天大模型做得好的其实就一个领域，就是 coding，
en: Right now, there’s really only one area where large models perform well: coding.

source_text: 就 coding，其他领域的智商水平不是他们做不到，是不在 priority 上。
zh: 就 coding，其他领域的智商水平不是他们做不到，是不在 priority 上。
en: Coding is the only area they’re really good at. It’s not that they can’t reach that level in other fields—it’s just not a priority.

source_text: 因为上个月刚刚跟一个这个大模型，在硅谷一个大模型公司的董事，我就问过他这个问题，
zh: 因为上个月刚刚跟一个这个大模型，在硅谷一个大模型公司的董事，我就问过他这个问题，
en: I asked a board member at a Silicon Valley large-model company about this just last month.

source_text: 为什么我用这个 OpenAI 的时候觉得就是有些生活当中的问题这么傻呢？
zh: 为什么我用这个 OpenAI 的时候觉得就是有些生活当中的问题这么傻呢？
en: Why does OpenAI seem so clueless about some everyday questions?

source_text: 我用的直接就是傻这个词，真的让我觉得有点无语。
zh: 我用的直接就是傻这个词，真的让我觉得有点无语。
en: I literally used the word “stupid.” It honestly left me speechless.

source_text: 写代码呢，很聪明，其实就是他们在 training 的时候，它这个 optimize 的方向的问题，其实是他们 priority 的问题，
zh: 写代码呢，很聪明，其实就是他们在 training 的时候，它这个 optimize 的方向的问题，其实是他们 priority 的问题，
en: It’s very smart when it comes to coding. It really comes down to what they optimize for during training—it’s a matter of priorities.

source_text: 并不是它能力做不到。
zh: 并不是它能力做不到。
en: It’s not that the model isn’t capable of doing it.

source_text: 所以我是觉得加剧还是在 agentic 这块有很多这个能力上面的期待，
zh: 所以我是觉得加剧还是在 agentic 这块有很多这个能力上面的期待，
en: So I think there’s still a lot of room to improve agents, and a lot of expectations for what they’ll be able to do.

source_text: 可以期待的。
zh: 可以期待的。
en: There’s a lot to look forward to.

source_text: 所以对于应用公司而言，那怎么利用它这个模型 agentic 能力的提升，
zh: 所以对于应用公司而言，那怎么利用它这个模型 agentic 能力的提升，
en: So for companies building applications, the question is how to take advantage of improvements in these models’ agentic capabilities.

source_text: 最后把这个刚才说的好的这些应用，这些体验给它做出来，我是非常非常好奇。
zh: 最后把这个刚才说的好的这些应用，这些体验给它做出来，我是非常非常好奇。
en: I’m very, very curious to see how they’ll turn the applications and experiences we’ve been talking about into reality.

source_text: 我说两个角度，第一个角度呢，是其实是一个问题，从最开始接触大模型，我其实一直在思考这问题，但我还没有完整的答案，
zh: 我说两个角度，第一个角度呢，是其实是一个问题，从最开始接触大模型，我其实一直在思考这问题，但我还没有完整的答案，
en: I’ll approach this from two angles. The first is a question I’ve been thinking about ever since I first started working with large language models, but I still don’t have a complete answer.

source_text: 就是大模型的边界的维度是什么。
zh: 就是大模型的边界的维度是什么。
en: What are the different dimensions of a large language model’s limitations?

source_text: 就是大家知道大模型的边界是什么，但是大模型要界定这个边界有哪些维度。
zh: 就是大家知道大模型的边界是什么，但是大模型要界定这个边界有哪些维度。
en: We all know large language models have limits, but what are the dimensions we should use to define those limits?

source_text: 如果说到 personal agent 的话，我觉得其实从不管是软件和硬件，我认为它肯定是大机会，但是都不是创业公司的机会。
zh: 如果说到 personal agent 的话，我觉得其实从不管是软件和硬件，我认为它肯定是大机会，但是都不是创业公司的机会。
en: When it comes to personal agents, I think there’s a huge opportunity in both software and hardware—but neither is really an opportunity for startups.

source_text: 还是那样，我相信今天的 manus 也好，James Park，我觉得他们未来也会很好，但是未必是，
zh: 还是那样，我相信今天的 manus 也好，James Park，我觉得他们未来也会很好，但是未必是，
en: That said, I believe companies like Manus and James Park have bright futures, but they may not necessarily be...

source_text: 包括 instinct，可能未必是现在这个形态，从最那个最简单的一些维度，算力、算法、数据这三个维度看，
zh: 包括 instinct，可能未必是现在这个形态，从最那个最简单的一些维度，算力、算法、数据这三个维度看，
en: Including Instinct. It may not take its current form. But if we look at the three most basic dimensions—compute, algorithms, and data—

source_text: 其实是做一个 agent，personal agent，你的这三个要素没有比大模型，不会比大模型更好。
zh: 其实是做一个 agent，personal agent，你的这三个要素没有比大模型，不会比大模型更好。
en: If you’re building a personal agent, you won’t have an advantage over the large model providers in any of those three areas.

source_text: 这件事情其实同样发生在，如果我们说大模型的技术，我们类比一下，像之前的电脑这个技术的话，它就是这个 operating system，
zh: 这件事情其实同样发生在，如果我们说大模型的技术，我们类比一下，像之前的电脑这个技术的话，它就是这个 operating system，
en: The same thing happened with computers: if we draw an analogy, large-model technology is like the operating system.

source_text: 它底层的这种技术，你会发现这个电脑的很多，不管是生产效率工具，还是你个人助理的很多东西，包括苹果手机，最后都是被平台级的公司给占据了。
zh: 它底层的这种技术，你会发现这个电脑的很多，不管是生产效率工具，还是你个人助理的很多东西，包括苹果手机，最后都是被平台级的公司给占据了。
en: When you look at the underlying technology, you find that many computer-based tools—whether productivity tools or personal assistants, including those on the iPhone—ultimately end up being dominated by platform companies.

source_text: 我不是说这个，这种方向完全不好，但如果是硬件层面的话，这个当然还有苹果这种公司在了，它也做硬件的。
zh: 我不是说这个，这种方向完全不好，但如果是硬件层面的话，这个当然还有苹果这种公司在了，它也做硬件的。
en: I’m not saying this direction has no potential. But on the hardware side, you’ve still got companies like Apple, which make hardware themselves.

source_text: 但它可能是另外一个形态，这是第一个，
zh: 但它可能是另外一个形态，这是第一个，
en: But it might take a different form. That’s my first point.

source_text: 从第一个视角。
zh: 从第一个视角。
en: From the first perspective.

source_text: 第二个视角，那我们看一下这些形态，它可能会是什么。
zh: 第二个视角，那我们看一下这些形态，它可能会是什么。
en: From a second perspective, let’s look at what forms it might take.

source_text: 我觉得第一个就是时间这个维度，时间什么呢？
zh: 我觉得第一个就是时间这个维度，时间什么呢？
en: I think the first dimension is time. What do I mean by that?

source_text: 是基本上凡是你总结一下过去这个稍微好的，
zh: 是基本上凡是你总结一下过去这个稍微好的，
en: Basically, if you look back at the ones that have done reasonably well...

source_text: 很好的，不一定伟大的商业模式，你会发现是凡是帮人节约时间的，都没有帮人消耗时间那么多。
zh: 很好的，不一定伟大的商业模式，你会发现是凡是帮人节约时间的，都没有帮人消耗时间那么多。
en: If you look at successful business models—not necessarily great ones—you’ll find that there are far more that help people spend time than ones that help them save it.

source_text: 你要让用户消耗的时间越来越多，本质上是用户消耗的资源越来越多，但是时间是一个对人来说是最免费的资源，当然还有金钱，
zh: 你要让用户消耗的时间越来越多，本质上是用户消耗的资源越来越多，但是时间是一个对人来说是最免费的资源，当然还有金钱，
en: You want users to spend more and more time on your product. Essentially, that means they’re consuming more resources—but time feels like the most freely available resource to people. Of course, there’s money too.

source_text: 我以前是在创业的时候就一直做 2C，第一个公司就是做中国最早的社交网络，跟那个王兴他们差不多是一代的。
zh: 我以前是在创业的时候就一直做 2C，第一个公司就是做中国最早的社交网络，跟那个王兴他们差不多是一代的。
en: When I was starting companies, I always focused on consumer products. My first company built one of China’s earliest social networks, around the same time as Wang Xing and his team.

source_text: 第二个公司做游戏，游戏里面有一句话是什么呢？
zh: 第二个公司做游戏，游戏里面有一句话是什么呢？
en: My second company made games. There’s a saying in the gaming industry—what is it?

source_text: 是花钱越多的人越会花钱，真的，这个特别逗。
zh: 是花钱越多的人越会花钱，真的，这个特别逗。
en: The more people spend, the more willing they are to keep spending. It’s true—and it’s kind of funny.

source_text: 我其实也花了一段时间才能理解这件事情，但确实是这样。
zh: 我其实也花了一段时间才能理解这件事情，但确实是这样。
en: It took me a while to understand this, but it really is true.

source_text: 所以这个从这个维度来讲，personal agent 像那个，尤其在中国这市场，它要帮人省时间，我觉得这件事情它会，
zh: 所以这个从这个维度来讲，personal agent 像那个，尤其在中国这市场，它要帮人省时间，我觉得这件事情它会，
en: So from that perspective, a personal agent—especially in the Chinese market—is meant to save people time. I think that will…

source_text: 我认为它也会不错，但会越做越小的。
zh: 我认为它也会不错，但会越做越小的。
en: I think it’ll do well too, but the market will get smaller and smaller.

source_text: 你订酒店、
zh: 你订酒店、
en: You book a hotel,

source_text: 订机票、订这些东西的需求，它不是无限的，但有一个东西，比如说我说一个新的 native 的方向，是情绪价值，它是无限的。
zh: 订机票、订这些东西的需求，它不是无限的，但有一个东西，比如说我说一个新的 native 的方向，是情绪价值，它是无限的。
en: The need to book flights, hotels, and things like that isn’t unlimited. But there’s another AI-native direction—emotional support—and the demand for that is limitless.

source_text: 娱乐这是无限的，还有很多，包括搜索，对信息的需求也是无限的。
zh: 娱乐这是无限的，还有很多，包括搜索，对信息的需求也是无限的。
en: Entertainment is limitless too. And there are plenty of other examples, including search—the demand for information is limitless as well.

source_text: 社交网络包括这些，
zh: 社交网络包括这些，
en: That includes social networks and things like that.

source_text: 我觉得可能还有一些别的维度，我就这个就先补充这一个视角来看一下 personal agent 吧。
zh: 我觉得可能还有一些别的维度，我就这个就先补充这一个视角来看一下 personal agent 吧。
en: There may be other angles to consider, but for now I just wanted to add this perspective on personal agents.

source_text: 反正到最后又要回到红果短剧上了。
zh: 反正到最后又要回到红果短剧上了。
en: Anyway, it all comes back to Hongguo’s short dramas in the end.

source_text: 那我一些，那我问一些你们个人，偏你们个人判断的事情，就比如说你们在过去一年，就是 2026 年里头，
zh: 那我一些，那我问一些你们个人，偏你们个人判断的事情，就比如说你们在过去一年，就是 2026 年里头，
en: Let me ask you something more about your personal judgment. Looking back over the past year—2026—

source_text: 你们拒掉的最多的方向的是什么领域赛道的，或者是说你们就有点像是什么，其实什么赛道你们已经不太看了。宇森你能先说说吗？
zh: 你们拒掉的最多的方向的是什么领域赛道的，或者是说你们就有点像是什么，其实什么赛道你们已经不太看了。宇森你能先说说吗？
en: Which sectors have you passed on most often? Or are there any areas you’ve pretty much stopped looking at? Yusen, could you go first?

source_text: 首先我们不是去根据赛道去判断投不投或者看不看，因为我们都还是根据团队的一些特点，这个，而不是说我们只投这个赛道或不投这个赛道。
zh: 首先我们不是去根据赛道去判断投不投或者看不看，因为我们都还是根据团队的一些特点，这个，而不是说我们只投这个赛道或不投这个赛道。
en: First, we don’t decide whether to invest—or even take a look—based on the sector. We focus more on the team’s strengths and characteristics. It’s not a matter of only investing in certain sectors or ruling others out.

source_text: 我整体觉得还是我们很喜欢的，还是说对于技术很了解，同时又对于怎么做产品和商业，
zh: 我整体觉得还是我们很喜欢的，还是说对于技术很了解，同时又对于怎么做产品和商业，
en: Overall, we’re still most drawn to people who really understand the technology and also know how to build products and businesses.

source_text: 至少是有很大的热忱去把它搞清楚的这样一个团队。
zh: 至少是有很大的热忱去把它搞清楚的这样一个团队。
en: At the very least, a team with a strong drive to figure those things out.

source_text: 所以我们今年确实很多这种年轻教授型创业，但它这个可能技术或者搞科研很厉害，但是确实对于怎么做一家公司，
zh: 所以我们今年确实很多这种年轻教授型创业，但它这个可能技术或者搞科研很厉害，但是确实对于怎么做一家公司，
en: So this year, we’ve seen quite a few startups founded by young professors. They may be excellent at technology or research, but when it comes to building a company…

source_text: 怎么去把这个技术和商业结合起来，
zh: 怎么去把这个技术和商业结合起来，
en: how to turn that technology into a viable business,

source_text: 它不只是说不知道，是可能没想过。
zh: 它不只是说不知道，是可能没想过。
en: It’s not just that they don’t know how—they may never have even thought about it.

source_text: 同时呢，可能又这个因为这个美国的 New Lab 很贵，对吧？
zh: 同时呢，可能又这个因为这个美国的 New Lab 很贵，对吧？
en: And at the same time, lab space in the U.S. can be very expensive, right?

source_text: 中国也有很多这个学者团队吧，变得比较贵的项目，这部分我们是就基本都没有投。
zh: 中国也有很多这个学者团队吧，变得比较贵的项目，这部分我们是就基本都没有投。
en: There are also quite a few academic teams in China whose projects have become rather expensive. We’ve generally passed on those.

source_text: 这可能是一个同行投了很多，我们没有投的，因为我们觉得搞科研和搞这个公司还是两个挺不一样的事情。
zh: 这可能是一个同行投了很多，我们没有投的，因为我们觉得搞科研和搞这个公司还是两个挺不一样的事情。
en: This is probably an area where our peers have invested a lot, but we haven’t, because we think doing research and building a company are two very different things.

source_text: 当然比如说那杨志林当时也是清华的这个插院的教授，但是他首先是个连续创业者，第二他后来也从清华出来了，
zh: 当然比如说那杨志林当时也是清华的这个插院的教授，但是他首先是个连续创业者，第二他后来也从清华出来了，
en: Of course, Yang Zhilin was also a professor at Tsinghua’s Institute for AI at the time. But first, he was a serial entrepreneur, and second, he later left Tsinghua.

source_text: 他是可能插院创业的教授里面唯一一个全职的，并且志林是一个非常对于产品、公司、商业都有很多思考和兴趣的人。
zh: 他是可能插院创业的教授里面唯一一个全职的，并且志林是一个非常对于产品、公司、商业都有很多思考和兴趣的人。
en: He may have been the only professor from Tsinghua’s Institute for AI to work full-time on his startup. And Zhilin is someone who thinks deeply about—and is genuinely interested in—products, companies, and business.

source_text: 但我觉得很多时候可能大家把这个好的科研和好的公司，可能这个划等号的话，我觉得可能会有些这个挑战。
zh: 但我觉得很多时候可能大家把这个好的科研和好的公司，可能这个划等号的话，我觉得可能会有些这个挑战。
en: But I think equating good research with a good company can be problematic.

source_text: 所以可能我们反而投的还是一些真的对于 AI 充满热忱、做一些动手去做，已经获得了一定的这个成果的年轻人，
zh: 所以可能我们反而投的还是一些真的对于 AI 充满热忱、做一些动手去做，已经获得了一定的这个成果的年轻人，
